reviewed_competitors.difference: L2X maximizes mutual information through a Gumbel–Softmax top-k subset and requires k in advance. Hide&Seek learns per-feature continuous masks with an adaptive thresholded subset size, adds a sparsity schedule, and replaces fixed ablations with sampled values.

reviewed_competitors.difference: The copula method explicitly models dependence among selected features and can wrap existing selection frameworks. Hide&Seek's replacement sampler deliberately uses the product of marginals for simplicity, so it addresses differentiability and the fixed-ablation channel but not faithful dependency modeling.

Off-Axis accepts the same depth sweep but argues the early position is functional insulation, using matched value rotations and no-mixing controls; it does not establish the multi-model benchmark improvements of the mitigation work.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Geometric Perspective on Next-Token Prediction in Large Language Models: Three Emerging Phases
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lombardo et al. use representation-lens subspaces on eight 1B-32B Qwen/OLMo models to identify seeding, disambiguation, and focal-convergence phases with late low-rank FFN writes. This paper uses one much smaller trained-from-scratch family but adds fixed-unembedding causal interventions, additive-versus-rotational tests, and frame prescription.

reviewed_competitors.title: An Analysis of Residual-Stream Geometry Across Transformer Depth
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bhattacharya and Kolli already separate rigid and non-rigid transition components with orthogonal Procrustes across six instruction-tuned models and find a final-transition residual peak. reviewed_competitors.title: Three-Phase Transformer
reviewed_competitors.difference: Abu Ayyash inserts per-block Givens rotations inside a channel-partitioned residual architecture and reports 7.2% perplexity and 1.93-fold step-count improvements at 123M. Off-Axis inserts one fixed, arbitrary boundary rotation oriented only through its loss, claims no raw quality gain, and focuses on reliable geometry prescription and gauge freedom.

reviewed_competitors.title: LayerSkip: Enabling Early Exit Inference and Self-Speculative Decoding
reviewed_competitors.difference: LayerSkip jointly applies layer dropout and a shared early-exit loss across several Llama sizes, tasks, and training regimes, achieving up to 2.16-fold inference speedups while reporting quality. This paper supplies a representation-level audit of a more direct shared-readout pressure, finding a participation-ratio reduction and cancellation pattern but measuring no deployed speed benefit.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Xiong et al. use mean-field theory to show large output-layer Post-LN gradients at initialization and explain why warmup helps, while Pre-LN gradients are better behaved. reviewed_competitors.difference: Noci et al. show at initialization that rank collapse causes query/key gradients to vanish and propose depth-dependent residual scaling. This paper separates attention-driven entry from RMSNorm-mediated repair failure during actual Post-Norm training, includes SwiGLU, and derives the shared frequency predictor at exact collapse.

reviewed_competitors.title: Why 'classic' Transformers are shallow and how to make them go deep
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yu and Zhang already use token similarity to prove linear escalation from attention's invariant leading eigenspace and spectral gap and propose subtracting excessive similarity in Post-Norm encoders. The current work adapts the scalar analysis to causal prefix attention, adds a SwiGLU correction, and contributes the training-time RMS repair and frequency-loss results.

reviewed_competitors.title: Mind the Gap: a Spectral Analysis of Rank Collapse and Signal Propagation in Attention Layers
reviewed_competitors.difference: Naderi et al. use random-matrix theory to distinguish rank collapse in depth and in width, identify the softmax attention spectral gap, and remove outlier eigenvalues. This paper uses a coarser equal-correlation/prefix-average surrogate but connects it to optimizer-time residual norms, gradient transport, and the collapsed loss floor.

reviewed_competitors.title: Exact Attention Sensitivity and the Geometry of Transformer Stability
reviewed_competitors.difference: Emadi derives exact softmax-Jacobian sensitivity and sequence-length-independent Lipschitz bounds, proving Post-LN compounds normalization Jacobians and validating on 774M models. This paper's novel conditional factor is the growth of pre-RMS norm after similarity collapse and its link to failed repair, but it has smaller-scale and less exact empirical evidence.

reviewed_competitors.title: Post-LayerNorm Is Back: Stable, ExpressivE, and Deep
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chen and Wei identify the ResNet-style Post-LN residual pathway as the main gradient failure and replace it with a Highway connection, reporting stable training beyond 1,000 layers. This paper offers a two-stage similarity/RMS mechanism and endpoint characterization but proposes no validated stabilizer or extreme-depth result.

reviewed_competitors.title: From Condensation to Rank Collapse: A Two-Stage Analysis of Transformer Training Dynamics
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chen and Luo already use a two-stage label for small-initialization training: parameter condensation followed by key-query-driven rank collapse in a simplified single-layer setting. The current two stages are materially different—causal attention amplification at initialization and RMS-mediated backward repair failure in a 48-layer Post-Norm decoder—but the generic two-stage framing is not itself novel.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Parametric Matrix Models already define and prove universality for broad learned matrix-equation models, including affine pencils with eigenvalue readouts. reviewed_competitors.difference: Spectrahedral regression fits the maximum eigenvalue of an affine matrix pencil, proves convex approximation/risk bounds, and analyzes alternating minimization. reviewed_competitors.title: Input Convex Neural Networks

reviewed_competitors.title: Deep Lattice Networks and Partial Monotonic Functions
reviewed_competitors.difference: Deep lattice networks guarantee partial monotonicity using constrained calibrators, lattices, and embeddings and report strong real-world results. reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Additive Models: Interpretable Machine Learning with Neural Nets

reviewed_competitors.title: Maxout Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: When all coefficient matrices commute, the largest-eigenvalue spectral neuron reduces to a maxout unit and other indices become order-statistic units. Noncommuting matrices are the source of the proposed model's additional smooth spectral interactions and motivate its initialization.

The current paper reuses that exact controlled regime and contributes the new interference experiment plus spectral correlates, not the equilibrium account of grokking itself.

reviewed_competitors.title: ePC: Fast and Deep Predictive Coding in Digital Simulation
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Diagnoses exponential signal decay in state-based PC and reparameterizes the computation to avoid it.

reviewed_competitors.title: SVD-LLM: Truncation-aware Singular Value Decomposition for Large Language Model Compression
reviewed_competitors.relationship: The direct host and experimental baseline; it whitens activations so coefficient magnitude aligns with layer reconstruction loss and provides post-truncation recovery.
reviewed_competitors.difference: SVD-Surgeon leaves the host factorization fixed and applies task-loss empirical-Fisher OBS compensation to retained coefficients; its comparison excludes SVD-LLM's iterative LoRA-style recovery.

reviewed_competitors.title: Optimal Brain Decomposition for Accurate LLM Low-Rank Approximation
reviewed_competitors.relationship: The closest second-order low-rank competitor; uses task-loss Hessian structure to derive bidirectional whitening and a closed-form decomposition.
reviewed_competitors.difference: OBD-LLM changes how the low-rank factors are formed using K-FAC input/output curvature, while SVD-Surgeon performs OBS repair in the coefficient basis of an already chosen host factorization.

reviewed_competitors.title: IO-SVD: Input-Output Whitened SVD for Adaptive-Rank LLM Compression
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A contemporary loss-aware SVD competitor that combines input whitening with an output metric from a second-order KL expansion and globally allocates heterogeneous ranks.
reviewed_competitors.difference: IO-SVD changes the factorization metric and rank allocation before truncation, whereas SVD-Surgeon projects per-sample task gradients into a fixed host coefficient basis and repairs only the retained coefficients afterward.

reviewed_competitors.title: Zero Sum SVD: Balancing Loss Sensitivity for Low Rank LLM Compression
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A close post-training competitor that uses activation whitening, first-order calibration-loss estimates, global component selection, and an optional single projected-gradient correction.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zero Sum SVD optimizes cross-layer selection and optionally updates/retruncates weights using first-order information; SVD-Surgeon uses an OBS block solve to compensate retained coefficients within each already selected factorization.

reviewed_competitors.title: SigmaScale: LLM Compression with SVD-based Low-Rank Decomposition and Learned Scaling Matrices
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A near-contemporaneous SVD compressor that learns diagonal row and column scalings under an activation-aware reconstruction loss before truncation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: SigmaScale iteratively learns a more compressible coordinate system and then decomposes it; SVD-Surgeon accepts a fixed host coordinate system and applies a closed-form task-gradient compensation after pruning.

reviewed_competitors.title: The LLM Surgeon
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Scales curvature-aware surgery and survivor updates to structured and unstructured LLM pruning.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It uses Kronecker-factored weight-space curvature to remove rows, columns, or weights; SVD-Surgeon reduces the problem to diagonal factor coefficients and targets dense low-rank deployment.

reviewed_competitors.title: ASVD: Activation-aware Singular Value Decomposition for Compressing Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A training-free low-rank compressor that rescales weights using activation statistics and allocates layer-specific ranks.
reviewed_competitors.difference: ASVD makes the decomposition activation-aware and includes iterative calibration; SVD-Surgeon uses per-sample task-loss gradients to repair retained coefficients after a host truncation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Language model compression with weighted low-rank factorization
reviewed_competitors.relationship: An earlier Fisher-aware low-rank method that weights reconstruction errors by parameter importance before factorization.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Fisher-Weighted SVD uses importance weighting to form the low-rank approximation for task-specific language models; SVD-Surgeon instead estimates a compact full coefficient covariance and solves for survivor compensation after a host truncation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Muown: Row-Norm Control for Muon Optimization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Muown already decomposes each matrix into Adam-updated row magnitudes and a Muon-updated stored direction and reports large-step robustness; AngularMuown's narrower addition is the row-oblique interpretation and explicit angular schedule.

reviewed_competitors.title: Improving Neural Network Training by Decoupling the Magnitude and Direction of Weight Vectors
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work also keeps a magnitude-direction factor on a fixed sphere and directly controls rotation, but uses row-and-column scale factors with an ambient chain-rule gradient rather than AngularMuown's rowwise Riemannian gradient and separate kappa schedule.

reviewed_competitors.title: Rotational Equilibrium: How Weight Decay Balances Learning Across Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Rotational Equilibrium already formalizes angular learning rates for scale-invariant weights and enforces a predicted equilibrium rotation; AngularMuown schedules direction angle independently of radial magnitude rather than matching a weight-decay equilibrium.

reviewed_competitors.title: Weight Normalization: A Simple Reparameterization to Accelerate Training of Deep Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Weight Normalization established learnable magnitude and direction factors; the present paper applies a rowwise manifold version inside a matrix-aware optimizer and adds spectral tangent updates plus an explicit angular schedule.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Spectral Condition for Feature Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: The spectral condition motivates dimension-aware matrix update scales for feature learning; AngularMuown specializes that principle to typical per-row rotation and does not establish the condition for every realized row.

reviewed_competitors.title: NorMuon: Making Muon more efficient and scalable
reviewed_competitors.difference: NorMuon adds neuron-wise adaptive scaling after orthogonalization and is the strongest reported non-Muown baseline in several sweeps; it does not split radial magnitude from an explicitly scheduled manifold direction.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Polar Express: Optimal Matrix Sign Methods and Their Application to the Muon Algorithm
reviewed_competitors.difference: Polar Express improves the matrix-sign computation used by Muon and is used in the experiments; it changes orthogonalization accuracy and cost, not radial-angular parameterization or scheduling.

reviewed_competitors.title: Training Deep Learning Models with Norm-Constrained LMOs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Norm-constrained linear minimization oracles already place spectral updates in an explicit norm geometry and study learning-rate transfer; AngularMuown adds a row-oblique retraction and separate radial optimizer.

reviewed_competitors.title: Muon is Scalable for LLM Training
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work establishes scalable Muon recipes and shape-dependent update scaling at much larger LLM scale; AngularMuown reports a new angular controller but does not yet match that scale or isolate throughput-adjusted gains.

reviewed_competitors.title: Training nGPT
reviewed_competitors.difference: Training nGPT combines unit-hypersphere parameters, angular update control, logarithmic decay, and GatedAdamW at up to 14B total parameters; it weakens any broad claim that explicit angular control or large-scale normalized training is unique to AngularMuown.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Simple and Effective Pruning Approach for Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wanda prunes pretrained LLM weights by magnitude times activation without retraining. It targets compression and perplexity, not coordinate-MLP compositionality, making it a weak direct baseline unless adaptation and budget matching are specified.

reviewed_competitors.title: LLM-Pruner: On the Structural Pruning of Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: LLM-Pruner removes coupled Transformer structures using gradient information and recovers them with LoRA. Its native architecture and objective differ sharply from CPPN neuron pruning, so zero EMC2 offers limited mechanism discrimination.

reviewed_competitors.title: Position: A Theory of Deep Learning Must Include Compositional Sparsity
reviewed_competitors.difference: Danhofer et al. argue that bounded-local-arity function structure explains deep approximation efficiency while leaving learnability open. The current paper claims to close that optimization gap, but its volume proof does not sustain the claim.

reviewed_competitors.title: Break It Down: Evidence for Structural Compositionality in Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lepori et al. test structural compositionality through functionally selective subnetworks across vision, language, architectures, tasks, and pretraining regimes. That is broader functional evidence than single-image perturbation robustness and narrows the present emergence claim.

reviewed_competitors.title: Compositional Generalization from First Principles
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wiedemer et al. derive support and architecture conditions sufficient for held-out compositional generalization from a data-generating-process view. The present work studies parameter robustness without held-out combinations, so it does not subsume that generalization claim.

reviewed_competitors.title: Compositional Generalization in Grounded Language Learning via Induced Model Sparsity
reviewed_competitors.difference: Spilsbury and Ilin explicitly induce sparse word-attribute correspondences and evaluate novel property combinations. It predates the sparsity-to-composition intuition and uses a genuine generalization split absent from EMC2.

reviewed_competitors.title: Toy Models of Superposition
reviewed_competitors.difference: Elhage et al. explain polysemanticity as capacity-efficient superposition and exhibit phase changes tied to feature sparsity and importance. That account provides an alternative to the paper's depth-volume explanation and does not equate orthogonality with semantics.

reviewed_competitors.title: Language Model Circuits Are Sparse in the Neuron Basis
reviewed_competitors.difference: Arora et al. use gradient-based attribution and causal steering to identify task-effective sparse neuron circuits in language models, including latent multi-hop steps. This is broader causal evidence for neuron-basis circuit sparsity than visual resemblance of coordinate-MLP feature maps, but it does not study emergence under the target paper's depth-pruning intervention.

reviewed_competitors.title: How Deep Neural Networks Learn Compositional Data: The Random Hierarchy Model
reviewed_competitors.difference: The Random Hierarchy Model already uses analytically controlled hierarchical synthetic tasks to study how deep networks learn invariant representations and sample complexity. reviewed_competitors.title: A is for Absorption: Studying Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work demonstrates that hierarchical features create SAE absorption and validates a detection metric on hundreds of LLM SAEs. reviewed_competitors.difference: Adversarial Tokenization already treats exponentially many byte-identical segmentations as an inference-time optimization axis and demonstrates safety-filter evasion on three models and adversarial datasets. The present paper uses stochastic rather than attack-optimized segmentation and emphasizes constructive diversity, but must account for this prior method and threat model.

reviewed_competitors.title: Word Recovery in Large Language Models Enables Character-Level Tokenization Robustness
reviewed_competitors.difference: Word Recovery decodes canonical word identities, causally removes the corresponding subspace, and masks early in-group character attention to connect recovery with task performance. That provides a specific causal mechanism stronger than the current paper's final-token displacement statistics, while the latter contributes training-stage and search-diversity views.

reviewed_competitors.title: From Tokens to Words: On the Inner Lexicon of LLMs
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work shows early/middle-layer intrinsic detokenization into whole-word representations, robustness to arbitrary splits and typos, and a vocabulary-expansion application. It anticipates the internal canonicalization interpretation; the present study focuses on exact valid-vocabulary segmentations, checkpoint evolution, and best-of-k behavior.

reviewed_competitors.title: BPE-Dropout: Simple and Effective Subword Regularization
reviewed_competitors.difference: BPE-Dropout stochastically exposes a model to multiple segmentations during training and reports translation gains, establishing segmentation as a regularization axis. The current work is training-free at inference and studies models not intentionally trained on such variants, but its general premise that alternate BPE segmentations are useful is longstanding.

reviewed_competitors.title: Tokenization counts: the impact of tokenization on arithmetic in frontier LLMs
reviewed_competitors.difference: This paper changes digit grouping at inference, shows large arithmetic effects and stereotyped errors, and finds the gap decreases with scale. It predates the claim that inference-time token boundaries expose different computations, though its comma-modified visible strings are not the exact byte-preserving control used here.

reviewed_competitors.title: zip2zip: Inference-Time Adaptive Tokenization via Online Compression
reviewed_competitors.difference: zip2zip learns dynamic hypertokens through online compression and light uptraining, reducing input and output token counts by 15-40%. It targets efficiency rather than stochastic diversity and changes the active vocabulary, but provides a more deployment-oriented adaptive-tokenization alternative to the current method's expensive prompt expansion.

reviewed_competitors.title: Subword Regularization: Improving Neural Network Translation Models with Multiple Subword Candidates
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kudo introduced sampling multiple subword segmentations from a unigram language model for training and decoding, establishing multiple segmentation candidates as a robustness and performance tool. The present paper's distinction is post-hoc valid decomposition of fixed-tokenizer LLM prompts and representational auditing rather than a new multiple-segmentation principle.

reviewed_competitors.title: Energy Transformer
reviewed_competitors.difference: Energy Transformer derives iterative Transformer-like updates from an engineered token energy and already evaluates image completion, graph anomaly detection, and graph classification. CDAT retains its core energy-based block and benchmarks, adding W, scalar damping, noise, and a two-energy presentation; ET is therefore the decisive matched baseline and bounds the incremental novelty.

reviewed_competitors.title: Hopfield Networks is All You Need
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work establishes continuous modern Hopfield networks, exponential storage, one-step retrieval, energy minima, and equivalence of the update to Transformer attention. CDAT's Hopfield refinement and attention-as-associative-memory motivation build directly on this established foundation rather than introducing the equivalence.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Iterative Reasoning through Energy Minimization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Du et al. train energy functions whose iterative minimization performs multi-step reasoning, directly testing the premise that learned computation can be an optimization trajectory. CDAT applies iterative energy dynamics to graph representation but does not establish that its extra controls improve reasoning depth or convergence on controlled energy landscapes.

reviewed_competitors.title: End-to-end Differentiable Clustering with Associative Memories
reviewed_competitors.difference: This paper uses associative-memory energy minimization as an end-to-end differentiable prototype-clustering solver and analyzes convergence to learned memories. It is a close precursor to CDAT's prototype refinement term; CDAT adds graph tasks and linear controls but does not compare on the controlled clustering/retrieval setting.

reviewed_competitors.title: Dense Associative Memory Through the Lens of Random Features
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work develops random-feature views and scalable approximations for dense associative memory while preserving its retrieval structure. It addresses the computational and theoretical scaling of the memory primitive more directly; CDAT instead adds an iterative feature-mixing controller with only small-benchmark runtime evidence.

reviewed_competitors.title: On Sparse Modern Hopfield Model
reviewed_competitors.difference: This paper derives sparse modern Hopfield retrieval and studies efficiency/capacity trade-offs in the core associative-memory operation. It offers a principled alternative control over interactions; CDAT's rank-4 W is sparse only in rank, not interaction topology, and its topology claim is not directly compared.

reviewed_competitors.title: Associative Transformer
reviewed_competitors.difference: Associative Transformer combines explicit learned memory, sparse bottleneck attention, and Hopfield-energy token reconstruction for vision classification and relational reasoning. It is an alternate route to associative inductive bias with broader reasoning tasks; CDAT instead uses repeated energy descent and reports graph benchmarks.

reviewed_competitors.title: Phase Transitions between Accuracy Regimes in L2 regularized Deep Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: This earlier work already studies L2-induced accuracy phases, local minima, hysteresis, and grokking-like jumps; the present paper's narrower addition is controlled deep-linear rank metastability and a proposed SGD escape-time law.

reviewed_competitors.title: Power-law escape rate of SGD
reviewed_competitors.difference: Mori et al. derive that multiplicative SGD noise for mean-square loss yields escape governed by a log-loss barrier and power-law behavior, contrary to a linear-loss Arrhenius borrowing; the present paper does not fit or falsify that alternative.

reviewed_competitors.title: Exact solutions to the nonlinear dynamics of learning in deep linear neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Saxe et al. already derive independent singular-mode plateaus and rapid stage-like learning under aligned balanced conditions; the present paper adds L2-created local minima and stochastic checkpoint escape.

reviewed_competitors.title: Implicit bias of SGD in $L_{2}$-regularized linear DNNs: One-way jumps from high to low rank
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wang and Jacot prove stochastic accessibility and absorbing low-rank sets for L2-regularized linear DNNs, with one-way high-to-low rank jumps; the present experiment emphasizes prepared low-to-high mode acquisition and an Arrhenius timing interpretation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Phase transitions reveal hierarchical structure in deep neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work studies sequential phase transitions as hierarchical feature structure is acquired in deep networks; the present paper instead assigns sequential steps to independent singular-mode escape in a prepared linear landscape.

reviewed_competitors.title: Grokking in Linear Estimators -- A Solvable Model that Groks without Understanding
reviewed_competitors.difference: Levi et al. derive delayed accuracy in linear estimators and show that thresholded accuracy can create apparent grokking without a representational phase change; the present paper uses loss and rank transitions but does not rule out metric-induced sharpness in its grokking framing.

reviewed_competitors.title: Dichotomy of Early and Late Phase Implicit Biases Can Provably Induce Grokking
reviewed_competitors.difference: This theory explains grokking through a change from early optimization bias to late regularized bias without requiring noise-driven barrier escape; the present paper does not compare basin residence against that deterministic two-phase account.

reviewed_competitors.title: Grokking as a First Order Phase Transition in Two Layer Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work attributes abrupt generalization to competition between memorizing and generalizing solutions in a tractable nonlinear setting; the present paper attributes timing to stochastic escape among rank states and does not include a memorizing solution in its sparse demonstration.

reviewed_competitors.title: Is Grokking a Computational Glass Relaxation?
reviewed_competitors.difference: The computational-glass account studies rugged nonlinear solutions and reports that grokking need not follow a simple entropy-barrier picture; the present paper's basin is an engineered low-rank linear minimum with an unmeasured entropic correction.

reviewed_competitors.title: Progress Measures for Grokking via Mechanistic Interpretability
reviewed_competitors.difference: Mechanistic progress measures reveal gradual Fourier-circuit formation before the accuracy jump in modular addition; the present model instead produces abrupt independent mode escapes and supplies no circuit-level nonlinear evidence.

reviewed_competitors.title: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
reviewed_competitors.difference: The canonical phenomenon requires fitting a small algorithmic training set long before test generalization; the present sparse linear experiment deliberately omits that memorization stage and should therefore be treated as grokking-like rather than a direct reproduction.

reviewed_competitors.title: Low-Dimensional and Transversely Curved Optimization Dynamics in Grokking
reviewed_competitors.difference: This Transformer study reports low-dimensional confinement and transverse-curvature growth before modular-arithmetic grokking, with interventions showing orthogonal motion is necessary but boosted curvature is insufficient. It supplies nonlinear metastable-regime evidence absent here, but does not establish an Arrhenius SGD escape law or the prepared deep-linear rank mechanism.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Stochastic--Geometric Theory of Scaling Laws in Grokking
reviewed_competitors.relationship: current stochastic escape and scaling competitor
reviewed_competitors.difference: This post-target theory models Adam with weight-shrinkage as escape from a shell-core memorization geometry and derives scaling in learning rate, batch size, and L2 regularization. Its broader factorial scaling claims are an exact current comparison for the present paper's fixed-batch learning-rate line, though its optimizer, geometry, and nonlinear experiments differ.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformative or Conservative? Conservation laws for ResNets and Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: Marcotte et al. already characterize conservation laws for modern residual/convolutional blocks and a single attention layer, introduce subset-supported laws to reduce full architectures to isolated blocks, and study discrete SGD persistence. The current paper directly resolves that work's multihead conjecture and adds exact modern activations, RoPE, and MoE, so its novelty is an extension of this framework rather than a new conservation-law program.

reviewed_competitors.title: Abide by the Law and Follow the Flow: Conservation Laws for Gradient Flows
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work rigorously defines dataset-independent gradient-flow laws, connects them to Lie algebras of model Jacobians, and gives algorithms for maximal polynomial and general independent laws. The current paper replaces Lie calculations with meromorphic pole analysis for specific modern components; the definition and completeness objective are inherited.

reviewed_competitors.title: Keep the Momentum: Conservation Laws beyond Euclidean Gradient Flows
reviewed_competitors.difference: This paper characterizes laws for momentum and non-Euclidean flows, finds temporal laws and conservation loss, and shows ReLU laws can disappear under momentum. It covers practical optimizer geometry omitted here and cautions that the current Euclidean-gradient-flow results need not survive modern optimization.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Mechanics: Symmetry and Broken Conservation Laws in Deep Learning Dynamics
reviewed_competitors.difference: Neural Mechanics derives architecture-symmetry constraints on gradients/Hessians and modified-gradient-flow expressions for finite learning rates and batches, validating them on VGG-16. It predates the symmetry/conservation interpretation and addresses finite-step breaking more mechanistically; the current work emphasizes complete C1 panels for newer blocks.

reviewed_competitors.title: Algorithmic Regularization in Learning Deep Homogeneous Models: Layers are Automatically Balanced
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work proves squared-norm differences across homogeneous layers remain invariant under gradient flow and connects balancing to convergence under finite-step optimization. It is an early concrete instance of the A/C-style balance laws generalized here, with stronger optimization consequences than the current tracking-only experiments.

reviewed_competitors.title: Gradient descent aligns the layers of deep linear networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: This paper proves risk convergence, rank-one asymptotics, and cross-layer alignment for deep linear networks, linking balanced dynamics to max-margin implicit bias. The current paper studies broader component-level laws but stops before deriving comparable consequences for learned functions or generalization.

reviewed_competitors.title: Conservation Laws from Data Symmetry in Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: This paper asks whether training-data symmetries add gradient-flow integrals, proves generic nonexistence for analytic non-polynomial losses, and finds MSE/data-augmentation exceptions for tensorizable networks including Lightning Attention. It complements rather than duplicates the target: its laws may depend on data symmetry, whereas the target quantifies over all datasets to isolate architecture-only laws.

reviewed_competitors.title: Conservation Law Breaking at the Edge of Stability: A Spectral Theory of Non-Convex Neural Network Optimization
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work derives and tests spectral formulas for discrete-gradient drift of ReLU balance laws across 23 experiments, including an eta-squared decomposition and edge-of-stability crossover. It provides quantitative finite-step consequences and fitted exponents that the target's qualitative O(tau^2 k) plots omit, while covering narrower homogeneous-network invariants rather than GELU, attention, RoPE, or MoE completeness.

reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest later direct competitor deriving a residual law specifically for revisited Transformer blocks.
reviewed_competitors.difference: DeepLoop models tied-depth update reuse with a visit-alignment coefficient and adapts Post-LN DeepNorm, using alpha=(2N)^(1/2) and beta=(8N)^(-1/2) in its own parameterization; it reports GPT-2-small/medium validation and downstream gains. The reviewed paper instead studies a pre-norm additive branch, proves a conditional ReLU positive-cone 1/N law, and factorizes physical depth. The exponents are not directly interchangeable because the architectures and alpha/beta conventions differ, but DeepLoop defeats any claim that 1/N is the only current tied-depth formulation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Depthwise Hyperparameter Transfer in Residual Networks: Dynamics and Scaling Limit
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest ordinary-depth scaling and hyperparameter-transfer precursor.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bordelon et al. combine muP with 1/sqrt(depth) residual scaling, demonstrate transfer on ResNets and ViTs, and derive a joint infinite-width/depth feature-learning limit for distinct layers. The reviewed paper's main novelty is showing that exact parameter reuse invalidates that independent-layer random walk under its ReLU conditions; it does not provide a comparable joint limit or multi-seed scale of validation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Don't be lazy: CompleteP enables compute-efficient deep transformers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest Transformer parameterization work joining depth transfer with useful feature learning.
reviewed_competitors.difference: CompleteP shows that hyperparameter transfer alone can remain in a lazy regime and reports 12-34% compute-efficiency improvements across distinct-layer shapes. The reviewed recipe imports a depth correction and adds a loop-specific 1/N factor, but measures neither non-lazy feature change nor compute efficiency per recurrent FLOP; norm stability therefore does not establish that added loops are used productively.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scaling Latent Reasoning via Looped Language Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest large-scale practical looped-language-model predecessor and same-lab motivation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ouro pretrains 1.4B/2.6B looped models on up to 7.7T tokens with entropy-regularized learned depth and broad reasoning evaluation. It establishes practical recurrent-depth value but does not isolate the residual exponent or loop-invariant learning-rate law. The reviewed paper contributes that focused mechanism, while its 183M-438M, 10B-token single-seed sweep is far smaller and has no adaptive-depth or reasoning outcome.

reviewed_competitors.title: Loop Neural Networks for Parameter Sharing
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct earlier empirical language-model study of looping residual model subsets.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ng and Wang revisit inputs through a looped subset of GPT-2 and report better language modeling at similar parameter count without extra data. They do not derive residual or learning-rate scaling. The reviewed paper supplies a stability prescription and controlled N-by-L sweeps, but does not compare directly with this architecture or show whether 1/N improves its iterative-refinement benefit.

reviewed_competitors.title: Reasoning with Latent Thoughts: On the Power of Looped Transformers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest theory-and-experiment predecessor on effective depth and reasoning in looped Transformers.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Saunshi et al. show k-layer models looped L times can approach kL untied layers on synthetic and language reasoning tasks and prove iterative expressivity/latent-thought results. They do not study the residual stability threshold. The reviewed paper addresses optimization parameterization instead, but its 1/N scaling could also attenuate the effective computation whose benefits this predecessor measures, a tradeoff left unevaluated.

reviewed_competitors.title: Universal Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: Universal Transformers repeatedly apply shared transition and attention computation and optionally halt per position, with algorithmic, language-understanding, and translation evaluations. The reviewed paper's residual/LR law is new relative to this architectural precursor, but its fixed-loop pre-norm stack does not cover dynamic halting, per-position recurrence, or the normalization and transition details of UT.

reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational attention-faithfulness challenge and direct non-identifiability comparator.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Jain and Wallace show that attention can be uncorrelated with importance and that very different attention distributions can yield equivalent predictions. Hayes et al. improve on purely observational attention by substituting executable matrices, but behavior preservation still demonstrates one sufficient routing surrogate rather than a unique explanation of the complete computation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Compositional Explanations of Neurons
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest same-coauthor predecessor using symbolic expressions to approximate component behavior.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Mu and Andreas search compositional logical concepts for vision/NLI neurons, relate them to behavior, and use them to generate predictable adversarial examples. The reviewed work scales from neuron predicates to executable attention-matrix Python in modern LMs and performs substitution, but does not match the predecessor's adversarial predictive test or independently validate its semantic categories.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Transformer Programs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Friedman et al. train a constrained Transformer that automatically decompiles into a discrete program, then use code-analysis tools on algorithmic and NLP tasks. Hayes et al. uniquely work post hoc on ordinary pretrained LMs, but only decompile attention routing while values, outputs, MLPs, and residual interactions remain neural; it therefore has broader checkpoint applicability and weaker end-to-end semantics.

reviewed_competitors.title: Opening the AI black box: program synthesis via mechanistic interpretability
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest direct predecessor extracting executable Python from learned neural algorithms.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Michaud et al.'s MIPS converts RNNs on 62 algorithmic tasks into finite-state machines and applies Boolean/integer symbolic regression, solving 32 tasks and extracting a more end-to-end algorithm. Hayes et al. use an LLM to scale proxy synthesis to 1,664 attention-head assignments in pretrained LMs, but their programs capture only the A matrix and are not validated for exact algorithm recovery.

reviewed_competitors.title: Towards Understanding the Nature of Attention with Low-Rank Sparse Decomposition
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest prior attention-component replacement and decomposition competitor in modern LLMs.
reviewed_competitors.difference: LoRSA learns a sparse replacement for multi-head attention, disentangles induction, successor, sink, and arithmetic components in models including Llama-3.1-8B, and evaluates interpretability/circuit discovery. Hayes et al. produce unrestricted human-readable Python without retraining the target, but approximate individual observed attention matrices and omit value-weighted or circuit-level decomposition. The two approaches compete directly on whether replacement structure yields interpretable attention components.

reviewed_competitors.title: Can Interpretation Predict Behavior on Unseen Data?
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest current primary standard for prospective predictive validity under distribution shift.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Li et al. use in-distribution attention patterns to predict which OOD rule hundreds of synthetic Transformers follow and explicitly decouple predictive value from causal support. Hayes et al. do behavioral replacement on six unseen task datasets, but never remeasure proxy-head alignment there or prospectively predict which inputs/programs will fail; its attention-level validation remains TinyStories-only.

reviewed_competitors.title: Analyzing Multi-Head Self-Attention: Specialized Heads Do the Heavy Lifting, the Rest Can Be Pruned
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct head-importance, linguistic-specialization, and pruning baseline.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Voita et al. show many heads can be removed with little performance loss—for example 38 of 48 encoder heads for only 0.15 BLEU—and that important heads often have interpretable roles. Hayes et al. replace rather than remove high-IoU heads, but without a matched pruning or random-head curve it cannot separate program fidelity from redundancy or beneficial pruning.

reviewed_competitors.title: Validating Mechanistic Interpretations: An Axiomatic Approach
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest formal standard for deciding whether a mechanistic interpretation captures network semantics compositionally.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Palumbo et al. formulate axioms inspired by abstract interpretation and validate interpretations on a known case and a Transformer 2-SAT solver. Hayes et al. provide executable substitution but test no completeness/compositionality axioms: a Python matrix proxy can preserve selected behavior while omitting values, OV maps, and compensating circuits. This primary comparator narrows the paper's 'formal description' rhetoric.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Marek et al. scale Adam's second-moment half-life in token units and show stable vanilla SGD at very small batches, directly addressing a confound in the present paper's mostly tied-beta sweeps. The present work contributes much broader architecture and modality counterexamples but does not adopt that moment-matching rule throughout.

reviewed_competitors.title: Is your batch size the problem? Revisiting the Adam-SGD gap in language modeling
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct precursor isolating batch size, momentum, and clipping in Transformer language modeling.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sreckovic et al. already show that carefully tuned momentum SGD can approach Adam at small batch and analyze the trend with SDE-inspired quadratics. The present paper expands that observation across four modalities and non-Transformer models, but its fixed-token sweeps still conflate batch with update count and its theory likewise uses simplified proxies.

reviewed_competitors.title: Heavy-Tailed Class Imbalance and Why Adam Outperforms Gradient Descent on Language Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Primary statement of the heavy-tailed class-imbalance mechanism explicitly stress-tested by the present paper.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kunstner et al. provide causal synthetic and cross-architecture evidence that class imbalance can generate correlated gradients and an Adam advantage. The present HG38, ZINC, and modernized-ViT results show that this mechanism is not necessary and can be recipe-sensitive, but do not refute it as a contributor in the settings Kunstner et al. study.

reviewed_competitors.title: Why Transformers Need Adam: A Hessian Perspective
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct Hessian block-heterogeneity explanation for Adam's Transformer advantage.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhang et al. measure blockwise Hessian heterogeneity and argue that one global SGD learning rate cannot accommodate it. The present hybrid and sign-reversal experiments show heterogeneity is not sufficient for a universal ranking and introduce a different clipped-geometry ratio, but they do not measure that ratio or fully arbitrate between the Hessian hypotheses.

reviewed_competitors.title: Noise Is Not the Main Factor Behind the Gap Between SGD and Adam on Transformers, but Sign Descent Might Be
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational direct comparison motivating both large-batch sign-descent behavior and the paper's Adam proxy.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kunstner et al. control stochasticity up to full batch and find that Adam benefits more from lower noise while sign descent closes much of the deterministic gap. The present work adopts sign momentum as a theoretical proxy and adds cross-domain counterexamples, but does not validate that proxy quantitatively on its neural runs.

reviewed_competitors.title: Deconstructing What Makes a Good Optimizer for Language Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct component- and optimizer-level comparison in autoregressive language-model training.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhao et al. compare SGD, Adam, Adafactor, Lion, and Sophia across scales and localize much of SGD's weakness to output-head and normalization treatment. The present hybrid table reproduces that localization and adds embedding plus cross-domain sign reversals; it does not match Zhao et al.'s optimizer breadth or establish why the remaining all-Adam gap persists.

reviewed_competitors.title: How to Fine-Tune Vision Models with SGD
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct vision-side parameter-block explanation tested by the hybrid and architecture interventions.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kumar et al. find that unusually large embedding-layer gradients drive an AdamW advantage in vision transfer and that freezing under 1% of parameters restores SGD. The present work trains from scratch, assigns Adam rather than freezing blocks, and shows the ranking can reverse on ImageNet-21K; the settings therefore constrain, rather than replicate, the fine-tuning mechanism.

reviewed_competitors.title: Revisiting the Adam-SGD Gap in LLM Pre-Training: The Role of Large Effective Learning Rates
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current direct alternative mechanism for the large-batch pretraining gap.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Glentis et al. attribute much of the gap to SGD's inability to sustain Adam-like effective learning rates because output-layer imbalance and gradient spikes limit stability, and recover most performance with clipping at 1B scale. The present paper spans more domains and architectures but uses much smaller models and does not isolate effective learning rate as the common mediator.

reviewed_competitors.title: Traces of Memorisation in Large Language Models for Code
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct predecessor measuring extractable training-code memorization and near-verbatim recovery across code models.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Al-Kaswan et al. build code extraction benchmarks and report substantial verbatim recovery from vulnerable prefixes, including model-size trends. The present work narrows to one transparent exposed/reference checkpoint pair and broadens the target from text to behavior, but lacks the predecessor's multi-model scale comparison.

reviewed_competitors.title: Unveiling Memorization in Code Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct multi-model empirical study of code-training memorization and extraction factors.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yang et al. search large sets of generated outputs for verbatim training-code fragments and study model size, output length, prompt, and duplication effects. The present paper gains a same-architecture pre-exposure reference and semantic metrics, but evaluates only one 32B model and does not test those scaling or duplication factors.

reviewed_competitors.title: Measuring memorization in RLHF for code completion
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest checkpoint-stage counterfactual study of code memorization across an additional training process.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Pappu et al. track how textual code memorization surfaces and propagates through RLHF and direct preference learning. The present paper studies midtraining exposure and adds structural, LLM-functional, and execution evidence; it does not isolate alignment-stage mechanisms or use controlled preference examples.

reviewed_competitors.title: How Much Do Code Language Models Remember? An Investigation on Data Extraction Attacks before and after Fine-tuning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct extraction-attack comparison before and after code-model fine-tuning.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Salerno et al. benchmark pretraining and fine-tuning sample extractability under textual attack categories. The present exposed/reference design addresses a similar stage-change question but makes functional clone detection the central estimand; its functional rates are consequently not comparable to textual extraction prevalence without calibration.

reviewed_competitors.title: Decoding Secret Memorization in Code LLMs Through Token-Level Characterization
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct code-model extraction study targeting sensitive credentials rather than whole functions.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Nie et al. distinguish real from hallucinated secrets with token-probability features and guide decoding to improve secret extraction across four code LLMs. The present work instead uses greedy signature completion and asks whether broader function behavior reappears; it does not implement an adaptive attack or verify that LLM-selected logic is actually confidential.

reviewed_competitors.title: Memorize or Generalize? Evaluating LLM Code Generation with Code Rewriting
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct behavioral alternative to surface-similarity definitions of code memorization.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhang et al. rewrite benchmark tasks semantically and define harmful memorization through high solution similarity plus failure on the rewritten task. The present paper instead knows a midtraining exposure boundary and compares generated functions directly with training code, but lacks the rewriting study's task-correctness/generalization control and multi-model comparisons.

reviewed_competitors.title: Extracting alignment data in open models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest cross-domain extraction work using semantic rather than only string-space leakage signals.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Barbero et al. use embedding-space distance to expose semantic leakage of alignment data beyond string overlap. The present work specializes that motivation to source code and adds AST and dynamic execution, while Barbero et al. study post-training alignment data and do not require executable equivalence.

reviewed_competitors.title: HyClone: Bridging LLM Understanding and Dynamic Execution for Semantic Code Clone Detection
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Primary source for the two-stage semantic-clone detector adapted as the strictest functional metric.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Liang et al. evaluate LLM screening plus dynamic cross-execution as a general Python clone detector. The present paper reuses that machinery for exposure attribution between checkpoints; its severe real-world execution attrition shows why clone-detector benchmark performance does not automatically transfer to memorization prevalence measurement.

reviewed_competitors.title: TabPFN-2.5: Advancing the State of the Art in Tabular Foundation Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: The TabPFN-2.5 report establishes architecture, scale, TabArena performance, and distillation across large tabular datasets; the localization paper analyzes one regression checkpoint's feature-attention internals on two synthetic functions without testing whether the mechanism explains those real benchmark gains.

reviewed_competitors.title: TabPFN: A Transformer That Solves Small Tabular Classification Problems in a Second
reviewed_competitors.difference: The original TabPFN formulates prior-data fitted in-context Bayesian inference and evaluates classification on 85 OpenML datasets; this paper performs component interventions in a newer regression model but does not connect the localized heads to Bayesian posterior approximation or real classification behavior.

reviewed_competitors.title: In Search of Grandmother Cells: Tracing Interpretable Neurons in Tabular Representations
reviewed_competitors.difference: Knauer and Rodner quantify statistically selective TabPFN neuron-concept pairs without intervention; the present work adds head patching and ablation but works at coarser head/block resolution and does not validate semantic head content.

reviewed_competitors.title: How to use and interpret activation patching
reviewed_competitors.difference: Heimersheim and Nanda explicitly distinguish patching variants, metrics, and circuit-evidence pitfalls; the TabPFN paper applies this tool but its negative signed recoveries and corruption sensitivity demonstrate precisely why patching magnitude alone cannot be called localization.

reviewed_competitors.title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT
reviewed_competitors.difference: ROME combines causal tracing with a native weight edit and evaluates specificity and generalization of changed factual outputs; the TabPFN study stops at activation patching/ablation and one unsuccessful steering attempt, without a successful behavior-preserving causal edit.

reviewed_competitors.title: In-Context Learning Creates Task Vectors
reviewed_competitors.difference: Hendel et al. show across multiple LLMs/tasks that a training set can often be compressed to one task vector; the TabPFN paper reports one failed global additive vector and infers a relational boundary, but does not test the broader task-vector extraction or conditional alternatives.

reviewed_competitors.title: Function Vectors in Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Function Vectors uses causal mediation across tasks, models, and contexts and injects extracted vectors to trigger behavior zero-shot; the TabPFN work finds a non-transferable mean direction on one function and therefore supplies much weaker evidence for an architectural contrast.

reviewed_competitors.title: Which Attention Heads Matter for In-Context Learning?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yin and Steinhardt compare induction and function-vector heads with detailed ablations in 12 LLMs and across training; the TabPFN paper analyzes three fixed-index heads in one checkpoint, so its functional taxonomy has far less replication and developmental evidence.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Closer Look at TabPFN v2: Understanding Its Strengths and Extending Its Capabilities
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ye et al. test attribute randomization, use TabPFN as a feature extractor, and extend inference via divide-and-conquer; the present study adds causal component interventions but only on synthetic regression and does not link head effects to heterogeneity handling or separability.

reviewed_competitors.title: Exploring Representations and Interventions in Time Series Foundation Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wiliński et al. analyze representation redundancy across time-series foundation models and successfully steer periodicity/trend in generated signals; the TabPFN paper has finer head-level causal assays but its only steering intervention fails to transfer.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Mechanistic Study of Tabular Foundation Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: direct earlier causal-mechanistic study of contemporary tabular foundation models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Biloš et al. locate representations and validate distinct TabPFNv2, TabICLv2, and Mitra readout rules with causal attention forcing, block knockouts, mechanism transplantation, and mechanism-targeted attacks over 49 classification and 10 regression datasets. It predates and contradicts the target's broad priority claim, while the target remains different in isolating three feature-attention heads in one TabPFN-2.5 regression checkpoint on two analytic functions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Is One Layer Enough? Understanding Inference Dynamics in Tabular Foundation Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: direct earlier layerwise mechanistic analysis across tabular foundation models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Rezaei Balef et al. compare inference dynamics across six tabular in-context models, identify iterative refinement and depth redundancy, and build a looped single-layer proof of concept using about 20% of the original parameters. It predates the target and is broader across models and tasks, whereas it does not perform the target's pre-output-projection head patching, per-head zero ablation, or signed-recovery audit.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Geometry of Phase Transitions in Diffusion Models: Tubular Neighbourhoods and Singularities
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct same-line predecessor connecting diffusion phase transitions to injectivity radius, tubular neighborhoods, and projection singularities.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yaguchi et al. develop the single-valued projection/tubular-neighborhood picture and empirical singularity diagnostics. The present paper extends that geometry to explicit finite-noise multi-branch log-sum-exp competition and introduces CBD/TAD interventions, while inheriting the need to validate manifold and score assumptions in learned models.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Phase Transition in Diffusion Models Reveals the Hierarchical Nature of Data
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Primary theoretical and empirical account of class-level phase transitions in hierarchical diffusion data.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sclocchi et al. derive a population transition where high-level class reconstruction changes sharply while low-level details evolve smoothly, and test ImageNet models. The present work supplies a local trajectory geometry and intervention diagnostic, but does not directly compare CBD against the hierarchical transition prediction.

reviewed_competitors.title: Dynamical Regimes of Diffusion Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational statistical-physics account of speciation and collapse transitions during reverse diffusion.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Biroli et al. characterize population-level speciation from covariance spectra and later collapse toward memorized samples in high-dimensional limits. The present paper instead targets local nearest-branch competition along individual trajectories; a head-to-head test could determine whether CBD adds information beyond predicted speciation time.

reviewed_competitors.title: Concurrence of Symmetry Breaking and Nonlocality Phase Transitions in Diffusion Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporary empirical study of critical windows in modern diffusion Transformers using symmetry-breaking and nonlocality diagnostics.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhang et al. compare two operational phase-transition notions and report near-concurrent critical times in modern DiTs. The present paper proposes projection-caustic geometry and score-direction instability as a mechanism and control signal, but does not benchmark CBD against those two direct diagnostics on the same trajectories.

reviewed_competitors.title: Manifolds, Random Matrices and Spectral Gaps: The geometric phases of generative diffusion
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest score-geometry phase analysis using Jacobian spectra under the manifold hypothesis.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ventura et al. derive score-Jacobian spectral gaps and three phases—trivial, manifold coverage, and consolidation—and compare them with trained networks. The target instead studies local nearest-projection branch competition and normalized direction instability, but it does not benchmark CBD against the spectral-gap diagnostic or establish that its peaks identify a distinct transition.

reviewed_competitors.title: The statistical thermodynamics of generative diffusion models: Phase transitions, symmetry breaking and critical instability
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct free-energy and critical-instability predecessor for diffusion dynamics.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ambrogioni formulates reverse diffusion as a stochastic adiabatic process minimizing free energy and derives mean-field symmetry-breaking transitions and critical exponents. The target adds projection-caustic branch geometry and an intervention heuristic, but its learned-model free-energy panels are TAD transforms rather than an independent thermodynamic measurement.

reviewed_competitors.title: How Out-of-Equilibrium Phase Transitions can Seed Pattern Formation in Trained Diffusion Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporary theory-plus-intervention competitor identifying critical times in trained diffusion models.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ambrogioni predicts criticality through softening Fourier modes and growing spatial correlation length, validates those signatures in convolutional and ImageNet diffusion models, and applies guidance pulses at the estimated critical time. The target proposes nearest-branch caustics and score-direction finite differences instead, but supplies no same-trajectory comparison against correlation-length or mode-softening diagnostics.

reviewed_competitors.title: Applying Guidance in a Limited Interval Improves Sample and Distribution Quality in Diffusion Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct predecessor for temporally restricted diffusion guidance and intervention efficiency.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kynkäänniemi et al. systematically show that guidance is harmful early, useful in a middle interval, and unnecessary late across architectures and datasets, improving ImageNet-512 FID from 1.81 to 1.40. The target tries to choose windows from a geometric diagnostic, but its CIFAR study compares only one fixed detector band with one late band and does not benchmark against this established limited-guidance schedule.

reviewed_competitors.title: Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking in Generative Diffusion Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational phase-transition and critical-window account with a sampling intervention.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Raya and Ambrogioni locate a stability-breaking transition from a central fixed point to data-manifold attraction and exploit it through Gaussian late initialization, reporting up to threefold FID improvements for fast samplers. The target uses local projection-branch competition and CBD/TAD rather than central stability, yet does not show that CBD outpredicts the earlier transition time or sampling intervention.

reviewed_competitors.title: Muon Optimizes Under Spectral Norm Constraints
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct theoretical account of Muon's implicit spectral-norm-constrained optimization and regularization.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chen et al. connect Muon with the Lion-K family and show that Muon with decoupled weight decay implicitly solves a spectral-norm-constrained problem. The present work makes constraints explicit and module heterogeneous, but its omission of weight decay on DGram-managed weights prevents a clean comparison with that scale-controlled Muon theory.

reviewed_competitors.title: Mano: Restriking Manifold Optimization for LLM Training
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest large-scale empirical work applying a manifold optimizer directly to LLM training.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Gu and Xie project momentum and constrain it on a rotational Oblique manifold, evaluating LLaMA and Qwen3 models with efficiency claims. The present workshop paper instead compares Stiefel and DGram assignment by module, but does so only on GPT-2 small and does not benchmark Mano, scale, memory, or wall-clock performance.

reviewed_competitors.title: Manifold constrained steepest descent for smooth and closed-set optimization
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporary theory for steepest-descent directions and efficient spectral-norm specialization on smooth manifolds.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yang and Lai propose MCSD, MCSD-TP, and the Stiefel spectral specialization SPEL with stationarity guarantees and non-LLM experiments. The present paper uses a nested dual-ascent Manifold Muon implementation and studies which Transformer modules receive which manifold, without comparable convergence guarantees or optimizer baselines.

reviewed_competitors.title: Muon is Scalable for LLM Training
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Primary large-scale Muon study identifying weight decay and per-parameter update scale as crucial stabilization techniques.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Liu et al. scale Muon to a 3B/16B MoE trained on 5.7T tokens and explicitly identify weight decay plus update-scale adjustment as necessary. The present paper's DGram failure occurs with no weight decay on manifold-managed matrices, making this competitor both a stronger scale benchmark and an unresolved control for the claimed manifold effect.

reviewed_competitors.title: Towards a Principled Muon under $\mu\mathsf{P}$: Ensuring Spectral Conditions throughout Training
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct contemporary spectral-control alternative for Muon in long-horizon LLM training.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhao's Muon++ controls optimizer-update spectra to maintain muP spectral conditions throughout training while avoiding repeated normalization of the weights, and explicitly foregrounds the overhead of weight-plus-update spectral normalization. The present paper instead constrains weights by module with 20 inner matrix-sign solves and a retraction, but reports neither wall time nor whether update-only spectral control can stabilize DGram attention.

reviewed_competitors.title: In-context Learning and Induction Heads
reviewed_competitors.difference: Olsson et al. identify induction heads, their abrupt formation, and their relationship to in-context learning in causal multi-layer language models; the present paper isolates only the first-layer copy subcircuit in a supervised cyclic one-layer task.

reviewed_competitors.title: The mechanistic basis of data dependence and abrupt learning in an in-context classification task
reviewed_competitors.difference: Reddy analyzes data-dependent abrupt learning through optimization-time competition and explicitly identifies progress measures that precede in-context learning. The present paper gives an equilibrium Bayesian action as dataset size varies, so Reddy is both a dynamics comparator and direct prior evidence against a broad no-precursor claim.

reviewed_competitors.title: What needs to go right for an induction head? A mechanistic study of in-context learning circuits and their formation
reviewed_competitors.difference: Singh et al. intervene on and decompose the prerequisites for induction-head formation in multi-layer models; the present work predicts a copy-order boundary but performs no causal circuit intervention.

reviewed_competitors.title: How Transformers Learn Causal Structure with Gradient Descent
reviewed_competitors.difference: Nichani et al. prove that gradient descent in a causal two-layer Transformer recovers latent causal graphs, with Markov-chain induction heads as a special case. The present model is unmasked and one-layer and replaces training dynamics with a posterior equilibrium calculation over a supervised cyclic-copy task.

reviewed_competitors.title: Unveiling Induction Heads: Provable Training Dynamics and Feature Learning in Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chen et al. give optimization-time feature-learning guarantees for induction heads, whereas the present paper gives equilibrium sample-complexity transitions for a fused copy head and does not prove Adam or SGLD dynamics.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Emergence of Induction Heads for In-Context Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Musat et al. prove that modified two-layer Transformer training stays in a 19-dimensional subspace, empirically localize emergence to three dimensions, and derive quadratic context-length scaling of emergence time. The present paper instead studies an equilibrium dataset-size boundary for a single fused copy subcircuit and does not analyze optimization time.

reviewed_competitors.title: Predicting the Emergence of Induction Heads in Language Model Pretraining
reviewed_competitors.difference: Aoyama et al. explicitly predict induction-head emergence during language-model pretraining, directly limiting the broad claim that softmax copy emergence is intrinsically unpredictable from observables.

reviewed_competitors.title: Linear attention is (maybe) all you need (to understand transformer optimization)
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ahn et al. use shallow linearized Transformers to reproduce and analyze optimization phenomena in in-context regression. The present paper uses linear attention as a symmetry-preserving Bayesian comparator for a copy task and focuses on dataset-size equilibrium phase order rather than gradient-descent convergence.

reviewed_competitors.title: Implicit Regularization of Gradient Flow on One-Layer Softmax Attention
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sheen et al. show nuclear-norm implicit regularization for separately trained key and query matrices, contrasting it with Frobenius regularization of a combined matrix. The present paper derives asymptotic attention-pattern equivalence for wide factorized Q/K but tests only the fused model, so it does not establish equivalent finite-width optimization or weight-prior selection.

reviewed_competitors.title: Emergent Capabilities Arise Randomly from Learning Sparse Attention Patterns
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct post-submission competitor on stochastic within-training attention-pattern emergence.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Baherwani et al. link abrupt capabilities to the stochastic learning of sparse task-relevant attention patterns in synthetic Transformers and Pythia, varying context length, sparsity, head count, head dimension, and alternative mixers. The present paper offers an analytic equilibrium boundary for a supervised copy pattern but does not measure stochastic within-training arrival, architecture controls, or natural-model capabilities.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Kinetics of Training: A Driven-Nucleation Rate Law for Emergence, Plasticity Loss, and Circuit Control in Language Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct current competitor on first-order-style emergence kinetics, precursors, and intervention.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Dong models circuit formation as a driven rare event, reports a prospective precursor that dates held-out capability arrival, and intervenes on data mixture and query-key slices in models up to 1.4B parameters. The present paper derives a cleaner exact posterior boundary for a single fused copy head, but its intrinsic-unpredictability claim is directly limited by this later primary evidence and it has no kinetic or causal test.
