reviewed_competitors.difference: TTT-Linear and TTT-MLP make a learned model the recurrent hidden state and replace sequence-model layers, reaching 125M-1.3B scale. In-Place TTT retains attention and reuses a pretrained MLP projection, trading the predecessor's standalone expressive state for checkpoint compatibility and much larger chunks.

reviewed_competitors.title: Test-Time Training Done Right
reviewed_competitors.difference: LaCT already advocates extremely large 2K-to-1M-token updates, nonlinear state up to 40% of parameters, and sophisticated online optimizers across language, images, and video. In-Place TTT's distinct contribution is to place the state in existing MLP down-projections and use a future-token target with attention still present; large-chunk efficiency alone is not new.

reviewed_competitors.title: End-to-End Test-Time Training for Long Context
reviewed_competitors.difference: TTT-E2E already uses a standard sliding-window Transformer, compresses the test context into weights with next-token prediction, and meta-learns an initialization; at 3B/164B tokens it reports constant-length latency and 2.7x speed over full attention at 128K. In-Place TTT updates only existing MLP down-projections with a closed-form learned target and demonstrates warm-start continuation of public full-attention checkpoints.

reviewed_competitors.title: Reinforced Fast Weights with Next-Sequence Prediction
reviewed_competitors.difference: REFINE predates the target and explicitly replaces token-level NTP with entropy-selected multi-token rollouts, self-supervised sequence rewards, and GRPO for LaCT and DeltaNet fast weights across mid-, post-, and test-time training. In-Place TTT's objective is cheaper and closed form, but the broad idea of training fast weights on future-sequence usefulness is not unique to it.

reviewed_competitors.title: Self-Guided Test-Time Training for Long-Context LLMs
reviewed_competitors.difference: S-TTT adapts pretrained Qwen3-4B-Thinking and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct only on model-selected evidence spans using the standard LM objective, and reports that random spans hurt while oracle spans help on LongBench-v2. In-Place TTT is a trained architectural memory that updates every chunk efficiently; it does not address relevance selection, the failure highlighted by this later work.

reviewed_competitors.title: StoryAnalogy: Deriving Story-level Analogies from Large Language Models to Unlock Analogical Understanding

NARB is smaller/inherited but uniquely contrasts layerwise decodability with prompted ranking on proverb and rhetorical data.

reviewed_competitors.title: AnaloBench: Benchmarking the Identification of Abstract and Long-context Analogies

NARB instead studies literary/proverb and local rhetorical ranking plus internal probes; it should compare its narrative conclusions against AnaloBench's controlled long-context retrieval/application failures.

reviewed_competitors.title: Aligned Probing: Relating Toxic Behavior and Model Internals
reviewed_competitors.difference: Aligned Probing was on arXiv in March 2025 and explicitly aligns outputs with internal probes across more than 20 OLMo, Llama, and Mistral models, includes multi-prompt studies, and reports correlational plus causal evidence for toxicity. NARB applies a simpler probe-versus-prompt comparison to analogy, but does not provide comparable causal use tests or broad model/prompt controls.

reviewed_competitors.title: Lookback Lens: Detecting and Mitigating Contextual Hallucinations in Large Language Models Using Only Attention Maps
reviewed_competitors.relationship: direct prior attention-based correctness detector and mitigation method
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lookback Lens uses a transparent per-head ratio of attention to context versus generated tokens, obtains cross-task and 7B-to-13B transfer, and guides candidate decoding to improve XSum correctness by 9.6 points. AP-MAE uses learned full-matrix cluster categories for single-token Java correctness, demonstrates only reconstruction transfer among StarCoder2 sizes, and mitigates errors by globally zeroing ranked heads rather than choosing decoded candidates.

reviewed_competitors.title: Gradient-guided Attention Map Editing: Towards Efficient Contextual Hallucination Mitigation
reviewed_competitors.difference: GAME trains a classifier to flag hallucination-prone attention maps and uses gradient-derived edit directions to redistribute attention at inference across multiple models and summarization/QA tasks, reporting a 10% XSum reduction. AP-MAE learns an unsupervised image embedding and discovers motifs at greater corpus scale, but its intervention removes whole task-ranked heads and does not condition an edit on the current map.

reviewed_competitors.title: Shapley Head Pruning: Identifying and Removing Interference in Multilingual Transformers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: direct prior head-attribution and beneficial-pruning method
reviewed_competitors.difference: Held and Yang approximate coalition-based Shapley values for attention heads and prune negative-value language-specific heads to reduce multilingual interference on sentence classification and structural prediction. AP-MAE attributes cluster-category features with CatBoost SHAP, targets Java next-token correctness, and adds learned two-dimensional motif discovery, but its SHAP values are predictive-model attributions rather than head coalition values.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the weak link between importance and prunability of attention heads
reviewed_competitors.relationship: direct negative-result prior for the attribution-to-pruning inference
reviewed_competitors.difference: Prasanna et al. find that many Transformer/BERT heads can be randomly pruned and that previously interpreted importance or layer location does not reliably improve pruning decisions. AP-MAE reports a stronger separation between extreme-SHAP and random/neutral removal on selected code tasks, but does not benchmark against causal or gradient head-importance methods and selects the best intervention point over many sweeps.

reviewed_competitors.title: Towards Automated Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability
reviewed_competitors.difference: ACDC automates edge-level circuit discovery against a task metric and validates recovered component types on known small-model circuits. AP-MAE is a cheaper, behavior-scale screen over attention-pattern shape and can rank heads across millions of natural code observations, but it neither recovers connections nor verifies that selected heads constitute a circuit.

reviewed_competitors.title: Distillation Scaling Laws
reviewed_competitors.difference: Busbridge et al. fit large-scale laws for distilled performance as a joint function of teacher, student, tokens, and compute and derive compute-allocation recipes. The target instead claims an internal-mechanism predictor from one teacher's SAE statistics and hidden width, but evaluates only five widths at one fixed training budget and therefore does not separate its supposed floor from the compute dependence modeled by the predecessor.

reviewed_competitors.title: Knowledge distillation through geometry-aware representational alignment
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bhattarai et al. prove limitations of projection MSE and CKA as geometry-preserving losses and test Procrustes/Gram alignment on BERT and OPT, with gains up to about two points and explicit objective comparisons. The target predicts a width cutoff from sparse-feature counts and uses only output KL; its claim that the remaining floor is objective-independent is not compared against this geometry-aware alternative, and the target's bibliography appears to misname and misdate the work.

reviewed_competitors.title: Logit-Based Losses Limit the Effectiveness of Feature Knowledge Distillation
reviewed_competitors.relationship: direct prior on geometry, objective choice, and teacher-layer quality
reviewed_competitors.difference: Cooper et al. define geometry-based separation/information/efficiency scores to select teacher layers and show that removing logit losses from the student backbone can improve feature KD by up to 15% top-1 across CNN/ViT pairs. The target uses an SAE importance tail to declare a hard logit-KL floor, but it never varies the objective or layer-selection strategy that this direct predecessor finds consequential.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: arXiv v1; NeurIPS 2025 NeurReps workshop paper

reviewed_competitors.title: Revisit the Essence of Distilling Knowledge through Calibration
reviewed_competitors.relationship: direct capacity-mismatch explanation and objective competitor
reviewed_competitors.difference: Fan et al. attribute teacher–student capacity mismatch partly to KL sensitivity to teacher calibration and improve transfer with a calibration-insensitive ranking loss. The target attributes width-dependent loss to sparse geometry and calls B objective/depth dependent, but does not measure teacher calibration or test the alternative loss, so it cannot rule out this established non-geometric explanation.

reviewed_competitors.title: What Mechanisms Does Knowledge Distillation Distill?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wu et al. operationalize transferred knowledge as shared counterfactual mechanisms and compare Jacobian matching and contrastive representation learning using teacher–student KL and OOD behavior. The target operationalizes knowledge as SAE feature count/importance and checks only six coarse probes; it does not track shared mechanisms or show that predicted missing features drive OOD fidelity.

reviewed_competitors.title: Solvable Model for Inheriting the Regularization through Knowledge Distillation
reviewed_competitors.difference: Saglietti and Zdeborová derive distillation behavior in a solvable shallow model with an explicit student–teacher mismatch and show dependence on teacher optimality and double descent. The target proposes a universal feature-capacity lower bound from width; its equal-architecture Pythia control lacks the explicit mismatch required for a nonzero representational impossibility and can reproduce the teacher by copying weights.

It studies single-cell gene embeddings rather than perturbation preservation, and its positive/null-controlled findings narrow any blanket claim that biological foundation-model geometry is vacuous.

It causally manipulates the balance-specialization tension, whereas the target observes fixed runs and fits a descriptive scalar without changing alpha or balance scope.

It provides an alternative mechanism to the target's alpha*M decomposition and shows why fitted balance need not decompose linearly into an explicit loss plus optimizer-internalized remainder.

reviewed_competitors.title: MoE Routing Testbed: Studying Expert Specialization and Routing Behavior at Small Scale

It emphasizes controlled routing comparisons rather than retrospectively fitting an equilibrium coefficient to public checkpoints.

reviewed_competitors.title: Leveraging Routing Dynamics in Mixture-of-Experts Models for Efficient Language Adaptation
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work tracks routing during continual multilingual pretraining and finds diffused early/middle-layer routing with specialization mainly in final layers, then uses that observation for less-than-2%-parameter adaptation. It studies language-conditional and layerwise dynamics with a downstream intervention, whereas the target studies base-pretraining checkpoint phases in an aggregate congestion fit.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Vaswani et al. define scaled dot-product attention as softmax(QK-transpose/sqrt(d_k))V with separate query, key, and value projections. That equation is the decisive baseline: the target paper's proof instead scores the current key against stored values and therefore is not an exact mapping for arbitrary Transformer parameters.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Turing Machines
reviewed_competitors.difference: Graves et al. introduce differentiable external-memory reads and writes with a recurrent controller. The target removes recurrent state and essentially all programmable memory operations; it also incorrectly cites this NTM paper as the source that introduced DNCs.

reviewed_competitors.title: Hybrid computing using a neural network with dynamic external memory
reviewed_competitors.difference: The 2016 Nature paper introduces the Differentiable Neural Computer with learned read/write heads, dynamic allocation, and temporal links and evaluates structured reasoning and reinforcement-learning tasks. It is absent from the target bibliography, whose sDNC removes the mechanisms that distinguish a DNC from simpler memory networks.

reviewed_competitors.title: Hopfield Networks is All You Need
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ramsauer et al. derive an equivalence between modern Hopfield associative-memory updates and Transformer attention, analyze storage and retrieval regimes, and evaluate applications. This is a better-established exact memory interpretation that the target does not discuss; it preserves separate patterns and queries rather than conflating key and value projections.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformers are RNNs: Fast Autoregressive Transformers with Linear Attention
reviewed_competitors.difference: Katharopoulos et al. show that kernelized linear attention admits an iterative recurrent-state formulation and demonstrate fast autoregressive inference. The target cites this work but offers neither its algebraic care nor empirical consequences, and its claim concerns ordinary softmax attention as a DNC-like memory.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Attention Memory
reviewed_competitors.difference: Nam and Seo explicitly formulate attention as readable and writable Neural Attention Memory, compare against DNCs on algorithmic generalization, and build efficient Transformer variants. This directly precedes the target's memory framing while providing implemented architectures and evaluations; the target's only distinctive claim is its invalid exact sDNC theorem.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformers Learn Shortcuts to Automata
reviewed_competitors.difference: Liu et al. characterize how Transformers simulate finite-state recurrence using explicit constructions, semigroup algebra, conditional lower bounds, and experiments. That work gives testable computational content to a stateless-versus-recurrent comparison; the target offers a one-layer memory analogy and unsupported claims about algorithmic behavior.

reviewed_competitors.title: Attention Approximates Sparse Distributed Memory
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bricken and Pehlevan derive a conditional approximation between Transformer attention and Kanerva sparse distributed memory and test the required conditions in pretrained GPT-2. Their careful use of 'approximates' and explicit data conditions contrasts with the target's unconditional exact-equivalence claim and supplies another omitted memory interpretation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformers are Multi-State RNNs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Oren et al. give a precise recurrent interpretation of decoder-only Transformers as unbounded multi-state RNNs whose state is the key-value cache, then turn that interpretation into TOVA cache compression and evaluate it on four long-range tasks and multiple LLMs. This is a closer computational-reframing precedent than the target acknowledges: it keeps separate keys and values, yields an operational compression method, and supplies experiments rather than renaming a value-addressed memory.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding Transformer from the Perspective of Associative Memory
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhong et al. explicitly survey Transformer attention and feed-forward layers through associative-memory capacity and update mechanisms, including softmax attention and DeltaNet, while labeling the record a blog-style perspective rather than a formal theorem. It predates the target and further weakens novelty for a memory-centric interpretation, although it does not claim a DNC identity and is less formal than the modern-Hopfield or NAM papers.

reviewed_competitors.title: Interpretable Neural Causal Models with TRAM-DAGs
reviewed_competitors.difference: TRAM-DAG already targets an interpretable, flexible SCM with a known DAG, mixed continuous/ordinal/binary variables, and queries across Pearl's three levels; it therefore narrows any broad 'first interpretable neural causal model' claim. KaCGM instead uses additive KAN edge functions, residual-independence falsification, pruning, and explicit symbolic formulas/plots; TRAM-DAG uses transformation models and also analyzes selected continuous counterfactual structures with unobserved confounding.

reviewed_competitors.title: CausalKANs: interpretable treatment effect estimation with Kolmogorov-Arnold networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: CausalKANs already combines KAN estimators with pruning, symbolic simplification, closed-form formulas, and interpretable plots, but only for conditional treatment-effect estimators. KaCGM extends the toolkit to a full query-agnostic SCM with one mechanism per DAG node, exogenous-noise diagnostics, mixed categorical conditionals, intervention sampling, and restricted counterfactual abduction.

reviewed_competitors.title: Causal normalizing flows: from theory to practice
reviewed_competitors.difference: Causal normalizing flows learn invertible, path-preserving SCM maps from a known graph or ordering and answer observational, interventional, and counterfactual queries, including mixed-data and partial-graph experiments. Their invertible flows cover nonadditive mechanisms and are less directly symbolic; KaCGM trades that density flexibility for inspectable additive KAN equations and explicit residual-independence diagnostics.

reviewed_competitors.title: Modeling Causal Mechanisms with Diffusion Models for Interventional and Counterfactual Queries
reviewed_competitors.difference: The diffusion-based causal model assigns a deterministic diffusion encoder-decoder to each node, obtains a latent proxy for exogenous noise, and handles all three query levels under causal sufficiency. It is a more flexible but opaque and computationally heavy mechanism class; KaCGM uses additive spline functions whose residuals and symbolic form can be audited, and openly fails in the nonadditive regime where diffusion is competitive.

reviewed_competitors.title: VACA: Designing Variational Graph Autoencoders for Causal Queries
reviewed_competitors.difference: VACA uses a variational graph autoencoder with architectural graph constraints to approximate observational, interventional, and counterfactual distributions without parametric structural equations, assuming a known graph and no hidden confounders. KaCGM models nodes separately with additive KANs and categorical likelihoods, enabling residual tests and closed-form mechanism extraction but accepting a stronger functional restriction.

reviewed_competitors.title: Deep Structural Causal Models for Tractable Counterfactual Inference
reviewed_competitors.difference: Deep SCMs compose normalizing-flow and variational mechanisms to abduct exogenous noise and answer all three causal levels, including high-dimensional image and medical examples plus discrete mechanisms. KaCGM is specialized to moderate-dimensional tabular DAGs and contributes inspectable KAN equations plus observational misspecification checks rather than high-dimensional generative capacity.

reviewed_competitors.title: DeCaFlow: A deconfounding causal generative model
reviewed_competitors.relationship: direct prior removing a central scope assumption
reviewed_competitors.difference: DeCaFlow is a query-agnostic causal generator trained once from observational data and a graph, but it targets continuous systems with hidden confounding and proves correctness for queries identifiable by do-calculus or sufficiently informative proxies. KaCGM instead assumes causal sufficiency and contributes inspectable additive KAN mechanisms, mixed categorical conditionals, and symbolic extraction; DeCaFlow therefore narrows any implication that hidden confounding is an unavoidable limitation of current causal generators rather than a deliberate price of KaCGM's auditability.

reviewed_competitors.difference: The companion establishes the infinite-depth Mean ODE and the finite-ResNet approximation O(1/L+sqrt(D/(LM))) at fixed D, together with the MLU phase diagram. The target imports that result and adds the rigorous D→infinity limit at O(1/sqrt(D)), then forms a joint nonproportional L,M,D theorem. Therefore the target's finite-to-Mean-ODE leg and scaling regime are prior rather than new here.

reviewed_competitors.title: Infinite Limits of Multi-head Transformer Dynamics
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bordelon, Chaudhry, and Pehlevan derive infinite-width/depth training dynamics for multi-head Transformers by path-integral DMFT, covering multiple residual scalings and attention behavior, and are identified by the target as the closest object of study. Their treatment is formal/numerical and uses proportional or sequential limits; the target supplies a rigorous quantitative joint rate for the narrower depth-two ResNet/MLU system and only claims formal Transformer applicability.

reviewed_competitors.title: Tensor Programs VI: Feature Learning in Infinite-Depth Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Tensor Programs VI classifies infinite-width-then-depth feature-learning limits, depth scaling, and feature diversity, including residual architectures; it finds distinct behavior and degeneracy for deeper blocks under its scalings. The target instead treats depth-two blocks in the MLU normalization, takes a Mean-ODE-first route, and proves a quantitative finite-size joint coupling rather than a sequential tensor-program limit.

reviewed_competitors.title: Depthwise Hyperparameter Transfer in Residual Networks: Dynamics and Scaling Limit
reviewed_competitors.relationship: prior ResNet width-depth DMFT and scaling competitor
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work develops a joint depth/width DMFT scaling limit and depthwise hyperparameter-transfer prescription for residual networks, with convolutional ResNet and Vision Transformer experiments. It analyzes depth-one-style residual blocks and gives a physics-style asymptotic account; the target focuses on practically different depth-two blocks and contributes a fully rigorous high-probability error decomposition across arbitrary admissible aspect ratios.

reviewed_competitors.title: Width and Depth Limits Commute in Residual Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Hayou and Yang rigorously show commutation and rates for width/depth limits of residual-network preactivations at initialization/forward propagation. The target extends the commutation theme to finite-step feature-learning training dynamics with a second hidden width M, but under MLU, smoothness, clipping, and fixed-horizon assumptions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Rigorous Asymptotics for First-Order Algorithms Through the Dynamical Cavity Method
reviewed_competitors.difference: This concurrent COLT 2026 work rigorizes dynamical-cavity asymptotics for broad first-order algorithms in high-dimensional generalized-linear/dense inference systems, also using Lindeberg replacement. It overlaps strongly in proof philosophy and weakens any broad claim to be uniquely first in rigorous quantitative cavity DMFT, but it does not analyze depth-two ResNet width/depth limits or give the target's three-term architecture error.

reviewed_competitors.title: Training Infinitely Deep and Wide Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: Barboni et al. rigorously formulate infinite-depth and infinite-head Transformer training as a conditional-Wasserstein mean-field control problem, prove well-posed gradient flows, and study NTK injectivity and small-initial-loss convergence. They do not provide the target's finite-size L,M,D coupling or its MLU ResNet rate, but their genuinely attention-specific theory shows why the target's reduction to a fixed-dimensional nonlinearity should be read only as formal Transformer applicability, not as the current rigorous Transformer result.

reviewed_competitors.difference: TiC-LM uses 114 dated Common Crawl dumps and time-stratified natural evaluations, finding fixed-ratio replay and meta-schedules competitive with retraining at lower compute. It is a much stronger scale-transfer and natural-stream comparator than RCB/NAB.

reviewed_competitors.difference: ELLA directly regularizes alignment with high-energy directions of an aggregated past-update matrix, proves an anisotropic interference bound, and evaluates classification and generation without replay. AAT instead hypothesizes that current-example abstractions suppress entity-gradient variance, but never measures those components or compares with a modern gradient-structure method.

reviewed_competitors.title: SCALE: Upscaled Continual Learning of Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: SCALE freezes pretrained weights and inserts preservation- and adaptation-oriented width expansions, evaluating a synthetic biography stream and Korean continual pretraining with English retention. It supplies a post-target architectural route and more natural language stream, whereas AAT adds no parameters but tests only constructed relation/proverb tasks at controlled 1.5B-3B scale.

reviewed_competitors.title: FOREVER: Forgetting Curve-Inspired Memory Replay for Language Model Continual Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current replay competitor and baseline challenge
reviewed_competitors.difference: FOREVER schedules replay by optimizer-update magnitude and adapts replay intensity, reporting three CL benchmarks and 0.6B-13B models. Its model-time replay is a substantially stronger current comparator than AAT's one selected 100-item reservoir configuration, although it retains memory and does not target structural abstraction.

reviewed_competitors.title: TRACE: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Continual Learning in Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: TRACE covers multiple continual LLM abilities and methods over sequential tasks. It does not target structural inference, but provides broader forgetting and transfer evaluation against which the two small AAT benchmarks should be situated.

reviewed_competitors.title: Continual Pre-training of Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ke et al. study domain-adaptive continual pretraining and mitigation strategies at the language-model level. AAT differs by constructing an abstraction of each current item, but offers less naturalistic scale and no matched pretraining-stream test.

reviewed_competitors.title: Efficient Lifelong Learning with A-GEM
reviewed_competitors.difference: A-GEM directly constrains current gradients using episodic-memory gradients to reduce interference. That makes measured gradient conflict and projection a priority causal baseline for AAT's claimed gradient-level mechanism, beyond the paper's replay-only comparison.

reviewed_competitors.title: Better Fine-Tuning by Reducing Representational Collapse
reviewed_competitors.difference: Aghajanyan et al. link fine-tuning instability and generalization loss to representational collapse and propose a regularization remedy. This is an alternative explanation for AAT's auxiliary-loss benefit that does not require schema-specific gradient decomposition.

reviewed_competitors.title: DEMix Layers: Disentangling Domains for Modular Language Modeling
reviewed_competitors.difference: DEMix routes domains through modular experts to reduce interference and enable domain updates. It is a parameter-separation alternative to AAT's loss-level bias and is closer to the paper's disjoint-parameter theory assumption.

reviewed_competitors.title: Experience Replay for Continual Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Rolnick et al. establish simple experience replay as a strong continual-learning method. AAT avoids long-term instance storage, but the present ER comparison is selected from only four small-buffer configurations and is not token/FLOP matched.

reviewed_competitors.title: ePiC: Employing Proverbs in Context as a Benchmark for Abstract Language Understanding
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ghosh and Srivastava introduce the 250-proverb narrative source and its abstract-language objective. NAB's base semantic inventory is therefore inherited; its additions are generated narratives, distractors, a pairwise continuation format, and online train/test use.

reviewed_competitors.title: Rationale-Enhanced Language Models are Better Continual Relation Learners
reviewed_competitors.difference: Xiong et al. already use LLM-generated relation rationales as an auxiliary target and contrastive rationale replay to make continual relation representations robust to future analogous relations. AAT removes entity surfaces from the current example and avoids a persistent buffer, but cannot claim that structure-oriented auxiliary supervision for continual relational learning is itself new.

AAT instead supplies an entity-masked or proverb-level current-example loss and uses no long-term buffer, but omits this close evidence that masking and non-surface training signals already support continual LLM generalization.

reviewed_competitors.title: Value-State Gated Attention for Mitigating Extreme-Token Phenomena in Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: VGA already writes the value gradient as the sum of attention weights times upstream gradients, interprets high sink attention as amplified value-state pressure, and derives how a sigmoid gate computed from the value itself changes that gradient. It aims to break the mutual reinforcement among attention sinks and value drains and thereby mitigate the sinks. V-scale instead uses a radial rational norm gate with one learned scalar per head, explicitly measures tokenwise gradient sinks, ties pressure to RMSNorm and massive residual activations, and seeks to preserve the attention sink. The overlap means the routing-identity-plus-value-gate combination is prior, while the target's narrower addition is the RMSNorm regulator hypothesis, diagnostic, and specific gate behavior.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Unified View of Attention and Residual Sinks: Outlier-Driven Rescaling is Essential for Transformer Training
reviewed_competitors.difference: Qiu et al. argue attention and residual outliers jointly provide useful forward rescaling through softmax and RMSNorm, validate across dense, linear, hybrid, and MoE models up to 24B/1T tokens, and replace outliers with PreAffine or GatedNorm. The target instead argues large token norms regulate backward pressure produced by attention columns. Both connect outliers, normalization, gated alternatives, stability, and quantization, but the prior work supplies a competing forward-rescaling purpose and broader architecture scale rather than tokenwise gradient-sink evidence.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Spike, the Sparse and the Sink: Anatomy of Massive Activations and Attention Sinks
reviewed_competitors.difference: This paper, submitted before the target, experimentally decouples massive activations and attention sinks and argues they have distinct forward roles: massive activations form persistent near-constant implicit parameters, while attention sinks locally bias heads toward short dependencies. It identifies pre-norm as enabling co-occurrence and shows either can be suppressed without language-modeling loss. The target adds a backward gradient-pressure account and V-scale, but its adaptive-regulator conclusion must compete with this explicit forward-function and architectural-artifact explanation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Attention Sinks and Compression Valleys in LLMs are Two Sides of the Same Coin
reviewed_competitors.difference: Queipo-de-Llano et al. connect attention sinks and massive activations to representational compression across 410M-120B models, derive entropy-reduction bounds, and propose a Mix-Compress-Refine forward account. The target focuses on transpose-attention gradients and inverse-norm backward attenuation; it does not exclude compression as the reason large activations are useful or show the backward account is primary.

reviewed_competitors.title: Massive Activations in Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sun et al. establish sparse activations up to roughly 100,000 times ordinary scale, show they remain nearly input-constant and act as indispensable implicit biases, and connect them forward to attention concentration. The target reverses the emphasis by treating sink attention as the source of backward pressure and large norms as regulators, but it does not disprove the prior forward-bias role.

reviewed_competitors.title: When Attention Sink Emerges in Language Models: An Empirical View
reviewed_competitors.difference: Gu et al. causally vary optimization, data, loss, and attention architecture, finding sink position tracks loss/data and sinks disappear in tested sigmoid attention models up to 1B. The target analyzes the backward consequence once a causal softmax sink exists and preserves it with V-scale; it does not reproduce the prior emergence-factor sweep.

reviewed_competitors.title: Why do LLMs attend to the first token?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Barbero et al. give a theoretical and empirical forward account in which first-token attention helps avoid over-mixing, and they test context length, depth, and packing. The target deliberately retains the attention sink while reducing its value-gradient concentration, so the accounts can coexist; preservation of a thresholded sink alone does not show its anti-overmixing function is unchanged.

reviewed_competitors.title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
reviewed_competitors.difference: StreamingLLM names and exploits the forward initial-token sink by retaining its KV states, enabling stable windowed inference over millions of tokens and up to 22.2x speedup. The target contributes a training-time backward diagnostic and small-model intervention rather than an inference-cache method, and its long-context tests are synthetic retrieval only through 8,192 tokens.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Single Layer to Explain Them All:Understanding Massive Activations in Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Shi et al. subsequently localize the first emergence of massive activations to a consistent layer where RMSNorm and FFN parameters jointly contribute, trace residual propagation, and mitigate representation rigidity in pretrained models. This is a more layer-specific origin account with instruction and math evaluations; the target supplies a backward attention-pressure hypothesis but does not predict or causally verify the emergence layer.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Structural Origin of Attention Sink: Variance Discrepancy, Super Neurons, and Dimension Disparity
reviewed_competitors.difference: Li et al. subsequently attribute sink formation to value-aggregation variance discrepancy amplified by sparse FFN super neurons, reproduce sinks at arbitrary positions with controlled interventions, and propose head-wise RMSNorm to restore positional variance parity during pretraining. That is a forward statistical and structural causal chain rather than the target's backward transpose-routing account, but it is a direct current competitor because it links value aggregation, extreme FFN activity, RMSNorm, sink formation, and pretraining convergence without invoking adaptive gradient regulation.

reviewed_competitors.difference: This prior already formalizes emergent bricks as functional neuron partitions, surveys self-organized FFN groupings, and explicitly identifies cross-layer organization as an open problem. ULCMOD's defensible novelty is a concrete cross-layer activation co-partition that addresses that stated gap, not the broader proposal that LLMs have discoverable function modules.

reviewed_competitors.title: Clustering units in neural networks: upstream vs downstream information
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct methodological warning about activation-defined functional modules.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lange, Rolnick, and Kording compare eight unit-similarity measures and find that upstream activation-based clusters and downstream effect-based clusters agree poorly. ULCMOD scales only an upstream co-activation definition to LLMs and does not test the downstream partition, so the prior directly limits its use of the word functional.

reviewed_competitors.relationship: Task-neuron localization predecessor with stronger causal validation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wang et al. use task labels and prompt tuning to rank overlapping skill neurons, repeat experiments across five random trials, and perturb selected neurons to show task-specific effects. ULCMOD jointly discovers hard neuron/sample groups without labels in its objective and spans layers, but it trades away overlap, repeated-run stability, and causal validation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Hedonic Neurons: A Mechanistic Mapping of Latent Coalitions in Transformer MLPs
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest pre-target discovery of disjoint neuron coalitions with causal synergy tests and cross-layer tracking.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chowdhury et al. model MLP neurons as players in a hedonic game, use PAC-Top-Cover to extract stable within-layer coalitions, validate non-additive importance by joint ablation, and track persistence, splitting, merging, and disappearance across layers in LLaMA, Mistral, and Pythia rerankers. They report +0.29 Pairwise and +0.49 Ratio synergy over the strongest baseline, 3-5× larger out-of-distribution ablation drops, and macro-feature predictive R² of 0.43-0.47. ULCMOD instead creates a single all-layer neuron/sample co-partition on broad instruction topics, but its activation-only evidence is weaker and its broad functional-coalition novelty must be narrowed because Hedonic Neurons predates it.

reviewed_competitors.title: Constructing Interpretable Features from Compositional Neuron Groups
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later 2026 current competitor for unsupervised activation decomposition into interpretable neuron groups, not prior-art preemption.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Shafran, Geiger, and Geva factor each MLP activation matrix with semi-nonnegative matrix factorization into sparse neuron combinations and nonnegative input coefficients, compare against SAEs and supervised difference-in-means, and causally evaluate concept steering on Llama 3.1, Gemma 2, and GPT-2. Their finding that semantically related features reuse overlapping neuron cores directly challenges ULCMOD's imposed exclusivity, while recursive composition supplies a tested hierarchy rather than visual K-to-K analogy. The ACL paper appeared in July 2026, after ULCMOD, so it describes the current frontier without preempting the March contribution.

The target uses simpler post-training scalar clusters to isolate order and candidly reports that its unstructured LUT paths are slower; its novelty is the structural probe, not low-bit clustering or accelerated lookup.

reviewed_competitors.title: Token Bottleneck: One Token to Remember Dynamics
reviewed_competitors.difference: ToBo is the closest architectural prior: it compresses a reference frame into one bottleneck token and predicts a heavily masked subsequent frame using sparse target patches, explicitly supervising temporal dynamics and validating simulated plus physical robots. CroBo retains the one-token decoder interface but replaces the uncertain future with a spatially contained same-frame crop, prioritizing scene composition; its main novelty is this substitution and the what-is-where framing, not the token bottleneck itself.

reviewed_competitors.title: Efficient Image Pre-Training with Siamese Cropped Masked Autoencoders
reviewed_competitors.difference: CropMAE already reconstructs one same-image crop from another under extremely high masking, showing that cropped static images can learn object-centric correspondence without video. CroBo adds the ToBo-style single CLS bottleneck by discarding source patch tokens and evaluates frozen robot policies; the global-to-local same-frame reconstruction signal itself is inherited.

reviewed_competitors.title: Siamese Masked Autoencoders
reviewed_competitors.difference: SiamMAE asymmetrically masks paired video frames and uses decoder cross-attention to learn dense visual correspondence across time, achieving video segmentation and keypoint/part propagation results. CroBo uses a shared encoder and asymmetric masking but samples one frame and restricts source information to a CLS token, exchanging explicit temporal correspondence for compact spatial scene memory.

reviewed_competitors.title: Visual Representation Learning with Stochastic Frame Prediction
reviewed_competitors.difference: RSP directly models uncertain future frames with a stochastic predictor and combines it with masked image modeling, evaluating video label propagation and robot control. CroBo argues that future ambiguity weakens the signal and instead reconstructs a deterministic contained crop; the tradeoff is cleaner spatial supervision without direct temporal learning.

reviewed_competitors.title: DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision
reviewed_competitors.difference: DINOv2 is the paper's strongest generic image-pretraining reference for several tasks and the only method with a numerical DAVIS-curvature comparison. It scales self-distillation and masked-image objectives on a large curated image corpus rather than enforcing a single-token source bottleneck or a contained target crop; its different pretraining data also prevents a clean objective-only comparison with Kinetics-trained CroBo.

reviewed_competitors.title: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners
reviewed_competitors.difference: MAE establishes asymmetric high-mask pixel reconstruction and supplies CroBo's normalized-pixel target and decoder lineage. MAE reconstructs one image from its own visible patches at 75% masking and retains a patch-token representation; CroBo raises masking, supplies a separate containing source view, and discards all source patch tokens in favor of one CLS state.

reviewed_competitors.title: Self-Supervised Learning from Images with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture
reviewed_competitors.difference: I-JEPA also learns from one image by predicting spatial target blocks from surrounding context, making it a direct alternative to CroBo's claim that spatially grounded prediction can replace temporal pairs. It predicts target representations with distributed context to favor semantics, whereas CroBo predicts normalized pixels and compresses the entire source crop into one CLS token for robot-policy transfer.

reviewed_competitors.title: Masked World Models for Visual Control
reviewed_competitors.difference: Masked World Models couples masked pixel representation learning to an explicit latent dynamics model and reward prediction on online robot-control data. CroBo instead freezes an offline Kinetics-pretrained spatial encoder and evaluates behavior cloning without learning transitions; it is cheaper as a reusable visual state but does not demonstrate action-conditioned prediction or planning.

reviewed_competitors.title: Dimension-free deterministic equivalents and scaling laws for random feature regression
reviewed_competitors.difference: Defilippis, Loureiro, and Misiakiewicz give non-asymptotic dimension-free deterministic equivalents for random-feature ridge-regression error and derive sharp rates when the feature-map spectrum and target decay satisfy power laws. They largely assume or abstract the relevant feature eigenvalues; the present paper derives those eigenvalues from a specific anisotropic Gaussian input plus monomial sketch but does not close the risk analysis.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: NeurIPS 2024 official proceedings, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37

reviewed_competitors.title: Asymptotics of Learning with Deep Structured (Random) Features
reviewed_competitors.relationship: deep random-feature covariance and learning predecessor
reviewed_competitors.difference: Schroder et al. derive population-feature covariance formulas and high-dimensional readout test error for broad deep structured random features under proportional asymptotics. Their scope includes depth and structured weights, but not ordered power-law eigenvalue bounds or the log correction for trace-class anisotropic inputs. The present paper is sharper on that narrow spectrum question and only experimental on depth.

reviewed_competitors.title: Sheaf Cohomology of Linear Predictive Coding Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Seely already maps neuron activations and local prediction errors in linear predictive-coding networks to vertex/edge stalks, identifies inference with sheaf-Laplacian diffusion, and uses Hodge/cohomology diagnostics for recurrent contradictions. The present paper adds affine bias augmentation, state-dependent ReLU restrictions, a unitriangular path proof, nonlinear-output local adjoints, and simultaneous rather than bilevel weight-state dynamics; Seely is broader on recurrent topology and genuine H1 obstructions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Selective Adaptation of Beliefs and Communication on Cellular Sheaves
reviewed_competitors.relationship: direct mathematical precursor by the same authors
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bosca and Ghrist already develop coordinate-level stubbornness, selective restriction-map learning, joint opinion-expression diffusion, regularized convergence in the affine case, and the stagnation bounds used here. The present work specializes those tools to neural forward-pass variables and ReLU CPWA inference; it does not extend the precursor's joint convergence theorem through moving nonlinear activation boundaries.

reviewed_competitors.title: Joint Diffusion Processes as an Inductive Bias in Sheaf Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Hernandez Caralt et al. already discretize joint feature and restriction-map diffusion, including the same residual outer-product 'learning to lie' ODE, inside trainable sheaf GNN layers for heterophily. The present paper does not design a sheaf GNN; it encodes an existing MLP computation as a path sheaf and uses the joint ODE as a local training rule, adding the forward-pass harmonic theorem but showing much weaker training-scale evidence.

reviewed_competitors.title: Predictive Coding Approximates Backprop along Arbitrary Computation Graphs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Millidge et al. already translate arbitrary differentiable computation graphs—including branching CNNs, RNNs, and LSTMs—into local predictive-coding inference and recover backprop-like gradients with competitive benchmark performance. The present method supplies a cellular-sheaf/topological interpretation and exact fixed-weight harmonic convergence for a ReLU path, but its local training neither matches backprop empirically nor covers arbitrary computation graphs.

reviewed_competitors.title: Equilibrium Propagation: Bridging the Gap Between Energy-Based Models and Backpropagation
reviewed_competitors.difference: Equilibrium propagation already uses recurrent relaxation, output nudging, bidirectional error influence, and local synaptic changes to compute an objective gradient in energy-based networks. The present paper instead embeds a pretrained directed feedforward ReLU network into an edge-discrepancy sheaf and evolves states and weights in one coupled flow; unlike equilibrium propagation, its joint nonlinear training convergence and gradient equivalence to backprop are not established.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Sheaf Diffusion: A Topological Perspective on Heterophily and Oversmoothing in GNNs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bodnar et al. establish learned sheaf diffusion and spectral/harmonic analysis as a neural message-passing architecture for heterophilic graphs. The present paper's object is different: it encodes the operations of an already specified feedforward network and analyzes the resulting path Laplacian. Its novelty should therefore not be phrased as introducing neural sheaf diffusion itself.

reviewed_competitors.title: Cache Me If You Must: Adaptive Key-Value Quantization for Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: AQUA-KV learns layer-wise predictors and stores quantized residuals for every KV vector, reaching near-lossless 2-2.5-bit caches on Llama 3.2 with under 1% relative error. This paper instead predicts across heads, retains selected references in full precision, and entirely omits target caches; its checkpoint-emergence analysis is distinct, while its compression needs a matched byte/accuracy/latency comparison against AQUA-KV.

reviewed_competitors.title: CHAI: Clustered Head Attention for Efficient LLM Inference
reviewed_competitors.difference: CHAI clusters heads with correlated attention behavior and shares cached representations at runtime, reporting up to 21.4% cache-memory reduction and 1.73x latency improvement. This paper predicts raw Q/K/V activation vectors with learned linear maps and traces their developmental origin rather than grouping attention maps, but reports no matching runtime measurement.

reviewed_competitors.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
reviewed_competitors.difference: GQA converts pretrained multi-head checkpoints to grouped KV heads with about 5% of original pretraining compute and reports quality close to multi-head attention with MQA-like speed. This paper leaves MHA weights unchanged and uses small post-hoc calibration, trading uptraining for reconstruction error and inference projections.

reviewed_competitors.title: Eigen Attention: Attention in Low-Rank Space for KV Cache Compression
reviewed_competitors.difference: Eigen Attention projects each layer's attention computation into learned low-rank spaces and reports up to 40% cache reduction plus up to 60% attention-latency reduction. This paper uses inter-head maps and preserves full-dimensional reference heads, so its structural claim is head redundancy rather than a layer-wide low-rank attention basis.

reviewed_competitors.title: xKV: Cross-Layer SVD for KV-Cache Compression
reviewed_competitors.difference: Current xKV exploits singular-vector alignment across grouped layers and consolidates their caches into shared low-rank spaces, with long-context RULER and MLA evaluations. This paper focuses on within- and preceding-layer inter-head activation prediction and pretraining emergence. Its bibliography points to arXiv:2504.12345, an unrelated urban-science paper, rather than xKV's actual record.

reviewed_competitors.title: Explicit Multi-head Attention for Inter-head Interaction in Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Explicit Multi-head Attention, posted before this work, parameterizes separate head-level linear compositions of K and V and reconstructs low-rank virtual heads, reporting 50% KV-cache reduction with negligible losses on several reasoning tasks and a 3.59% drop on Olympiad math. That substantially overlaps inter-head linear reconstruction; this paper's clearest added value is the post-hoc raw-activation R2 atlas, OLMo checkpoint-emergence study, and key/value asymmetry rather than the compression primitive.

reviewed_competitors.title: Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle: A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Dodson et al. already partition the schedule into low-, medium-, and high-noise regimes using Gaussian-shell coverage and posterior concentration and identify the middle as the danger zone; this paper adds large-model reconstruction-versus-trajectory measurements and an error-smoothed circle model.

reviewed_competitors.title: Biased Generalization in Diffusion Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Garnier-Brun et al. show that test loss can improve while generations become anomalously close to their own training set using disjoint-model comparisons; that tailors a sample-level bias metric and complicates any benign reading of the present paper's saturated average inference gap.

reviewed_competitors.title: Why Diffusion Models Don't Memorize: The Role of Implicit Dynamical Regularization in Training
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bonnaire et al. identify separated generation and memorization timescales in U-Nets and a random-feature model; this paper instead locates train favoritism across noise and argues actual sampling paths avoid much of it.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Edge of Memorization in Diffusion Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Buchanan et al. predict a model-size crossover between memorizing and generalizing solutions from their training losses in controlled data; this paper empirically relates size to a noise-resolved gap but emphasizes the disconnect between denoising and completed inference.

reviewed_competitors.title: Provable Separations between Memorization and Generalization in Diffusion Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ye et al. separate the empirical and population score objectives and the network sizes needed to represent them, then mitigate memorization by pruning; this paper gives an error-smoothed flow account and trajectory-state measurements rather than an estimation/approximation theorem.

reviewed_competitors.title: On Memorization in Diffusion Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Gu et al. define effective model memorization and sweep data, model, training, and even random conditioning labels; this paper refines those factors by noise level and separates reconstruction probes from actual sampler trajectories.

reviewed_competitors.title: Classifier-Free Guidance inside the Attraction Basin May Cause Memorization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Jain et al. locate CFG-induced copying inside low-noise attraction basins and delay or reverse guidance to escape them; this paper measures CFG and autoguidance gaps across noise and finds their reconstruction effect mainly where primary and auxiliary predictions diverge late.

reviewed_competitors.title: Data Distributional Properties Drive Emergent In-Context Learning in Transformers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: The direct Omniglot burstiness-and-Zipf predecessor and source of the ICL/IWL evaluators used by CoQE.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chan et al. show the two modes can coexist at a skewed Zipfian sweet spot by changing the data distribution. CoQE reuses that setting but changes the architecture to separate context and query pathways, seeking coexistence across five distributions rather than at one favorable distribution.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Transient Nature of Emergent In-Context Learning in Transformers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: The direct predecessor establishing that ICL can emerge and then yield to IWL during continued training.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Singh et al. diagnose transience and test L2 regularization while retaining a standard Transformer. CoQE adds distinct task/sample encoders and an anti-collapse intervention; its novelty is architectural, while its noise-free ablation still exhibits the predecessor's transience.

reviewed_competitors.title: Dual Process Learning: Controlling Use of In-Context vs. In-Weights Strategies with Weight Forgetting
reviewed_competitors.relationship: The closest prior method explicitly claiming coexistence of in-context and in-weights solutions in one model.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Anand et al. use active and probabilistic temporary forgetting to induce a controllable dual-process strategy on structural ICL in toy, masked, and autoregressive language models. CoQE instead hard-separates query and context representations and combines dynamic and static class vectors. This prior work means coexistence or a 'dual process' is not itself new.

reviewed_competitors.title: Differential learning kinetics govern the transition from memorization to generalization during in-context learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A direct mechanistic alternative for the memorization-to-ICL transition in small synthetic Transformers.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Nguyen and Reddy model memorizing and generalizing subcircuits as largely independent and explain their transition through relative learning rates and task diversity. CoQE instead posits interference in a shared representation and removes it architecturally, but does not experimentally distinguish its causal account from differential kinetics.

reviewed_competitors.title: Toward Understanding In-context vs. In-weight Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A direct theory-and-LLM predecessor modeling a gate between explicit in-context and in-weight predictors.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chan et al. analyze when a stylized gate selects each strategy and reproduce related behavior in Transformers and Gemma fine-tuning. CoQE replaces mixture selection with separate representation pathways and an inner-product readout, but its broader theoretical claims are weakened by the proof gaps identified here.

reviewed_competitors.title: Strategy Coopetition Explains the Emergence and Transience of In-Context Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A direct circuit-level account of simultaneous cooperation and competition between ICL and an in-weight-like strategy.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Singh et al. identify shared subcircuits, a context-constrained IWL strategy, and a setup with truly emergent persistent ICL in a two-layer attention model. CoQE deliberately prevents sharing between task and sample encodings; thus the competitor also cautions that shared circuitry can be beneficial rather than purely interfering.

reviewed_competitors.title: Gradient Descent on Neural Networks Typically Occurs at the Edge of Stability
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Cohen et al. are the closest established account of large-step neural training through the real Hessian stability threshold and progressive sharpening.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ghosts of Softmax proposes a directional complex-analytic scale that can stay finite when cross-entropy curvature becomes small, then measures the actual proposal through logit JVPs. It complements rather than displaces edge-of-stability theory because it neither predicts the full Hessian dynamics nor proves the complex radius is the active boundary in nonlinear networks.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Loss Curvature Perspective on Training Instability in Deep Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Gilmer et al. directly study neural-training instability, warmup, normalization, and architecture through loss-curvature evolution.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Their mechanism and diagnostics are real-axis curvature based; the new paper instead derives a softmax partition-zero lower bound from directional logits. The latter's clearest novelty is this alternative observable, while its universal safety interpretation is weaker than its rhetoric suggests.

reviewed_competitors.title: Why Gradient Clipping Accelerates Training: A Theoretical Justification for Adaptivity
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Zhang et al. provide the closest prior theory for clipping as an adaptive response to generalized smoothness and gradient magnitude.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ordinary clipping constrains gradient norm, whereas radius control evaluates the class-logit spread induced by an already proposed direction and varies by batch and direction. The spike experiments compare the two, but the proposed controller pays an extra directional-pass cost and lacks comparable convergence guarantees.

reviewed_competitors.title: Temperature check: theory and practice for training models with softmax-cross-entropy losses
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Agarwala et al. are a primary predecessor on how temperature and logit scale govern softmax-cross-entropy optimization dynamics.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ghosts uses temperature as a falsifiable scaling intervention for a particular inverse directional-spread coordinate and converts that coordinate into a step controller. Temperature Check does not derive the complex partition-zero radius, while the new paper does not supersede its broader dynamical account.

reviewed_competitors.title: The large learning rate phase of deep learning: the catapult mechanism
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Lewkowycz et al. are the key counterpoint showing that large steps, transient loss growth, and curvature reduction can be productive rather than failed training.
reviewed_competitors.difference: That result narrows any claim that r>1 is unsafe: Ghosts itself observes benign above-radius steps and can at most treat r as a hazard scale. Radius clipping may prevent destructive spikes, but it may also suppress useful catapult dynamics unless the target adapts.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Surprising Effectiveness of Large Learning Rates under Standard Width Scaling
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Haas et al. provide a current primary competitor on controlled divergence and beneficial very-large-learning-rate regimes under standard parameterization.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Their results reinforce that real training can remain useful beyond a local approximation's nominal regime. Ghosts contributes a proposal-dependent coordinate that might separate moderate from extreme risk, but does not test whether clipping by it preserves the controlled-divergence benefits documented by Haas et al.

reviewed_competitors.title: Locating the Closest Singularity in a Polynomial Homotopy
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Telen and Van Barel are a close numerical-analysis predecessor using the closest complex singularity of an analytic continuation to govern safe continuation step sizes.
reviewed_competitors.difference: That work concerns polynomial homotopy paths and numerical root tracking rather than neural cross-entropy. It weakens any broad novelty claim for complex-singularity-aware step control, while leaving novel the paper's softmax exponential-sum specialization, directional logit bound, and optimizer experiment.

reviewed_competitors.title: What Trace Powers Reveal About Log-Determinants: Convergence Radius, Spectral Geometry, and Diagnostic Value
reviewed_competitors.relationship: This same-author preprint is the nearest internal precursor on reading a Taylor convergence radius and hidden spectral geometry from logarithmic singularities and series coefficients.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The precursor studies log determinants and trace powers rather than softmax cross-entropy or optimizer proposals. Ghosts transfers the complex-radius perspective to exponential partition sums, derives a JVP-computable bound, and adds controller experiments; the general conceptual move from logarithmic singularities to convergence diagnostics is not wholly new within the author's own work.

reviewed_competitors.title: Do Language Models Plan Ahead for Future Tokens?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wu et al. introduce myopic training and distinguish pre-caching from breadcrumb explanations of look-ahead at model and task scale. This paper reuses myopic training but adds circuit sharing, an exact three-way gradient partition, per-feature trajectory attribution, and a large-model SAE proxy.

reviewed_competitors.title: Future Lens: Anticipating Subsequent Tokens from a Single Hidden State
reviewed_competitors.difference: Future Lens decodes and intervenes on future-token predictions already present in static hidden states. This paper asks which training paths create individual features and finds that high delayed causal effect is negatively related to its linear look-ahead subspace.

reviewed_competitors.title: Emergent World Representations: Exploring a Sequence Model Trained on a Synthetic Task
reviewed_competitors.difference: Li et al. establish linear Othello board representations and causal interventions in a trained model. This paper accepts that testbed but partitions cells by immediate legal-move utility and attributes their unequal emergence to direct, pre-cached, and shared gradients.

reviewed_competitors.title: Evaluating the World Model Implicit in a Generative Model
reviewed_competitors.difference: Vafa et al. use Myhill-Nerode-style state equivalence and counterfactual tests to show that generative world models can be incoherent despite decodable state. This paper offers a developmental explanation for the Othello fragility but does not replace those stronger behavioral coherence tests.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Pitfalls of Next-Token Prediction
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bachmann and Nagarajan construct tasks where teacher-forced next-token prediction learns undesirable shortcuts or cannot elicit planning and motivate alternative objectives. This paper shows why standard NTP can nevertheless create immediately useless features through later-position and shared-parameter gradients.

reviewed_competitors.title: Better & Faster Large Language Models via Multi-token Prediction
reviewed_competitors.difference: Gloeckle et al. add several future-token prediction heads and show gains in code and induction, directly modifying the supervision signal. This paper leaves ordinary NTP unchanged and decomposes the implicit future and shared gradient routes it already contains.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Belief State Transformer
reviewed_competitors.difference: The Belief State Transformer uses prefix and suffix information to train compact predictive belief states and evaluates state sufficiency. This paper diagnoses how decoder-only NTP features emerge without a bidirectional auxiliary objective and makes the narrower claim that non-direct gradients can create locally useless representations.

reviewed_competitors.title: Crosscoding Through Time: Tracking Emergence & Consolidation Of Linguistic Representations Throughout LLM Pretraining
reviewed_competitors.difference: Crosscoding Through Time aligns sparse features across real LLM checkpoints and uses Relative Indirect Effects to identify when linguistic features become causally important, directly competing on feature development rather than static interpretation. It scales through saved checkpoints and causal mediation but does not decompose the NTP gradient into direct, pre-cached, and shared paths; this paper offers finer gradient provenance on small replayable models but a weaker large-model bridge.

reviewed_competitors.title: Tracking the Feature Dynamics in LLM Training: A Mechanistic Study
reviewed_competitors.difference: SAE-Track follows semantic formation and directional drift across a continual series of sparse autoencoders, providing direct evidence that feature axes evolve during training. That evidence challenges this paper's assumption that a final probe direction can stand in for the feature throughout replay; conversely, SAE-Track describes feature trajectories without attributing them to direct, future-position, or shared-parameter gradient paths.

reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct linear-probing and intervention antecedent on Othello world state.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Nanda et al. show a simple player-relative linear board representation and use vector arithmetic to control behavior; this paper analyzes an easier closed-form spatial process and bidirectional span, but leaves its decoded coordinates causally untested.

reviewed_competitors.title: What Should Embeddings Embed? Autoregressive Models Represent Latent Generating Distributions
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct theoretical and empirical sufficient-statistics antecedent.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhang et al. argue from a Bayesian account that autoregressive embeddings should encode predictive sufficient statistics and reconstruct embeddings from those statistics; this paper sharpens one toy setting with affine reverse fits, layer staging, exact grid geometry, and architecture comparisons.

reviewed_competitors.title: Cognitive Maps in Language Models: A Mechanistic Analysis of Spatial Planning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest spatial random-walk and causal-map competitor.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Baumgartner et al. train GPT-2 on grid foraging and planning, find a map-like coordinate system, and use causal interventions to distinguish map-based from path-dependent algorithms and generalization; this paper provides exact predictive-statistic derivations and constraint universality but no causal or shift test.

reviewed_competitors.title: Linearly Structured World Representations in Maze-Solving Transformers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct spatial representation and attention-head antecedent.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ivanitskiy et al. linearly reconstruct maze topology and valid paths and identify adjacency heads in maze-solving transformers; this paper uses random walks rather than solution sequences and relates its coordinate map exactly to predictive distributions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformers learn factored representations
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct contemporary theory of how latent predictive factors occupy transformer subspaces.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It derives and tests product-space versus orthogonal factorized representations, including accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs under dependent factors; this paper instead distinguishes a shared full-future state from task-specific next-token geometry across layers and architectures.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural networks leverage nominally quantum and post-quantum representations
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct cross-architecture predictive-state geometry competitor and contrary evidence on architecture dependence.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Riechers et al. report future-distribution geometries largely independent of transformer versus RNN architecture for more exotic generators; this paper finds the underlying state readable in both but a clean world/task stage only in attention, making the scope of architecture dependence an open conflict.

reviewed_competitors.title: Symmetry in language statistics shapes the geometry of model representations
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Competing data-statistics explanation for emergent representation geometry.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Karkada et al. derive circles, ripples, and coordinate decodability from translation symmetry in pairwise co-occurrence statistics across embedding and language models; this paper uses full predictive distributions and architectural computation, so pairwise-statistics and sufficient-state explanations need direct ablation against each other.

reviewed_competitors.title: Manifold Steering Reveals the Shared Geometry of Neural Network Representation and Behavior
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct causal alternative for testing whether decoded geometry actually shapes outputs.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wurgaft et al. fit activation and behavior manifolds and intervene along curved paths to establish bidirectional geometry-behavior agreement; this paper has stronger analytic ground truth but uses probes and visualization without an equivalent behavioral intervention.

reviewed_competitors.title: Thinking in Space: How Multimodal Large Language Models See, Remember, and Recall Spaces
reviewed_competitors.difference: The same group introduced VSI-Bench for short, single-scene spatial QA and found benefits from explicit cognitive maps. Cambrian-S extends that line with 10-240 minute edited/concatenated streams, a 590K training mixture, and bounded predictive-memory prototypes; therefore the new benchmark's credible novelty is continual length scaling and event-selective processing, not visual-spatial QA itself.

reviewed_competitors.title: MovieChat: From Dense Token to Sparse Memory for Long Video Understanding
reviewed_competitors.difference: MovieChat already uses Transformer tokens and an Atkinson-Shiffrin-inspired short/long-term memory to sparsify long video. Cambrian-S's narrower addition is a learned next-latent prediction error for query-agnostic compression and event boundaries plus explicit spatial recall/count extrapolation; its own Table 17 uses MovieChat as a direct baseline.

reviewed_competitors.title: Flash-VStream: Memory-Based Real-Time Understanding for Long Video Streams
reviewed_competitors.difference: Flash-VStream already targets asynchronous questions over online streams with spatial, temporal, retrieved, and learned abstract memory and introduces VStream-QA. Cambrian-S differs by using explicit prediction error to prioritize memory and to trigger spatial count segments, but the paper omits Flash-VStream's trained abstract-memory component in its comparison, so superiority over the full prior method is unestablished.

reviewed_competitors.title: V-JEPA 2: Self-Supervised Video Models Enable Understanding, Prediction and Planning
reviewed_competitors.difference: V-JEPA 2 learns joint-embedding video prediction at internet scale and demonstrates action-conditioned robot planning, which is substantially stronger evidence for a predictive world model. Cambrian-S contributes a much lighter MLLM-side one-frame predictor used as a surprise control signal for memory and segmentation; its novelty is the continual spatial systems use of prediction error, not latent predictive modeling or planning itself.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Niedoba et al. reproduce network behavior by aggregating local empirical denoisers after measuring a shared local bias; this paper derives the proposed masks from data statistics and allows nonlocal, position-dependent support.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding Generalizability of Diffusion Models Requires Rethinking the Hidden Gaussian Structure
reviewed_competitors.difference: Li, Dai, and Qu already show that generalizing neural denoisers approach the Gaussian denoiser defined by empirical mean and covariance; this paper's narrower addition is to connect that structure to spatial Jacobians, intervene on covariance, and reuse its support in a nonlinear empirical sampler.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Hidden Linear Structure in Score-Based Models and its Application
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wang and Vastola derive and validate a Gaussian linear score primarily at high noise and use it to skip early sampling; this paper studies the spatial sensitivity of that operator across noise and combines it with finite-data nonlinear weights.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Gaussian Score Approximation for Diffusion Models and its Applications
reviewed_competitors.difference: An expanded successor to the same authors' arXiv:2311.10892, this work extends Gaussian and Gaussian-mixture score approximations into moderate noise and analytical teleportation; the present paper focuses on data-dependent locality, per-pixel masks, and explaining a trained denoiser rather than accelerating it.

reviewed_competitors.title: Closed-Form Diffusion Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Scarvelis et al. explicitly smooth the finite-data closed-form score and accelerate it with nearest-neighbor estimation; the present method constrains empirical distances to covariance-derived subspaces instead of applying isotropic score smoothing.

reviewed_competitors.title: Generalization in diffusion models arises from geometry-adaptive harmonic representations
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kadkhodaie et al. argue neural inductive bias learns geometry-adaptive harmonic shrinkage and show it can persist where such a basis is suboptimal; this paper emphasizes global data covariance. The two accounts may be complementary, and the current experiments do not eliminate architecture-data interaction.
