reviewed_competitors.title: End-to-End Multi-Task Learning with Attention
reviewed_competitors.difference: MTAN learns task-specific feature-level attention on a shared feature pool and explicitly reports robustness to loss weighting. TS-sigma-BN replaces attention modules with static per-channel normalization gates and uses fewer parameters, but still incurs task-conditioned repeated computation.

reviewed_competitors.title: AdaShare: Learning What To Share For Efficient Deep Multi-Task Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: AdaShare learns task-specific layer-execution policies with an explicit resource-efficiency objective. TS-sigma-BN uses much finer static channel scaling without architecture search, but does not optimize or consistently win on actual compute efficiency.

reviewed_competitors.title: Task Adaptive Parameter Sharing for Multi-Task Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: TAPS learns which pretrained layers need task-specific copies across ResNet, DenseNet, and ViT and penalizes task-specific resource use. TS-sigma-BN restricts adaptation to normalization, yielding a smaller storage footprint but a less expressive adapter and no task-copy sparsity objective.

reviewed_competitors.title: TaskExpert: Dynamically Assembling Multi-Task Representations with Memorial Mixture-of-Experts
reviewed_competitors.difference: TaskExpert dynamically decodes task representations from multiple expert feature spaces and a cross-layer memory. TS-sigma-BN is static, smaller, and simpler; its Table 3 uses fewer parameters and better four-of-five point metrics, but similar FLOPs and no uncertainty are reported.

reviewed_competitors.title: Multi-Task Dense Prediction via Mixture of Low-Rank Experts
reviewed_competitors.difference: MLoRE combines a generic convolution path with dynamically parameterized low-rank experts and explicitly controls expert cost. TS-sigma-BN uses 29M versus 44M parameters in the paper's protocol and improves four task means, but needs 214G versus MLoRE's 72G FLOPs, reversing the compute-efficiency comparison.

reviewed_competitors.title: MTLoRA: A Low-Rank Adaptation Approach for Efficient Multi-Task Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: MTLoRA uses task-agnostic and task-specific low-rank adapters in a hierarchical transformer. TS-sigma-BN obtains a larger displayed aggregate mean with fewer trainable parameters, but its LayerNorm/downsampler modifications are structurally different and the table omits run dispersion and training compute.

reviewed_competitors.title: Receding Neuron Importances for Structured Pruning
reviewed_competitors.difference: The predecessor already introduces bounded sigmoid BatchNorm scales as neuron-importance variables for structured pruning. The new work's defensible novelty is applying task-indexed copies, faster gate optimization, and cross-task analyses to MTL, not the sigmoid-normalization parameterization itself.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Options via Compression
reviewed_competitors.difference: Jiang et al. address degenerate maximum-likelihood skill decompositions by adding description-length compression and show downstream sample-efficiency gains, including image observations. Internal RL instead relies on the bottleneck and frozen residual representation to obtain sparse switches; it does not compare against the explicit compression objective despite citing it as a close predecessor.

reviewed_competitors.title: Variational Temporal Abstraction
reviewed_competitors.relationship: variational temporal-segmentation and accelerated planning antecedent
reviewed_competitors.difference: VTA learns hierarchical latent dynamics and boundary variables for jumpy imagination in model-based control. This paper instead turns inferred temporal codes into residual-stream policies inside a frozen action predictor and applies model-free policy gradients over them; its Appendix E follows the same stochastic temporal-abstraction lineage but contains sign errors in the printed ELBO.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Robot Skills with Temporal Variational Inference
reviewed_competitors.difference: Shankar and Gupta infer continuous robot options and a high-level policy from demonstration trajectories using temporally causal variational inference across three robotic datasets. Internal RL uses a privileged full-sequence encoder during discovery, places the skill interface in a pretrained model's residual stream, and evaluates one simulated ant composition rather than diverse robot datasets.

reviewed_competitors.title: Latent Space Policies for Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Haarnoja et al. train entropy-rich lower policies whose invertible latent variables become actions for a higher policy and solve sparse-reward tasks. The present paper acquires the lower action prior by autoregressive imitation, discovers durations from unlabeled trajectories, and intervenes internally; acting with RL in a compact latent controller space is therefore established rather than new by itself.

reviewed_competitors.title: Self-Consistent Trajectory Autoencoder: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with Trajectory Embeddings
reviewed_competitors.difference: SeCTAR learns generative trajectory embeddings and plans or reinforces a high-level policy over those temporally extended behaviors. Internal RL decodes a latent to a feedback controller acting through residual states rather than an open-loop trajectory distribution, and learns option boundaries dynamically rather than fixing a trajectory horizon.

reviewed_competitors.title: Leveraging Skills from Unlabeled Prior Data for Efficient Online Exploration
reviewed_competitors.difference: SUPE learns VAE skills from unlabeled trajectories, pseudo-labels prior data optimistically, and combines it with off-policy high-level RL across 42 long-horizon sparse-reward tasks. Internal RL uniquely acts inside a pretrained autoregressive model and learns termination, but its two-task evaluation and tens-of-millions interaction budget are much narrower.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Temporal Abstractions via Variational Homomorphisms in Option-Induced Abstract MDPs
reviewed_competitors.relationship: current option-latent reasoning and control competitor
reviewed_competitors.difference: VMOC explicitly models latent thoughts as options, learns them with off-policy variational option-critic machinery, and supplies an abstract-MDP homomorphism argument plus language and locomotion experiments. Internal RL discovers residual controllers through next-action prediction and uses a learned causal switch, but offers no optimality-preservation result or language evaluation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Reinforcement Learning for Latent-Space Thinking in LLMs
reviewed_competitors.relationship: concurrent direct latent-step RL competitor and negative result
reviewed_competitors.difference: Özeren and Aßenmacher apply GRPO and a direct Latent RL objective to actual LLM latent thinking and report that the RL-trained latent systems still trail language-space chain of thought on mathematical reasoning. The present paper predates no such negative evidence in its discussion and succeeds only on constructed navigation; its dynamic termination and residual-controller hypernetwork are different, but transfer to LLM reasoning remains unshown.

reviewed_competitors.title: Reinforcement Learning from Passive Data via Latent Intentions
reviewed_competitors.difference: Latent Intentions converts passive trajectories into a latent behavioral prior for downstream RL without task annotations. Internal RL instead relies on successful action-labeled expert trajectories and controls a pretrained predictor at mid-depth; the shared deployment claim is that latent behavior variables improve exploration from offline data.

reviewed_competitors.title: Saddle-to-Saddle Dynamics in Deep Linear Networks: Small Initialization Training, Symmetry, and Sparsity
reviewed_competitors.difference: Jacot et al. formulate the small-initialization saddle-sequence conjecture for deep linear networks and prove the transition between the first two saddles. The present work broadens the architectural language through unit embeddings and invariant manifolds and proposes two timescale classes, but likewise does not prove full trajectories outside the diagonal-linear special case.

reviewed_competitors.title: Saddle-to-Saddle Dynamics in Diagonal Linear Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Pesme and Flammarion fully characterize the vanishing-initialization gradient-flow path, visited saddles, jump times, and L1-minimum endpoint for diagonal linear regression. This paper trades that rigor for architectural breadth; its manifold connections and later-stage dynamics remain heuristic, a distinction it explicitly acknowledges.

reviewed_competitors.title: SGD learning on neural networks: leap complexity and saddle-to-saddle dynamics
reviewed_competitors.difference: Abbe et al. prove sequential support learning and sample/time complexity for two-layer networks under specified isotropic data and SGD conditions, going beyond gradient-flow approximations. The present paper uses effective unit count across more architectures but provides no stochastic complexity bound or full-trajectory theorem.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformers learn through gradual rank increase
reviewed_competitors.difference: Boix-Adsera et al. rigorously prove gradual rank growth for transformers under diagonal weights and small initialization and show broader empirical rank increase. The present work interprets multi-head attention through sparse unit recruitment and invariant manifolds, but its scalar quadratic proposition does not directly cover the matrix-valued attention implementation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Training Dynamics of In-Context Learning in Linear Attention
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhang et al. derive fixed points and reduce separate-key/query linear-attention saddle dynamics to scalar ODEs, showing principal-component count increases over training; merged key/query attention instead has one abrupt transition. The present paper abstracts that case into an initialization-driven quadratic-unit mechanism and predicts width effects, but offers less exact attention-specific dynamics.

reviewed_competitors.title: Saddle-to-Saddle Dynamics in Deep ReLU Networks: Low-Rank Bias in the First Saddle Escape
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bantzis, Simon, and Jacot prove low-rank structure for optimal escape directions from the origin in deep ReLU networks and carefully limit their full saddle sequence to conjecture. The present paper supplies general embedding/invariance algebra and broader simulations, but its ReLU trajectory analysis is also conjectural and has an unaddressed nonsmooth-gradient convention.

reviewed_competitors.title: Semi-flat minima and saddle points by embedding neural networks to overparameterization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Fukumizu et al. study three width-embedding constructions and distinguish when smooth and ReLU narrow minima become semi-flat minima or saddles. The present work adds homogeneous and general linear-dependence constructions and invariant-dynamics language, while its broad nested-saddle wording is weaker than the predecessor's explicit type conditions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Geometry of the Loss Landscape in Overparameterized Neural Networks: Symmetries and Invariances
reviewed_competitors.difference: Simsek et al. explicitly characterize symmetry-induced critical affine subspaces and connected global-minimum manifolds created by added neurons. This paper focuses instead on invariant sets under gradient flow and a proposed stagewise trajectory, but it does not establish the connecting heteroclinic orbits that would turn landscape geometry into full dynamics.

reviewed_competitors.title: Embedding Principle of Loss Landscape of Deep Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhang et al. prove that critical points of narrower differentiable networks embed into higher-degeneracy critical points or affine subspaces of wider deep networks while preserving the function. The present Theorem 1 gives mechanism-specific constructive families including convolution and attention notation, then adds invariant-manifold and timescale hypotheses; critical embedding itself is not new.

reviewed_competitors.title: Gradient flow dynamics of shallow ReLU networks for square loss and orthogonal inputs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Boursier, Pillaud-Vivien, and Flammarion precisely characterize small-initialization shallow-ReLU gradient flow for orthogonal data, including alignment, a specific saddle sequence, zero-loss convergence, and implicit bias. The present work spans more architectures and data controls but offers only a ReLU conjecture and selected simulations outside that special case.

reviewed_competitors.title: Simplicity Bias and Optimization Threshold in Two-Layer ReLU Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Boursier and Flammarion analyze early directional alignment, convergence to simpler non-interpolating solutions, an optimization threshold, and resulting test-loss benefits. This paper studies temporal effective-width stages rather than the final generalization bias and does not measure whether its simpler stages help or hurt test performance.

The present paper's defensible increment is a conditional finite-width Gaussian projection, a uniform initialization W2 rate, and a claimed O(L^-2) second-moment control/NFD approximation for its narrower ResNet—not first identification of the correlation.

reviewed_competitors.difference: This dynamical-mean-field analysis studies depth-muP residual-network training, simultaneous width/depth scaling, feature-learning dynamics, and hyperparameter transfer. The present work gives more explicit conditional control of a forward-backward correction but covers a simpler block and only a sequential fixed-K post-training limit.

reviewed_competitors.title: Width and Depth Limits Commute in Residual Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Hayou and Yang prove width/depth commutativity for residual networks at initialization and characterize covariance behavior. The present paper adds backward variables and feature-learning correlation, but its post-training theorem no longer proves commutativity and instead takes width before depth.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Neural Covariance SDE: Shaped Infinite Depth-and-Width Networks at Initialization
reviewed_competitors.difference: The Neural Covariance SDE develops joint depth-width initialization limits for shaped networks through a covariance SDE. The present work specializes to depth-muP preactivation ResNets, includes backward dynamics, and attempts a fixed-horizon feature-learning extension via explicit training corrections.

reviewed_competitors.title: Infinitely Deep Neural Networks as Diffusion Processes
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work established diffusion-process limits for randomly initialized deep residual networks. The present paper adds a width-dependent depth-muP scaling, backward dynamics, Wasserstein rates, and a training-dependent neural field rather than only a forward initialization diffusion.

reviewed_competitors.title: Tensor Programs IV: Feature Learning in Infinite-Width Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Tensor Programs IV supplies a master-theorem framework for feature learning under maximal-update parameterization at infinite width. The present paper relies on this line but adds an infinite-depth limit and explicit depth scaling; its theorem is correspondingly restricted to fixed training horizon and covariance regularity.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scaling Limits of Wide Neural Networks with Weight Sharing: Gaussian Process Behavior, Gradient Independence, and Neural Tangent Kernel Derivation
reviewed_competitors.difference: This paper formalizes when gradient independence is valid or invalid in wide networks with reused weights and derives correction behavior at initialization. The present work seeks a uniform-in-depth quantitative coupling and then tracks the new dependence created by feature-learning updates.

reviewed_competitors.title: Tensor Programs II: Neural Tangent Kernel for Any Architecture
reviewed_competitors.difference: Tensor Programs II provides a simple-check framework for gradient-independence calculations and NTK limits across architectures. The present work is in the feature-learning rather than frozen-kernel regime and focuses on the depth accumulation of an explicit forward-backward correction.

reviewed_competitors.title: Mean Field Residual Networks: On the Edge of Chaos
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work analyzes forward and backward signal propagation and stability in deep random residual networks through mean-field recursions. The present paper uses depth-muP and conditional Gaussian methods to obtain diffusion and feature-learning limits rather than an initialization stability analysis alone.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Geneva and Zabaras already combine Koopman-style embeddings with Transformers for Lorenz, reaction-diffusion, and Navier-Stokes surrogate evolution and assess predictive performance. The present paper explicitly avoids proposing a new forecaster and instead inspects a minimal model's AR restriction and latent geometry, with much smaller-scale one-step evidence.

reviewed_competitors.title: Delayformer: Spatiotemporal Transformation for Predicting High-Dimensional Dynamics
reviewed_competitors.difference: Delayformer explicitly turns each observed variable into a delay-embedded state and cross-learns multivariate states with a shared Transformer, including limited/noisy high-dimensional forecasting and cross-domain tests. The present paper's delay-as-attention framing is therefore not first; its distinction is mechanistic inspection of a minimal latent and a softmax sign boundary rather than a forecasting architecture.

reviewed_competitors.title: Can Transformers Overcome Lack of Data in Simulation of History-Dependent Flows?
reviewed_competitors.difference: This preprint predates the target's initial submission by six days and directly tests Transformers under scarce data and unresolved history variables in flow simulation against a structure-preserving recurrent alternative. The present work gives cleaner small-system interpretability and a scalar cylinder probe, but lacks the matched structural baselines and history-dependent rollout focus.

reviewed_competitors.title: Zero-Shot Forecasting of Chaotic Systems
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work evaluates pretrained time-series models across 135 chaotic systems and analyzes a context-parroting mechanism and long-term dynamical statistics. The present paper trains per-system minimal models and provides local AR/delay interpretations, but it does not test zero-shot breadth or long-horizon chaotic invariants despite motivating that setting.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformers for Dynamical Systems Learn Transfer Operators In-Context
reviewed_competitors.difference: This post-submission paper gives a transfer-operator account of in-context dynamical prediction using explicit delay embeddings and a minimal two-layer single-head Transformer, with attention interpreted as kernel evaluation over invariant-set context. It overlaps the target's goal of mechanistically linking attention and delay dynamics but offers a different operator-level explanation and appeared after the target's first version.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhang et al. study chains of equality and group operations, identify association attention patterns, and test pretraining, chain length, and architecture. In-Context Algebra removes fixed token referents on every sequence and adds targeted finite-group mechanisms, but its weak association result shows that the earlier multi-step reasoning problem remains unsolved.

reviewed_competitors.title: Grokking Group Multiplication with Cosets
reviewed_competitors.difference: Stander et al. fully reverse engineer one-hidden-layer networks that grok S5 and S6 multiplication using subgroup and coset structure. In-Context Algebra studies a Transformer whose element names change per sequence and finds sparse retrieval/elimination heuristics rather than fixed coset representations; it covers broader prompt-local behavior but does not attain the antecedent's claimed end-to-end circuit completeness.

reviewed_competitors.title: Schema-learning and rebinding as mechanisms of in-context learning and emergence
reviewed_competitors.difference: Swaminathan et al. use interpretable clone-structured causal graphs to show template retrieval and rebinding of novel tokens, then argue for similar mechanisms in LLMs. In-Context Algebra supplies a Transformer-native finite-group task and causal circuit analyses, while the antecedent already establishes that contextual schema use can be separated from stable token meaning.

reviewed_competitors.title: How Do Transformers Learn Variable Binding in Symbolic Programs?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wu et al. train standard Transformers to dereference variable-assignment chains with distractors and causally identify addressable-memory and dereferencing mechanisms. In-Context Algebra changes the computation to partial finite-group products and finds identity and elimination heuristics, but variable binding without fixed semantics and causal circuit localization are not new in themselves.

reviewed_competitors.title: How do Language Models Bind Entities in Context?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Feng and Steinhardt causally recover continuous binding-ID vectors that pair entities with attributes across sufficiently large Pythia and LLaMA models. In-Context Algebra avoids pretrained semantics and exposes algorithms in a controlled small model; its novelty is the algebraic task and rule-specific mechanisms rather than the existence of contextual binding.

reviewed_competitors.title: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
reviewed_competitors.difference: Power et al. establish late generalization on small algorithmic datasets and its dependence on data size and optimization. In-Context Algebra adds per-sequence symbol randomization and skill-level checkpoint traces, but its phase-transition language and delayed held-out improvement inherit this benchmark lineage.

reviewed_competitors.title: Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability
reviewed_competitors.difference: Nanda et al. reverse engineer the Fourier algorithm learned for fixed-token modular addition and validate continuous progress measures with Fourier-space ablations. In-Context Algebra finds different relational heuristics after removing stable element embeddings and traces several task metrics, but its stage graph is less causally validated than the antecedent's circuit account.

reviewed_competitors.title: Interchangeable Token Embeddings for Extendable Vocabulary and Alpha-Equivalence
reviewed_competitors.relationship: direct architecture-and-evaluation antecedent for semantically interchangeable variables
reviewed_competitors.difference: Işık et al. formalize alpha-covariance and use shared-plus-random embeddings to generalize across variable renamings and unseen vocabularies in logic and copying. In-Context Algebra uses ordinary embeddings but randomizes assignments in the data, enabling emergent-mechanism study rather than guaranteed covariance; it does not compare against this explicit interchangeable-token prior.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Hindupur et al. show SAE architecture determines which nonlinear and heterogeneous-dimensional concepts can be seen; Bereska et al. assume tied linear SAE latents form an adequate feature alphabet and treat architectural improvements as reducing measurement error.

reviewed_competitors.title: Adversarial Examples Are Not Bugs, They Are Superposition
reviewed_competitors.difference: Gorton and Lewis report interventions on superposition and robustness in toy models plus adversarial-training effects in ResNet-18 as evidence for causation; Bereska et al. test a broader set of architectures with an SAE entropy proxy and find sign changes, but do not directly manipulate geometric overlap.

reviewed_competitors.title: Adversarial Attacks Leverage Interference Between Features in Superposition
reviewed_competitors.difference: Stevinson et al. derive attack directions from known interference geometry, intervene in controlled synthetic superposition, and connect predicted structure to image attacks; Bereska et al. measures activation diversity after adversarial training and cannot observe which feature pairs interfere.

reviewed_competitors.title: From Data Statistics to Feature Geometry: How Correlations Shape Superposition
reviewed_competitors.difference: Prieto et al. show that correlations can make interference constructive and directly inspect known-coordinate geometry; Bereska et al.'s independent-feature entropy aggregation ignores whether co-activation is redundant, synergistic, constructive, or adversarially exploitable.

reviewed_competitors.title: Spectral Superposition: A Theory of Feature Geometry
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ivanov et al. measure each assumed feature's allocation over frame eigenspaces and derive localization/tight-frame structure; Bereska et al. scales to real networks via SAEs but collapses direction and interference geometry into marginal activation entropy.

reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct methodological predecessor from overlapping authors: it uses context-dependent sparse transformer attention and sparsity regularization to expose local interaction graphs while preserving predictive world-model accuracy.
reviewed_competitors.difference: SPARTAN learns sparse object-interaction graphs in world models and validates against known environmental structure; the reviewed paper reuses the hard-gate/constrained-optimization idea for post-training pretrained LLMs and adds activation-patching and CLT circuit analyses up to 7B.

reviewed_competitors.title: Stream: Scaling up Mechanistic Interpretability to Long Context in LLMs via Sparse Attention
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporaneous direct sparse-attention interpretability method, submitted before the reviewed paper, that hierarchically prunes attention blocks to trace long-context information flow while preserving next-token behavior.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Stream is a post-hoc near-linear tracing approximation for existing long-context models and does not claim to reorganize their learned circuits; the reviewed method changes model architecture and weights to create intrinsically sparse routing, but its detailed mechanistic study uses much shorter contexts.

reviewed_competitors.title: Weight-sparse transformers have interpretable circuits
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest contemporaneous intrinsic-interpretability competitor: it constrains transformer weights to zero and recovers small human-understandable circuits, including preliminary adaptation to existing dense models.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Weight sparsity simplifies neuron and residual-channel connections and studies an explicit capability-interpretability frontier, mostly at smaller nonzero-parameter scales; the reviewed paper sparsifies token attention edges after pretraining, scales loss preservation to 7B, and emphasizes attention-mediated circuit tracing.

reviewed_competitors.title: Is Sparse Attention more Interpretable?
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct negative study of the proposition that sparse attention yields better explanations; it finds sparse attention does not reliably identify influential input tokens and can make that interpretation less plausible.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Meister et al. test attention-as-input-explanation on classification, whereas the reviewed paper uses causal component patching and CLT mediation rather than reading attention weights as input importance. The negative result still constrains any broad use of 'intrinsically interpretable' and motivates the reviewed paper's narrower circuit diagnostics.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Adaptive entmax is trained in machine translation and makes the normalized attention distribution sparse; the reviewed paper adds a separate hard Bernoulli gate after softmax, applies it through post-training to pretrained LMs, and evaluates component and feature circuits rather than mainly head diversity.

reviewed_competitors.title: Memory-efficient Transformers via Top-k Attention

reviewed_competitors.difference: Top-k fixes the same nonzero count per query and targets runtime memory, so it cannot express the reviewed paper's below-one-edge-per-query average or head/context-varying counts; the reviewed method requires long post-training but uses flexible learned Bernoulli connectivity as an interpretability prior.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Voita et al. prune at whole-head granularity in trained translation models and analyze head specialization; the reviewed method learns much finer token-edge gates, permits a head to be active only for selected contexts, and connects the resulting routing to task and feature-level circuits.

The distinction is source-video editing versus image-conditioned generation, but the trajectory interface and control objective substantially overlap.

reviewed_competitors.title: Generative Video Motion Editing with 3D Point Tracks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Subsequent direct source-video motion editor using paired source and target point tracks.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The later method lifts control into 3D tracks with explicit depth/occlusion reasoning and joint camera/object manipulation; MotionV2V uses simpler 2D rasterized correspondences and emphasizes arbitrary timestamp and temporal reversal. The later work narrows MotionV2V's claim to being the first or only point-track video-motion editor and exposes the importance of geometry-aware comparisons.

reviewed_competitors.title: TRACE: Object Motion Editing in Videos with First-Frame Trajectory Guidance
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Subsequent direct video-to-video competitor for changing object paths under source camera motion.
reviewed_competitors.difference: TRACE converts an easy first-frame trajectory specification into frame-aligned boxes and focuses on object motion, while MotionV2V asks for sparse point correspondences across time and also targets camera and temporal edits. TRACE's narrower task may reduce user effort and handle camera motion more explicitly; MotionV2V offers a broader edit vocabulary.

reviewed_competitors.title: TrajectoryMover: Generative Movement of Object Trajectories in Videos
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Subsequent direct competitor for generative relocation of an object's trajectory in an existing video.
reviewed_competitors.difference: TrajectoryMover builds a synthetic paired TrajectoryAtlas and edits the object's 3D relative trajectory, whereas MotionV2V constructs generic counterfactual motion pairs and uses 2D tracks for objects, camera, and time. Its explicit paired 3D formulation is a stronger comparator for object relocation; MotionV2V remains broader in edit type.

reviewed_competitors.title: CamDirector: Towards Long-Term Coherent Video Trajectory Editing
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Subsequent full-video trajectory editor specializing in camera motion and long-horizon consistency.
reviewed_competitors.difference: CamDirector uses world caching and history-aware autoregression to edit camera trajectories over long videos; MotionV2V handles object, camera, and temporal edits but trains and evaluates short 49-frame clips without a long-term benchmark. It is therefore a narrower but materially stronger comparator for the camera-control and duration claims.

reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest acknowledged spectral antecedent: it analyzes low-rank singular-vector channels through which attention heads communicate across layers.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Talking Heads focuses on inter-component communication through attention value/output geometry across two language models and includes causal interventions and weight edits; Beyond Components extends the affine SVD lens inside QK, OV, and both MLP projections with task masks. The extension in component coverage is real, but its causal validation is weaker and should be compared directly to the prior channel-level interventions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Towards Understanding the Nature of Attention with Low-Rank Sparse Decomposition
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Close pre-publication competitor decomposing attention into fine-grained low-rank sparse functional units rather than treating heads as atomic.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The low-rank sparse decomposition replaces multi-head self-attention with learned sparse low-rank units and evaluates larger Llama-3.1-8B circuits and reconstruction against SAE-style alternatives; Beyond Components uses the fixed SVD basis of frozen GPT-2 weights, folds in biases, and adds MLP maps. This is an important omitted direct comparator because it challenges the breadth and novelty of the general 'below components' framing while differing in learned versus intrinsic axes.

reviewed_competitors.title: Interpreting Attention Layer Outputs with Sparse Autoencoders
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct fine-grained attention-output interpretability competitor using learned sparse features instead of singular directions.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The SAE work decomposes attention outputs into sparse activation features, studies models up to 2B parameters, reports widespread head polysemanticity, and performs IOI causal analysis. Beyond Components obtains orthogonal directions directly from weights and spans QK plus MLPs without training a dictionary. The tradeoff is intrinsic/exact spectral axes versus empirically sparse nonlinear features with stronger feature-level validation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transcoders Find Interpretable LLM Feature Circuits
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct competitor for decomposing MLP computation into interpretable subcomponent feature circuits, including the Greater-Than task.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Transcoders learn a sparse nonlinear replacement whose features and feature-to-feature edges support circuit analysis; Beyond Components retains frozen weights and uses their orthogonal singular rank-one maps across both attention and MLPs. Transcoders offer a more expressive learned basis and circuit graph, while the SVD method is simpler and exact at the matrix level before masking.

reviewed_competitors.title: Singular Vectors of Attention Heads Align with Features
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Subsequent direct analysis of when attention-head singular vectors correspond to true model features.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The later work gives theoretical conditions and controlled ground-truth experiments for feature alignment in QK singular vectors, showing that alignment is conditional rather than automatic. Beyond Components supplies broader empirical QK/OV/MLP case studies but assumes singular axes are natural functional coordinates. This later result is the most precise primary-source test of that core assumption.

reviewed_competitors.title: Is This the Subspace You Are Looking for? An Interpretability Illusion for Subspace Activation Patching
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Methodological counterpoint on the causal validity of behavior-changing subspace interventions.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The illusion paper shows that subspace patching can produce the expected behavior through a dormant or unintended pathway and argues for additional causal-faithfulness checks. Beyond Components infers causal building blocks from final-residual SVD-vector injection, precisely the kind of sufficiency result that can outstrip mediation evidence. Equal-norm controls, source-site patching, and completeness tests are therefore decisive missing comparisons.

reviewed_competitors.title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 Small
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational IOI circuit source whose head categories and task structure are reused as ground truth for the paper's directional analysis.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The IOI work identifies a 26-head, seven-class circuit with causal faithfulness, completeness, and minimality analyses at component level. Beyond Components refines selected known heads into SVD axes but does not repeat those causal criteria direction by direction. Its novelty is resolution below the known circuit, not discovery of the underlying IOI algorithm or heads.

reviewed_competitors.title: How does GPT-2 compute greater-than? Interpreting mathematical abilities in a pre-trained language model
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational Greater-Than circuit source whose task, heads, and functional interpretation are reused for the SVD case study.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The prior paper identifies and causally analyzes the GPT-2 Small Greater-Than circuit; Beyond Components decomposes already implicated heads 6.9, 9.1, and 5.5 into rank-one QK score patterns. The later decomposition exposes finer geometry, but without direction ablations it does not supersede the prior mechanistic circuit evidence.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformers Provably Solve Parity Efficiently with Chain of Thought
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kim and Suzuki already prove efficient parity learning with chain-of-thought supervision: teacher forcing can produce a one-step effect, while non-teacher-forced learning needs augmented verification/filtering. The reviewed paper's genuine additions are an explicit process-reward policy-gradient analysis and gate examples beyond parity, but its headline unfiltered-SFT theorem inherits a proof-level zeroing operation analogous to a hidden stage schedule.

reviewed_competitors.title: Simplicity Bias in Transformers and their Ability to Learn Sparse Boolean Functions
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bhattamishra et al. empirically establish a Transformer simplicity bias toward sparse Boolean functions and analyze which functions are learnable. The reviewed work narrows to a supplied recursive circuit and derives stylized attention-gradient dynamics, adding process-versus-SFT timing but offering much thinner empirical coverage.

reviewed_competitors.title: Minimalist Softmax Attention Provably Learns Constrained Boolean Functions
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work proves learning guarantees for minimalist softmax attention on constrained Boolean functions, including AND/OR-style structure and supervision boundaries. The reviewed paper instead studies a recursive autoregressive trace with process reward on self-generated prefixes; its advantage depends on a known tree mask and exact local verifier rather than a broader Boolean attention class.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Compositional Functions with Transformers from Easy-to-Hard Data
reviewed_competitors.difference: The predecessor proves Transformer learnability of compositional functions through explicit easy-to-hard or mixture curricula with runtime/sample guarantees. The reviewed paper claims autoregressive SFT self-organizes stages and process reward learns all stages simultaneously; however, the SFT proof's manual residual zeroing and serial phase filtering behave like an implicit schedule and no finite-sample guarantee is given.

reviewed_competitors.title: Multi-head Transformers Provably Learn Symbolic Multi-step Reasoning via Gradient Descent
reviewed_competitors.difference: This paper analyzes multi-head Transformers learning symbolic path reasoning through gradient descent, with a richer architecture and an explicit multi-step reasoning target. The reviewed paper gives sharper process-reward versus SFT dynamics for Boolean trees, but only for one head, a hard structural mask, fixed components, and population sign gradients.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Emergence of Implicit Curriculum in RLVR Learning Dynamics
reviewed_competitors.difference: This later work proves that terminal-reward RLVR can bootstrap compositional reasoning across a fixed difficulty mixture when easy horizons create aligned gradients, and documents relay/grokking regimes. It qualifies any broad reading of the reviewed paper's final-reward pessimism: Proposition 3.2 is a random-target first-gradient bound, whereas outcome reward can work with structured data and shared parameters.

reviewed_competitors.title: Sub-Task Decomposition Enables Learning in Sequence to Sequence Tasks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wies et al. provide a general theoretical account of why intermediate subtask labels make decomposable sequence tasks learnable. The reviewed paper specializes this information advantage to exact Transformer attention gradients and contrasts local policy reward with self-generated-prefix SFT, but does not remove the predecessor's central dependence on correctly specified intermediate supervision.

reviewed_competitors.title: Why are Sensitive Functions Hard for Transformers?
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work analyzes why sensitive functions such as parity are hard for Transformers through sensitivity and loss-landscape limitations. The reviewed paper demonstrates that a supplied chain-of-thought decomposition plus dense local labels can bypass that barrier; it therefore changes supervision and architecture rather than refuting hardness for ordinary end-to-end learning.

reviewed_competitors.title: What needs to go right for an induction head? A mechanistic study of in-context learning circuits and their formation
reviewed_competitors.difference: Singh et al. causally manipulate activations and subcircuits during training to establish conditions for induction-head formation. The reviewed paper instead freezes whole layers and measures later behavioral thresholds; this tests continued plasticity but cannot attribute a stage to a head, activation, or stored circuit.

reviewed_competitors.title: How Transformers Learn Causal Structure with Gradient Descent
reviewed_competitors.difference: This paper gives theory for gradient descent causing attention to encode latent causal structure in a controlled in-context setting. The reviewed work supplies empirical learning curves for an Alchemy graph and bidirectional composition/decomposition tasks, but proves neither recovery of the latent transition structure nor a parameter-level mechanism.

reviewed_competitors.title: Out-of-distribution generalization via composition: a lens through induction heads in Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work connects compositional OOD generalization to induction heads and a common bridge subspace across synthetic and pretrained Transformers. The reviewed paper isolates stage timing on a tiny latent cube and contrasts composition with decomposition, but offers neither comparable model breadth nor a mechanistic subspace/head account.

reviewed_competitors.title: Uncovering Graph Reasoning in Decoder-only Transformers with Circuit Tracing
reviewed_competitors.difference: This current graph-reasoning study traces decoder-only Transformer circuits, identifying mechanisms such as structural memorization and token merging. The reviewed paper's Alchemy trajectories expose interpretable behavioral ordering, but output curves and whole-layer freezing do not rule out shortcut circuits or reveal how graph relations are represented.

reviewed_competitors.title: The mechanistic basis of data dependence and abrupt learning in an in-context classification task
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work develops a mechanistic account of abrupt in-context learning and its dependence on training data in a controlled classification task. The reviewed paper adds explicit latent graph semantics and composition/decomposition interventions, but its nested stages remain descriptive and its data/hyperparameter dependence is not experimentally isolated.

reviewed_competitors.title: Evolution Strategies at Scale: LLM Fine-Tuning Beyond Reinforcement Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Qiu et al. establish that simple dense full-parameter ES can adapt billion-scale LLMs with populations near 30. EGGROLL targets its matrix-noise and population-throughput bottlenecks with low-rank factors and much larger parallel populations.

reviewed_competitors.title: Fine-Tuning Language Models with Just Forward Passes
reviewed_competitors.difference: MeZO uses two forward evaluations to estimate a supervised-loss gradient with minimal memory. EGGROLL instead uses many low-rank candidates, arbitrary scalar/group objectives, and population batching; its largest gains trade many more queries for throughput.

reviewed_competitors.title: Low-Rank Curvature for Zeroth-Order Optimization in LLM Fine-Tuning
reviewed_competitors.difference: LOREN exploits estimated low-rank curvature to concentrate queries in informative directions. EGGROLL factorizes random perturbation matrices primarily for memory and batching, without explicitly learning curvature.

reviewed_competitors.title: LLM Zeroth-Order Fine-Tuning is an Inference Workload
reviewed_competitors.difference: This later systems work explicitly characterizes zeroth-order LLM fine-tuning through inference kernels and end-to-end workload behavior. It is the closest primary comparator for testing how much of EGGROLL's linear-layer microbenchmark advantage survives the whole pipeline.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Thickets: Diverse Task Experts Are Dense Around Pretrained Weights
reviewed_competitors.difference: Neural Thickets studies the density and diversity of nearby useful experts, probing why random parameter search can find signal. EGGROLL focuses on factorized evaluation and asymptotic update approximations rather than empirical local-solution geometry.

reviewed_competitors.title: Matching Accuracy, Different Geometry: Evolution Strategies vs GRPO in LLM Post-Training
reviewed_competitors.difference: The geometry study compares ES and GRPO updates at similar accuracy, exposing off-target differences hidden by endpoint metrics. EGGROLL emphasizes target throughput and would need the same retention and update-spectrum controls to validate behavioral equivalence.

reviewed_competitors.title: Evolutionary Strategies lead to Catastrophic Forgetting in LLMs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Abdi et al. measure substantial retention loss and dense, large-norm ES updates under comparable task compute. EGGROLL does not test whether low-rank member perturbations and high-rank aggregate updates reproduce or mitigate that failure.

reviewed_competitors.title: Hyper-ES: Effective Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning via Descent Direction Merging
reviewed_competitors.difference: Hyper-ES structures how evolutionary descent directions are merged to improve reasoning adaptation. EGGROLL's distinctive contribution is low-rank batched evaluation; combining the two would test systems versus estimator gains.

reviewed_competitors.title: Evolution Strategies as a Scalable Alternative to Reinforcement Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: OpenAI ES establishes massively parallel dense perturbation search for RL policies and supplies the full-rank OpenES baseline. EGGROLL changes the perturbation geometry and kernel to remain practical as matrix dimensions and populations grow.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Razzhigaev et al. track anisotropy and ID over layers and training, finding decoder bell-shaped anisotropy and expansion-then-compression dynamics. This paper holds pretrained encoders mostly fixed and asks which text properties change per-document ID, finding only weak isotropy coupling.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Intrinsic Dimension of Prompts in Internal Representations of Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Viswanathan et al. relate token-cloud ID, neighborhood overlap, and cosine to next-token loss and shuffled-text controls, reporting higher loss with higher-dimensional representations. This paper challenges any necessary ID-entropy dependence with counterexamples and shows their pooled correlation largely fades after length control, then pivots to genre and lexical determinants.

reviewed_competitors.title: Geometric Signatures of Compositionality Across a Language Model's Lifetime
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lee et al. manipulate dataset compositionality and follow nonlinear versus linear dimensionality across training, attributing nonlinear ID to learned semantic composition. reviewed_competitors.title: Less is More: Local Intrinsic Dimensions of Contextual Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ruppik et al. use mean local dimension shifts during training/fine-tuning to anticipate saturation, overfitting, grokking, and later performance gains. This paper analyzes text-level PHD across genre and style and does not prospectively validate an optimization transition predictor.

reviewed_competitors.title: Characterizing Truthfulness in Large Language Model Generations with Local Intrinsic Dimension
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yin et al. use local activation ID to predict truthfulness on four QA datasets against entropy/uncertainty alternatives. reviewed_competitors.title: Intrinsic Dimension Estimation for Robust Detection of AI-Generated Texts
reviewed_competitors.difference: Tulchinskii et al. propose text-manifold ID as a cross-domain human-text invariant and report AI text about 1.5 dimensions lower. The present paper finds strong domain/style stratification, newer-model detection erosion, and malformed-output extremes, substantially narrowing the earlier invariant interpretation while adding linguistic and SAE analyses.

reviewed_competitors.title: Redundancy, Isotropy, and Intrinsic Dimensionality of Prompt-based Text Embeddings

reviewed_competitors.title: Tackling the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus with Vision Transformers: the Importance of 2D Representation, Positions, and Objects
reviewed_competitors.difference: ViTARC v2 adds pixel-level, spatial, and object-aware representations and fits task-specific models with abundant generated examples, but does not solve unseen tasks under ARC's few-shot cross-task protocol. VARC's narrower but meaningful advance is to combine a canvas-based vision representation with shared offline training and per-unseen-task adaptation; this predecessor prevents claiming that ARC had not previously been studied with ViTs.

reviewed_competitors.title: Hierarchical Reasoning Model
reviewed_competitors.difference: HRM v3 uses coupled recurrent modules operating at different timescales and reports 40.3/5.0 on ARC-1/ARC-2 in VARC's table. VARC instead adapts a visual encoder and votes over augmented views, reporting 54.5/8.3, but the papers do not share a matched data, update, or inference-compute protocol.

reviewed_competitors.title: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: TRM v1 simplifies recurrent reasoning to a two-layer 7M-parameter network and reports 44.6/7.8 in VARC's ARC-1/ARC-2 table. The 18M VARC reaches 54.5/8.3 through visual priors, synthetic offline data, 100-epoch adaptation, and 510-view voting; the ARC-2 separation is only 0.5 points and no matched replication is given.

reviewed_competitors.title: Searching Latent Program Spaces
reviewed_competitors.difference: LPN v3 learns a latent space of implicit programs and optimizes a compact latent code at test time, bridging program search and neural prediction. VARC instead updates a vision model/task token from pixel pairs and has no explicit latent-program variable; comparing the two would distinguish visual representation gains from the choice of adaptation space.

reviewed_competitors.title: Combining Induction and Transduction for Abstract Reasoning
reviewed_competitors.difference: This v4 system trains both a program-induction model and a direct transduction model on synthetic variants of Python solutions, finding complementary strengths and ensembling them. VARC is purely transductive at the output level and encodes spatial rather than executable-program bias, so its novelty is not the first trainable cross-task ARC learner but a vision-native alternative.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Test-Time Training for Few-Shot Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: This v2 work fine-tunes an 8B language model on ARC demonstrations and reports 53.0 percent public-validation accuracy, or 61.9 percent when ensembled with program synthesis. VARC reuses the same broad parameter-update principle with an 18M vision model trained from scratch on ARC-derived data, then adds scale/translation views; the mechanism of test-time learning itself is prior work.

reviewed_competitors.title: Product of Experts with LLMs: Boosting Performance on ARC Is a Matter of Perspective
reviewed_competitors.difference: The v2 Product-of-Experts system uses task augmentations, depth-first candidate search, and an LLM as both generator and scorer, reporting 71.6 percent on the public ARC-AGI evaluation set. VARC is much smaller and avoids language pretraining but reports 60.4 with an eight-adaptation ensemble; the competitor shows that augmentation plus explicit candidate scoring can outperform majority voting at different resource assumptions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Programming with a Differentiable Forth Interpreter
reviewed_competitors.difference: Differentiable Forth v3 lets programmers supply procedural sketches whose missing local actions are trained end to end and evaluates sorting, addition, and question answering. Cajal is far less expressive empirically but contributes a typed linear compilation construction and ground behavior-preservation proof rather than an interpreter-level relaxation alone.

reviewed_competitors.title: Differentiable Programs with Neural Libraries
reviewed_competitors.difference: TerpreT v2 combines differentiable programs with learned neural library functions and studies modular transfer and lifelong learning. Cajal's distinctive contribution is exact compilation of a linear higher-order Boolean core into real matrices with explicit preservation lemmas; it does not match TerpreT's task breadth or library-learning evaluation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scallop: A Language for Neurosymbolic Programming
reviewed_competitors.difference: Scallop v1 provides Datalog-style recursion, aggregation, negation, relational data, provenance-semiring differentiation, and eight application evaluations. Cajal has a much smaller linear lambda calculus and MNIST case study, but aims at a compiler-correctness account for exact real linear neurons and higher-order hypernetworks that Scallop does not claim.

reviewed_competitors.title: TensorLog: A Differentiable Deductive Database
reviewed_competitors.difference: TensorLog v2 compiles logical clauses to factor graphs and unrolls belief-propagation queries into differentiable functions, with compilation and inference complexity claims. Cajal compiles higher-order linear functional programs directly to neuron matrices and focuses on exact Boolean behavior, but lacks TensorLog's recursion, database scale, and explicit inference-complexity evaluation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Probabilistic Logic Programming in DeepProbLog
reviewed_competitors.difference: DeepProbLog v2 integrates neural predicates with expressive probabilistic logic, symbolic inference, program induction, and end-to-end learning. Cajal instead provides a deterministic linear type discipline and matrix compiler with a narrow preservation theorem; its exact compilation is cleaner formally but far less expressive and not probabilistic.

reviewed_competitors.title: Logic Tensor Networks: Deep Learning and Logical Reasoning from Data and Knowledge
reviewed_competitors.difference: Logic Tensor Networks v2 gives first-order Real Logic continuous truth semantics implemented with tensor neural networks. Cajal also targets real-valued neural computation but derives matrices from linear functional programs and preserves discrete basis behavior; it does not offer LTN's first-order knowledge representation or soft-constraint learning.

reviewed_competitors.title: Thinking Like Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: RASP v2 offers a language for programming Transformer computations and derives attention/head-depth requirements for histogram, sorting, and Dyck tasks, after which a Transformer can mimic the program. Cajal targets exact linear neurons and differentiable linking to learned modules, with a formal ground preservation theorem but no comparable algorithmic task breadth or Transformer compilation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Thermodynamically consistent physics-informed neural networks for hyperbolic systems
reviewed_competitors.difference: Patel et al. build entropy and total-variation biases on a least-squares space-time control-volume discretization for hyperbolic shocks and inverse equations of state. IRR-PINN instead keeps strong-form residuals and penalizes a chosen local derivative sign across transport and phase-field systems.

reviewed_competitors.title: Energy Dissipation Preserving Physics Informed Neural Network for Allen-Cahn Equations
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kütük and Yücel penalize violation of an Allen-Cahn energy-dissipation property and test multiple mobilities, energy functionals, initial conditions, dimensions, and advection. IRR-PINN uses local phase monotonicity and covers more physical domains, but does not compare against the energy penalty on its melting benchmark.

reviewed_competitors.title: Phase-Field Modeling of Fracture with Physics-Informed Deep Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Manav et al. use Deep Ritz energy minimization for crack nucleation, propagation, kinking, branching, and coalescence and test multiple initializations. IRR-PINN's narrower novelty is a strong-form space-time PINN with pointwise KKT and non-healing penalties on one notched-tension benchmark.

reviewed_competitors.title: Sharp-PINNs: staggered hard-constrained physics-informed neural networks for phase field modelling of corrosion
reviewed_competitors.relationship: direct same-author corrosion predecessor and baseline component
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sharp-PINNs introduce staggered Allen-Cahn/Cahn-Hilliard training, Fourier features, a modified MLP, and hard output constraints. The reviewed corrosion baseline reuses the first three documented components and adds temporal monotonicity; it does not separately compare the new penalty with Sharp-PINN's hard-constraint contribution.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Physical Models that Can Respect Conservation Laws
reviewed_competitors.difference: ProbConserv combines an integral conservation law with a Bayesian update, provides uncertainty, and targets volume conservation and shocks in generalized porous-medium equations. IRR-PINN is simpler inside a PINN but enforces only chosen one-way derivatives and supplies neither conservation guarantees nor uncertainty quantification.

reviewed_competitors.title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wang et al. introduce diverse chain sampling and majority aggregation and report accuracy gains at fixed sample counts. The reviewed paper analyzes mode-estimation scaling and reallocates a dataset-level budget rather than changing the sampled reasoning prompt or vote rule.

reviewed_competitors.title: Let's Sample Step by Step: Adaptive-Consistency for Efficient Reasoning and Coding with LLMs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Adaptive-Consistency stops each question from a beta-posterior confidence threshold and reports up to 7.9x budget reduction across 17 datasets. Blend-ASC converts ASC confidence to a global fixed-budget ranking and gradually mixes it with PPR, avoiding a user threshold but adding a schedule and cap.

reviewed_competitors.title: Escape Sky-high Cost: Early-stopping Self-Consistency for Multi-step Reasoning
reviewed_competitors.difference: ESC stops when a recent response window is unanimous and reports 33.8%-84.2% sampling reductions with comparable task accuracy on six benchmarks. Blend-ASC instead preserves empirical-mode voting and allocates a shared exact budget, but evaluates primarily cached mode error rather than the broader task-accuracy suite.

reviewed_competitors.title: Make Every Penny Count: Difficulty-Adaptive Self-Consistency for Cost-Efficient Reasoning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Difficulty-Adaptive SC uses batch-query difficulty before sampling and posterior evidence afterward, and reports lower cost than ASC and ESC at comparable accuracy. The reviewed paper cites it but substitutes an oracle-smoothed fixed allocator in the main comparison, so Blend-ASC's state-of-the-art claim lacks a direct DSC run.

reviewed_competitors.title: Confidence Improves Self-Consistency in LLMs
reviewed_competitors.difference: CISC uses model-provided within-question confidence to weight reasoning paths and reports over 40% fewer paths on average across nine models and four datasets. Blend-ASC leaves plurality voting unchanged and reallocates calls across questions, so the methods are complementary and were not combined or compared directly.

reviewed_competitors.title: Sample Complexity and Representation Ability of Test-time Scaling Paradigms
reviewed_competitors.difference: Huang et al. derive Theta(1/Delta^2) self-consistency sample complexity and a separation from best-of-n's Theta(1/Delta), with theory spanning other test-time paradigms. The reviewed paper claims a tighter square-root-margin bound and uniquely develops dataset-level fixed and dynamic allocation, but its Blend scheduler itself remains unproved.

reviewed_competitors.title: Gradient Descent on Neural Networks Typically Occurs at the Edge of Stability
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct empirical predecessor establishing progressive sharpening and full-batch GD operation just above eta*lambda_max=2.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It documents EoS across neural networks without the RPE/HOCM mechanism; the reviewed paper adds eigenvector-rotation measurements but does not supersede the predecessor's broader empirical characterization.

reviewed_competitors.title: The large learning rate phase of deep learning: the catapult mechanism
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Early direct account of a stable large-learning-rate phase, loss catapults, convergence to flatter minima, and improved performance.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It uses solvable wide-network dynamics and catapult transitions rather than Hessian-eigenvector polarity or a stochastic HOCM process, so flatness and generalization beyond the classical threshold predate the reviewed paper.

reviewed_competitors.title: Self-Stabilization: The Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent at the Edge of Stability
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest formal alternative mechanism for curvature reduction and implicit bias at EoS.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It derives cubic self-stabilization and approximate projected GD under a sharpness constraint with quantitative trajectory predictions. The reviewed paper proposes RPE plus an assumed random walk, whose general flatness theorem is not valid as written.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding Gradient Descent on Edge of Stability in Deep Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Prior theorem showing deterministic EoS dynamics can induce flow along a minima manifold toward lower top Hessian eigenvalue.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It proves a sharpness-minimizing flow for normalized GD and a transformed constant-rate loss under regularity conditions, whereas the reviewed paper targets ordinary GD through product-network RPE and an abstract curvature process.

reviewed_competitors.title: Catapults in SGD: spikes in the training loss and their impact on generalization through feature learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct SGD competitor connecting instability-like catapults, minibatch size, feature learning, and test performance.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It locates catapults in top tangent-kernel eigenspaces and measures alignment with the true predictor's AGOP. That feature-learning explanation is an untested confound for the reviewed paper's claim that HOCM flattening dominates minibatch noise.

reviewed_competitors.title: Large Learning Rate Tames Homogeneity: Convergence and Balancing Effect
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Prior rigorous large-rate implicit-bias result in homogeneous matrix factorization, structurally close to the reviewed paper's product-network analysis.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It proves convergence beyond 2/L and balancing of factor magnitudes. The reviewed paper instead claims leading-eigenvector rotation and flatness, but does not control balancing as an alternative source of its product-coordinate effects.

reviewed_competitors.title: The instabilities of large learning rate training: a loss landscape view
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Same-author direct predecessor reporting instability-associated landscape flattening and landscape shift.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It already contains the central empirical observation that large-rate instabilities flatten/shift the landscape. The reviewed paper's incremental claim is the RPE label, product-network calculation, and HOCM stochastic formalization; arXiv also flags text overlap between this predecessor and arXiv:2305.18490.

reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest prior formalization of hallucination inevitability through computable LLMs, computable ground truths, and learning-theoretic limits.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It predates and substantially overlaps the reviewed paper's first theoretical branch, while also adding task characterization and empirical validation. The reviewed paper broadens the taxonomy but its new diagonalization Theorems 1-2 are invalid as written.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Fundamental Impossibility of Hallucination Control in Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current direct impossibility competitor analyzing trade-offs among truthfulness, information conservation, knowledge revelation, optimality, and externally authorized support.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It uses a mechanism-design/semantic-support framework and explicitly separates truth from support, rather than a five-domain survey. Its current v8 postdates the reviewed paper's v1 and offers a different formal target for what hallucination control can certify.

reviewed_competitors.title: Limits for Learning with Language Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Prior theoretical limits result for semantic entailment, consistency, universal quantification, and the Borel hierarchy.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It proves a focused learnability boundary for formal semantic properties. The reviewed paper cites it but replaces domain-specific formalism with much broader propositions that often lack valid premises or proofs.

reviewed_competitors.title: Why Does the Effective Context Length of LLMs Fall Short?
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct mechanistic and empirical competitor for relative-position undertraining and effective context shorter than nominal training context.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It measures the left-skewed relative-position distribution, proposes inference-time STRING remapping, and reports more than ten-point gains on RULER and InfiniteBench for Llama 3.1 70B and Qwen2 72B. The reviewed paper offers a flawed position-gradient lemma and no experiment.

reviewed_competitors.title: Faith and Fate: Limits of Transformers on Compositionality
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct predecessor on reasoning/compositionality limits with controlled tasks, computation-graph analysis, and theoretical error accumulation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It evaluates multi-digit multiplication, logic-grid puzzles, and dynamic programming and analyzes linearized subgraph matching. The reviewed paper surveys reasoning degradation and proposes causal formulas but supplies no model-level evidence.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Illusion of Thinking: Understanding the Strengths and Limitations of Reasoning Models via the Lens of Problem Complexity
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current empirical scaling-limit competitor for large reasoning models under controllable problem complexity.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It identifies three complexity regimes and accuracy/reasoning-effort collapse using controllable puzzles and trace analysis. The reviewed paper claims general reasoning ceilings without comparable experiments or a valid causal identification theorem.

reviewed_competitors.title: LLLMs: A Data-Driven Survey of Evolving Research on Limitations of Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest broad survey competitor covering reasoning, generalization, hallucination, security, alignment, knowledge editing, and multimodality.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It derives a bottom-up taxonomy from 14,648 relevant papers selected from 250,000 ACL/arXiv records, validates its classification methodology, and releases annotations. The reviewed paper's taxonomy is more theory-styled but neither systematic-search methodology nor proposition validity supports its 'first unified rigorous framework' claim.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Survey on Hallucination in Large Language Models: Principles, Taxonomy, Challenges, and Open Questions
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Established hallucination taxonomy and mitigation survey spanning retrieval-augmented systems and large vision-language models.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It focuses on principles, causes, detection benchmarks, mitigation, retrieval limitations, and multimodal hallucination rather than presenting new impossibility propositions. It predates much of the reviewed paper's cross-branch taxonomy and is a more appropriate source for descriptive claims than unsupported new equations.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scaling Laws and Interpretability of Learning from Repeated Data
reviewed_competitors.difference: Hernandez et al. show that repeating even 0.1% of data can create double-descent degradation and damage induction heads, plausibly through memorization consuming capacity. The reviewed study repeats entire subsets but reports neither memorization nor mechanistic diagnostics, leaving this known competing mechanism unaudited.

reviewed_competitors.title: Improved Scaling Laws in Linear Regression via Data Reuse
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lin et al. derive sharp multi-pass SGD risk under power-law covariance and source spectra, showing improved iteration scaling over one pass for L up to an N-dependent limit. The reviewed paper adds the explicit fresh-data-equivalent E(K,N), o(1)-relative strong-convex formulas, and additional spectra, but priority for theoretical data-reuse scaling is shared.

reviewed_competitors.title: Repetita Iuvant: Data Repetition Allows SGD to Learn High-Dimensional Multi-Index Functions
reviewed_competitors.difference: Arnaboldi et al. prove that just two passes can unlock relevant-direction learning in nonlinear two-layer networks and overcome information/leap-exponent limits. This is a qualitatively different benefit of reuse—feature discovery—that a fixed-feature excess-risk equivalence cannot capture.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Benefits of Reusing Batches for Gradient Descent in Two-Layer Networks: Breaking the Curse of Information and Leap Exponents
reviewed_competitors.difference: Dandi et al. use dynamical mean-field theory to show batch reuse changes which multi-index functions a two-layer network can learn, sometimes in two steps. The reviewed paper quantifies risk-equivalent sample size but cannot represent newly accessible functions, underscoring its theory-to-neural extrapolation gap.

reviewed_competitors.title: Emergent properties with repeated examples
reviewed_competitors.difference: Charton and Kempe show repeated small sets can outperform larger single-use sets at fixed training steps on algorithmic math and that mixing a repeated core with fresh samples can help. Their compute-matched finding and selective two-set design go beyond whole-corpus loss equivalence in the reviewed paper.

reviewed_competitors.title: Deduplicating Training Data Makes Language Models Better

reviewed_competitors.title: Sparse Feature Circuits: Discovering and Editing Interpretable Causal Graphs in Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sparse Feature Circuits builds causal graphs from human-interpretable SAE features in an already-trained dense language model and scales to automatically discovered behaviors. The reviewed paper changes training itself so low-level weights and granular nodes are sparse, yielding far smaller hand-inspected circuits on curated tasks, but it requires de novo inefficient models and offers no matched-task head-to-head with the SAE pipeline.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transcoders Find Interpretable LLM Feature Circuits
reviewed_competitors.difference: Transcoders replace dense MLP computations with sparse input-output feature maps and report circuit analysis up to 1.4B-parameter language models, including a previously unknown greater-than mechanism. The reviewed method sparsifies the original Transformer end to end and exposes attention and residual connections at a lower level, but only in small code models; its bridges are a preliminary analogue to post-hoc dense-model access.

reviewed_competitors.title: Finding Transformer Circuits with Edge Pruning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Edge Pruning optimizes masks on edges of existing dense Transformers, recovers ground-truth Tracr circuits, and scales behavioral localization to CodeLlama-13B with over 99.96% sparsity. The reviewed paper prunes finer node types inside a deliberately weight-sparse model and obtains more human-readable selected examples, but its own limitations say edge pruning would be preferable and it supplies no controlled comparison at CodeLlama scale.

reviewed_competitors.title: Towards Automated Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability
reviewed_competitors.difference: ACDC iteratively selects coarse graph edges in pretrained dense models and validates recovery of known GPT-2 circuits, including 68 of 32,000 edges for greater-than. The reviewed paper uses learned masks at neuron, residual-channel, and attention-channel granularity after sparse training, producing smaller qualitative programs but relying on a redesigned model, 256 pruning trials per model-task pair, and manual cleanup.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scaling and evaluating sparse autoencoders
reviewed_competitors.difference: Scaling Sparse Autoencoders trains k-sparse dictionaries as large as 16 million latents on GPT-4 activations for 40 billion tokens and introduces feature-quality and downstream-sparsity metrics. The reviewed paper uses a related top-k instinct at the level of model weights and original activations, giving direct computation graphs rather than an auxiliary reconstruction basis, but it cannot approach the dense model's scale or efficiency and does not compare those feature-quality metrics.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Geshkovski et al. introduced the interacting-particle self-attention dynamics and proved spectrum-dependent clustering and low-rank limiting behavior. reviewed_competitors.difference: Rodríguez Abella et al. give control-theoretic consensus results for continuous and discrete attention, including autoregressive/time-varying settings and GPT experiments. Their consensus conclusions contrast with this paper's multistability because assumptions and attention structure differ; they also provide substantially stronger contact with practical models.

reviewed_competitors.title: Clustering in Causal Attention Masking
reviewed_competitors.difference: Karagodin et al. analyze the practically important causal mask and prove single-cluster convergence for arbitrary key-query matrices with identity V, plus metastability connections. The reviewed paper instead permits general symmetric V but omits causal masking and provides only informal numerical treatment of metastable transients.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Role of Attention Masks and LayerNorm in Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wu et al. already show that LayerNorm attention dynamics can possess equilibria of every rank and provide noncollapse counterexamples for suitable value matrices. That result narrows the reviewed paper's novelty claim about rich equilibrium landscapes and treats masks/LayerNorm more explicitly, although it does not give the same Oja or bipartite-eigenvector story.

reviewed_competitors.title: Recurrent Self-Attention Dynamics: An Energy-Agnostic Perspective from Jacobians
reviewed_competitors.difference: Tomihari and Karakida use Jacobians and Lyapunov exponents without requiring a global energy, relax symmetry and single-head restrictions, and connect criticality to looped-Transformer performance. The reviewed paper gives more explicit fixed-point algebra for symmetric single-head V but lacks comparable architectural breadth and empirical validation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Normalization in Attention Dynamics
reviewed_competitors.difference: Karagodin et al. formulate Post-LN, Pre-LN, Mix-LN, Peri-LN, and nGPT as speed-regulated particle systems and prove normalization-dependent clustering behavior. The reviewed paper fixes one exact sphere projection, so its multistability cannot be transferred across normalization schemes without this missing analysis.

reviewed_competitors.title: Spectral Selection in Symmetric Self-Attention Dynamics
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kuehn and Yoon impose QᵀK=V=Vᵀ to obtain a genuine gradient flow and rigorous finite-particle global selection between dominant positive alignment and most-negative sign polarization. It postdates this paper but supplies a more defensible spectral-selection theorem in a narrower symmetry regime.

reviewed_competitors.title: Gradient Flow Structure and Quantitative Dynamics of Multi-Head Self-Attention
reviewed_competitors.difference: Pendharkar extends spherical attention dynamics to multiple heads, identifies radial-shadow obstructions, gives conditional energy monotonicity, and derives temperature-dependent clustering rates. This directly addresses a multi-head extension that the reviewed paper labels trivial at consensus but leaves unanalyzed elsewhere.

reviewed_competitors.title: Clustered Attractor Manifolds and Dynamical Condensation in Self-Attention
reviewed_competitors.difference: Gao et al. analyze high-dimensional clustered fixed-point manifolds, their stability, and a finite sharpness threshold for attention condensation. This newer thermodynamic treatment turns the reviewed paper's informal catch-all cluster class into quantitative attractor and transition claims in a different large-dimension regime.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Scholl et al. already formulate symbolic differential-equation recovery as a uniqueness problem, derive necessary and sufficient criteria for several ODE/PDE classes, and build numerical uniqueness tests.
