reviewed_competitors.difference: Casolo et al. characterize positive-probability non-identifiability for practically sparse linear ODEs from one trajectory and show that modern estimators do not remove it. The reviewed work moves to continuous and analytic infinite-dimensional classes and dynamical coverage; its broader impossibility is not a quantitative replacement for the sparse finite-dimensional result.

reviewed_competitors.title: Extracting Sparse High-Dimensional Dynamics from Limited Data

reviewed_competitors.difference: Cartridges trains a compact corpus-specific KV representation offline with synthetic self-study and reports serving memory/throughput; Hope updates recurrent nested memories and targets online continual adaptation. The target paper acknowledges but omits Cartridges from one figure.

reviewed_competitors.title: Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Primary predecessor equating linear attention with fast-weight associative memory and introducing delta-rule corrections and learned learning rates.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It already supplies the memory-programming and delta-update foundation; Nested Learning generalizes the vocabulary to optimizers/nested levels and uses deep self-modifying memories plus CMS.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Modern Self-Referential Weight Matrix That Learns to Modify Itself
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest prior primary architecture for a scalable weight matrix that modifies itself during runtime.
reviewed_competitors.difference: SRWM uses self-referential outer-product/delta programming and demonstrates few-shot/RL performance; Hope extends self-reference to deep projection/update memories and combines it with a multi-frequency CMS.

reviewed_competitors.title: In-context Continual Learning Assisted by an External Continual Learner
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Official continual-learning baseline used by the target, combining frozen-LLM ICL with a compact external class selector.
reviewed_competitors.difference: InCA avoids updating the LLM and scales prompts by class preselection; Hope continually changes internal memories and targets a broader sequence-model architecture, with different compute and forgetting risks.

reviewed_competitors.difference: This paper studies pullback Riemannian geometry induced by neural mappings and measures how trained networks magnify input regions near decision boundaries. reviewed_competitors.title: How to Guess a Gradient
reviewed_competitors.difference: Singhal et al. develop structured gradient guessing, including the W-tilde-T estimator that this paper directly extends. The audited paper's contribution is to orthogonalize/truncate that upstream projection and add Newton-Schulz and preconditioning variants.

reviewed_competitors.title: Gradients without Backpropagation
reviewed_competitors.difference: Baydin et al. formulate forward-gradient learning via JVPs with unbiased random directions. The audited paper accepts that estimator's variance problem and introduces architecture-informed low-rank projections that trade unbiasedness for alignment and lower variance.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scaling Forward Gradient With Local Losses
reviewed_competitors.difference: This ICLR 2023 paper scales forward gradients by decomposing credit assignment with local losses. The audited paper instead keeps a global directional derivative and reduces guessing-space variance with an upstream-Jacobian singular subspace.

reviewed_competitors.title: Can Forward Gradient Match Backpropagation?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Fournier et al. study when forward gradients can approach backpropagation and explore variance-reduction conditions at ICML 2023. The audited paper offers a specific Jacobian-SVD estimator but tests a much narrower toy regime and does not match backpropagation quality.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning by Directional Gradient Descent
reviewed_competitors.difference: This ICLR 2022 work studies optimization using directional derivatives and direction choices without standard backpropagation. The audited paper specializes direction design to neural upstream-Jacobian singular structure and forward-mode AD.

reviewed_competitors.title: Fine-Tuning Language Models with Just Forward Passes
reviewed_competitors.difference: MeZO demonstrates memory-efficient forward-only fine-tuning of large language models using zeroth-order perturbations. It operates at parameter-level loss evaluations rather than exact JVPs and addresses realistic LLM scale that the audited paper has not tested.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Forward-Forward Algorithm: Some Preliminary Investigations
reviewed_competitors.difference: Hinton's Forward-Forward algorithm replaces forward/backward passes with positive and negative local forward phases. The audited method preserves a global loss and automatic differentiation but estimates its gradient through forward-mode directions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Gradient Descent Happens in a Tiny Subspace
reviewed_competitors.difference: Gur-Ari et al. show that neural gradients concentrate in a small Hessian eigenspace. The audited paper invokes related low-dimensional structure but selects a subspace from an upstream Jacobian's right singular vectors, not Hessian eigenvectors.

reviewed_competitors.difference: METRA learns temporally grounded latent directions for broad state coverage but has no explicit period coordinate. PSD adds temporal length; the paper's failed naive sum and mutual-conditioning repair show that the two objectives are coupled rather than automatically orthogonal.

reviewed_competitors.title: Dynamics-Aware Unsupervised Discovery of Skills
reviewed_competitors.difference: DADS maximizes skill information in predictable state transitions and supports model-based planning. It seeks distinguishable dynamics without specifying a cycle length; PSD supplies direct timescale control but lacks DADS's explicit predictive-dynamics test.

reviewed_competitors.title: Diversity is All You Need: Learning Skills without a Reward Function
reviewed_competitors.difference: DIAYN maximizes mutual information between a latent skill and visited states, favoring distinguishability but not temporal organization. PSD targets phase/timescale explicitly, though its main experiments add velocity shaping absent from DIAYN's reward-free framing.

reviewed_competitors.title: Controllability-Aware Unsupervised Skill Discovery
reviewed_competitors.difference: CSD rewards transitions that remain difficult for the current repertoire and demonstrates manipulation as well as locomotion. PSD instead controls cycle length, but does not directly seek hard-to-control states or validate nonperiodic manipulation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Behavior Contrastive Learning for Unsupervised Skill Discovery
reviewed_competitors.difference: BeCL contrasts multiple trajectories to make same-skill behavior consistent and different skills diverse while improving coverage. That cross-rollout consistency is an independent axis missing from PSD's primarily within-replay circular constraints; BeCL has no explicit period dial.

reviewed_competitors.title: FLD: Fourier Latent Dynamics for Structured Motion Representation and Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: FLD explicitly parameterizes periodic and quasi-periodic motion in a Fourier latent space from motion trajectories and uses tracking/fallback control. PSD discovers skills online without a reference dataset, but its Fourier analysis is post hoc and its circular geometry handles a narrower periodic family.

reviewed_competitors.title: Divide, Discover, Deploy: Factorized Skill Learning with Symmetry and Style Priors
reviewed_competitors.difference: Divide, Discover, Deploy uses embodiment symmetry and style priors to factorize transferable locomotion repertoires. PSD factorizes temporal length from direction with less embodiment structure, but its transfer and real-robot evidence are substantially narrower.

reviewed_competitors.title: Unsupervised Skill Discovery as Exploration for Learning Agile Locomotion
reviewed_competitors.difference: Rho et al. use unsupervised skill discovery as a bi-level exploration mechanism for obstacle-rich agile locomotion and emphasize task learning. PSD emphasizes a controllable frequency repertoire, with less direct evidence that its discovery process improves flat-policy exploration or hardware agility.

reviewed_competitors.title: Efficient Skill Discovery via Regret-Aware Optimization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Regret-aware discovery expands skills toward currently improvable weak regions with a population of generators and reports efficiency/diversity gains. PSD adapts only the scalar period bounds using its own reward thresholds, which is simpler but more exposed to self-confirming mastery signals.

reviewed_competitors.title: Unsupervised Skill Discovery for Learning Shared Structures across Changing Environments
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lee and Seo explicitly discover skill structure shared across changing maze and locomotion environments. PSD tests period control largely within fixed dynamics and identifies persistent disturbances as a limitation, so cross-environment invariance remains unvalidated.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Feng et al. theoretically characterize imperfect verification in Gaussian-mixture linear classification and test it on transformer eigenvalue computation and LLM summarization. The reviewed paper generalizes correctness-only verification with a difficulty filter, but assumes a near-perfect oracle for its sharp optimum and provides no comparable language-model intervention.

reviewed_competitors.title: Model Collapse Demystified: The Case of Regression
reviewed_competitors.difference: Dohmatob et al. derive high-dimensional regression formulas and adaptive-regularization mitigation for recursive model collapse. reviewed_competitors.title: Strong Model Collapse

reviewed_competitors.title: The Curse of Recursion: Training on Generated Data Makes Models Forget

The reviewed paper focuses on linear label shift and average classification error, so it does not directly test preservation of rare modes—the central failure mode in the earlier work.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Stability of Iterative Retraining of Generative Models on their own Data
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bertrand et al. prove stability when the initial generator is accurate enough and each generation retains sufficient clean data, then validate normalizing flows and diffusion models. reviewed_competitors.difference: Makkeh et al. introduce PID-parameterized local infomorphic neurons and already demonstrate associative memory by maximizing local coherence, reporting roughly 0.35 capacity. The target's credible advance is the binary sign-test construction, soft binning, optimizer and target-scale redesign, systematic redundancy analysis, and capacity up to 1.59-1.70; its ablation shows those engineering changes, not the redundancy concept alone, drive much of the gain.

reviewed_competitors.relationship: direct high-capacity binary Hopfield learning competitor
reviewed_competitors.difference: Hillar et al. minimize a smooth convex energy-margin objective, prove that every storable pattern set can be found and that random capacity is at least one pattern per neuron, and empirically reach the 1.5-1.7 range. The target reports a slightly higher clean-capacity curve through neuron-local information goals, but gives up MPF's convex storage guarantee and does not compare optimization cost.

reviewed_competitors.title: New Insights on Learning Rules for Hopfield Networks: Memory and Objective Function Minimisation
reviewed_competitors.difference: Tolmachev and Manton derive multiple descent-type learning rules, including the Descent L2/pseudoinverse family, and compare capacity, basin stability, biases, and self-coupling. The target supplies a locally interpretable information decomposition and higher clean capacity in its reimplementation, while the prior has a broader learning-rule and self-coupling audit and the target's stability is only comparable.

reviewed_competitors.title: Dense Associative Memory for Pattern Recognition
reviewed_competitors.difference: Krotov and Hopfield raise storage through higher-order energy interactions and hidden-unit-like dense associative memory, with pattern-recognition experiments beyond random-bit recall. The target keeps the classical pairwise binary recurrent architecture and interpretable neuron-local goals, so its alpha=1.70 result is relevant within that narrower class but does not compete with dense memory's superlinear or exponential regimes.

reviewed_competitors.title: On a model of associative memory with huge storage capacity
reviewed_competitors.difference: Demircigil et al. analyze a nonlinear interaction model with rigorous huge-storage and retrieval guarantees. The target's local PID rule stays in the pairwise Hopfield setting and provides empirical finite-N gains plus a conditional redundancy identity, not a comparable asymptotic huge-capacity theorem.

reviewed_competitors.title: Hopfield Networks is All You Need
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ramsauer et al. develop continuous modern Hopfield updates equivalent to attention, prove exponential storage under separation conditions, and evaluate practical retrieval and learning applications. The target instead studies classical binary synchronous networks and asks which local information objective learns their recurrent weights; its analysis is more neuron-interpretable but far narrower in architecture and data scale.

reviewed_competitors.title: Concise Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Fatemi et al. already analyze PPO/GRPO verbosity as an optimization artifact and use a brief second RL phase on a small set of solvable problems to shorten reasoning while preserving accuracy. Frugal-Thinking's narrower distinction is a two-stage difficulty-skewed and domain-curriculum recipe with no explicit length objective, but it omits this direct predecessor and provides a weaker causal ablation of the data mechanism.

reviewed_competitors.title: Walk Before You Run! Concise LLM Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: ConciseR first develops reasoning with GRPO++ and then applies length-aware GRPO only when every rollout is correct. That directly handles the ability-efficiency sequence with an explicit conditional length signal; Frugal-Thinking instead claims the difficulty mix alone induces brevity, avoiding reward shaping but lacking ConciseR's explicit trigger and controlled length objective.

reviewed_competitors.title: ConciseRL: Conciseness-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Reasoning Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: ConciseRL uses an LLM judge to provide a hyperparameter-free semantic conciseness score, reports difficulty-adaptive length and large token reductions, and ablates judge, reward composition, and difficulty. Frugal-Thinking removes the judge and explicit concision reward, making training signals cheaper and verifiable, but it neither measures semantic redundancy nor supplies comparable component ablations.

reviewed_competitors.title: Stable Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Reasoning
reviewed_competitors.difference: GRPO-lambda monitors within-group correctness and switches off length penalties for low-correctness groups, reporting 47.3% shorter chains with a 1.48-point average accuracy gain. Frugal-Thinking obtains similar 4B compression through data selection and a fixed cap rather than an adaptive reward, but has no matched evidence that its implicit mechanism is more stable or general.

reviewed_competitors.title: Overthinking Reduction with Decoupled Rewards and Curriculum Data Scheduling
reviewed_competitors.difference: DECS combines curriculum batch scheduling with token-level rewards that distinguish redundant from exploratory tokens and reports over 50% token reduction across seven benchmarks. Its v1 predates Frugal-Thinking and already couples curriculum with efficiency; Frugal-Thinking's remaining distinction is achieving brevity with ordinary outcome reward only, at the cost of less direct control and no token-level redundancy diagnosis.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Formation of Representations proposes and tests alignment relations among representations, weights, and neuron gradients, with predictions for compactness, neural collapse, and noise–regularization balance. BBD instead derives depth-local energy currents after reparameterization; it neither predicts representation alignment nor evaluates the claimed information redistribution.

reviewed_competitors.title: Hamiltonian Mechanics of Feature Learning: Bottleneck Structure in Leaky ResNets

BBD offers a training-time mechanical current representation rather than correlation dynamics; its use of 'information flow' is qualitative and has no finite-size or empirical propagation test.

reviewed_competitors.difference: SWIM already samples all hidden weights and biases from supervised data pairs, proves universality and a shallow Barron-function rate, and evaluates OpenML, neural operators, and transfer learning without iterative hidden optimization. reviewed_competitors.difference: Homma and Ohkubo's prior work treats ridgelet-derived parameter distributions as importance sampling, proposes extensions, and finds weight magnitude more consequential than intercept choice on one- and high-dimensional examples. It is limited mainly to shallow integral representations; the new paper instead modifies deep SWIM scales, but offers no direct empirical comparison to its own ridgelet method.

reviewed_competitors.title: Random Feature Representation Boosting
reviewed_competitors.difference: RFRBoost builds deep residual random-feature networks by fitting functional-gradient representation updates, gives closed-form or constrained least-squares subproblems, and evaluates 91 tabular datasets against RFNN and trained ResNet baselines. Ordered SWIM is simpler and samples all hidden features directly, but has a much thinner baseline/task panel and no comparable optimization guarantee.

reviewed_competitors.title: Fast training of accurate physics-informed neural networks without gradient descent
reviewed_competitors.difference: The current Frozen-PINN revision combines random features with explicit space–time separation and evaluates eight challenging PDEs, reporting accuracy and training-efficiency gains over state-of-the-art PINNs. Ordered SWIM contributes a generic depth schedule for dense supervised networks but does not measure time, test scientific tasks, or supply the causal architectural structure used by Frozen-PINN.

reviewed_competitors.title: Rapid training of Hamiltonian graph networks using random features
reviewed_competitors.difference: The Hamiltonian-graph method replaces iterative optimization with random-feature construction while preserving permutation, rotation, and translation structure, compares 15 optimizers, and reports 150–600× training speedups plus size generalization. Ordered SWIM has no graph or physical inductive bias, runtime comparison, or zero-shot scaling test; its novelty lies only in hand-scheduled depth scales.

reviewed_competitors.title: Koopman-informed recurrent neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Koopman-informed RNNs construct recurrent models through random features and extended dynamic mode decomposition, then test chaotic forecasting, control, and real data with explicit training-time comparisons. Ordered SWIM remains feedforward and supervised-pair based; it cannot yet address temporal credit assignment and does not quantify training speed.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Spectral Bias of Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Rahaman et al. use Fourier analysis to establish an expressivity bias of deep ReLU networks toward low-frequency functions and study data-manifold and perturbation effects. Ordered SWIM borrows a coarse-to-fine intuition but uses sine activations and does not measure Fourier content, so its 'hierarchical features' evidence is not a direct validation or exploitation of that ReLU spectral-bias theory.

reviewed_competitors.title: Frequency Principle: Fourier Analysis Sheds Light on Deep Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: The F-Principle paper directly measures and models the tendency of gradient-trained networks to fit low frequencies before high ones across MNIST, CIFAR-10, and VGG16. The reviewed method instead imposes a low-to-high allocation across layer depth in a network whose hidden weights are not gradient-trained; temporal learning order and depth-wise representation order are distinct, and the paper itself acknowledges that distinction.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Malladi et al. derive SDE approximations and scaling rules for Adam and RMSprop in the conventional optimization phase and validate hyperparameter-transfer rules. reviewed_competitors.title: On the Implicit Bias of Adam
reviewed_competitors.difference: Cattaneo et al. use backward-error/modified-equation analysis of full-batch Adam and identify a gradient regularization term that can anti-regularize sharpness when beta_1<beta_2. The target explicitly studies stochastic label noise over a longer eta^-2 horizon and predicts positive coordinate-sharpness regularization, so noise model and timescale reconcile some but not all apparent tension.

reviewed_competitors.title: How Memory in Optimization Algorithms Implicitly Modifies the Loss
reviewed_competitors.difference: Cattaneo and Shigida derive modified losses for optimizers with memory and analyze methods including AdamW and Lion on shorter discrete-to-flow scales. The target instead follows projected stochastic motion on a minimizer manifold, retains a slowly evolving second-moment state, and excludes weight decay; the two frameworks answer complementary temporal questions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Label Noise SGD Provably Prefers Flat Global Minimizers
reviewed_competitors.difference: Damian, Ma, and Lee prove that constant-step SGD with label noise favors minima with lower Hessian trace under broad smooth-loss geometry. The target uses this tr(H) result as its central SGD control and claims Adam replaces it by coordinate-dependent tr(Diag(H)^(1/2)); the target's exact Adam proof has the boundary and block inconsistencies noted in this review.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Implicit Bias of Adam on Separable Data
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhang et al. characterize Adam's asymptotic bias toward an l-infinity max-margin solution for linearly separable classification. The target studies stochastic wandering among finite global minimizers with label noise and a Hessian-diagonal stationary measure, so it neither subsumes nor duplicates the separable-data trajectory result.

reviewed_competitors.title: Why Transformers Need Adam: A Hessian Perspective
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhang et al. empirically attribute Adam's transformer advantage to heterogeneous blockwise Hessian spectra and show SGD can improve with blockwise updates. The target derives a coordinate-diagonal sharpness bias near a minimizer manifold and tests only synthetic regression/factorization; real transformer Hessian heterogeneity is a competing structural explanation and a missing external-validity test.

reviewed_competitors.title: Thought Anchors: Which LLM Reasoning Steps Matter?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Thought Anchors already introduces sentence-level counterfactual resampling with 100 rollouts and combines it with attention-based and causal-link analyses. Thought Branches extends that black-box method with repeated semantic-removal resilience, counterfactual++, on-policy steering, and safety, hint, and resume case studies; sentence-level resampling itself is not new here.

reviewed_competitors.title: Forking Paths in Neural Text Generation
reviewed_competitors.difference: Forking Paths locates individual tokens where resampling creates divergent continuations across seven tasks and four domains, framing the result as uncertainty dynamics. Thought Branches operates at sentence and semantic-content level, conditions on categorized final decisions, and repeatedly removes regenerated ideas, but its broad claim that reasoning requires trajectory resampling has a clear token-level predecessor.

reviewed_competitors.title: Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lanham et al. test CoT faithfulness by interventions such as mistakes, paraphrases, truncation, and filler, establishing task- and model-dependent reliance on the trace. Thought Branches' closest incremental claim is that those artificial interventions can be off-policy and that prefix-conditioned resampling plus semantic filtering yields more coherent effects in its decision tasks.

reviewed_competitors.title: Are DeepSeek R1 And Other Reasoning Models More Faithful?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chua and Evans provide the professor-hinted MMLU setup and quantify whether reasoning models explicitly acknowledge causally effective cues. Thought Branches reuses that artificial-cue regime but asks where the cue's unmentioned influence accumulates by transplanting progressively longer hinted prefixes; it does not originate the hint-faithfulness finding.

reviewed_competitors.title: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning In The Wild Is Not Always Faithful
reviewed_competitors.difference: Arcuschin et al. document implicit post-hoc rationalization and illogical shortcuts on naturally worded prompts without injected bias, including reasoning-model evaluations. Thought Branches offers a causal resampling toolkit and bias case studies, but most of its faithfulness evidence uses selected artificial hints or resume-name variants rather than the natural-prompt breadth of this competitor.

reviewed_competitors.title: Causal Sufficiency and Necessity Improves Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yu et al. quantify causal sufficiency and necessity of reasoning steps under interventions, then add missing steps and prune redundant ones on math and commonsense benchmarks. Thought Branches instead estimates black-box continuation distributions and semantic resilience, providing richer trajectory descriptions but not the competitor's optimized efficiency or explicit sufficiency-necessity objective.

reviewed_competitors.title: Faithfulness as Information Flow: Evaluating and Training Faithful Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Jia et al. define task-agnostic sufficiency, completeness, and necessity diagnostics using entropy, masked KL, and gradients, and modify on-policy RL to route information through CoT. Thought Branches remains a behavior-only, post-hoc sampling analysis; as of this later work, its distinct contribution is semantic trajectory resampling rather than a general causal-faithfulness framework or training intervention.

reviewed_competitors.title: Counterfactual Simulation Training for Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness
reviewed_competitors.difference: Hase and Potts train CoTs to let a simulator predict outputs under counterfactual inputs and evaluate cue reliance, reward hacking, and sycophancy. Thought Branches uses counterfactual continuation sampling to interpret fixed models and provides resilience to regenerated text, but it neither improves trace faithfulness nor tests counterfactual simulatability as this later competitor does.

reviewed_competitors.title: Greedy Layerwise Learning Can Scale to ImageNet
reviewed_competitors.difference: Belilovsky et al. already show auxiliary-classifier greedy block training on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet with deep convolutional networks. Greedy-DIB adds a matrix-entropy compression term and traffic-sign case studies, but evaluates generic scale only through CIFAR-100 and therefore does not establish the paper's broad novelty claim that prior local methods are limited to MNIST or simple networks.

reviewed_competitors.title: Training Neural Networks with Local Error Signals
reviewed_competitors.difference: Nokland and Eidnes train deep networks through local auxiliary losses without global backpropagation and supply the Greedy LE baseline used in this paper. Greedy-DIB's incremental element is entropy regularization of each representation; the traffic result is only 0.05 accuracy and 0.67 mIoU above Greedy LE on CTSRD and 0.40 accuracy above it on GTSRB, without uncertainty.

reviewed_competitors.title: The HSIC Bottleneck: Deep Learning without Back-Propagation
reviewed_competitors.difference: The HSIC Bottleneck already supplies layer-local information-theoretic objectives without auxiliary classifiers or ordinary error backpropagation. Greedy-DIB replaces normalized HSIC with a deterministic-IB entropy-plus-CE surrogate and performs much better in the authors' implementation, but it reintroduces auxiliary heads, local CE, and local backpropagation and provides no compute-matched reproduction audit.

reviewed_competitors.title: Deep Deterministic Information Bottleneck with Matrix-based Entropy Functional
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yu et al. already combine deterministic information bottleneck with the matrix-based entropy functional in deep networks. The present paper's principal methodological change is to deploy that objective greedily per CNN block with temporary classifiers, rather than originate either DIB or the eigenvalue entropy estimator.

reviewed_competitors.title: End-to-End Training Induces Information Bottleneck through Layer-Role Differentiation: A Comparative Analysis with Layer-wise Training
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sakamoto and Sato directly compare end-to-end and layer-wise training through information bottleneck and layer-role differentiation, including saturation of usable label information. Greedy-DIB adds cross-MI/MDS visualizations and turns its descriptive observations into a local entropy objective, but does not rigorously identify that the observations require or validate that objective.

reviewed_competitors.title: Deep Layer-wise Networks Have Closed-Form Weights
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wu et al. provide the NIK baseline and a layer-wise system with closed-form kernel-alignment weights, avoiding iterative backpropagation for the local objective. Greedy-DIB is substantially more accurate in the paper's reported CNN tables but requires SGD, cross-entropy, auxiliary heads, and Gram eigendecompositions; the tradeoff is not evaluated in time or memory.

reviewed_competitors.title: Towards Interpretable Deep Local Learning with Successive Gradient Reconciliation
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yang et al. reconcile successive local gradients, report competitive CNN and Transformer performance including ImageNet, and measure more than 40% training-memory savings. This is a closer current test of Greedy-DIB's accuracy-and-efficiency claims than the older baselines, yet Greedy-DIB neither compares against it nor measures the resource outcome at the center of its motivation.

reviewed_competitors.title: NoProp: Training Neural Networks without Back-propagation or Forward-propagation
reviewed_competitors.difference: NoProp is a current official-proceedings competitor that explicitly avoids both back-propagation and forward-propagation in its training formulation. It sharpens the terminology problem in Greedy-DIB: Greedy-DIB still performs local forward computation, CE optimization, and backpropagation, so its defensible claim is gradient isolation rather than training without backpropagation.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Wang et al. study comparison and composition over parametric knowledge, show implicit reasoning emerging through extended grokking, and trace a generalizing circuit. Kinetics adds explicit-trace versus direct supervision, log-step curve fits, trace-agreement dynamics, sorting and intersection, but reuses the same known-atomic-fact compositional regime.

reviewed_competitors.title: Chain of Thought Empowers Transformers to Solve Inherently Serial Problems
reviewed_competitors.difference: Li et al. prove complexity-theoretic gains from intermediate decoding and test serial problems such as permutation composition. Kinetics empirically tracks when a fixed model learns trace-supervised composition and where it fails, but its kinetic explanation does not extend or replace those formal expressivity results.

reviewed_competitors.title: How do Transformers Learn Implicit Reasoning?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ye et al. identify memorization, ID generalization, and cross-distribution stages and use semantic patching plus a representational lens for implicit multi-hop reasoning. Kinetics contrasts explicit trace supervision and fits takeoff curves, while using simpler linear probes and single-state corruption for mechanism.

reviewed_competitors.title: Implicit Reasoning in Transformers is Reasoning through Shortcuts
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lin et al. show strong implicit multi-step performance can depend on fixed training patterns and fail under further distribution shift. Kinetics reports a transient answer/trace gap as shortcut learning, but its OOD split leaves all atomic facts known and does not vary pattern structure as directly.

reviewed_competitors.title: Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lanham et al. intervene on generated traces by adding mistakes, paraphrasing, and other perturbations to measure whether answers condition on them. Kinetics instead subtracts exact full-sequence accuracy from answer accuracy over training, so it studies trace agreement but not the same causal notion of faithfulness.

reviewed_competitors.title: Making Reasoning Matter: Measuring and Improving Faithfulness of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Paul et al. use causal mediation across twelve LMs and train FRODO to make answers depend more robustly on intermediate reasoning. Kinetics contributes a training-time trace-alignment trajectory in a controlled symbolic model, but does not perform mediation or demonstrate trace causality.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Expressive Power of Transformers with Chain of Thought
reviewed_competitors.difference: Merrill and Sabharwal characterize how the number of intermediate decoding steps changes decoder-transformer language classes. Kinetics gives empirical curves for fixed synthetic tasks and a fixed architecture, so its composition result is an optimization observation within the broader formal possibility result.

reviewed_competitors.title: Is Chain-of-Thought Reasoning of LLMs a Mirage? A Data Distribution Lens
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhao et al. systematically vary task, length, and format discrepancy in a controlled training environment and find brittle CoT outside training distributions. Kinetics varies arity and data ratio and reports intersection/Mamba failures, but its OOD protocol is narrower and does not disentangle trace-format shift from task complexity.

reviewed_competitors.title: Steering Language Models With Activation Engineering
reviewed_competitors.difference: Activation Addition constructs a contrastive vector and adds a scalar multiple to residual activations. AAS instead constrains the edit to a fixed norm-preserving two-dimensional target-angle rotation and maps a full circle of behaviors.

reviewed_competitors.title: Steering Llama 2 via Contrastive Activation Addition
reviewed_competitors.difference: Contrastive Activation Addition averages paired activation differences and applies an additive coefficient. AAS uses a refusal direction plus a PCA-derived orthogonal axis, rotates to an absolute angle, and conditionally gates individual activations.

reviewed_competitors.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work supplies the difference-in-means refusal direction and directional-ablation framing used by AAS. AAS adds automatic candidate selection, a PCA-derived second axis, continuous rotations, and a sign mask, while reusing the same single-direction premise.

reviewed_competitors.title: Householder Pseudo-Rotation: A Novel Approach to Activation Editing in LLMs with Direction-Magnitude Perspective
reviewed_competitors.difference: Householder Pseudo-Rotation already performs norm-preserving rotation-like activation editing for safety. AAS's narrower distinction is a fixed feature-plus-PCA plane, explicit target-angle full-circle traversal, and a per-activation sign gate; broad claims that rotation itself is new are not sustained.

reviewed_competitors.title: Programming Refusal with Conditional Activation Steering
reviewed_competitors.difference: CAST applies additive steering when a semantic prompt condition fires, supporting programmable categories and rules. AAS rotates and uses a local hard sign condition on each activation rather than a learned prompt-level condition.

reviewed_competitors.title: Representation Surgery: Theory and Practice of Affine Steering
reviewed_competitors.difference: Representation Surgery derives affine least-squares steering maps and evaluates representation correction for bias and toxicity. AAS sacrifices affine generality for a norm-preserving rank-two rotation aimed at continuous behavioral traversal.

reviewed_competitors.title: Spectral Editing of Activations for Large Language Model Alignment
reviewed_competitors.difference: Spectral Editing derives projections from positive and negative activation covariance and includes nonlinear variants. AAS uses PCA only to choose a complementary axis, then applies a prescribed two-dimensional angular transformation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Steering Without Side Effects: Improving Post-Deployment Control of Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: KTS changes model weights during training so the deployed model tolerates subsequent additive steering. AAS is training-free and seeks lower side effects through a geometric restriction and hard gate, but does not create steering-aware weights.

reviewed_competitors.difference: This paper introduces the adversarial synthetic graph-navigation setting and analyzes failure when a fresh graph is supplied in context. The reviewed work fixes a much larger graph in model weights, exposes its edge bigrams during training, and studies held-out paths plus token geometry.

reviewed_competitors.title: Grokked Transformers are Implicit Reasoners: A Mechanistic Journey to the Edge of Generalization
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work analyzes grokking, associative memorization, and generalizing circuits on synthetic composition and comparison tasks. The reviewed paper focuses instead on fixed graph-edge memory, six-to-ten-hop held-out paths, and global spectral geometry, but inherits the broader associative-versus-structured circuit question.

reviewed_competitors.title: How do Transformers Learn Implicit Reasoning?
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work reports a staged learning trajectory and cosine clustering on symbolic multi-hop tasks. The reviewed paper more explicitly contrasts parametric memory data structures, demonstrates geometry under edge-only supervision, and pushes to longer fixed-graph compositions across Transformer and Mamba.

reviewed_competitors.title: Generalization or Hallucination? Understanding Out-of-Context Reasoning in Transformers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: contemporary out-of-context reasoning and geometry competitor
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work gives a stronger formal treatment of implicit bias and nuclear-norm geometry in shallow factorized two-hop reasoning, including hallucination. The reviewed paper emphasizes many-hop local edge memorization in deep Transformer and Mamba models and offers a preliminary Node2Vec spectral account.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding Factual Recall in Transformers via Associative Memories
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work studies capacity and gradient flow for factual recall through shallow associative memories. The reviewed paper challenges associative memory as a complete account by exhibiting organized graph embeddings and held-out multi-hop behavior, though it does not causally exclude a coexisting associative circuit.

reviewed_competitors.title: Do LLMs Dream of Elephants (When Told Not To)? Latent Concept Association and Associative Memory in Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work analyzes one-layer attention and value parameters as context-sensitive associative memory for latent concepts. The reviewed paper instead studies graph-global organization of token embeddings and many-hop in-weights navigation across deeper sequence models.

reviewed_competitors.title: Birth of a Transformer: A Memory Viewpoint
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work tracks how a Transformer learns global and contextual bigram statistics and interprets weight matrices as associative memories. The reviewed paper asks whether locally memorized graph bigrams instead organize token embeddings into a global graph geometry useful for many-hop queries.

reviewed_competitors.title: Implicit Geometry of Next-token Prediction: From Language Sparsity Patterns to Model Representations
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work analytically connects next-token sparsity, low-rank logit structure, nuclear norm, and subspace collapse to learned representations. The reviewed paper specializes geometry to memorized graph spectra, supplies deep-model empirical controls, and analyzes a Node2Vec softmax dynamic; therefore broad novelty claims about implicit next-token geometry must be narrowed.

reviewed_competitors.title: Breaking the Softmax Bottleneck: A High-Rank RNN Language Model
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yang et al. formalize the one-step softmax bottleneck: standard hidden-to-vocabulary logits impose a low-rank next-token matrix and restrict expressivity. The reviewed paper's empirical novelty is to index logits additionally by multi-token futures and study the resulting sequence-level row relations; its top-token sketches nevertheless inherit the original next-token output geometry.

reviewed_competitors.title: Input Switched Affine Networks: An RNN Architecture Designed for Interpretability
reviewed_competitors.difference: Foerster et al. introduce the time-invariant ISAN as an interpretable recurrent language model with token-selected affine transitions. The reviewed work allows parameters to vary with time and newly proves that this enlarged fixed-horizon class is exactly equivalent to globally bounded extended-logit rank.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Hidden Markov Models Using Conditional Samples
reviewed_competitors.difference: Conditional-sample access already makes latent sequential models efficiently learnable under structural conditions. The reviewed paper uses the stronger exact full-logit query interface and targets time-varying affine predictive states rather than HMM latent states, while emphasizing an LLM/model-stealing interpretation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Model Stealing for Any Low-Rank Language Model
reviewed_competitors.difference: Liu and Moitra already study efficient model stealing for broad low-rank language-model classes under query access. The reviewed work organizes rank through the extended mean-centered-logit matrix, proves an exact time-varying-ISAN characterization, and supplies empirical spectrum/Lingen demonstrations, but does not connect its approximate LLM measurements to its exact stealing theorem.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Logits of API-Protected LLMs Leak Proprietary Information
reviewed_competitors.difference: Finlayson et al. exploit returned logits to infer hidden dimensions and recover proprietary output-layer information from black-box APIs. The reviewed paper instead uses relationships across history-future logit rows for generation and exact-model learning; its guardrail-bypass idea is not experimentally tested.

reviewed_competitors.title: Stealing Part of a Production Language Model
reviewed_competitors.difference: Carlini et al. demonstrate recovery of a production model's hidden size and output projection from API log probabilities. The reviewed paper proposes a model-agnostic longer-horizon logit geometry and a generative query-learning theorem, but evaluates only open-weight OLMo and assumes much richer exact query access in theory.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Linear Representation Hypothesis and the Geometry of Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Park et al. develop a geometric account of linearly represented concepts in LLM representation spaces. The reviewed work studies model-agnostic output-logit row spaces and tests transfer with principal angles, but its nearest-history and generation tables do not establish that the recovered dimensions correspond to interpretable concepts.

reviewed_competitors.difference: CoBA integrates nonlinear conjugate-gradient directions into an AMSGrad-like stochastic optimizer and supplies a regret analysis plus text/image experiments. The target instead performs a one-way phase handoff from Adam to line-search CG and proposes a new scalar trigger; its exact combination may differ, but the broad claim of innovatively combining Adam and CG is substantially narrowed by this omitted direct predecessor.

reviewed_competitors.title: ADAHESSIAN: An Adaptive Second Order Optimizer for Machine Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: AdaHessian estimates and smooths diagonal Hessian curvature with Hutchinson products and applies one stochastic optimizer across non-convex training, with CV, NLP, and recommendation results. It directly measures curvature rather than inferring convexity from gradient norm, but pays Hessian-vector overhead; the target uses a cheaper detector and line-search CG without an actual Hessian measurement.

reviewed_competitors.title: Sophia: A Scalable Stochastic Second-order Optimizer for Language Model Pre-training
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sophia periodically estimates a diagonal Hessian, clips curvature-scaled updates to tolerate non-convexity, and reports matched step, total-compute, and wall-clock speedups on 125M-1.5B language models. The target avoids explicit curvature and is far smaller, but therefore lacks Sophia's direct curvature signal, scale evidence, and exact compute accounting.

reviewed_competitors.title: SOAP: Improving and Stabilizing Shampoo using Adam
reviewed_competitors.difference: SOAP continuously runs Adam-like moment updates in a slowly refreshed Shampoo eigenbasis, avoiding a discrete phase claim and reporting iteration and wall-clock savings on 360M and 660M language models. The target's optimizer handoff is simpler, but its local-convexity detector and tiny vision suite do not establish an advantage over this stable hybrid design.

reviewed_competitors.title: Shampoo: Preconditioned Stochastic Tensor Optimization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Shampoo uses tensor-dimension preconditioners throughout stochastic training and provides convex convergence analysis while demonstrating deep-learning speed. Unlike the target's postulated phase boundary and line search, it adapts geometry continuously; its memory and matrix-root costs are the principal tradeoff.

reviewed_competitors.title: Optimizing Neural Networks with Kronecker-factored Approximate Curvature
reviewed_competitors.difference: K-FAC approximates layerwise Fisher blocks with Kronecker factors and works in highly stochastic regimes, supplying a genuine curvature-based update rather than classifying nonlinear CG as second order. The target requires less matrix state but offers no direct curvature validation, scale comparison, or matched-compute baseline against K-FAC.

reviewed_competitors.difference: MAC already introduces one auxiliary coordinate per layer and example and alternates parameter and coordinate optimization with parallelism and convergence analysis. The present paper specializes a quadratic-penalty gradient sweep and claims objective convergence to zero under stronger rank, activation, and conditioning assumptions.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: PMLR volume 33, AISTATS 2014, pages 10-19 (official proceedings final)

reviewed_competitors.title: Convergent Block Coordinate Descent for Training Tikhonov Regularized Deep Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct prior BCD method for lifted ReLU networks.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhang and Brand lift ReLU into a smooth multiconvex Tikhonov-regularized formulation and claim R-linear convergence to a stationary point, with MNIST comparisons to SGD variants. The present work removes proximal/Tikhonov updates and targets arbitrarily small loss, but only after changing the ReLU architecture and under restrictive interpolation assumptions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Lifted Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Askari et al. encode non-decreasing activations as convex argmin penalties so block steps become shallow supervised problems and emphasize initialization and robustness. The present paper instead uses squared consistency penalties and a strict inverse-slope condition to claim zero lifted loss.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Proximal Block Coordinate Descent Algorithm for Deep Neural Network Training
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lau et al. use proximal BCD and a Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz analysis to obtain global convergence of the iterate sequence and report standard-dataset comparisons. The present paper uses vanilla local gradient steps and seeks the stronger zero-training-loss conclusion, but supplies much narrower synthetic evidence.

reviewed_competitors.title: Global Convergence of Block Coordinate Descent in Deep Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest prior convergence framework spanning common DNN splitting schemes and ResNets.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zeng et al. prove convergence to critical points at O(1/k) for two- and three-splitting BCD models under KL-style conditions and cover general smooth losses and ResNets. The present paper's novelty is specifically convergence of objective value to zero/global infimum, not the broader phrase 'global convergence.'
reviewed_competitors.source_version: PMLR volume 97, ICML 2019, pages 7313-7323 (official proceedings final)

reviewed_competitors.title: A block coordinate descent optimizer for classification problems exploiting convexity
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct layer-block alternative for neural-network classification.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Patel et al. alternate a globally optimized convex cross-entropy output layer with gradient-trained hidden layers and evaluate dense and convolutional classifiers. The present paper updates every layer through auxiliaries and proves a scalar squared-regression interpolation result; its classification discussion is not a proved or tested counterpart.

reviewed_competitors.title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
reviewed_competitors.difference: Classical dropout independently samples thinned networks during training and supplies broad evidence across vision, speech, text, and biology. Dynamic Dropout changes the mask generator to an epoch-evolving GoL lattice but does not match its effective keep rate or reproduce that breadth.

reviewed_competitors.title: Adaptive Dropout for Training Deep Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Standout learns input-conditioned unit-drop probabilities jointly with the network through an overlaid belief network. Dynamic Dropout's local GoL transition is not input-conditioned or learned; only its occasional random reset watches validation loss.

reviewed_competitors.title: Regularization of Neural Networks using DropConnect
reviewed_competitors.difference: DropConnect randomizes weights rather than unit activations and includes a generalization bound plus multi-dataset experiments. Dynamic Dropout keeps activation gating but introduces temporal and spatial correlation through GoL without a bound.

reviewed_competitors.title: Fast Dropout Training
reviewed_competitors.difference: Fast Dropout integrates or samples a Gaussian approximation to the dropout objective for speed and stability. Dynamic Dropout instead evolves an explicit binary mask and merely asserts negligible, parallel overhead without a timing comparison.

reviewed_competitors.title: Improved Dropout for Shallow and Deep Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Evolutional Dropout computes nonuniform sampling probabilities online from minibatch second-order statistics and reports CIFAR-100 accuracy and convergence gains. It is a direct data-adaptive predecessor; Dynamic Dropout offers interpretable lattice patterns but no example- or minibatch-conditioned adaptation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Concrete Dropout
reviewed_competitors.difference: Concrete Dropout differentiably learns dropout probabilities using a continuous relaxation and a variational objective. Dynamic Dropout has no learned mask parameters or calibrated uncertainty objective and relies on fixed GoL rules plus an unspecified reset heuristic.

reviewed_competitors.title: DropBlock: A Regularization Method for Convolutional Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: DropBlock drops contiguous feature-map regions and gradually increases the drop schedule, grounding structure in spatially meaningful CNN features and validating on ImageNet and COCO. Dynamic Dropout places arbitrary dense-unit indices in a spatial lattice and has no CNN experiment.

The target's narrower novelty is transient component learning and early population risk under imbalance rather than the optimizer's canonical form or implicit-bias framework.

reviewed_competitors.difference: This work formalizes Muon-like updates as norm-constrained linear-minimization oracles and studies optimization. The target reuses the spectral-norm steepest-descent reduction but contributes an imbalance-specific generalization model.

reviewed_competitors.title: Isotropic Curvature Model for Understanding Deep Learning Optimization: Is Gradient Orthogonalization Optimal?
reviewed_competitors.difference: This paper identifies regimes where exact gradient orthogonalization is not optimal. It is negative evidence against treating equalized singular updates as universally beneficial and complements the target's own Adam and pretrained-fine-tuning failures.

reviewed_competitors.title: Preconditioning Benefits of Spectral Orthogonalization in Muon
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work derives benefits from low-rank gradients and structured Hessians rather than class-prior-aligned moment components. It broadens the possible Muon mechanism and makes the target's imbalance story one sufficient model rather than a general explanation.

reviewed_competitors.title: To Use or not to Use Muon: How Simplicity Bias in Optimizers Matters
reviewed_competitors.difference: This paper directly argues that Muon's simultaneous learning removes SGD's useful simplicity bias and gives cases where Muon fits spurious features or misses shared structure. reviewed_competitors.title: Scalable Multitemperature Free Energy Sampling of Classical Ising Spin States
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest direct prior and omitted experimental baseline: multitemperature discrete flow matching on the 2D Ising model.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Tuo et al. directly model discrete spin states with one temperature- and size-conditioned flow, evaluate free-energy sampling, and extrapolate to larger lattices. This paper instead learns paired cooling transitions in a continuous latent with a projector at every prescribed temperature and frames those staged endpoints as interpretability; the current v3 title and scope make the overlap stronger than the older title cited in this paper suggests.

reviewed_competitors.title: Discrete Flow Matching
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational direct mechanism competitor for flow matching on discrete state spaces.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Gat et al. derive probability paths and posterior parameterizations directly for discrete variables and sample non-autoregressively. This paper avoids direct discrete flow by encoding spins continuously, regressing adjacent cooling slopes, and using an external projector, gaining explicit temperature checkpoints but losing a learned discrete transition distribution.

reviewed_competitors.title: Energy Matching: Unifying Flow Matching and Energy-Based Models for Generative Modeling
reviewed_competitors.difference: Energy Matching learns a time-independent scalar potential whose near-data dynamics target a Boltzmann equilibrium and supports explicit energy priors. This paper uses a time-conditioned vector field plus a separate Ising-energy projector penalty; its distinctive claim is semantic cooling stages rather than a unified scalar energy-based flow or tractable equilibrium formulation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Physics vs Distributions: Pareto Optimal Flow Matching with Physics Constraints
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct contemporary physics-constrained flow-matching framework cited by the paper.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Baldan et al. explicitly optimize the conflict between distributional and physical objectives using conflict-free gradients and unrolling across PDE benchmarks. This paper instead labels adjacent Ising cooling endpoints and relies on projection; it neither analyzes a physics/distribution Pareto frontier nor demonstrates that constraints hold along the continuous path.

reviewed_competitors.title: Flow-based generative models for Markov chain Monte Carlo in lattice field theory
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational flow-based lattice sampler and missing exact-correction baseline.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Albergo et al. train a tractable normalizing-flow proposal and insert it into MCMC, providing asymptotic correctness and autocorrelation comparisons without requiring target samples. This paper uses supervised cooling data, a noninvertible encoder/projector pipeline, and observable agreement without likelihood or an exact acceptance correction.

reviewed_competitors.title: Boltzmann Generators -- Sampling Equilibrium States of Many-Body Systems with Deep Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Noé et al. use invertible transformations, reweighting, and free-energy estimation to obtain unbiased one-shot equilibrium samples across metastable states. This paper emphasizes a sequential, temperature-interpretable path on Ising grids but provides neither exact reweighting nor independent-sample and free-energy guarantees.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning the Ising Model with Generative Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct Ising generative-model antecedent and observable-evaluation baseline.
reviewed_competitors.difference: D'Angelo and Böttcher assess RBM and convolutional-VAE samples over temperature using energy, magnetization, and spin correlations and expose representational limitations. This paper adds an autoregressive cooling trajectory with an explicit latent vector field, but omits spin-correlation and distributional diagnostics that the antecedent uses to distinguish model fidelity.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning to Compose: Improving Object Centric Learning by Injecting Compositionality
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest direct predecessor from overlapping authors and the source of the object-composition objective.
reviewed_competitors.difference: L2C already mixes arbitrary object slots from two images and maximizes composite likelihood inside a slot-attention object-centric model. This paper replaces L2C's conditional prior with an unconditional diffusion prior, adds relative consistency, removes slot attention in its object encoder, and generalizes the mixing interface to indexed attributes and a prespecified joint partition; modular cross-factor mixing, not compositional likelihood itself, is the main increment.

reviewed_competitors.title: Provable Compositional Generalization for Object-Centric Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct theoretical and loss-level predecessor for compositional consistency.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wiedemer et al. prove compositional generalization under structural decoder and consistency assumptions and supply the consistency principle reused here. This paper trades the additive-decoder guarantee for a learned diffusion-prior realism constraint and broader attribute/object mixing, gaining empirical scope while losing identifiability and compositional-generalization guarantees.

reviewed_competitors.title: Disentanglement of Correlated Factors via Hausdorff Factorized Support
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest factorized-support predecessor and missing correlated-factor baseline.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Roth et al. explicitly optimize pairwise support factorization with a Hausdorff distance and test severe correlations and correlation shift. This paper encodes stronger support-role assumptions through random mixing and extends them to exchangeable objects and a joint partition, but only tests mild sigma=0.1 correlations and does not compare against HFS.

reviewed_competitors.title: DisDiff: Unsupervised Disentanglement of Diffusion Probabilistic Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: DisDiff decomposes a pretrained diffusion model's gradient field into factor-conditioned subfields using information-theoretic invariant/variant objectives. This paper shares its attribute encoder and diffusion-decoder family but replaces mutual-information structure with latent remix validity and also handles object slots; its joint advantage partly comes from being told which latent is global style.

reviewed_competitors.title: Object-Centric Slot Diffusion
reviewed_competitors.difference: Latent Slot Diffusion conditions an expressive latent diffusion decoder on slot-attention object representations and demonstrates object-centric generation on synthetic and real images. This paper replaces slot attention with a QFormer and makes object validity explicit through unrestricted slot mixing, but relies on extra procedures for masks and does not match LSD's real-image scope.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Systematic Binder
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Prior joint object-and-factor representation framework that narrows the paper's 'unique joint disentanglement' claim.
reviewed_competitors.difference: SysBinder builds block-slot representations by combining spatial object binding with within-object factor binding and demonstrates unseen factor combinations, including CLEVR-Tex. This paper targets a different joint structure—one global style plus exchangeable objects—and modularizes it as mixing rather than a specialized binder, so it is not the first joint structured disentanglement method in the broader sense.

reviewed_competitors.title: Additive Decoders for Latent Variables Identification and Cartesian-Product Extrapolation
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Theoretical object-centric identifiability and recombination competitor.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lachapelle et al. prove block identification and novel Cartesian-product generation under additive decoding with weak distributional assumptions. This paper avoids additive-decoder expressivity and spatial-exclusivity constraints by using a diffusion prior and mixing rules, but its corresponding support argument does not prove identification or extrapolation for the trained neural system.

reviewed_competitors.title: Provably Learning Object-Centric Representations
reviewed_competitors.difference: Brady et al. identify ground-truth object latents up to allowed transformations under compositionality, irreducibility, and invertible inference, including dependent objects. This paper offers a practical shared-loss recipe with stronger empirical images and global attributes, but explicitly lacks a guarantee that its mixed slots recover objects rather than another consistency-preserving code.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Lim et al. introduce the fixed-point/Newton sequence-parallel approach for generic nonlinear sequential models and report large time-series speedups; ParaRNN designs tractable GRU/LSTM Jacobians and production CUDA kernels and scales language models much further.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Gonzalez et al. reduce DEER's cubic cost with quasi-Newton approximations and add ELK/parallel Kalman smoothing for numerical stability; ParaRNN instead changes the cells to obtain exact diagonal/block Jacobians and relies on undamped three-step Newton.

reviewed_competitors.title: Predictability Enables Parallelization of Nonlinear State Space Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current theoretical criterion for nonlinear time-parallel solvers
reviewed_competitors.difference: Gonzalez et al. connect Lyapunov predictability to optimization conditioning and prove polylogarithmic time for predictable systems while diagnosing slow convergence for chaotic ones; ParaRNN supplies a much larger engineering demonstration but no comparable convergence theory.

reviewed_competitors.title: Parallelization of Non-linear State-Space Models: Scaling Up Liquid-Resistance Liquid-Capacitance Networks for Efficient Sequence Modeling
reviewed_competitors.difference: LrcSSM likewise enforces a diagonal Jacobian for O(TD) work/memory and O(log T) depth, but adds a formal gradient-stability guarantee and targets forecasting; ParaRNN targets GRU/LSTM-like LLMs, custom CUDA, and 7B scale.

reviewed_competitors.title: Implicit Language Models are RNNs: Balancing Parallelization and Expressivity
reviewed_competitors.difference: Implicit LMs use iterative fixed-point transformations and a convergence curriculum, scale to 1.3B/207B tokens, and emphasize state tracking; ParaRNN recovers an explicit nonlinear recurrence with Newton scans and scales parameters to 7B but trains on fewer tokens and lacks long-context/state-tracking LM evaluation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Primary efficiency/quality baseline and direct architecture competitor
reviewed_competitors.difference: Mamba2 uses a structured linear selective recurrence with mature scan algorithms and is the strongest perplexity/downstream model in ParaRNN's experiments; ParaRNN adds nonlinear state transitions and wins selected synthetic expressivity tasks at greater solver complexity.

reviewed_competitors.title: Were RNNs All We Needed?
reviewed_competitors.difference: minGRU/minLSTM remove dependencies to preserve linear-scan parallelism with simpler recurrence but no nonlinear state transition; ParaRNN retains nonlinear recurrence through iterative solving and tests far larger language models.

reviewed_competitors.title: xLSTM: Extended Long Short-Term Memory
reviewed_competitors.difference: xLSTM changes gating/memory and mixes sLSTM/mLSTM blocks, with the parallel component derived architecturally; ParaRNN focuses on automatically time-parallelizing nonlinear GRU/LSTM-like recurrences through a numerical solver and custom kernel.

reviewed_competitors.title: Fixed-Point RNNs: Interpolating from Diagonal to Dense
reviewed_competitors.difference: Fixed-Point RNNs parameterize implicitly dense linear state transitions as fixed points of parallelizable diagonal recurrences and target state tracking; ParaRNN directly solves nonlinear explicit recurrence and emphasizes kernel/training scale.

reviewed_competitors.title: Improved state mixing in higher-order and block diagonal linear recurrent networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: H-LRU/BD-LRU increase temporal/channel mixing with higher-order or block-linear recurrences while retaining a single scan and competitive throughput; they directly challenge the premise that expensive nonlinear solves are the only route beyond diagonal state mixing.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Saparov et al. also find that the right graph distribution lets Transformers learn parallel reachability expansion and that learning degrades with graph size; this paper adds an exact restricted-model capacity theorem and an I/J gradient-decomposition account, but does not test size extrapolation.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Little Depth Goes a Long Way: The Expressive Power of Log-Depth Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: Merrill and Sabharwal prove highly uniform log-depth Transformers can express connectivity and quantify asymptotic depth scaling; this paper sharpens one simplified model to a nonasymptotic 3^L diameter bound and studies optimization, at the cost of stronger architectural and sign assumptions.

reviewed_competitors.title: How Transformers Learn Causal Structure with Gradient Descent
reviewed_competitors.difference: Nichani et al. prove gradient descent learns latent causal structure and induction heads in a simplified two-layer model using mutual-information gradients; this paper borrows the disentangling philosophy but targets graph reachability and a competition between local and global equivariant channels.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Transformer Programs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Friedman et al. train modified Transformers that can be compiled into discrete programs across algorithmic and NLP tasks; this paper uses appended attention slices for algebraic proofs and weight projections rather than extracting an executable learned connectivity program.

reviewed_competitors.title: What Algorithms can Transformers Learn? A Study in Length Generalization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhou et al. connect length generalization to short RASP programs and improve hard tasks such as parity and addition; this paper instead predicts success from diameter-relative capacity and data composition, while evaluating only fixed-n graph-family shifts.

reviewed_competitors.title: Unveiling Induction Heads: Provable Training Dynamics and Feature Learning in Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chen et al. analyze gradient-flow convergence in a richer two-attention-layer model with softmax-like components, normalization, relative positions, and feed-forward selection on Markov data; this paper obtains graph-specific channel signs and capacity by imposing nonnegativity and an equivariant algebra.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Neural Thickets studies the local abundance and diversity of useful experts around pretrained weights, offering a geometry-based account for why random search can work; the present paper reports performance and only hypothesizes a favorable smoothed landscape.

reviewed_competitors.title: Matching Accuracy, Different Geometry: Evolution Strategies vs GRPO in LLM Post-Training

reviewed_competitors.title: Low-Rank Curvature for Zeroth-Order Optimization in LLM Fine-Tuning

reviewed_competitors.difference: Salimans et al. established communication-efficient, massively parallel ES for RL policies with antithetic sampling and fitness shaping; this paper strips several of those refinements and extends full-parameter reward search to modern LLMs.

reviewed_competitors.difference: CF-ViT runs a coarse classification stage and conditionally re-splits informative patches for a fixed two-stage inference pathway. reviewed_competitors.difference: DynamicViT learns feature-dependent importance predictors and prunes tokens progressively inside the network. APT preserves full image coverage at mixed resolution and reduces sequence length before every transformer layer, avoiding the learned scorer's long fine-tune but relying on a hand-tuned entropy proxy.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning to Merge Tokens via Decoupled Embedding for Efficient Vision Transformers

APT's scorer is nonlearned and precedes the backbone; its Figure 4 comparison also modifies DTEM by disabling weighted attention for fused inference, so the systems comparison is not an exact official-method reproduction.

reviewed_competitors.title: Not All Patches are What You Need: Expediting Vision Transformers via Token Reorganizations

APT makes a cheaper raw-image decision once, before the model, enabling whole-network sequence reduction and packed attention but sacrificing task-aware semantic scoring.

This paper asks why the same mechanism weakens in multivariate boundary geometry and claims recovery of univariate-like rates on embedded low-dimensional components.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Nacson et al. connect multivariate shallow-ReLU minima stability to a weighted Laplacian/variation constraint and test its tightness. The present paper uses a related data-dependent regularity as a starting point and adds distribution-specific generalization upper/lower bounds via depth and cap geometry.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Wu and Su distinguish SGD trace/Frobenius stability from GD top-eigenvalue stability and argue the latter is too weak for satisfactory generalization in their setting. This paper refines the GD conclusion: top-eigenvalue BEoS regularity can generalize on favorable geometries but permits memorization on highly shatterable ones.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Damian et al. model the actual edge dynamics through cubic self-stabilization and projected GD under a sharpness constraint. This paper takes that constraint as a static hypothesis-class proxy and studies distribution-dependent generalization, explicitly leaving the trajectory-level connection heuristic.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Cohen et al. establish the empirical progressive-sharpening and edge-of-stability phenomena that motivate the 2/eta constraint. reviewed_competitors.difference: Parhi and Nowak obtain near-minimax estimation for Radon-domain variation spaces using explicit weight decay and provide metric-entropy tools used here. The present paper studies a data-weighted variation ball induced by curvature rather than an explicit regularizer, which becomes weak near shallow support regions.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Kornowski et al. show a dimension-driven transition from tempered to benign overfitting for two-layer ReLU classification under different assumptions. This paper instead predicts worse BEoS generalization for isotropic boundary-concentrated high-dimensional geometry and better behavior on low-dimensional mixtures, emphasizing data geometry and optimizer stability rather than minimum-norm interpolation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Dion: Distributed Orthonormalized Updates
reviewed_competitors.difference: Dion replaces full Newton-Schulz reconstruction with amortized low-rank power iteration, error feedback, and rank-controlled updates compatible with sharded weights, reporting models through 3B. MuonBP preserves ordinary Muon updates on periodic full steps and has simpler state, but retains O(mn/P) communication and full-tensor transient memory; its direct Dion comparison is only 160M.

reviewed_competitors.title: Practical Efficiency of Muon for Pretraining
reviewed_competitors.difference: This primary study evaluates Muon's compute-time Pareto frontier, large-batch data efficiency, and muP-aware hyperparameter transfer through 4B parameters. MuonBP addresses a different bottleneck—model-parallel orthogonalization collectives—and does not match its batch-size, architecture, or hyperparameter-transfer ablations.

reviewed_competitors.title: MuLoCo: Muon is a practical inner optimizer for DiLoCo
reviewed_competitors.difference: MuLoCo reduces data-parallel synchronization frequency by using Muon inside DiLoCo and extensively tunes models from 150M to 3.1B before a 15B extrapolation, including quantized and long-interval variants. MuonBP instead reduces optimizer-specific model-parallel traffic within a synchronized step; the methods address orthogonal communication axes and could be combined.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Polar Express: Optimal Matrix Sign Methods and Their Application to the Muon Algorithm
reviewed_competitors.difference: Polar Express accelerates the polar/sign computation itself with adaptive minimax polynomial iterations, bfloat16 safeguards, and GPT-2 validation-loss tests. MuonBP reduces shard communication and block compute by changing when and where full orthogonalization occurs; it retains fixed Newton-Schulz and could incorporate the newer kernel.

reviewed_competitors.title: DMuon: Efficient Distributed Muon Training with Near-Adam Overhead
reviewed_competitors.difference: DMuon integrates a drop-in distributed implementation into existing stacks and reports 1.48-3.01x end-to-end step-time and 6.85-163x optimizer-step speedups across LLM and embodied-model workloads. It is later evidence that systems and kernel redesign can close the overhead gap without MuonBP's fixed periodic approximation, narrowing any current efficiency-leading claim.

reviewed_competitors.title: Dion3: Full-Stack Orthogonal Updates
reviewed_competitors.difference: Dion3 combines Gram Newton-Schulz, symmetry-aware kernels, megabatching, and partial-row orthogonalization, reporting up to 6x lower optimizer-step time while matching or improving Muon loss. MuonBP's periodic shard/full schedule is simpler and theoretically motivated, but it is not compared against this current full-stack implementation and retains periodic full-tensor work.
