reviewed_competitors.difference: Pfau et al. train on dense supervision for algorithmic tasks and analyze computational depth; the reviewed paper claims an off-the-shelf prompt effect and attributes it to activation redistribution.

reviewed_competitors.title: Pause Tokens Strictly Increase the Expressivity of Constant-Depth Transformers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Formal expressivity account for why filler positions can increase Transformer computation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: London and Kanade prove circuit-class separations for bounded models and demonstrate parity learning; the reviewed paper's Taylor argument concerns activation variance in pretrained LLMs and does not establish expressivity or task-computation gains.

reviewed_competitors.title: Meaningless is Better: Hashing Bias-Inducing Words in LLM Prompts Improves Performance in Logical Reasoning and Statistical Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Prior use of meaningless replacements to improve reasoning and reduce lexical bias.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chadimova et al. hash bias-inducing semantic words, changing lexical cues; the reviewed paper uses long repeated prefixes and proposes a model-internal randomized substitute.

reviewed_competitors.title: Massive Activations in Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Mechanistic work connecting extreme activations and special tokens to attention behavior.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sun et al. characterize naturally occurring massive activations and attention-sink-like behavior; the reviewed paper actively moves near-zero gate outputs outward and interprets this as improved reasoning capacity.

reviewed_competitors.title: Steering Language Models With Activation Engineering
reviewed_competitors.difference: Activation engineering adds behavior-linked directions to residual streams; ARM uses no labeled steering direction and instead samples coordinate-wise outward shifts after the first MLP nonlinearity.

reviewed_competitors.title: Probing out-of-distribution generalization in machine learning for materials
reviewed_competitors.difference: This same-senior-author study uses more than 700 chemistry and symmetry shifts and already shows that more data or training can improve ID error while barely helping or worsening true OOD performance. The target changes from materials-property prediction to atomistic energy curves and adds controlled SchNet capacity plus Coulomb probes.

reviewed_competitors.title: MLIP Arena: Advancing Fairness and Transparency in Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials via an Open, Accessible Benchmark Platform
reviewed_competitors.difference: MLIP Arena densely scans periodic-table homonuclear pair curves from short-range repulsion through dissociation and defines jumps, force flips, ranks, and tortuosity. It predates the target's first public OpenReview posting by one day; the target adds joint data/capacity scaling, OMol25 molecular models, high-level BDE comparisons, and a two-proton query.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks spotlight, published 2025-09-18, modified 2026-04-23

reviewed_competitors.title: Global properties of the energy landscape: a testing and training arena for machine learned potentials
reviewed_competitors.difference: Landscape17 evaluates complete kinetic transition networks and finds missed DFT paths plus spurious stable structures. It is a richer multidimensional PES-topology audit; the target uses simpler interpretable curves and directly separates ID data scaling from one OOD task.

reviewed_competitors.title: Data efficiency and extrapolation trends in neural network interatomic potentials
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work shows test errors obey scaling trends yet fail to predict OOD error and MD stability, and proposes loss entropy as a training-only diagnostic. It anticipates the target's core ID-versus-physics warning but studies NequIP/MACE landscapes rather than diatomic asymptotes.

reviewed_competitors.title: Systematic softening in universal machine learning interatomic potentials
reviewed_competitors.difference: M3GNet, CHGNet, and MACE-MP-0 systematically underpredict PES curvature and high-energy states because pretraining is near-equilibrium biased, and one-point fine-tuning repairs much local softening. The target changes to molecular models and controlled H2/data scaling but does not offer a repair.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding and Mitigating Distribution Shifts For Machine Learning Force Fields
reviewed_competitors.difference: This paper benchmarks multiple force-field shifts and adds test-time spectral alignment plus cheap-physics gradient updates. It has broader shift taxonomy and mitigation; the target provides a more elementary dissociation/Coulomb stress test and scale contrast.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Smooth and Expressive Interatomic Potentials for Physical Property Prediction
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work shows lower held-out error need not improve downstream physics and introduces energy-conservation screening plus the eSEN architecture. The target audits an OMol25 eSEN checkpoint far outside its usual MD evaluation rather than designing a smooth model.

reviewed_competitors.title: Forces are not Enough: Benchmark and Critical Evaluation for Machine Learning Force Fields with Molecular Simulations
reviewed_competitors.difference: This benchmark establishes that static energy/force errors misalign with MD observables and stability across water, molecules, peptides, and materials. The target's simpler curves are more interpretable physical unit tests but do not introduce the error-versus-deployment distinction.

reviewed_competitors.title: Beyond MD17: the reactive xxMD dataset
reviewed_competitors.difference: xxMD supplies reactive and nonadiabatic bond-breaking configurations that expose much larger errors than equilibrium MD17. It is a dataset remedy and benchmark; the target compares equilibrium-heavy with broader data and tests the latest foundation checkpoints.

reviewed_competitors.title: Beyond potential energy surface benchmarking: a complete application of machine learning to chemical reactivity
reviewed_competitors.difference: Negative design and metadynamics actively seek high-energy or unphysical combustion states and trigger ab initio labeling. The target diagnoses static coverage failures without an active correction loop.

reviewed_competitors.title: MLIPAudit: A benchmarking tool for Machine Learned Interatomic Potentials
reviewed_competitors.difference: MLIPAudit spans fourteen molecular and industrial tasks and discloses training overlap, with UMA-Small leading external models. The target's curve tests are narrower but isolate known qualitative limits and controlled scaling.

reviewed_competitors.title: Does AI for science need another ImageNet Or totally different benchmarks? A case study of machine learning force fields
reviewed_competitors.difference: This paper explicitly argues for sample-efficiency, time, and cross-dataset OOD metrics instead of IID leaderboards. The target operationalizes that warning with dissociation but omits time, uncertainty, and grouped OOD evaluation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Matbench Discovery -- A framework to evaluate machine learning crystal stability predictions
reviewed_competitors.difference: Matbench Discovery uses a prospective materials-stability task and exposes regression/classification mismatch near the convex hull. It concerns solid discovery rather than energy-curve physics but reinforces application-aligned evaluation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Orbital-free Bond Breaking via Machine Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: A learned density functional self-consistently dissociates one-dimensional diatomics with densities and forces. It establishes ML bond breaking much earlier but is system-specific and electronic-density-based, unlike coordinate-only universal MLIPs.

reviewed_competitors.title: PhysNet: A Neural Network for Predicting Energies, Forces, Dipole Moments and Partial Charges
reviewed_competitors.difference: PhysNet includes explicit electrostatics and dispersion and demonstrates their importance for qualitative asymptotic PES behavior. The target tests whether much larger pretrained models acquire such behavior without task-specific enforcement.

reviewed_competitors.title: Incorporating long-range physics in atomic-scale machine learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: This equivariant nonlocal representation builds a Coulomb asymptote and tests charged points, dimers, and dielectric response. It is a constructive architectural answer rather than a scale audit.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Fourth-Generation High-Dimensional Neural Network Potential with Accurate Electrostatics Including Non-local Charge Transfer
reviewed_competitors.difference: Charge equilibration and environment-dependent electronegativities address nonlocal charge-transfer failures of local potentials. The target's proton query instead probes unsupported state semantics in off-the-shelf foundation APIs.

reviewed_competitors.title: SpookyNet: Learning Force Fields with Electronic Degrees of Freedom and Nonlocal Effects
reviewed_competitors.difference: SpookyNet explicitly accepts total charge and spin and combines nonlocal interaction with analytic corrections. It makes charge/multiplicity verification a necessary condition for the target's bare-proton conclusion.

reviewed_competitors.title: Latent Ewald summation for machine learning of long-range interactions
reviewed_competitors.difference: Latent Ewald removes unphysical charged-dimer and interface artifacts at moderate cost without relying only on local cutoffs. The target documents failures but does not compare against a purpose-built long-range model.

reviewed_competitors.title: Physically-informed artificial neural networks for atomistic modeling of materials
reviewed_competitors.difference: A bond-order analytical baseline plus neural correction is motivated by accurate interpolation but poor pure-ML transfer. It supplies a physics-plus-learning alternative aligned with, and predating, the target's conclusion.

reviewed_competitors.title: Big Data meets Quantum Chemistry Approximations: The $Δ$-Machine Learning Approach
reviewed_competitors.difference: Delta-learning corrects a cheap physical calculation instead of relearning total quantum chemistry. The target briefly recommends this older strategy but does not test it on the failed curves.

reviewed_competitors.title: E(3)-Equivariant Graph Neural Networks for Data-Efficient and Accurate Interatomic Potentials
reviewed_competitors.difference: NequIP obtains orders-of-magnitude data efficiency from symmetry. It challenges scale as the only route, but does not claim arbitrary extrapolation or exact asymptotes.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Local Equivariant Representations for Large-Scale Atomistic Dynamics
reviewed_competitors.difference: Allegro combines strict locality, equivariance, accuracy, and 100-million-atom execution. Its OOD demonstrations remain within sampled application structure; the target probes unseen physical limits of later universal models.

reviewed_competitors.title: MACE: Higher Order Equivariant Message Passing Neural Networks for Fast and Accurate Force Fields
reviewed_competitors.difference: Higher-body equivariant messages give steep learning curves and better data efficiency, showing that inductive prior changes scaling. The target studies whether larger coordinate models acquire unsupported physical behavior.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural scaling of deep chemical models
reviewed_competitors.difference: This study scales chemical language models and SchNet, PaiNN, Allegro, and SpookyNet toward billion parameters and ten million structures, finding power laws for energy and force errors. It explicitly notes that force validation may retain seen species; the target operationalizes the requested unseen-species and geometry stress test.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scaling Laws of Graph Neural Networks for Atomistic Materials Modeling
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work scales atomistic GNNs to billion parameters and terabyte datasets on predictive losses. It supplies a much larger ID scaling study but does not test far-OOD PES limits.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Material Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Four days before the target's arXiv posting, this paper fits data, model, and compute laws for energy-force-stress learning with Transformer and EquiformerV2 models. It complements rather than contradicts the target because its endpoints are in-distribution losses.

reviewed_competitors.title: Beyond Scaling: Chemical Intuition as Emergent Ability of Universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
reviewed_competitors.difference: E3D extracts edgewise BDE-like values from Allegro/SPICE2 and reports agreement with literature and emergent reactivity. Those latent local decompositions are not full PEC repulsive walls, forces, tails, or charged Coulomb behavior, so they do not directly refute the target's curves.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Scaling Laws Surpass Chemical Accuracy for the Many-Electron Schrödinger Equation
reviewed_competitors.difference: LAVA neural wavefunctions improve energy, wavefunction properties, and N2 dissociation with model and compute scale. They optimize an explicit-electron wavefunction per system rather than a supervised coordinate-to-energy MLIP, so this directly limits the target's broad quantum-chemistry wording while leaving its MLIP result intact.

reviewed_competitors.title: ANI-1: An extensible neural network potential with DFT accuracy at force field computational cost
reviewed_competitors.difference: Normal-mode sampling deliberately covers distorted conformations and transfers to larger organic molecules. It is early positive evidence that targeted geometric coverage, not equilibrium count alone, controls useful transfer.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Universal Graph Deep Learning Interatomic Potential for the Periodic Table
reviewed_competitors.difference: M3GNet establishes periodic-table universality for solid-state relaxation and properties. Later softening and pair-curve audits delimit that domain; the target focuses molecular dissociation and charged states.

reviewed_competitors.title: CHGNet: Pretrained universal neural network potential for charge-informed atomistic modeling
reviewed_competitors.difference: CHGNet trains on inorganic trajectories and uses magnetic moments as electronic proxies. Charge-informed solid modeling is not equivalent to explicit electron-count and fragment asymptotes in the target's molecular proton query.

reviewed_competitors.title: A foundation model for atomistic materials chemistry
reviewed_competitors.difference: MACE-MP-0 demonstrates broad stable simulations across phases, reactions, interfaces, and a protein, often with optional fine-tuning. Its claims are practical and domain-conditioned rather than a guarantee of unseen diatomic asymptotes.

reviewed_competitors.title: MatterSim: A Deep Learning Atomistic Model Across Elements, Temperatures and Pressures
reviewed_competitors.difference: Active learning deliberately samples 0-5000 K and up to 1000 GPa and yields strong deployment results plus data-efficient fine-tuning. It shows that scale can work when deployment regimes are represented; it does not test molecular bond dissociation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Orb: A Fast, Scalable Neural Network Potential
reviewed_competitors.difference: Orb emphasizes diffusion pretraining, speed, and materials-workflow robustness. The target uses a later conservative OMol25 Orb-v3 checkpoint in an unadvertised far-OOD molecular regime.

reviewed_competitors.title: Orb-v3: atomistic simulation at scale
reviewed_competitors.difference: Orb-v3 advances the speed-memory frontier and studies conservative versus non-conservative behavior. The target specifically audits the conservative OMol25 variant on elementary curves outside its published evaluation.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Open Molecules 2025 (OMol25) Dataset, Evaluations, and Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: OMol25 provides more than 100 million high-level DFT structures over 83 elements with reactive, charge, spin, and solvation metadata. The target's contribution is to show that marginal breadth and thousands of diatomics do not by themselves guarantee selected curve behavior.

reviewed_competitors.title: UMA: A Family of Universal Models for Atoms
reviewed_competitors.difference: UMA scales mixture-of-linear-experts models to 150 million and 1.4 billion parameters over about half a billion multi-domain structures. Its reported scaling concerns broad task performance; the target audits unverified physical limits of the S and M OMol variants.

reviewed_competitors.title: Foundation Models for Atomistic Simulation of Chemistry and Materials
reviewed_competitors.difference: This perspective frames data and parameter scaling plus pretraining as a route to transferable and OOD-robust atomistic models. The target is an empirical qualification of that program rather than the first statement that physical support matters.

reviewed_competitors.title: Extrapolation of Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials for Organic and Polymeric Systems
reviewed_competitors.difference: Submitted one day before the target's arXiv version, this control study links chemical-environment convergence and neighbor-list construction to transfer across n-alkanes. It studies size extrapolation rather than physical asymptotes but reinforces coverage over raw scale.

reviewed_competitors.title: Evaluating the Transferability of Machine-Learned Force Fields for Material Property Modeling
reviewed_competitors.difference: The study finds solid-phase behavior is recovered only when solid configurations appear in training and proposes phase-sensitive tests. It anticipates the target's coverage conclusion in a materials simulation rather than a molecular curve setting.

reviewed_competitors.title: Single-model uncertainty quantification in neural network potentials does not consistently outperform model ensembles
reviewed_competitors.difference: Across interpolation and extrapolation challenges, the work finds no single uncertainty method wins and ensembles remain stronger for robustness. The target exposes unsupported curves but offers no uncertainty or refusal mechanism.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scaling Laws and Symmetry, Evidence from Neural Force Fields
reviewed_competitors.difference: This successor fits robust laws over data, parameters, and compute and finds better exponents for equivariant higher-order models. It supports ID scaling while reinforcing that architectural priors cannot be delegated to scale; it does not test dissociation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Universally Converging Representations of Matter Across Scientific Foundation Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Across about sixty models, representations align as ID performance improves but collapse to low-information states on far-OOD structures. This gives representational support for the target's narrower empirical warning.

reviewed_competitors.title: Long-range electrostatics for machine learning interatomic potentials is easier than we thought
reviewed_competitors.difference: A latent Ewald-style Coulomb functional with environment-dependent charges models electrostatics without supervising ambiguous DFT partial charges. It counters any implication that explicit electrostatics cannot work; formulation and state coverage matter.

reviewed_competitors.title: Symmetry-restricted energy landscapes as a benchmark for machine learned interatomic potentials
reviewed_competitors.difference: Two-dimensional Wyckoff-coordinate PES slices reveal artificial minima and saddles in MACE, CHGNet, M3GNet, Orb, and SevenNet. It confirms the target's warning in crystals with richer topology but does not isolate scale.

reviewed_competitors.title: From Evaluation to Design: Using Potential Energy Surface Smoothness Metrics to Guide Machine Learning Interatomic Potential Architectures
reviewed_competitors.difference: BSCT standardizes stretch/compression tests, connects discontinuities and false minima to MD stability, and uses the metrics to design smoother attention. It goes beyond the target with quantitative metrics and a fix, while the target retains the controlled data/capacity and modern molecular-model panel.

reviewed_competitors.title: Broken neural scaling laws in materials science
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work finds dataset-size scaling breaks and parameter scaling saturates for dielectric spectra. It supports non-universality of scaling in a different materials-property task rather than atomistic PESs.

reviewed_competitors.title: Bias in Universal Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials and its Effects on Fine-Tuning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Parallel-trajectory fine-tuning creates constrained biased data and extrapolation failure, while periodic fine-tuning and Q-residual diagnostics improve coverage. It supplies a practical correction loop absent from the target.

reviewed_competitors.title: Unprecedented robustness of physics-informed atomic energy models at and beyond room temperature
reviewed_competitors.difference: Physics-informed atomic energies and a high-energy prior yield stable high-temperature simulations from about one thousand points. This system-specific positive result supports targeted priors rather than universal coordinate-only scaling.

reviewed_competitors.title: Prediction and Experimental Verification of Electrolyte Solvation Structure from an OMol25-Trained Interatomic Potential
reviewed_competitors.difference: UMA-OMol reproduces densities and X-ray structure factors for electrolyte solvation and beats inorganic MLIPs. It demonstrates real value inside a covered domain without contradicting elementary far-OOD failure.

reviewed_competitors.title: Dyna-Mat: End-to-end benchmarking of foundation machine learning interatomic potentials in finite-temperature ensembles
reviewed_competitors.difference: Across fifteen foundation MLIPs, lower force error correlates on average with observable error, yet individual low-error systems still fail qualitatively and pressure is weak without stress labels. It refines rather than overturns the target's MAE warning.

reviewed_competitors.title: Fast and Accurate Foundation Models for Equivariant Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
reviewed_competitors.difference: NequIP and Allegro foundation models offer favorable accuracy-speed results on discovery, thermal conductivity, and near-equilibrium tasks when data are diverse and consistent. They are positive scaling-with-priors evidence but make no far-OOD dissociation guarantee.

reviewed_competitors.title: Data-Efficient Construction of Material-Specific Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials from Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics Trajectories
reviewed_competitors.difference: Five universal MLIPs over seven rare-event systems need hundreds to thousands of targeted frames; scratch training can beat naive fine-tuning and low trajectory error need not preserve reaction profiles. This gives practical coverage thresholds supporting the target's narrow conclusion.

reviewed_competitors.title: Activation Matching for Explanation Generation
reviewed_competitors.difference: This same-author immediate predecessor already contains the per-image autoencoder, activation/output matching, mask priors, and abductive robustness used by EXP-CAM. EXP-CAM's defensible increment is the channel-graph readout and broader qualitative comparisons, not the explanation generator itself; the manuscript does not quantitatively isolate that increment.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding Deep Networks via Extremal Perturbations and Smooth Masks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Extremal Perturbations directly optimizes smooth preservation/deletion masks under an explicit area constraint, removes tunable tradeoff weights from the core problem, reports area-response analyses, and extends attribution to intermediate channels. EXP-CAM adds multi-layer activation matching and a heuristic circuit graph but returns to numerous manually tuned weights and does not benchmark against this strongest mask-based predecessor.

reviewed_competitors.title: What made you do this? Understanding black-box decisions with sufficient input subsets
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sufficient Input Subsets formalizes minimal observed feature subsets under an explicit missingness semantics and clusters them across examples to expose global behavior. EXP-CAM is differentiable and image-specialized with activation alignment, but its weighted area objective does not certify subset minimality and its MNIST comparison supplies no equivalent quantitative test.

reviewed_competitors.title: Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps
reviewed_competitors.difference: Adebayo et al. show that visually appealing saliency can be independent of learned parameters or labels and provide model- and data-randomization tests. EXP-CAM relies on selected visual appeal and output preservation but never runs these necessary sanity checks, despite claiming model-specific internal faithfulness.

reviewed_competitors.title: New Definitions and Evaluations for Saliency Methods: Staying Intrinsic, Complete and Sound
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work formalizes intrinsic, complete, and sound saliency and scrutinizes the masked-input evaluations on which preservation methods rely. EXP-CAM combines several intuitive proxy losses but does not test completeness or soundness, leaving its baseline and perturbation semantics underdetermined.

reviewed_competitors.title: Towards Automated Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability
reviewed_competitors.difference: ACDC defines circuits as computational subgraphs and validates edge removal by activation patching and retained task metrics, rediscovering known transformer components. EXP-CAM's channel graph is cheaper and tied to one image explanation, but it ranks activations and weights without ever testing the returned subgraph's causal sufficiency.

reviewed_competitors.title: Automatic Discovery of Visual Circuits
reviewed_competitors.difference: This visual-circuit method specifies concepts with multiple examples, traces functional connectivity across layers, tests causal output effects, and edits circuits to improve adversarial robustness. EXP-CAM instead derives a per-image top-energy graph with no causal intervention, so it offers local visualization but substantially weaker evidence that the edges implement recognition.

reviewed_competitors.title: Formal Mechanistic Interpretability: Automated Circuit Discovery with Provable Guarantees
reviewed_competitors.difference: This ICLR 2026 work uses neural-network verification to certify circuit agreement over continuous input regions, robust patching, and several notions of minimality for vision models. It directly supplies the formal causal guarantees EXP-CAM claims rhetorically but identifies as future work, at higher verification cost and with a more restricted formal setup.

reviewed_competitors.title: InterpBench: Semi-Synthetic Transformers for Evaluating Mechanistic Interpretability Techniques
reviewed_competitors.difference: InterpBench provides realistic semi-synthetic transformers with known circuits and evaluates discovery precision against ground truth. Although transformer-focused, it establishes the kind of circuit-level validation EXP-CAM lacks; a visual analogue would reveal whether energy-ranked channel graphs recover actual mechanisms.

reviewed_competitors.title: W-Kernel and Its Principal Space for Frequentist Evaluation of Bayesian Estimators
reviewed_competitors.difference: Iba defines the observation-wise posterior log-likelihood covariance matrix W, explicitly calls it a reproducing kernel, studies its principal space, and relates it to the Fisher kernel. The loss kernel is this object extended to a localized deep-network probe and arbitrary evaluation points, then visualized with UMAP; the manuscript's introduction claim should be narrowed accordingly.

reviewed_competitors.title: Bayesian Influence Functions for Hessian-Free Data Attribution
reviewed_competitors.difference: The same-author companion defines local BIF between a training and query loss as negative covariance under the same localized Gibbs probe, prints the beta-correct SGLD update, and validates against retraining and EK-FAC up to billion-parameter models. The loss-kernel paper symmetrizes the train/query roles and emphasizes global maps but offers weaker causal attribution validation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Daunce: Data Attribution through Uncertainty Estimation
reviewed_competitors.difference: Daunce independently computes covariance of per-example losses across perturbed fine-tuned models, the same scoring primitive, and evaluates attribution on vision, LLM fine-tuning, and black-box models. Its perturbation ensemble and TDA focus differ from local SGLD geometry, but it makes a direct empirical competitor for scalability and retraining fidelity.

reviewed_competitors.title: Input Similarity from the Neural Network Perspective
reviewed_competitors.difference: Charpiat et al. ask nearly the identical interpretability question and define input similarity by how a parameter variation designed to change one input affects another, yielding a normalized gradient/Jacobian kernel. It is a cheap first-order baseline for whether loss covariance discovers anything beyond local parameter sensitivity.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization in Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: NTK is the Gram kernel of output parameter gradients and describes function-space response to gradient descent. A local quadratic expansion makes the loss kernel a Hessian-weighted per-loss gradient Gram matrix and, at large gamma, a normalized gradient kernel, so NTK-style baselines delimit the higher-order claim.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding Black-box Predictions via Influence Functions
reviewed_competitors.difference: Koh and Liang trace test behavior to training points with inverse-Hessian-weighted gradient interactions and validate uses such as debugging and detecting mislabeled data. The loss kernel avoids explicit Hessian inversion through sampling but does not test its ImageNet similarities against retraining or removal effects.

reviewed_competitors.title: Estimating Training Data Influence by Tracing Gradient Descent
reviewed_competitors.difference: TracIn aggregates per-example gradient dot products across ordinary training checkpoints and directly targets how a training example changes query loss. It supplies a far cheaper checkpoint-path kernel and a necessary comparison for both functional coupling and developmental analysis.

reviewed_competitors.title: TRAK: Attributing Model Behavior at Scale
reviewed_competitors.difference: TRAK uses randomly projected after-kernel features and a small ensemble to approximate counterfactual data attribution at ImageNet and language-model scale. Unlike the loss-kernel evaluation, it benchmarks against retraining-derived datamodel scores; loss covariance should be compared at matched compute and query volume.

reviewed_competitors.title: Datamodels: Understanding Predictions with Data and Data with Predictions
reviewed_competitors.difference: Datamodels learn how outputs vary across training subsets and produce data embeddings, semantic neighbors, brittleness measures, and counterfactual predictions. They are expensive but causal with respect to dataset composition, whereas loss-kernel perturbations vary parameters while holding the dataset fixed.

reviewed_competitors.title: Sample based Explanations via Generalized Representers
reviewed_competitors.difference: Generalized representers axiomatize sample-based explanations as global training-point importance times a local kernel similarity and compare multiple kernel choices. This framework highlights that a PSD sample kernel alone does not establish influence or explanation fidelity; the loss kernel still needs an importance or intervention validation for attribution claims.

reviewed_competitors.title: Distributional Training Data Attribution: What do Influence Functions Sample?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Distributional TDA explicitly models randomness across training runs and derives influence functions as a distributional limit, then validates data pruning and diffusion-model applications. It distinguishes stochastic training distributions from the arbitrary local posterior around one checkpoint, a distinction the loss-kernel interpretation leaves unresolved.

reviewed_competitors.title: ExPLAIND: Unifying Model, Data, and Training Attribution to Study Model Behavior
reviewed_competitors.difference: ExPLAIND generalizes exact gradient-path kernels to optimizers such as AdamW and jointly attributes behavior to data, parameters, and training steps, including a grokking study. Its explicit training-path decomposition offers a current, intervention-oriented alternative to independently sampled local loss geometry for developmental interpretability.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhu et al. analyze SGD dynamics in a bilinear model and one-layer Transformers, attributing reversal failure to asymmetric effective weights under loss and optimization choices. reviewed_competitors.title: In-context Learning and Induction Heads
reviewed_competitors.difference: Olsson et al. establish the basic previous-token-plus-induction match-and-copy circuit and provide causal evidence in small attention-only models but only correlational evidence in large models. The reviewed paper keeps successor copying but asks how a pretrained model selects among multiple successors using higher-order context and adds supporting-head ablations.

reviewed_competitors.title: In-Context Language Learning: Architectures and Algorithms
reviewed_competitors.difference: Akyurek et al. already show that earlier previous-token heads can be composed so a later n-gram head matches longer contexts, and they probe n-gram statistics and latent DFA-state equivalence in Transformers trained on regular languages. The reviewed paper's narrower increment is to locate an analogous context-selective circuit in pretrained LLMs, extend the controlled generator to a second nested chunk level, and causally ablate probe-selected supporting heads; it should not claim the general previous-token-to-higher-order-matching mechanism as wholly new.

reviewed_competitors.title: Interpretability of Language Models for Learning Hierarchical Structures
reviewed_competitors.difference: Allen-Zhu and Li study GPTs trained on locally ambiguous recursive context-free grammars and report hidden-state representations of the grammar plus attention resembling dynamic-programming message passing. That work targets a stronger form of hierarchy but not in-context adaptation of pretrained models or the context-matching-to-induction-head intervention developed here, making it a direct neighboring result that narrows any broad 'hierarchical structure' priority claim.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformers represent belief state geometry in their residual stream
reviewed_competitors.difference: Shai et al. predict and recover full belief-state geometry for hidden generators in Transformer residual streams, including distributed and fractal geometries, but explicitly do not test a causal updating circuit. The reviewed paper uses a weaker binary adjacent-context probe yet contributes attention-head-level interventions linking selected representations to hierarchical successor choice.

reviewed_competitors.title: Identifying Semantic Induction Heads to Understand In-Context Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ren et al. identify heads that retrieve syntactic-dependency and knowledge-graph relations in natural-language contexts and connect their outputs to relevant logits. The reviewed paper instead conditions token-level successor retrieval on a procedurally controlled hierarchy and identifies separate upstream context-routing heads, but its natural-language validation is substantially smaller and less causal.

reviewed_competitors.title: Which Attention Heads Matter for In-Context Learning?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yin and Steinhardt compare induction and function-vector heads across 12 models and 37 natural-language tasks, finding that function-vector heads dominate few-shot ICL in larger models after controlling for overlapping head scores. The reviewed paper provides strong task-specific evidence for induction on repetitive successor prediction, but that result cannot support a unifying claim about broad few-shot ICL without the same overlap control.

reviewed_competitors.title: Beyond Induction Heads: In-Context Meta Learning Induces Multi-Phase Circuit Emergence
reviewed_competitors.difference: Minegishi et al. train two-layer attention-only models on task inference rather than copying and find phase-dependent circuits in which early heads bind example chunks and later heads select labels, with analogous layer ordering in GPT2-XL. The reviewed paper studies pretrained models and nested repeated successors with stronger head ablations, but the broader idea of an earlier context-building stage feeding a later retrieval stage is concurrent rather than unique.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Dual-Route Model of Induction
reviewed_competitors.difference: Feucht et al. use causal mediation, ablation, and activation patching to distinguish token induction from concept-level induction that transports language-independent lexical meaning in 7B-8B models. The reviewed paper isolates context-dependent token successor selection rather than semantic multi-token copying, but the dual-route results show that attention heads can support multiple parallel induction mechanisms and provide stronger content-specific interventions to emulate.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Emergence of Induction Heads for In-Context Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Musat et al. subsequently analyze how an induction head emerges in a minimal two-layer setting, proving confinement of training dynamics to a 19-dimensional subspace, identifying a three-dimensional emergence process, and deriving quadratic context-length timing. It does not address nested contextual choice or pretrained supporting heads, but supplies the kind of training-dynamics account absent from the reviewed endpoint analysis.

The current work supplies a random-feature identifiability analysis and a concrete nd threshold for a projection attack, while extrapolating rather than proving the trained-network cases.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding Reconstruction Attacks with the Neural Tangent Kernel and Dataset Distillation
reviewed_competitors.difference: Loo et al. prove whole-training-set recovery in an infinite-width NTK setting and study which outliers are recoverable, also linking reconstruction to dataset distillation. The present paper's main advance over that asymptotic regime is a finite random-feature sufficient scaling tied to nd, but its no-duplicate theorem is only for n=2 and its finite-network transfer remains empirical.

reviewed_competitors.title: Simulating Training Dynamics to Reconstruct Training Data from Deep Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: SimuDy differentiates through simulated nonlinear training dynamics and reports reconstructing most examples from a trained ResNet, directly addressing regimes where shallow or frozen-feature dynamics fail. The projection method here is structurally simpler and motivates a capacity law, but assumes initialization and feature-span leakage and does not compare attack quality or compute head-to-head with SimuDy.

reviewed_competitors.title: Provable Privacy Attacks on Trained Shallow Neural Networks

reviewed_competitors.difference: Cai et al. diagnose clusters, centered within-cluster cosine, frequency/position structure, and local intrinsic dimension in pretrained contextual activations. Probability Signature instead targets learned input/output parameter geometry and derives conditional-distribution gradient terms, but its natural-language evidence is narrower and correlational.

reviewed_competitors.title: How Contextual are Contextualized Word Representations? Comparing the Geometry of BERT, ELMo, and GPT-2 Embeddings
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ethayarajh quantifies anisotropy, context specificity, and the small variance explained by static word identity across pretrained layers. This paper asks what data distribution creates parameter-level similarities and adds controlled training dynamics rather than describing contextual activation geometry alone.

reviewed_competitors.title: Representation Degeneration Problem in Training Natural Language Generation Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Gao et al. analyze how likelihood training with weight tying produces a narrow cone and propose a cosine regularizer with language-modeling and translation gains. Probability Signature models pair-specific organization from conditional data distributions and does not propose an isotropy regularizer or downstream improvement.

reviewed_competitors.title: Analyzing Transformers in Embedding Space
reviewed_competitors.difference: Dar et al. project trained transformer parameters into vocabulary space for zero-pass interpretation, model alignment, and classifier translation. This paper instead explains how selected embedding/unembedding similarities arise during training from data-conditionals and does not interpret every transformer block.

reviewed_competitors.title: Initialization is Critical to Whether Transformers Fit Composite Functions by Reasoning or Memorizing
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhang et al. show initialization scale selects inferential versus memorizing solutions and analyzes their information flow and vector structures. Probability Signature keeps small initialization fixed and varies conditional data distributions to attribute which statistic organizes anchors; it does not compare solution generalization regimes.

reviewed_competitors.title: Reasoning Bias of Next Token Prediction Training
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yao et al. compare next-token and critical-token objectives and attribute NTP's reasoning advantage to noise-induced regularization, validated on reasoning tasks and perturbations. Probability Signature derives adjacent-token conditional geometry under NTP but supplies no matched reasoning-performance test.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Latent Variable Model Approach to PMI-based Word Embeddings
reviewed_competitors.difference: Arora et al. derive co-occurrence statistics and linear analogy structure from a latent discourse model for static embeddings, providing a theoretical account of PMI, word2vec, and GloVe. Probability Signature treats several conditional distributions dynamically in supervised and autoregressive neural training rather than positing a static generative discourse model.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Word Embedding as Implicit Matrix Factorization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Levy and Goldberg prove that SGNS implicitly factorizes shifted PMI and compare explicit SVD/PPMI solutions on similarity and analogy tasks. Probability Signature generalizes beyond one static co-occurrence matrix to embedding and unembedding gradient dynamics, nonlinear synthetic tasks, and adjacent-token distributions in decoders, but does not offer the same optimum-level equivalence.

reviewed_competitors.title: All-but-the-Top: Simple and Effective Postprocessing for Word Representations
reviewed_competitors.difference: Mu, Bhat, and Viswanath remove the global mean and a few dominant directions from static embeddings and show downstream gains. The target extends centering to contextual clusters but does not remove local top directions or connect the adjusted geometry to task quality.

reviewed_competitors.title: How Contextual are Contextualized Word Representations? Comparing the Geometry of BERT, ELMo, and GPT-2 Embeddings
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ethayarajh establishes global anisotropy and decreasing self-similarity with depth for the same model families. The target reproduces that starting point and argues that clustering plus centering reveals a different local view.

reviewed_competitors.title: Visualizing and Measuring the Geometry of BERT
reviewed_competitors.difference: Coenen et al. combine visualization and quantitative tests to identify syntactic, semantic, and word-sense subspaces in BERT. The target broadens the model set and studies clusters/manifolds, but its manual sense inspection finds no population-level semantic organization.

reviewed_competitors.title: Intrinsic dimension of data representations in deep neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ansuini et al. show nonlinear intrinsic dimension can predict generalization and include untrained and randomized-label controls. The target imports the dimension lens into language-model token states but lacks those causal controls and behavioral correlations.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Sentence Embeddings from Pre-trained Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: BERT-flow maps sentence embeddings to a smooth isotropic Gaussian and measures gains on semantic textual similarity. It operationalizes a performance consequence of geometry, while the target only describes token-state geometry and cautions implicitly that global transforms can miss clusters.

reviewed_competitors.title: Whitening Sentence Representations for Better Semantics and Faster Retrieval
reviewed_competitors.difference: Whitening explicitly flattens covariance, reduces dimension, and evaluates semantics and retrieval speed. This is a stronger distributional operation than the target's mean subtraction, though it addresses sentence embeddings rather than token-level local manifolds.

reviewed_competitors.title: SimCSE: Simple Contrastive Learning of Sentence Embeddings
reviewed_competitors.difference: SimCSE jointly studies alignment and uniformity and reports large semantic-similarity gains from contrastive training. It demonstrates that geometric uniformity and task alignment must be assessed together, a link absent from the target's frozen-state study.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Cluster-based Approach for Improving Isotropy in Contextual Embedding Space
reviewed_competitors.difference: Rajaee and Pilehvar turn local clustering into a postprocessing method, remove cluster-specific dominant directions, and evaluate semantic tasks. They also give a concrete line-shaped GPT-2 counterexample in which centering makes average cosine look isotropic although the cloud remains directionally concentrated; their intervention is behaviorally stronger than the target's diagnosis but requires dev-tuned cluster and component counts.

reviewed_competitors.title: All Bark and No Bite: Rogue Dimensions in Transformer Language Models Obscure Representational Quality
reviewed_competitors.difference: Timkey and van Schijndel find that only one to three rogue dimensions dominate cosine and Euclidean similarity while contributing little to model behavior. This provides a sharper alternative explanation for the target's global cone and shows why both raw and recentered average-cosine conclusions need behavioral checks.

reviewed_competitors.title: IsoScore: Measuring the Uniformity of Embedding Space Utilization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Rudman et al. reproduce the target's WikiText-2 BERT, DistilBERT, GPT, and GPT-2 setting with a covariance-based utilization score, find very low isotropy throughout, and demonstrate that zero-centering can mechanically maximize average-cosine isotropy. IsoScore is global and does not settle cluster semantics or topology, but it directly overturns the target's inference from recentered mean cosine to nearly perfect isotropy.

reviewed_competitors.title: How Does Fine-tuning Affect the Geometry of Embedding Space: A Case Study on Isotropy
reviewed_competitors.difference: This study shows that fine-tuning can increase elongated directions and place essential linguistic information in them, making isotropy enhancement ineffective. It limits the target's frozen-pretraining geometry from generalizing to task-adapted representations.

reviewed_competitors.title: On Isotropy Calibration of Transformer Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ding et al. explicitly test isotropy-calibration methods and find no consistent improvement across models and tasks, interpreting the target's local-isotropy result as a reason. It supports caution against optimizing global isotropy while adding the missing behavioral evaluation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Is anisotropy really the cause of BERT embeddings not being semantic?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Fuster Baggetto and Fresno find that anisotropy is not the root cause of weak semantic isometry and analyze frequency, subword, punctuation, and case biases. This directly challenges any inference from the target's geometric isotropy score to semantic quality.

reviewed_competitors.title: The geometry of hidden representations of large transformer models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Valeriani et al. analyze dimension and neighbor composition across text, protein, and vision transformers, find expansion/contraction profiles, and relate dimension minima to semantic layer quality. Their multi-domain and behavioral layer-selection results go beyond the target's mostly monotonic older-model profile.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Shape of Learning: Anisotropy and Intrinsic Dimensions in Transformer-Based Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Razzhigaev et al. track geometry during training and find decoder anisotropy peaking in middle layers plus dimension expansion and later compression. It adds temporal evidence and a broader encoder/decoder comparison to the target's frozen final checkpoints.

reviewed_competitors.title: Anisotropy is Not Inherent to Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: Machina and Mercer identify large Pythia models with isotropic embedding spaces and trace geometry across training, showing anisotropy is not universal to transformers. This substantially widens the model and scale regime beyond the target's older base checkpoints.

reviewed_competitors.title: Isotropy, Clusters, and Classifiers
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work shows that strict isotropy is incompatible with nontrivial cluster structure and can oppose objectives that support linear classification. It makes the target's phrase 'clusters reveal isotropy' mathematically scale- and metric-dependent, while leaving open the possibility of locally centered low-rank regions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Less is More: Local Intrinsic Dimensions of Contextual Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ruppik et al. estimate heterogeneous local dimensions across modern language models and connect their shifts to exhausted training, overfitting, grokking, and later performance gains. It turns the target's descriptive LID into a candidate behavioral diagnostic and explicitly avoids relying only on one global mean.

reviewed_competitors.title: Linguistic Profiling of Transformer Embedding Geometry
reviewed_competitors.difference: Domenichelli et al. partition BERT and GPT-2 states by position, length, part of speech, head distance, and arity and report that GPT-2 anisotropy is driven by a compact cluster of sentence-initial tokens. This sharpens the target's qualitative position finding and supplies the multivariate linguistic profiling it lacked.

reviewed_competitors.title: From Directions to Regions: Decomposing Activations in Language Models via Local Geometry
reviewed_competitors.difference: Shafran et al. use mixtures of factor analyzers to model activations as regions with centroids and local covariance, then test localization and steering in Llama and Gemma. It realizes the target's local-region intuition while retaining covariance structure and validating behavioral control.

reviewed_competitors.title: Position: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational hypothesis and direct methodological predecessor that introduced crossmodal scale-convergence evidence and the mutual-neighborhood framing.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Huh et al. survey broad vision-language evidence and explicitly present a position with limitations and counterexamples. The target transfers the test to crossmatched astronomical instruments and spectra, adding a scientifically grounded domain but largely reusing the same interpretation and metric logic.

reviewed_competitors.title: Revisiting the Platonic Representation Hypothesis: An Aristotelian View
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Subsequent direct reassessment of PRH evidence and the strongest metric-level competitor to the target's size trend.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Groeger, Wen, and Brbic show that depth and width can systematically inflate similarity scores, introduce permutation-based null calibration, and find that much global convergence disappears while local neighborhood agreement remains. Because the target uses uncalibrated MKNN across scale, this work directly challenges its significance while potentially supporting a narrower local-neighborhood claim.

reviewed_competitors.title: Objective drives the consistency of representational similarity across datasets
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct PRH audit testing whether representational-similarity conclusions generalize across stimulus datasets.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ciernik et al. find that objective strongly controls cross-dataset consistency and that behavior-similarity correspondence is dataset-dependent. The target spans survey modalities but evaluates one family of crossmatched astronomical samples at a time and does not separate dataset/objective effects from scale.

reviewed_competitors.title: Not all solutions are created equal: An analytical dissociation of functional and representational similarity in deep linear neural networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct conceptual counterpoint separating representational geometry from learned function and generalization.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Braun, Grant, and Saxe prove representational similarity can coexist with functional dissimilarity and vice versa, then test nonlinear networks. This undercuts the target's jump from MKNN alignment to downstream usefulness; the target contributes real multimodal astronomy evidence but no functional equivalence test.

reviewed_competitors.title: AstroCLIP: A Cross-Modal Foundation Model for Galaxies
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct astronomical crossmodal predecessor aligning galaxy image and spectrum encoders and validating the shared space on scientific tasks.
reviewed_competitors.difference: AstroCLIP explicitly contrastively aligns Legacy images and DESI spectra, then evaluates retrieval, redshift, physical properties, and morphology. The target asks whether independently trained models align without joint training and adds multiple surveys and scale trends, but lacks AstroCLIP's functional task validation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Similarity of Neural Network Representations Revisited
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Core representation-comparison predecessor introducing centered kernel alignment and documenting metric invariance pitfalls.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kornblith et al. systematically characterize similarity measures and show CKA can identify layer correspondence across widths and seeds. The target uses only MKNN and defers CKA, so it does not establish that its conclusion is metric-robust.

reviewed_competitors.title: Revisiting Model Stitching to Compare Neural Representations
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Functional alternative to geometric similarity metrics for asking whether two learned representations are interchangeable.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bansal, Nakkiran, and Barak train a simple connector between frozen network halves and show good representations can be stitched across objectives, with stronger models improving weaker ones. The target's neighbor overlap needs no learned adapter and works crossmodal, but cannot establish functional substitution or downstream benefit.

reviewed_competitors.title: Convergent Learning: Do different neural networks learn the same representations?
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Early predecessor directly asking whether independently trained neural networks converge to shared units and subspaces.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Li et al. distinguish consistently learned individual features from shared low-dimensional subspaces with different bases. The target scales the question to foundation models and instruments and uses local neighborhoods, but should not imply that representational convergence itself is a new question.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Multimodal Universe: Enabling Large-Scale Machine Learning with 100TB of Astronomical Scientific Data
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct data and benchmark infrastructure predecessor on which the target's cross-survey experiment depends.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The Multimodal Universe assembles hundreds of millions of observations across images, spectra, time series, and metadata with benchmark tasks. The target uses its crossmatches for one representation-convergence question; much broader modality and downstream validation is already enabled but remains unexplored.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Usama and Chang report high representational agreement even on collectively failed problems, large pre- versus post-decision divergence, and low causal flip rates for shared information. Although in language rather than astronomy, it reinforces the need for causal and downstream tests before the target's MKNN trend can support claims about shared understanding or model choice.

reviewed_competitors.difference: TracIn accumulates checkpointed gradient dot products to attribute a test loss to training examples. AKG instead factorizes one-step output-distribution change into A, K, and G for qualitative mechanistic interpretation, but provides less direct attribution validation at scale.

reviewed_competitors.title: TRAK: Attributing Model Behavior at Scale
reviewed_competitors.difference: TRAK uses random projections and an after-kernel construction to approximate data attribution across trained ensembles at ImageNet and language-model scale. The thesis keeps the full local kernel conceptually and spans more training rules, but its influence estimates are mainly explanatory and smaller scale.

reviewed_competitors.title: LESS: Selecting Influential Data for Targeted Instruction Tuning
reviewed_competitors.difference: LESS builds optimizer-aware low-rank gradient features for practical instruction-data selection and reports that selected 5% subsets can outperform full data. AKG analyzes response interactions and preference dynamics rather than validating large-datastore selection.

reviewed_competitors.title: Unintentional Unalignment: Likelihood Displacement in Direct Preference Optimization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Razin et al. characterize harmful likelihood displacement through centered hidden-embedding similarity and mitigate it by filtering preference pairs. The thesis explains related downward likelihood through positive/negative forces and squeezing, then adds rejected-response SFT; both rely on representation similarity but intervene at different stages.

reviewed_competitors.title: What Do Learning Dynamics Reveal About Generalization in LLM Reasoning?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kang et al. use pre-memorization train accuracy to predict reasoning generalization and guide data curation across Llama and Gemma. The thesis offers a gradient-factor mechanism and broader finetuning coverage, but lacks an equally strong out-of-sample predictive test of its central diagnostic.

reviewed_competitors.title: Fine-Tuning can Distort Pretrained Features and Underperform Out-of-Distribution
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kumar et al. motivate linear probing before full tuning to preserve already optimal features. The thesis relaxes that endpoint by treating initial residual as adaptation energy and argues that intermediate probing can help when source features require controlled change.

reviewed_competitors.title: Alignment Dynamics in LLM Fine-Tuning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Huang et al. derive alignment-score updates as rebound and driving forces and validate reversal and rehearsal priming in safety, emergent-misalignment, and sentiment settings. It is narrower than the thesis but targets function-space alignment with a task-specific score and later empirical predictions.

reviewed_competitors.difference: The predecessor develops the video-as-decision-interface thesis and benchmarks decision settings; the focal paper broadens black-box zero-shot demonstrations across visual tasks and makes the stronger chain-of-frames claim.

reviewed_competitors.title: From Generation to Generalization: Emergent Few-Shot Learning in Video Diffusion Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Close prior evidence that video diffusion models can perform visual in-context learning beyond conventional generation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work studies few-shot examples embedded in video context and predates the focal preprint; the focal paper emphasizes zero-shot breadth through a proprietary image-to-video API.

reviewed_competitors.title: RealGeneral: Unifying Visual Generation via Temporal In-Context Learning with Video Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct prior generalist-video work using temporal in-context learning to unify visual generation tasks.
reviewed_competitors.difference: RealGeneral deliberately structures temporal demonstrations for unified generation; the focal study probes unmodified commercial models with a single input image and natural-language prompt.

reviewed_competitors.title: PixWizard: Versatile Image-to-Image Visual Assistant with Open-Language Instructions
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A general image-to-image competitor for diverse perception and manipulation tasks under open-language instructions.
reviewed_competitors.difference: PixWizard trains and evaluates a dedicated still-image visual assistant, avoiding temporal oracle selection; Veo offers a richer trajectory but is proprietary and not shown superior under matched sampling and metrics.

reviewed_competitors.title: Images Speak in Images: A Generalist Painter for In-Context Visual Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: An early generalist visual-output predecessor representing many vision tasks as image-to-image in-context completion.

reviewed_competitors.title: OmniGen: Unified Image Generation
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A unified image-generation alternative that handles varied instructions and visual conditions without the overhead of video.
reviewed_competitors.difference: OmniGen targets unified still-image generation with a simpler open architecture; the focal paper argues that temporal generation adds a reasoning workspace but does not causally isolate that benefit.

reviewed_competitors.title: Unified-IO 2: Scaling Autoregressive Multimodal Models with Vision, Language, Audio, and Action
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A generalist multimodal predecessor solving many perception, generation, and action tasks through one token interface.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Unified-IO 2 is explicitly trained and evaluated across a task mixture with inspectable modalities; the focal paper instead argues that task breadth emerges in a video generator without task-specific adaptation by the authors.

reviewed_competitors.title: Florence-2: Advancing a Unified Representation for a Variety of Vision Tasks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A compact generalist-vision baseline for prompt-based perception tasks such as detection, segmentation, and captioning.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Florence-2 provides task-oriented outputs and broad standardized evaluation; the focal paper uses pixels and motion as the output language, enabling novel demonstrations but making correctness extraction harder.

reviewed_competitors.title: Peekaboo: Text to Image Diffusion Models are Zero-Shot Segmentors
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A direct predecessor showing zero-shot spatial segmentation information in generative diffusion models.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Peekaboo derives masks from diffusion-model attention/gradients and evaluates segmentation directly; the focal system renders colored masks as video and relies on prompt following plus oracle frame selection.

reviewed_competitors.title: V-JEPA 2: Self-Supervised Video Models Enable Understanding, Prediction and Planning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A close world-model and planning competitor that evaluates video representations on understanding, prediction, and robot planning.
reviewed_competitors.difference: V-JEPA 2 supplies trained representations and closed-loop action evidence rather than visually inspecting generated movies; the focal paper has broader zero-shot demonstrations but substantially weaker causal and interactive validation.

reviewed_competitors.title: WorldModelBench: Judging Video Generation Models As World Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A direct benchmark for judging whether generated videos obey instructions and physical dynamics sufficiently to act as world models.
reviewed_competitors.difference: WorldModelBench uses roughly 67,000 human labels across 14 models and trains structured evaluators; the focal paper covers more task forms but depends on small custom scorers and qualitative author judgments.

reviewed_competitors.title: VideoPhy: Evaluating Physical Commonsense for Video Generation
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A prior benchmark directly testing instruction following and physical commonsense in generated video.
reviewed_competitors.difference: VideoPhy finds that even its best evaluated system succeeds jointly on fewer than half of prompts, providing large-scale quantitative counterweight to the focal paper's selected modeling demonstrations and motivating explicit physics metrics.

reviewed_competitors.title: How Far is Video Generation from World Model: A Physical Law Perspective
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Prior systematic evidence that video quality and physical-law consistency are distinct properties.
reviewed_competitors.difference: This benchmark targets explicit physical-law violations across generators; the focal paper interprets successful-looking trajectories as modeling ability while its own appendix reveals many such violations.

reviewed_competitors.title: Evaluating Newtonian Mechanics in Video Generative Models with Real Physical Systems
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A current real-physics stress test of video generators as simulators rather than visual storytellers.
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work grounds evaluation in controlled real physical systems and Newtonian measurements; the focal paper uses mostly visual task endpoints and anecdotal physics demonstrations.

reviewed_competitors.title: Are Video Models Ready as Zero-Shot Reasoners? An Empirical Study with the MME-CoF Benchmark
reviewed_competitors.relationship: The closest subsequent standardized audit of the focal claim across chain-of-frames reasoning dimensions.
reviewed_competitors.difference: MME-CoF evaluates multiple models on a structured 12-dimension suite and finds promise on local short-horizon tasks but substantial failures in long-horizon causality, strict geometry, and abstract logic, tempering the focal paper's broad ability framing.

reviewed_competitors.title: V-ReasonBench: Toward Unified Reasoning Benchmark Suite for Video Generation Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A subsequent unified benchmark designed to make video-generation reasoning answer-verifiable and comparable across models.
reviewed_competitors.difference: V-ReasonBench evaluates six video models, compares image models, and analyzes duration and hallucination; the focal study uses heterogeneous bespoke metrics that inhibit cross-task or cross-model conclusions.

reviewed_competitors.title: World-in-World: World Models in a Closed-Loop World
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A subsequent closed-loop evaluation of video world models in interactive environments.
reviewed_competitors.difference: World-in-World finds that visual quality does not imply task success and that controllability and action-observation post-training matter more than merely upgrading the generator; it directly addresses the open-loop limitation of the focal demonstrations.

reviewed_competitors.title: WorldReasonBench: Human-Aligned Stress Testing of Video Generators as Future World-State Predictors
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A current human-aligned stress test of causal and dynamic validity in generated future states.
reviewed_competitors.difference: WorldReasonBench uses 436 controlled cases across 22 subcategories plus structured question answering and exposes a persistent gap between plausible imagery and dynamics, causality, and information preservation that the focal metrics often conflate.

reviewed_competitors.title: OpenCoF: Learning to Reason Through Video Generation
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A current open attempt to train and release explicit chain-of-frames reasoning supervision.
reviewed_competitors.difference: OpenCoF argues that general video corpora lack diverse reasoning supervision, releases OpenCoF-17K and a fine-tuned Wan-CoF model with visual and textual reasoning tokens, and is therefore more testable than the focal proprietary emergence claim.

reviewed_competitors.title: Video Models Reason Early: Exploiting Plan Commitment for Maze Solving
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A direct mechanistic follow-up on when video models commit to maze solutions during denoising.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The follow-up reports that plans stabilize in early denoising steps, challenging a literal interpretation in which visible output frames themselves perform sequential reasoning and motivating early-plan probes absent from the focal paper.

reviewed_competitors.title: Demystifying Video Reasoning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A direct subsequent mechanistic study of where reasoning occurs inside video diffusion models.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Noise interventions and internal probes indicate that candidate solutions are resolved across diffusion denoising steps and middle transformer layers rather than sequential output frames. This supports nontrivial internal computation while replacing the focal paper's literal chain-of-frames mechanism with a chain-of-steps account.

reviewed_competitors.title: Do generative video models understand physical principles?
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A prior targeted evaluation of whether generative-video behavior reflects physical understanding.
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work directly probes physical principles and failure patterns, whereas the focal paper mixes physical demonstrations with perception and puzzle tasks and lacks a common validity metric.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Fu et al. decompose changes in generalization error across optimization updates and derive a bound based on trajectory complexity and training-set bias/diversity, with experiments tracking generalization under learning-rate and label-noise changes. The present paper studies trajectories inside feature space through checkpoint-swapped depth modules and proposes temporal augmentation rather than a parameter-update complexity measure.

reviewed_competitors.title: Residual Alignment: Uncovering the Mechanisms of Residual Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Li and Papyan characterize cross-depth residual Jacobian alignment, line-like feature trajectories, low-rank structure, and inverse-depth singular scaling that disappear without skips and correlate with generalization. The present paper instead follows representations across training time, swaps checkpoints, and links SGD noise to temporal compatibility.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformer Block Coupling and its Correlation with Generalization in LLMs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Aubry et al. trace token trajectories through transformer depth, measure Jacobian singular-vector coupling, and report correlations with model performance and training emergence. The present work studies checkpoint time rather than only forward depth and adds hybrid-module interventions, but has not demonstrated the mechanism at LLM scale.

reviewed_competitors.title: Assessing Generalization of SGD via Disagreement
reviewed_competitors.difference: Jiang et al. estimate test error from disagreement between independently SGD-trained models on unlabeled test inputs and connect the equality to ensemble calibration. The present paper measures agreement within one training run after recombining checkpoint modules, diagnosing internal feature reuse rather than cross-run output disagreement.

reviewed_competitors.title: Unsupervised Data Augmentation for Consistency Training
reviewed_competitors.difference: Xie et al. deliberately apply high-quality external augmentations to unlabeled examples and train prediction invariance, obtaining semi-supervised gains across language and vision. The present paper posits that ordinary SGD organically produces structured latent variants and primarily diagnoses rather than optimizes their consistency.

reviewed_competitors.title: Distributional Generalization: A New Kind of Generalization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Nakkiran and Bansal study how entire train and test output distributions match, including structured label-noise behavior across neural networks, kernels, and trees. The present paper moves the distributional object into an internal latent space and mixes checkpoints, but its proposed TV quantity is not yet measurable.

The reviewed work covers more graph-task formats and uses transcoders, but its token-merging label is less algorithmically specific and it does not reproduce the predecessor's scale or causal-computation tests.

reviewed_competitors.title: ALPINE: Unveiling the Planning Capability of Autoregressive Learning in Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: ALPINE gives theoretical and empirical evidence that autoregressive Transformers store adjacency and incomplete reachability matrices for path finding and identifies a transitivity/concatenation failure. The reviewed paper reframes edge aggregation and backbone recall through circuit traces and adds attributed and substructure tasks, but offers no comparable theory or direct test of transitive reachability.

reviewed_competitors.title: From Sequence to Structure: Uncovering Substructure Reasoning in Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: Dai et al. already describe layerwise Induced Substructure Filtration through empirical and theoretical analysis and extend it to attributed and molecular graphs. The reviewed paper applies a newer circuit-tracing visualization and joins substructure extraction with path tasks, but progressive token merging substantially overlaps the earlier filtration account and the present synthetic scope is narrower than the predecessor's molecular demonstration.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding Transformer Reasoning Capabilities via Graph Algorithms
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sanford et al. separate nine algorithmic tasks by the depth, width, and extra-token scaling regimes needed to solve them, prove logarithmic-depth requirements for connectivity, and validate on GraphQA. The reviewed paper instead offers descriptive internal traces in one five-layer family; its two width settings do not test the representational hierarchy or distinguish capacity from learned shortcut.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Dunefsky et al. develop weights-based transcoder circuit analysis through MLPs and evaluate sparsity, faithfulness, and interpretability on language models from 120M to 1.4B parameters. The reviewed work applies cross-layer transcoders to graph tasks but does not report those foundational fidelity metrics or show that highlighted graph features are causally necessary for the original model.
