reviewed_competitors.title: Extrapolation and learning equations
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A direct predecessor that learns compositions of analytic functions in an end-to-end differentiable network for interpretable equation recovery.
reviewed_competitors.difference: EQL uses sparsity to select concise analytical expressions and explicitly tests extrapolation and source-equation recovery. CFN offers a broader software library and composition taxonomy, but its showcased physics task supplies the exact sinusoidal structure and does not compare with EQL.

reviewed_competitors.title: KAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: The closest recent high-profile alternative to MLPs built from visualizable compositional functions and applied to scientific-law rediscovery.
reviewed_competitors.difference: KAN learns univariate spline functions on edges and supplies scaling-law, fitting, PDE, and interactive interpretability studies. CFN chooses heterogeneous semantic node types and richer flow operators, but omits KAN from related work and provides weaker controlled evidence for accuracy and interpretation.

reviewed_competitors.title: GAMI-Net: An Explainable Neural Network based on Generalized Additive Models with Structured Interactions
reviewed_competitors.relationship: An intrinsically explainable neural model that directly contradicts the suggestion that existing interpretable approaches are confined to simple additive effects.
reviewed_competitors.difference: GAMI-Net includes sparse main effects and pairwise interactions with heredity and marginal-clarity constraints, addressing identifiability of interpretations. CFN permits arbitrary deeper compositions and mixtures but supplies no corresponding clarity or sparsity guarantees.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Additive Models: Interpretable Machine Learning with Neural Nets
reviewed_competitors.relationship: The cited differentiable additive-model baseline that establishes a clearer, feature-wise form of intrinsic neural interpretability.
reviewed_competitors.difference: NAM deliberately limits interactions so each feature shape can be plotted and audited, and evaluates across a broader task set. CFN gains interaction expressiveness through composition, but that expressiveness removes the simple feature-attribution semantics unless additional constraints and tests are added.

reviewed_competitors.title: Deep Lattice Networks and Partial Monotonic Functions
reviewed_competitors.relationship: An earlier gradient-trained deep composition of semantically constrained calibrators, lattices, and linear embeddings.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Deep lattices sacrifice unrestricted function choice to provide verifiable monotonicity with respect to specified inputs and report controlled benchmarks. CFN supports more node types and graph patterns but provides no comparable behavioral guarantee.

reviewed_competitors.title: Towards Robust Interpretability with Self-Explaining Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A primary framework for testing whether an intrinsically explanatory neural architecture is explicit, faithful, and stable.
reviewed_competitors.difference: SENN designs and regularizes models around stated explanation desiderata and evaluates them. CFN treats known mathematical node types as sufficient for interpretability, without measuring whether composed explanations satisfy these criteria.

reviewed_competitors.title: Concept Bottleneck Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A cited intrinsic vision-model alternative that makes intermediate variables human-named and supports interventions.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Concept bottlenecks require concept supervision but can test semantics by editing concepts and propagating predictions. Hybrid DeepCFN avoids concept labels yet offers no evidence that its convolution and SE nodes correspond to concepts or enable useful interventions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Science with PySR and SymbolicRegression.jl
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A mature symbolic-regression system and benchmark for discovering explicit scientific expressions when structure is unknown.
reviewed_competitors.difference: PySR searches, simplifies, and optimizes expression populations and evaluates historical equation recovery with EmpiricalBench, trading differentiable end-to-end training for structural discovery. CFN is faster to optimize once a graph is chosen but does not validate automated structure recovery.

reviewed_competitors.title: Data Free Metrics Are Not Reparameterisation Invariant Under the Critical and Robust Layer Phenomena
reviewed_competitors.difference: Mason-Williams, Mason-Williams, and Dahlqvist directly test data-free weight metrics under reinitialization and rerandomization controls and find lost predictive capacity. SETOL does not test reparameterization invariance, although its determinant and scale-adjusted metrics can change while network behavior does not.

reviewed_competitors.title: Random matrix analysis of deep neural network weight matrices
reviewed_competitors.difference: Thamm, Staats, and Rosenow use RMT eigenvalue and eigenvector statistics plus a Hill tail estimator and conclude that large singular values generally cannot be characterized by one tail index. SETOL instead treats a fitted power-law alpha as the central state and quality variable.

reviewed_competitors.title: From Spikes to Heavy Tails: Unveiling the Spectral Evolution of Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kothapalli et al. study how optimizer-dependent large learning rates produce bulk-plus-spike and heavy-tail spectral evolution in a controlled two-layer setting without gradient noise, with released code. SETOL starts from a heavy-tailed Student ensemble and seeks a data-free accuracy interpretation rather than deriving training-time spectral evolution.

reviewed_competitors.title: Models of Heavy-Tailed Mechanistic Universality
reviewed_competitors.difference: Hodgkinson, Wang, and Mahoney propose a high-temperature Marchenko-Pastur ensemble in which data correlations, training temperature, and eigenvector entropy generate heavy tails through an eigenvalue-repulsion parameter. It offers a generative random-matrix mechanism but does not equate a determinant-selected subspace with generalization accuracy.

reviewed_competitors.title: In Search of Robust Measures of Generalization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Dziugaite et al. require generalization measures to predict paired-network changes robustly across intervention environments and show that average correlations can conceal complete failures. SETOL reports favorable within-sweep trends and same-spectrum cutoff concordance without worst-case sign tests or held-out environments.

reviewed_competitors.title: Fantastic Generalization Measures and Where to Find Them
reviewed_competitors.difference: Jiang et al. compare more than forty measures over more than ten thousand controlled CNN trainings and explicitly search for conditional or potentially causal relationships. SETOL's empirical foundation is one MNIST MLP plus observational pooling of pretrained layers.

reviewed_competitors.title: On Generalization Bounds for Neural Networks with Low Rank Layers
reviewed_competitors.difference: Pinto, Rangamani, and Poggio use Gaussian-complexity chain rules to prove sample-dependent bounds for rank- and spectral-norm-constrained deep networks. This supplies a formal low-rank route to generalization without a power-law fit, annealed Teacher construction, or determinant-one cutoff.

reviewed_competitors.title: Generalization Bounds for Rank-sparse Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ledent, Alves, and Lei prove generalization bounds that interpolate between rank and norm regimes through Schatten-p quasi-norms and compare them empirically with parameter and norm bounds. SETOL also invokes Schatten-like quantities but obtains them through heuristic R-transform substitutions and does not provide a risk bound.

reviewed_competitors.title: Spectrally-normalized margin bounds for neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bartlett, Foster, and Telgarsky derive a multiclass risk bound from the product of layer spectral norms, correction norms, input scale, and observed margins. Unlike SETOL it is function- and data-aware and mathematically bounds risk, but it cannot operate without examples and may be numerically loose.

reviewed_competitors.title: Implicit Self-Regularization in Deep Neural Networks: Evidence from Random Matrix Theory and Implications for Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Martin and Mahoney introduce the 5+1 spectral phases and heavy-tailed self-regularization evidence on trained networks. SETOL's novelty is its attempted Student-Teacher, HCIZ, and determinant-cutoff explanation of those earlier Alpha-style diagnostics, not discovery of the phenomenology itself.

reviewed_competitors.title: NormFormer: Improved Transformer Pretraining with Extra Normalization
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest prior architecture that inserts normalization inside Transformer sublayers to correct gradient-magnitude imbalance.
reviewed_competitors.difference: NormFormer adds post-attention normalization, head-wise scaling, and an FFN-interior LayerNorm and reports faster/better causal and masked pretraining from 125M to 2.7B with Adam-family optimization. DNT adds embedding, query/key, and residual-branch normalization specifically to make mSGDW viable, but does not compare against NormFormer's placements or scale its language data as broadly.

reviewed_competitors.title: nGPT: Normalized Transformer with Representation Learning on the Hypersphere
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest contemporary deeply normalized Transformer and explicitly discussed architectural alternative.
reviewed_competitors.difference: nGPT constrains embeddings, matrix-vector directions, and hidden states to unit hyperspheres with learned residual step sizes and reports 4-20x step reductions. DNT leaves weights unconstrained, normalizes selected activations, and targets Adam-free momentum training with a Jacobian/heavy-tail explanation; its gains are much smaller and its theory contains an omitted normalization chain rule.

reviewed_competitors.title: Is your batch size the problem? Revisiting the Adam-SGD gap in language modeling
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct pre-existing investigation of the same Adam-SGD language-model gap and its proposed heavy-tail explanation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sreckovic et al. extensively tune momentum, clipping, and batch size and find momentum SGD can approach Adam at small batch; they report that heavy-tailed class imbalance, directional sharpness, and Hessian heterogeneity do not directly explain the gap. DNT changes architecture at large effective batches and assumes gradient tails are the main cause without testing batch-size controls.

reviewed_competitors.title: Small Batch Size Training for Language Models: When Vanilla SGD Works, and Why Gradient Accumulation Is Wasteful
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Near-concurrent competing route to stable state-free SGD language-model training without modifying Transformer normalization.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Marek et al. use very small batches and token-time scaling of Adam moments, showing even vanilla SGD without momentum can train stably and efficiently. DNT instead preserves large accumulated batches, modifies the architecture, and uses momentum SGDW; comparing the two at matched tokens, FLOPs, and wall time would separate architectural from noise-scale effects.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformers without Normalization
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporary architectural counterpoint showing that widespread normalization is not necessary for competitive Transformer training.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhu et al. replace normalization with elementwise Dynamic Tanh across vision, language, supervised, self-supervised, and generative settings. DNT argues that several carefully placed normalizers are precisely what make simple momentum optimization possible; a DyT+mSGDW control would test whether bounded nonlinearities rather than normalization-specific Jacobians are sufficient.

reviewed_competitors.title: Revisiting the Adam-SGD Gap in LLM Pre-Training: The Role of Large Effective Learning Rates
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later direct explanation and intervention for the same optimizer gap at approximately 1B-parameter Llama scale.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Glentis et al. attribute much of the gap to SGD's inability to sustain Adam-like effective learning rates because of output-class imbalance and gradient spikes, then recover most performance with clipping while retaining the conventional architecture. DNT reaches large raw mSGDW learning rates through normalization but neither isolates effective update size nor compares against the simpler clipping intervention.

reviewed_competitors.relationship: Central competing philosophical account of whether text-trained systems can learn meaning.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bender and Koller distinguish form from communicative intent and argue that text alone is insufficient for meaning; Santoro et al. agree on richer interaction but define symbolic fluency through convention-sensitive behavior rather than a formal meaning criterion.

reviewed_competitors.title: Pragmatic Norms Are All You Need – Why The Symbol Grounding Problem Does Not Apply to LLMs
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later philosophical challenge to treating symbol grounding as an LLM deficit.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Gubelmann argues that pragmatic norms can support language meaning and dissolves the classical grounding problem under alternative semantics; the reviewed paper treats active convention participation and richer sociocultural interaction as missing competencies to cultivate.

reviewed_competitors.title: Do Multimodal Large Language Models and Humans Ground Language Similarly?
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Empirical human-model comparison of embodied grounding in multimodal LLMs.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Jones et al. use preregistered sensorimotor simulation experiments to operationalize one grounding hypothesis; Santoro et al. propose a wider convention-centered taxonomy but provide no comparable measurement protocol.

reviewed_competitors.title: Emergent social conventions and collective bias in LLM populations
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct later test of decentralized convention formation in LLM agent populations.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ashery et al. operationalize arbitrary agreement with naming games and measure convergence, bias, and committed minorities; the reviewed paper anticipated this social route but demands broader construction, revision, embeddedness, and meaningful explanation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Emergent LLM behaviors are observationally equivalent to data leakage
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct methodological rebuttal to interpreting LLM naming-game convergence as emergent convention formation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Barrie and Tornberg show that task recognition and pretraining recall can reproduce the same observations, exposing a validation gap in purely behavioral convention tests and motivating stronger novelty controls for the reviewed agenda.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Mechanistic Emergence of Symbol Grounding in Language Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current behavioral and mechanistic study of grounding emergence in language models.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The 2025 work combines behavior with internal mechanism to predict grounding reliability; the reviewed paper is intentionally mechanism-neutral and therefore needs independent causal controls to distinguish imitation from grounded competence.

reviewed_competitors.title: Do Language Models Have Semantics? On the Five Standard Positions
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current synthesis of inferential, referential, internal-causal, and external-causal semantics for LLMs and chatbots.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sogaard separates multiple semantic attribution positions and argues for a hybrid sixth view; the reviewed paper centers conventional behavior, leaving these distinct semantics and their evidence requirements less differentiated.

reviewed_competitors.title: Infinite Feature Selection
reviewed_competitors.relationship: The primary method on which the reviewed paper bases its origin and superset thesis.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The accepted ICCV paper defines an undirected dataset-level feature graph from standard deviation and Spearman correlation, computes one global resolvent ranking, and evaluates feature selection. It does not define arbitrary token operators, per-example affinities, query-key-value aggregation, or self-attention.

reviewed_competitors.title: Infinite Latent Feature Selection: A Probabilistic Latent Graph-Based Ranking Approach
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Learned-affinity extension invoked to broaden Inf-FS beyond its original handcrafted graph.
reviewed_competitors.difference: ILFS learns one training-set feature graph with a supervised PLSA-inspired model and still returns a global feature ranking. It is learned but not dynamically recomputed as token self-attention for each input.

reviewed_competitors.title: Infinite Feature Selection: A Graph-based Feature Filtering Approach
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Mature Inf-FS framework and Markov-chain account cited as evidence for general affinity-based ranking.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It supports customizable dataset-level feature relations, supervised and unsupervised rankings, and empirical benchmarks, but remains a filtering operator rather than a Transformer layer.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Earlier learned compatibility-and-weighted-value mechanism in neural sequence modeling.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bahdanau attention is cross-attention rather than self-attention, but its input-dependent learned weights and value aggregation are functionally closer to Transformer attention and predate Inf-FS.

reviewed_competitors.title: Attentional Neural Network: Feature Selection Using Cognitive Feedback
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Earlier neural feature-selection mechanism already framed explicitly as attention.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It uses top-down cognitive bias to gate learned features and was published at NeurIPS 2014, directly weakening the claim that 2015 Inf-FS first established attention-like feature weighting.

reviewed_competitors.title: Long Short-Term Memory-Networks for Machine Reading
reviewed_competitors.difference: It explicitly lets sequence positions attend within a memory-augmented recurrent model; unlike Inf-FS, it is input-conditioned and produces contextual sequence representations.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Structured Self-attentive Sentence Embedding
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Pre-Transformer work explicitly using multiple learned self-attention views over a sentence.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It provides an actual neural self-attention operator and empirical task evaluation, whereas the reviewed manuscript retroactively groups such operators under Inf-FS without an equivalence proof.

reviewed_competitors.title: Attention Is All You Need
reviewed_competitors.relationship: The canonical Transformer self-attention formulation being reinterpreted.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It defines learned query, key, and value projections, masks, multi-head aggregation, residual blocks, and end-to-end experiments. It does not cite Inf-FS, so it supports functional comparison but not historical transmission.

reviewed_competitors.title: Non-local Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A closer general operator that explicitly treats self-attention as a special case of non-local weighted aggregation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The non-local family preserves attention's pairwise weight-and-value output and explores several affinity functions with experiments. It therefore substantiates a super-family relation more directly than Inf-FS scalar centrality does.

reviewed_competitors.title: Graph Attention Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Sparse graph message-passing instantiation of learned attention.
reviewed_competitors.difference: GAT learns directed neighbor-specific coefficients and aggregates transformed node values on a supplied graph; it offers a direct message-passing formalism rather than Inf-FS global ranking.

reviewed_competitors.title: Set Transformer: A Framework for Attention-based Permutation-Invariant Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Attention framework for unordered sets, close to the paper's element-agnostic affinity thesis.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It supplies permutation-equivariant/invariant constructions, induced attention for scalability, theory, and experiments; the reviewed paper provides only a post hoc analogy.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformer Dissection: A Unified Understanding of Transformer's Attention via the Lens of Kernel
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Established unifying account of attention as kernel smoothing over inputs.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The kernel view is type-aligned with normalized affinity-weighted values and yields new attention compositions plus experiments. It is a closer and better validated unification than feature-centrality ranking.

reviewed_competitors.title: Attention is not Explanation
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct challenge to the manuscript's interpretation of attention weights as importance and interpretability.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It empirically finds attention weights can diverge from gradient importance and can change without changing outputs, showing why dense attention should not automatically be called feature selection or explanation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Concrete Autoencoders for Differentiable Feature Selection and Reconstruction
reviewed_competitors.difference: Concrete selectors learn an actual discrete subset through a continuous relaxation, clarifying the distinction between selecting support and densely mixing every token with soft attention.

reviewed_competitors.title: Hopfield Networks is All You Need
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Formal connection between attention and associative-memory energy dynamics.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It derives an explicit equivalence to modern Hopfield updates, analyzes convergence and storage, and evaluates models; the reviewed paper offers no comparable derivation for Inf-FS.

reviewed_competitors.title: Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Historical and formal predecessor account tying linear attention to 1990s fast-weight programming.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It proves an operator equivalence and tests improved update rules, providing both historical evidence and mathematics absent from the Inf-FS origin narrative.

reviewed_competitors.title: Geometric Deep Learning: Grids, Groups, Graphs, Geodesics, and Gauges
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Broad established framework positioning attention inside message passing and latent graph inference.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It states Transformers can be posed exactly as attentional GNNs over a complete graph while carefully treating equivariance and positional information. This is more formal and less method-specific than the reviewed affinity taxonomy.

reviewed_competitors.title: Sequential Attention for Feature Selection
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Actual ICLR 2023 attention-based feature-selection work that the manuscript attempts to cite.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It uses attention weights as a greedy forward-selection proxy, relates a linear version to orthogonal matching pursuit, and evaluates feature subsets. The reviewed bibliography gives it the wrong title and authors.

reviewed_competitors.title: The underlying structures of self-attention: symmetry, directionality, and emergent dynamics in Transformer training
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporary mathematical analysis of attention matrices across objectives and modalities.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It derives and validates how bidirectional and autoregressive objectives induce different symmetry and directionality, properties ignored by a comparison based on undirected Inf-FS affinities.

reviewed_competitors.title: Self-Attention And Beyond the Infinite: Towards Linear Transformers with Infinite Self-Attention
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct 2026 follow-up by the reviewed paper's author that operationalizes the proposed bridge.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It defines an actual content-adaptive Neumann diffusion operator, derives a linear approximation, and reports ImageNet, shift, throughput, energy, eigenvector-match, and extreme-resolution results. Those formal and empirical contributions are absent from the 2025 position paper.

reviewed_competitors.title: Recurrent Networks: Second Order Properties and Pruning
reviewed_competitors.difference: This early work studies Hessians and Optimal Brain Surgeon pruning in a fully recurrent architecture that contains feedforward networks as a special case, reporting preserved internal memory. The present paper's distinctive target is emergent weighted acyclicity under simpler pruning, but the broad claim that recurrent pruning had not been investigated is not defensible without engaging this precedent.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Hierarchical Information Flow with Recurrent Neural Modules
reviewed_competitors.difference: ThalNet learns routing among recurrent modules and observes hierarchical chains, feedforward networks, skip connections, and novel patterns on sequential benchmarks. It hard-wires modular routing machinery but learns functional information flow; the pruning paper starts from denser unit-level recurrence and measures static topology on toy functions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Using Noise to Probe Recurrent Neural Network Structure and Prune Synapses
reviewed_competitors.difference: Noise-prune derives a local biologically inspired rule from graph sparsification and proves spectral/dynamical preservation for classes of linear and rectified-linear recurrent networks at extreme sparsity. The orderedness work uses global magnitude masks and measures acyclicity without dynamics guarantees; noise-prune is the stronger recurrent-pruning baseline omitted from its experiments.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: Finding Sparse, Trainable Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lottery-ticket pruning asks whether sparse subnetworks preserve dense-model trainability and accuracy under favorable initialization. The present study instead asks what topology magnitude pruning reveals inside tied recurrence; it cites the hypothesis but does not apply its stronger performance protocols or resetting controls.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Sculpting: Uncovering Hierarchically Modular Task Structure in Neural Networks through Pruning and Network Analysis
reviewed_competitors.difference: Neural Sculpting iteratively prunes units and edges, detects modules, and validates recovered hierarchical subfunctions across Boolean and MNIST vision tasks. It studies feedforward networks rather than tied recurrence, but provides much stronger task-structure validation than a scalar orderedness score and substantially narrows the claimed novelty around pruning-induced hierarchy.

reviewed_competitors.title: Weight-sparse Transformers Have Interpretable Circuits
reviewed_competitors.difference: This later work trains weight-sparse transformers, extracts task circuits, validates natural concepts and causal connectivity, and measures an explicit capability-interpretability frontier at scale. It supports sparsity as a structural inductive bias while showing the rigorous functional validation and performance tradeoff analysis missing from the orderedness toy study.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Graphon Limit Hypothesis: Understanding Neural Network Pruning via Infinite Width Analysis
reviewed_competitors.difference: The Graphon Limit Hypothesis characterizes masks induced by pruning methods as limiting graphons and connects their spectra to trainability through a graphon neural tangent kernel. It offers a route to analyze topology-specific pruning effects beyond tiny graphs; the orderedness work provides an empirical finite-width hypothesis that such theory could test.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scikit-dimension: a Python package for intrinsic dimension estimation
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct software and benchmark predecessor providing a uniform API, synthetic generators, tests and a comparison over more than 500 real and synthetic datasets.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The reviewed paper builds on an augmented fork and adds several estimators plus deeper known-ground-truth hyperparameter, noise and curvature studies, but it is not the first unified package or broad benchmark.

reviewed_competitors.title: LIDL: Local Intrinsic Dimension Estimation Using Approximate Likelihood
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Learned likelihood competitor for local intrinsic dimension in very high ambient dimension.
reviewed_competitors.difference: LIDL reports scaling to thousands of dimensions and lies outside the main benchmark; it broadens the method space but introduces density-model, ambient-extension, architecture and noise-scale dependence.

reviewed_competitors.title: CA-PCA: Manifold Dimension Estimation, Adapted for Curvature
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Pre-submission curvature-adapted PCA method directly relevant to the survey's tangential-estimator curvature study.
reviewed_competitors.difference: CA-PCA calibrates spectra against a quadratic rather than flat local model; its omission means the lPCA-versus-MLE experiment does not cover the main curvature-specific tangential alternative.

reviewed_competitors.title: Diffusion Models Encode the Intrinsic Dimension of Data Manifolds
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Score-based theoretical and empirical competitor that extracts normal-bundle dimension information from diffusion models.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It targets image-scale learned distributions and a different information regime than nearest-neighbor estimators, but its training, representation and diffusion-time choices are additional sources of uncertainty absent from the classical benchmark.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Geometric View of Data Complexity: Efficient Local Intrinsic Dimension Estimation with Diffusion Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: FLIPD is a direct modern local-dimension competitor based on a Fokker-Planck identity and one pretrained diffusion model.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It supports mixed-dimensional synthetic and large image settings omitted by the survey and can operate at Stable Diffusion scale, but its estimates remain sensitive to architecture and the diffusion-time or noise-scale choice.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scale adaptive and robust intrinsic dimension estimation via optimal neighbourhood identification
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Adaptive-neighborhood competitor that directly attacks the scale, noise and curvature tradeoff emphasized by the survey.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Its ABIDE procedure selects the largest locally constant-density neighborhood without a ground-truth dimension oracle, but it is specialized to constant-dimensional smooth manifolds and nearest-neighbor likelihood assumptions rather than universal method selection.

reviewed_competitors.title: Intrinsic Dimension Estimation Using Wasserstein Distances
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Theory-focused estimator with finite-sample nonasymptotic guarantees based on Wasserstein distances between empirical measures.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The survey mentions this family but does not benchmark it; it offers guarantees under explicit assumptions rather than the paper's broad empirical ranking, at higher computational and modeling cost.

reviewed_competitors.title: Topological Singularity Detection at Multiple Scales
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Multi-scale local method that jointly estimates intrinsic dimension and deviation from Euclidean manifold structure.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It can flag singular or non-manifold regions rather than presuming one smooth global dimension, directly addressing a benchmark assumption left largely untested in the reviewed paper.

reviewed_competitors.title: CW Complex Hypothesis for Image Data
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Competing structural hypothesis and empirical study in which local intrinsic dimension varies across points within a connected image-data component.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It challenges the constant smooth-manifold target underlying most of the survey benchmark and motivates stratified or cell-complex outputs instead of a single ground-truth d.

reviewed_competitors.title: Robust estimation of the intrinsic dimension of data sets with quantum cognition machine learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Spectral-gap estimator emphasizing robustness to noise and evaluations on real datasets.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It extends beyond the survey's narrow synthetic noise generators, but has its own Hilbert-space dimension and loss choices and is mentioned only briefly rather than included in the matched cohort.

reviewed_competitors.title: On consistent estimation of dimension values
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporaneous theory competitor proving consistency and some rates for Minkowski, correlation and pointwise-dimension estimators.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It contributes formal guarantees and an empirical study where the reviewed paper primarily synthesizes prior theory and supplies a wider implementation benchmark.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Survey and Comparative Evaluation of Intrinsic Dimension Estimators under the Manifold Hypothesis
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Independent direct successor survey with eighteen manifolds, one hundred replicates, nonuniformity, noise and real ISOMAP, MNIST and ISOLET studies.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Its stability-based per-dataset tuning and different estimator panel recommend CA-PCA and TwoNN as defaults with DANCo as a third opinion, demonstrating that recommendations depend strongly on cohort, tuning and benchmark design.

reviewed_competitors.title: Quantum-inspired Benchmark for Estimating Intrinsic Dimension
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct successor benchmark using infinite families of topologically nontrivial homogeneous spaces, multiple embeddings, controllable curvature and noise, and a fractal case.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Six estimators are generally less accurate on QuIIEst than on standard benchmarks under equal resources, supporting the survey's anti-universality message while showing that its inherited sphere-and-cube-like suite is not sufficiently discriminating.

reviewed_competitors.title: Score-based Pullback Riemannian Geometry: Extracting the Data Manifold Geometry using Anisotropic Flows
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Geometry-rich score-model alternative that estimates tangent geometry, metric, charts, geodesics and intrinsic dimension jointly.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It moves beyond scalar dimension estimation toward recovering manifold geometry from learned anisotropic flows, at the cost of model training and score-quality assumptions absent from classical estimators.

reviewed_competitors.title: Mutual Information and Task-Relevant Latent Dimensionality
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Successor that changes the estimand from geometric support dimension to the number of latent directions informative for a downstream task.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It addresses cases where noise or nuisance variation makes classical support dimension unhelpful; it is not a drop-in replacement because task-relevant dimension answers a different question.

reviewed_competitors.title: Local Hessian Spectral Filtering for Robust Intrinsic Dimension Estimation
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later score-and-Hessian method designed for robust high-codimension local dimension estimation with stochastic spectral computation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It targets aggregate-signal failures of LIDL and FLIPD and reports improved synthetic and real robustness, so the survey's nonlinear-above-six finding should remain explicitly limited to its tested methods rather than projected onto later approaches.

reviewed_competitors.title: Universal Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: Dehghani et al. recurrently apply a shared self-attentive transition across depth and incorporate adaptive computation, directly anticipating parameter-efficient, input-dependent encoder iteration. SELF narrows recurrence to Q/K alignment with static values inside every layer and freezes elements locally, but does not compare against a Universal Transformer or establish a corresponding computational universality result.

reviewed_competitors.title: Deep Equilibrium Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bai, Kolter, and Koltun already apply root-solved equilibrium models to weight-tied self-attention Transformers, derive implicit gradients, report constant activation memory, release code, and evaluate controlled language models including WikiText-103. SELF explicitly iterates only the alignment-state update and uses early freezing, but its convergence and backward formulas are less complete and it does not compare accuracy, solver time, or residuals with DEQ attention.

reviewed_competitors.title: PonderNet: Learning to Ponder
reviewed_competitors.difference: PonderNet learns a distribution over computation steps and explicitly optimizes the accuracy-compute tradeoff, demonstrating extrapolation and compute savings. SELF uses an unlearned numerical residual threshold with no ponder cost or budget; it is simpler, but it never validates that its stopping time tracks task difficulty or produces a favorable compute frontier.

reviewed_competitors.title: Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically Allocating Compute in Transformer-Based Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Mixture-of-Depths routes a fixed top-k token budget through blocks, retaining a static graph and predictable total FLOPs while reporting matched-FLOP and wall-clock comparisons. SELF instead varies recurrent steps according to convergence and claims parameter/memory efficiency, but offers neither a hard budget nor a controlled wall-clock comparison and can reach 100 dense attention iterations.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: arXiv version available on checked date

reviewed_competitors.title: Looped Transformers are Better at Learning Learning Algorithms
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yang et al. loop Transformer blocks and train them to emulate iterative data-fitting algorithms, obtaining comparable performance to standard Transformers with under 10% of the parameters. SELF loops attention inside each encoder layer and asserts latent reasoning from generic tasks; the looped-Transformer work supplies a more direct algorithmic test, while SELF offers per-input numerical stopping but no identified learned algorithm.

reviewed_competitors.title: On Expressive Power of Looped Transformers: Theoretical Analysis and Enhancement via Timestep Encoding
reviewed_competitors.difference: Xu and Sato prove an approximation-rate result for looped Transformers, identify saturation from exact weight tying, and use timestep-conditioned scaling to improve expressivity. SELF motivates itself with circuit expressivity but provides no theorem or iteration encoding, so this work illustrates both the kind of formal separation needed and a failure mode that repeated identical attention may face.

reviewed_competitors.title: Training Large Language Models to Reason in a Continuous Latent Space
reviewed_competitors.difference: Coconut feeds an LLM's continuous hidden state back as the next reasoning state and evaluates planning/backtracking behavior, reporting emergent breadth-first search and releasing code. SELF cites the preprint but uses encoder attention refinement and ordinary classification/QA tables; it does not demonstrate a multi-step reasoning state or compare the information and compute carried by its full-sequence latent loop.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach
reviewed_competitors.difference: Geiping et al. train recurrent-depth language models and test whether additional latent loops at inference improve reasoning, reporting modern language and reasoning evaluations and test-time scaling. The work is contemporaneous/post-submission and loops a model block rather than an attention alignment; it directly tests the scaling claim that SELF motivates but does not evaluate beyond a fixed 100-step cap on mostly encoder benchmarks.

reviewed_competitors.title: Towards Vision Transformer Unrolling Fixed-Point Algorithm: a Case Study on Image Restoration
reviewed_competitors.difference: Qiao et al. propose FPformer, parameter-shared FPRformer, and Anderson-accelerated FPAformer for 161 image-restoration tasks, with controlled pretraining/fine-tuning and efficiency comparisons. SELF cites this work and uses an Uformer-like restoration setup, but does not isolate its attention-only fixed point against FPR/FPA variants; its Table 5 also assigns FPAFormer an unexplained detection mAP outside the cited paper's stated scope.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: arXiv version available on checked date

reviewed_competitors.title: The Expressive Power of Transformers with Chain of Thought
reviewed_competitors.difference: Merrill and Sabharwal carefully parameterize precision, architecture, and scratchpad length to characterize how decoder CoT changes recognized language classes. SELF cites the high-level fixed-depth ceiling but gives no corresponding upper/lower bound for encoder fixed-point iterations, no growing-iteration regime, and no account of whether latent full-sequence state has the same memory resource as generated tokens.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Mathematical Theory of Attention
reviewed_competitors.difference: Vuckovic, Baratin, and Tachet des Combes establish Lipschitz continuity of a measure-theoretic attention operator under suitable assumptions and study infinitely deep weight sharing. SELF treats this as a contraction theorem for its different learned recurrence; a bounded Lipschitz estimate alone does not give a coefficient below one, so the source supports a route to analysis but not the claimed convergence conclusion.

reviewed_competitors.title: One Policy to Control Them All: Shared Modular Policies for Agent-Agnostic Control
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Shares local policy modules and message passing across robot components and morphologies, including generalization to unseen agents.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Modular Robot Control Policies

reviewed_competitors.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chinchilla fits parameter- and data-scaling laws from more than 400 models up to 16B parameters and concludes that model size and tokens should scale roughly equally under a fixed pretraining budget. Sub-Scaling Laws adopts this loss form and its approximate OTR optimum, then adds penalties for deliberately non-optimal allocations and separately studies data density; it does not match Chinchilla's scale or downstream validation breadth.

reviewed_competitors.title: Language models scale reliably with over-training and on downstream tasks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Gadre et al. fit 104 models from 11M to 6.9B over three distributions and report reliable extrapolation to a 32-times-overtrained 1.4B/900B-token run and a compute-optimal 6.9B run, plus downstream error prediction. That directly qualifies the premise that ordinary scaling necessarily fails under overtraining and offers a stronger held-out target-run and downstream benchmark for the new OTR correction.

reviewed_competitors.title: Resolving Discrepancies in Compute-Optimal Scaling of Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: This NeurIPS 2024 Spotlight reproduces the Kaplan/Chinchilla discrepancy and traces it to last-layer compute, warmup duration, and scale-dependent optimizer tuning; after correction it recovers Chinchilla behavior. Sub-Scaling Laws attributes curvature mainly to density and allocation but does not run the corresponding optimizer/warmup/compute-accounting controls, so Porian et al. supplies a critical alternative explanation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scaling Data-Constrained Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Muennighoff et al. release 400 runs up to 9B parameters and 900B tokens, find that up to four repeats can approximate unique data under fixed compute before repeated-token value decays, and fit a law with decreasing effective repeated tokens and excess parameters. Sub-Scaling Laws uses geometric density and a bounded sigmoid OTR penalty instead; it should compare whether density predicts degradation beyond explicit epoch/repetition variables.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scaling Laws and Interpretability of Learning from Repeated Data
reviewed_competitors.difference: Hernandez et al. control the fraction and frequency of duplicated data, reveal repetition-induced double descent, and connect damage to memorization and induction-head degradation. Sub-Scaling Laws aggregates heterogeneous redundancy into corpus density but lacks this controlled repetition intervention and mechanism test; the earlier design better separates duplication from other quality shifts.

reviewed_competitors.title: How to Train Data-Efficient LLMs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sachdeva et al. compare 19 selectors and hundreds of pretraining/evaluation runs, including feature-space Density sampling for coverage and Ask-LLM for quality; they report that coverage can match full data and quality filtering can reject 90% while improving performance. Sub-Scaling Laws reuses the density-selection direction but proposes a cluster-volume score and predictive law without comparing against quality-based selection or fully specifying the feature pipeline.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scaling Laws Revisited: Modeling the Role of Data Quality in Language Model Pretraining
reviewed_competitors.difference: The ICLR 2026 work places an explicit dimensionless quality parameter Q inside a Chinchilla extension, gives corruption-rate and deficiency estimators, controls noise and coverage synthetically, and performs out-of-sample validation. Sub-Scaling Laws predates it and has broader Pile-scale experiments, but its measured density never enters the final OTR loss law and its density intervention is confounded; Q is the closer current formulation of the claimed quality-aware objective.

reviewed_competitors.title: Larger Datasets Can Be Repeated More: A Theoretical Analysis of Multi-Epoch Scaling in Linear Regression
reviewed_competitors.difference: This ICLR 2026 poster derives a multi-epoch effective-sample relationship and supports it with LLM experiments, showing that the number of approximately useful repeats depends on data size and distribution. It challenges any universal OTR-only penalty: two corpora with the same D/N can have different repeat value, exactly the interaction Sub-Scaling Laws motivates but does not encode in its final formula.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: ICLR 2026 poster forum record, last modified 2026-04-11

reviewed_competitors.title: Test-Time Scaling Makes Overtraining Compute-Optimal
reviewed_competitors.difference: Train-to-Test scaling jointly optimizes model size, pretraining tokens, and inference samples under end-to-end budgets and validates heavily overtrained optima across eight downstream tasks and post-training. It shows why Sub-Scaling Laws' label 'non-optimal' is objective-dependent: overtraining that raises pretraining loss at fixed training compute can still minimize lifetime compute once inference and test-time sampling matter.

reviewed_competitors.title: DuoAttention: Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference with Retrieval and Streaming Heads
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Head-role identification with measured KV-memory and latency savings.
reviewed_competitors.difference: DuoAttention uses synthetic data to distinguish retrieval from streaming heads, retains different KV windows, and reports smaller speed and memory gains for GQA than MHA. It directly exposes the systems work and GQA constraints absent from the target.

reviewed_competitors.title: Not All Heads Matter: A Head-Level KV Cache Compression Method with Integrated Retrieval and Reasoning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Head-level KV-budget competitor validated on long-context retrieval and reasoning.
reviewed_competitors.difference: HeadKV allocates cache by head and retains 97% of full-cache contextual-QA performance using 1.5% of the KV cache. It studies realizable cache compression rather than post-compute whole-head output ablation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Why do LLMs attend to the first token?
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Near-contemporaneous functional account of attention sinks.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Barbero et al. argue theoretically and empirically that first-token sinks prevent over-mixing, so high sink mass can encode a useful control mechanism. The target asks the complementary causal question of whether a sink-like head can be removed in a specific benchmark context.

reviewed_competitors.title: Efficient LLMs with AMP: Attention Heads and MLP Pruning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporary structural LLM-pruning competitor with measured inference speed.
reviewed_competitors.difference: AMP jointly scores and removes head and MLP structures and reports speed improvements. It is static and weight/input-projection based, whereas the target isolates natural per-context head-output redundancy without changing weights.

reviewed_competitors.title: Garbage Attention in Large Language Models: BOS Sink Heads and Sink-aware Pruning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct 2026 successor evaluating sink-aware head pruning on newer GQA LLMs.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It reports static BOS-sink ranking outperforming weight- and activation-based criteria, which conflicts with the target's AHON-over-AWFT average under a different static protocol. The disagreement makes matched causal, task, and systems evaluation important.

reviewed_competitors.title: Attention Sink Forges Native MoE in Attention Layers: Sink-Aware Training to Address Head Collapse
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct successor that cites inactive-head behavior as an implicit mixture-of-experts gate.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Rather than pruning dormant capacity, the paper adds sink-aware load balancing during training to prevent head collapse and distribute use across heads. It treats inactivity as a training-allocation problem rather than only post-hoc redundancy.

reviewed_competitors.title: Greedy-Gnorm: A Gradient Matrix Norm-Based Alternative to Attention Entropy for Head Pruning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current competitor addressing stale scores during iterative head removal.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Greedy-Gnorm recalculates gradient-based head importance after each pruning step on a hold-out validation set. That directly targets the target paper's unmodeled cascade feedback, though it studies smaller encoder models and static pruning.

reviewed_competitors.title: SinkRouter: Sink-Aware Routing for Efficient Long-Context Decoding in Large Language and Multimodal Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct systems successor turning sink diagnosis into pre-execution routing.
reviewed_competitors.difference: SinkRouter detects sink signals, skips near-zero computations, supplies Triton kernels, and reports 2.03x speedup at 512K context. It addresses the target's central practical gap: AHON itself is computed too late to save attention work.

reviewed_competitors.title: Complementary Attention Head Pruning for Efficient Transformers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current complementarity-aware alternative to independent per-head magnitude ranking.
reviewed_competitors.difference: CAHP models heads globally as a graph, preserves a diverse complementary subset, and automatically estimates a pruning knee. It addresses interactions and redundancy among selected heads that the target's independent thresholds and aggregate ablation cannot disentangle.

reviewed_competitors.title: Grouped Query Experts: Mixture-of-Experts on GQA Self-Attention
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current GQA-aware dynamic query-head routing design.
reviewed_competitors.difference: GQE selects query-head experts within each shared KV group while explicitly keeping KV heads dense. This cleanly separates query compute from cache memory and demonstrates the architectural distinction missing from the target's per-head cache implication.

reviewed_competitors.title: Multiscale Deep Equilibrium Models

reviewed_competitors.difference: This prior augments an ImageNet-pretrained VGG16 with predictive-coding recurrent feedback and measures robustness to natural and adversarial noise. reviewed_competitors.title: Transformers Learn Shortcuts to Automata
reviewed_competitors.difference: Liu et al. prove low-depth transformers can exactly simulate automata through hierarchical shortcut computations and empirically document brittleness. This supplies a mechanism-level reason why correct sequential behavior need not use the recurrent state abstraction that the present behavioral probe tests.

reviewed_competitors.title: Rediscovering orbital mechanics with machine learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lemos et al. recover inverse-square gravity and latent masses from real Solar System trajectories using a graph network constrained by translation/rotation equivariance and Newton's second and third laws, followed by symbolic regression. It demonstrates success when substantial physical structure is built in, whereas the present paper diagnoses a generic transformer's weak Newtonian transfer bias.

reviewed_competitors.title: Arithmetic Without Algorithms: Language Models Solve Math With a Bag of Heuristics
reviewed_competitors.relationship: parallel causal evidence for heuristic computation
reviewed_competitors.difference: Nikankin et al. identify and causally test sparse neuron-level arithmetic heuristics, providing internal evidence for a bag-of-heuristics mechanism. The present paper reaches a related behavioral diagnosis in physics and games through transfer and partition structure, without identifying a causal circuit.

reviewed_competitors.title: From Kepler to Newton: Inductive Biases Guide Learned World Models in Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: Liu et al. directly revisit this orbital failure and report that continuous regression with noisy contexts restores spatial smoothness/stability, while a two-step context induces force variables with reported linear-probe R-squared near 0.999; long context instead encodes Keplerian ellipse parameters. It shows the negative result is highly contingent on tokenization and temporal locality, although that follow-up uses probing and a simplified one-timescale setup rather than the original full behavioral test.

reviewed_competitors.difference: This method changes Adam by squaring each microbatch gradient before averaging, preserving a second-moment signal across global batch. Marek et al. retain ordinary Adam and instead preserve the estimator's token half-life by rescaling beta2.

reviewed_competitors.difference: This work argues that small-scale conventional wisdom, including small-batch benefits, can reverse in the scaling regime. Marek et al. provide language-model counterevidence through 1.3B parameters and 10B tokens, but do not establish the frontier-scale asymptote.

reviewed_competitors.title: An Empirical Model of Large-Batch Training

reviewed_competitors.title: On the SDEs and Scaling Rules for Adaptive Gradient Algorithms
reviewed_competitors.difference: Malladi et al. derive SDE limits and square-root scaling rules for RMSprop and Adam. Marek et al. find that optimal LM learning rate grows much slower than square root and identify beta2 token half-life as the more consequential small-batch correction.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Marginal Value of Momentum for Small Learning Rate SGD
reviewed_competitors.difference: This theory and experiment study finds little marginal value from momentum in noise-dominated small-learning-rate SGD. PEM-UDE remains distinct in placing the idea inside a missing-physics UDE, giving a local zero-set and gain analysis, and adding sparse symbolic projection plus the neural-mass application.

It threatens PEM-UDE's empirical robustness claim through far broader modern evaluation. PEM-UDE instead targets interpretable residual equations and handles one channel at five-times-signal noise, but needs a matched comparison.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Fourier Weak SINDy is derivative-free, uses orthogonal sinusoidal test functions and multitaper spectral selection, and evaluates multiple chaotic and hyperchaotic ODEs. It directly undermines the use of naive derivative STLSQ as the only symbolic baseline and may recover explicit equations without training a UDE. PEM-UDE may retain an advantage when strong prior physics and partial model specification make a neural residual easier than fitting the whole library.

reviewed_competitors.title: Fast and principled equation discovery from chaos to climate
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bayesian-ARGOS combines frequentist screening with focused Bayesian inference, uncertainty and influence diagnostics, and reports support-recovery rates across seven chaotic systems, sample sizes, and noise levels. It threatens PEM-UDE's data-efficiency and interpretability positioning because it offers explicit uncertainty and much broader support benchmarks at low cost. PEM-UDE is structurally better suited to a small unknown residual inside known dynamics, but does not quantify that comparative advantage.

reviewed_competitors.relationship: closest prior for missing physics plus symbolic recovery
reviewed_competitors.difference: UPINN also inserts a neural representation of unknown terms into partially known differential equations and converts those terms to explicit formulas through symbolic regression, with sparse noisy ODE and PDE data. This narrows PEM-UDE's pipeline novelty; its sharper contribution is observer-based stabilization specifically for chaos and autonomous validation, whereas UPINN uses physics-informed residual constraints and is not centered on chaotic trajectory divergence.

This is less a drop-in optimizer than a direct challenge to PEM-UDE's evidence: attractor plots and short forecasts are insufficient without statistical and derivative validation. PEM-UDE's symbolic equations could make those audits easier, but the paper does not perform them systematically.

It threatens the need for a purely learned deterministic closure and supplies fluctuation mechanisms PEM-UDE omits. The model uses Poisson rather than adaptive Izhikevich neurons, so PEM-UDE still covers a different and biophysically richer simulator family.

reviewed_competitors.difference: LeCun's proposal already combines hierarchical JEPA world models, energy-based latent prediction, intrinsic objectives, and planning under uncertainty. reviewed_competitors.difference: V-JEPA trains solely by feature prediction on two million videos and obtains strong frozen visual representations without pixel reconstruction. reviewed_competitors.title: V-JEPA 2: Self-Supervised Video Models Enable Understanding, Prediction and Planning
reviewed_competitors.difference: V-JEPA 2 pretrains on more than one million hours of video, post-trains an action-conditioned latent model on robot data, and performs zero-shot real-robot planning. reviewed_competitors.title: DINO-WM: World Models on Pre-trained Visual Features enable Zero-shot Planning
reviewed_competitors.difference: DINO-WM predicts pretrained spatial patch features and optimizes action sequences toward image goals across six task families without rewards or pixel decoding. reviewed_competitors.title: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models

reviewed_competitors.title: Diffusion for World Modeling: Visual Details Matter in Atari

reviewed_competitors.title: Cosmos World Foundation Model Platform for Physical AI

reviewed_competitors.difference: Genie learns latent actions from unlabeled Internet video and generates frame-by-frame controllable worlds at 11B parameters. It demonstrates interactive generative simulation without PAN's explicit conceptual state or broad agent claims, narrowing novelty of the action-controllable video component.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Hoffmann et al. train over 400 models from 70M to 16B parameters and validate near-equal model/token scaling with a 70B model. reviewed_competitors.difference: Pearce and Song explain discrepant exponents through parameter counting and finite-scale bias and recommend total parameters/compute. The target paper assumes c=6tp and uses a narrow ladder; its trajectory collapse could complement, but does not replace, those accounting and scale-range audits.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Paquette et al. solve an infinite-data SGD model and derive optimizer-noise, capacity, and feature-embedding phases plus exponents. The target paper uses the resulting multi-power intuition to explain empirical trajectory collapse and adds schedule/noise observations, but takes the relevant power laws as given.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scaling Law with Learning Rate Annealing
reviewed_competitors.difference: Tissue, Wang, and Wang fit an explicit law using accumulated learning-rate and annealing areas to predict full curves from one or two runs across schedules. reviewed_competitors.title: A Multi-Power Law for Loss Curve Prediction Across Learning Rate Schedules

The target paper gives a simpler noise-based deformation that explains collapse, but its own appendix notes a constant-covariance variant underperformed and it does not optimize schedules prospectively.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scaling Exponents Across Parameterizations and Optimizers

reviewed_competitors.title: In-context Reinforcement Learning with Algorithm Distillation
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational competing route to a transformer that improves its policy entirely through context.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Algorithm Distillation autoregressively imitates complete learning histories from source RL agents, whereas the reviewed paper uses random exploration memories and direct supervision from an oracle optimal policy. AD therefore inherits an update trajectory; the reviewed model is freer to compile task-distribution-specific shortcuts, but requires optimal labels.

reviewed_competitors.title: Distilling Reinforcement Learning Algorithms for In-Context Model-Based Planning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct competing account in which a transformer explicitly learns dynamics and performs model-based policy improvement in context.
reviewed_competitors.difference: DICP jointly trains an in-context dynamics model and planning objective and evaluates Darkroom variants plus Meta-World. It demonstrates that transformer ICRL can be deliberately model-based, so the reviewed paper's negative conclusion is best read as a task- and objective-specific circuit finding rather than a taxonomy of transformer ICRL.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformers Learn Temporal Difference Methods for In-Context Reinforcement Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Mechanistic and theoretical counterpoint showing classical model-free updates can emerge in a transformer forward pass.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wang et al. prove explicit linear-transformer constructions for TD, residual-gradient, eligibility-trace, and average-reward evaluation and demonstrate TD emergence under multi-task TD training. The reviewed paper instead finds no useful long-range linear value signal after oracle-action DPT training, highlighting how the outer objective and task distribution select different inner algorithms.

reviewed_competitors.title: Towards Provable Emergence of In-Context Reinforcement Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporary theory of why a pretraining loss can yield an in-context TD learner.
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work proves that a global minimizer of a policy-evaluation pretraining loss can implement TD learning. The reviewed paper provides empirical circuit hypotheses for an oracle-action transformer but neither characterizes the training-loss minimizers nor proves that its decoded map and path tags implement the policy.

reviewed_competitors.title: Vintix II: Decision Pre-Trained Transformer is a Scalable In-Context Reinforcement Learner
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Post-publication scale test of the same DPT family across hundreds of diverse tasks.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Vintix II extends DPT with flow matching and demonstrates online and offline generalization in a multi-domain setting. It makes the reviewed paper's three-layer maze circuit a concrete hypothesis to test at scale, but does not by itself show that Euclidean maps or cached path tags persist in the larger agent.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformers Provably Implement In-Context Reinforcement Learning with Policy Improvement
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Post-publication constructive and training-dynamics account of classical control algorithms inside transformers.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Liang and Lai construct linear self-attention blocks for semi-gradient SARSA and actor-critic and prove local exponential convergence of teacher-mimicking gradient flow under richness assumptions. This narrows the novelty of a general claim that transformer ICRL lies outside standard RL: the reviewed paper's contribution is the empirical discovery of a different specialized circuit under its DPT setup.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Kuo et al. use predictive auxiliary modules and bidirectional state-machine simulation to test equivalence with Bayes-optimal belief states across POMDPs, explicitly warning that decodability alone can be misleading. The reviewed paper uses PCA, CKA, and mostly linear probes without an equivalence metric to an algorithmic state machine.

reviewed_competitors.title: Competition Dynamics Shape Algorithmic Phases of In-Context Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Competition Dynamics decomposes one Markov-mixture model into four retrieval/inference and unigram/bigram algorithms whose dominance changes with context and training. The target's novelty is token-position-resolved counterfactual evidence within one recall episode, but its two-route description is less algorithmically explicit.

reviewed_competitors.title: Strategy Coopetition Explains the Emergence and Transience of In-Context Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Strategy Coopetition identifies shared subcircuits and competitive/cooperative learning between ICL and context-constrained in-weights learning. reviewed_competitors.title: Larger language models do in-context learning differently

reviewed_competitors.title: Dual Operating Modes of In-Context Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Dual Operating Modes derives a posterior split between retrieving a pretrained skill and learning a task from context. reviewed_competitors.title: What needs to go right for an induction head? A mechanistic study of in-context learning circuits and their formation

reviewed_competitors.relationship: Automatically constructs permutation-equivariant weight-space models and applies them to learned optimization of small classifiers and language models.
reviewed_competitors.difference: UNF is both a direct baseline and a component of GradMetaNet; GradMetaNet adds decomposed per-example gradient sets before the UNF weight-space stage.

reviewed_competitors.title: VeLO: Training Versatile Learned Optimizers by Scaling Up
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Meta-trains a learned optimizer at very large compute scale over a broad task distribution and releases an extensive optimizer benchmark.
reviewed_competitors.difference: VeLO attacks optimizer generality through task and meta-compute scale using conventional optimizer features; GradMetaNet attacks input sufficiency and structural equivariance but evaluates much smaller tasks.

reviewed_competitors.title: Fast Model Editing at Scale
reviewed_competitors.relationship: MEND also consumes a low-rank gradient decomposition with learned auxiliary networks to produce fast parameter edits.
reviewed_competitors.difference: MEND demonstrates factual edits in transformer language models above 10B parameters, whereas GradMetaNet provides a more general symmetry-aware factor-set interface but tests editing only on tiny image INRs.
