reviewed_competitors.title: DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model
reviewed_competitors.difference: This is the primary technical report from which the reviewed MLA equations and Figure 1 are adapted. It reports 236 billion total and 21 billion active parameters, 128K context, 93.3% KV-cache reduction, 5.76-times maximum generation throughput, and model evaluations; the review provides tutorial derivation but no reproduction or component ablation.

reviewed_competitors.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
reviewed_competitors.difference: The primary GQA paper reports uptrained GQA quality close to MHA with speed comparable to MQA. That result directly qualifies the review's categorical claim that GQA does not match MHA and motivates matched quality-cache comparisons rather than a universal ordering.

reviewed_competitors.title: DeepSeekMoE: Towards Ultimate Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: This ACL paper introduces fine-grained expert segmentation and shared expert isolation and contains the balancing equations reviewed on pages 4-5. Comparing the primary definitions exposes the review's mistaken P_i normalization and uniform-loss calculation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Better & Faster Large Language Models via Multi-token Prediction
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work predicts multiple future tokens with independent heads over a shared trunk and reports higher sample efficiency, code gains, and faster inference without training-time overhead in its implementation. DeepSeek-V3 instead uses causally chained modules with independent transformer blocks, so overhead conclusions must be architecture-specific.

reviewed_competitors.title: Zero Bubble Pipeline Parallelism
reviewed_competitors.difference: It introduces the split backward computation used in the review's DualPipe account, gives automatically searched schedules, releases code, and reports throughput gains against baseline schedules. The review neither benchmarks DualPipe against it nor provides equivalent evidence for the blog-derived cut-in-half claim.

reviewed_competitors.title: FP8-LM: Training FP8 Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: FP8-LM is a primary end-to-end FP8 training system predating V3. It offers an empirical baseline for stability, memory, and speed, whereas the reviewed section only narrates V3's fine-grained scaling and accumulation choices without a matched comparison.

reviewed_competitors.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: DeepSeekMath introduces GRPO in the context of a 7B math model continued on 120 billion math-related tokens and evaluates it against mathematical-reasoning baselines. The review reproduces the objective but omits that pretraining context and later estimator caveats.

reviewed_competitors.title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
reviewed_competitors.relationship: primary source for the reviewed V3 stack
reviewed_competitors.difference: This report is the source for V3's MLA, auxiliary-loss-free routing, MTP, DualPipe, FP8, training budget, and model evaluations. Its 2.788-million-H800-hour total includes 2.664 million pretraining hours plus context extension and post-training, correcting the review's pretraining label; it also excludes prior research and ablation costs.

reviewed_competitors.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: primary source for R1-Zero and R1 post-training
reviewed_competitors.difference: The R1 report supplies the base model, rewards, four-stage pipeline, evaluations, and distilled models that the review summarizes. Its current revision postdates the cached review and should be versioned separately; neither source makes no-SFT RL equivalent to learning without pretraining or engineered reward signal.

reviewed_competitors.title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
reviewed_competitors.difference: DAPO introduces clip-higher, dynamic sampling, token-level policy-gradient loss, and overlong-reward shaping, with code and data for large-scale reasoning RL. It directly operationalizes several stability and efficiency issues absent from the review's simplified GRPO treatment.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training: A Critical Perspective
reviewed_competitors.difference: This study varies base models and critically separates pretrained capabilities from RL effects; it reports reasoning already present in bases and identifies GRPO response-length bias. It is the closest direct empirical check on the review's claims of capabilities arising and generalizing solely through pure RL.

reviewed_competitors.title: 100 Days After DeepSeek-R1: A Survey on Replication Studies and More Directions for Reasoning Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: This later survey organizes R1 replication evidence and explicitly notes that implementation details were not fully open-sourced. It provides wider post-release coverage and a more precise reproducibility caveat than the reviewed manuscript's unqualified open-source label.

reviewed_competitors.title: Native Sparse Attention: Hardware-Aligned and Natively Trainable Sparse Attention
reviewed_competitors.difference: NSA co-designs natively trainable sparse attention with hardware-aligned kernels for long context. It broadens the efficiency frontier beyond MLA's KV compression and provides a direct candidate for joint quality, prefill, decode, and hardware comparisons omitted by the review.

reviewed_competitors.title: Kimi Linear: An Expressive, Efficient Attention Architecture
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kimi Linear combines Kimi Delta Attention with MLA in a hybrid architecture and reports stronger long-context performance with large cache and decoding reductions versus full attention or MLA-based designs. It is a current alternative unavailable to the March 2025 review and makes an MLA-only research agenda incomplete.

reviewed_competitors.title: DeepSeek-V3.2: Pushing the Frontier of Open Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: official DeepSeek architecture and RL successor
reviewed_competitors.difference: DeepSeek-V3.2 adds DeepSeek Sparse Attention and a scalable RL framework with task synthesis for reasoning and agent settings. It is the direct later state of the line reviewed here and should supersede claims that V3 and the initial R1 pipeline define the current frontier.

reviewed_competitors.title: Phi-Balancing for Mixture-of-Experts Training
reviewed_competitors.difference: Phi-Balancing targets population-level expert balance with a strictly convex symmetric differentiable potential instead of noisy batch-level heuristics. It directly advances the balancing-theory question, but from a corrected objective foundation rather than the review's erroneous normalization argument.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Impossibility of Unbiased and Length-Invariant Policy Optimization with Outcome Rewards
reviewed_competitors.difference: This paper formalizes a tradeoff between unbiasedness and response-length invariance for outcome-reward policy gradients, placing GRPO and Dr. GRPO at different ends. It turns an omission in the review into a precise limitation: no simple normalization choice eliminates both concerns.

reviewed_competitors.title: GRPO, Dr. GRPO, and DAPO Are Three Operations on One Number: The Group-Standard-Deviation Identity
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work argues that GRPO, Dr. GRPO, and DAPO differ through operations on group standard deviation, foregrounding prompt-level disagreement weighting. That mechanism is invisible in the review's value-model-versus-group-baseline explanation and offers a sharper comparison axis.

reviewed_competitors.title: Stabilizing Transformer Training by Preventing Attention Entropy Collapse
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sigma-Reparam controls every linear layer's spectral norm and derives a lower bound linking attention-logit scale to entropy collapse; it can train competitive ViTs without layer normalization, warmup, weight decay, or adaptive optimization. DyT is a much simpler activation-site substitution and beats the paper's tuned sigma-Reparam vision numbers, but offers no comparable stability theorem or attention-specific diagnostic.

reviewed_competitors.title: AERO: Softmax-Only LLMs for Efficient Private Inference
reviewed_competitors.difference: AERO removes LayerNorm and GELU as part of a four-stage decoder redesign optimized for encrypted inference, using entropy regularization and reducing communication and latency. DyT preserves the surrounding architecture and adds a bounded nonlinearity at each former normalization site, prioritizing broad training parity rather than minimizing nonlinear operations for private inference.

reviewed_competitors.title: Stronger Normalization-Free Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chen et al., including two DyT authors, systematically vary pointwise-function properties and search designs, selecting shifted dynamic erf as a stronger replacement that reports gains over LayerNorm, RMSNorm, and DyT across vision, speech, and DNA. It confirms DyT's broader design premise while showing tanh is not uniquely or optimally responsible for the effect.

reviewed_competitors.title: Bounded Hyperbolic Tangent: A Stable and Efficient Alternative to Pre-Layer Normalization in Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: BHyT argues that DyT remains fragile at depth because a learned scalar does not control variance growth or prevent saturation. It reintroduces one data-driven variance calculation per block plus an approximation for the second site, supplies an input/Jacobian bound, and reports higher training and generation throughput than RMSNorm. This trades DyT's fully statistic-free simplicity for explicit scale robustness.

reviewed_competitors.title: KAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: KAN places learned univariate spline functions on network edges and motivates KArAt's operator parameterization. KArAt applies this idea specifically to entire self-attention score rows and substitutes Fourier bases plus a rank bottleneck.

reviewed_competitors.title: KAN or MLP: A Fairer Comparison
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yu et al. control parameters and FLOPs and find MLPs generally outperform KANs outside symbolic representation. It motivates a missing compute-matched MLP row-operator baseline for determining whether KArAt gains come from KAN structure rather than extra capacity.

reviewed_competitors.title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Transformer
reviewed_competitors.difference: KAT replaces channel-mixing MLPs with rational Group-KAN layers, uses weight sharing, CUDA kernels, and variance-preserving initialization, and reports ImageNet scaling. KArAt leaves the MLP intact and instead learns the attention score transform, with much worse memory scaling.

reviewed_competitors.title: KAA: Kolmogorov-Arnold Attention for Enhancing Attentive Graph Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: KAA predates KArAt's arXiv submission and inserts a KAN into graph neighbor-pair scoring, then normalizes the scores for GNN aggregation. KArAt instead maps a complete ViT score row to a new complete row, so its narrow MHSA construction remains distinct but the broad name and 'first learnable attention' framing do not.

reviewed_competitors.title: Adaptively Sparse Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: Adaptive entmax learns a shape/sparsity parameter for each attention head, replacing fixed softmax with a trainable differentiable normalizer while retaining probability semantics. It is far less expressive than KArAt but directly refutes an unqualified claim that attention activation had not previously been learned.

reviewed_competitors.title: Synthesizer: Rethinking Self-Attention in Transformer Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Synthesizer directly learns synthetic attention weights, including factorized variants, without query-key token interactions. KArAt retains query-key scores and learns their row transformation, but it is not the first Transformer mechanism to learn attention weights with an auxiliary network.

reviewed_competitors.title: Escaping the Gradient Vanishing: Periodic Alternatives of Softmax in Attention Mechanism
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wang et al. replace the exponential in attention normalization with periodic functions and test a LeViT-style vision model. Their functions are hand-designed rather than a general learned KAN row operator, but the paper is a close uncited predecessor to Fourier-based alternatives for vision attention.

reviewed_competitors.title: Replacing softmax with ReLU in Vision Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: ReLU attention divided by sequence length approaches or matches softmax scaling from small to large ImageNet-21k ViTs without a learned N-to-N operator. It is the essential efficiency and scaling baseline absent from KArAt's experiments.

reviewed_competitors.title: Theory, Analysis, and Best Practices for Sigmoid Self-Attention
reviewed_competitors.difference: Properly normalized sigmoid attention matches softmax across language, vision, and speech at scale, has a universality/regularity analysis, and a hardware-aware kernel reported faster than FlashAttention2. KArAt is more expressive per row but fixed-length and dramatically heavier.

reviewed_competitors.title: Rethinking Attention: Polynomial Alternatives to Softmax in Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work argues attention stability comes from Frobenius-norm regularization and uses simple polynomials that need not be positive, normalized, or sparse. It offers a theory-driven signed alternative and a much cheaper control for KArAt's claim that basis-learned flexibility is necessary.

reviewed_competitors.title: Vision KAN: Towards an Attention-Free Backbone for Vision with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: ViK replaces pairwise attention with patch-wise RBF-KAN transforms, separable local mixing, and a low-rank global map, reporting ImageNet-1K performance at linear complexity. It directly targets KArAt's fixed-length, quadratic, and memory-heavy failure modes rather than learning the softmax replacement.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Lotfi et al. supply the learned-subspace quantization experiments behind several claims that compression bounds track model size, equivariance, label noise, and double descent. The position paper generalizes their interpretation, but its simple file-size recipe omits the specialized optimization needed to obtain those tight bounds.

reviewed_competitors.title: Fantastic Generalization Measures and Where to Find Them
reviewed_competitors.difference: Jiang et al. evaluate more than forty proposed measures across over ten thousand ConvNets and find surprising failures as well as promising correlations. It exemplifies the broader, controlled empirical adjudication missing from the position paper and cautions that correlation of a bound term with generalization is not causal explanation.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: ICLR 2020 conference version, OpenReview id SJgIPJBVfH

reviewed_competitors.title: Fantastic Generalization Measures Are Nowhere to Be Found
reviewed_competitors.difference: Gastpar et al. prove impossibility results for certain uniformly tight generalization bounds in overparameterized settings. Their target is stronger than Wilson's hypothesis-specific non-vacuity claim, so there is no direct contradiction, but the result sharply limits any reading that a single complexity term should uniformly and tightly explain observed risk.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Pitfalls of Simplicity Bias in Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Shah et al. construct settings where networks exclusively use the simplest feature even when it is less predictive and show failures under benign shifts and adversarial perturbations. This does not refute soft bias for i.i.d. compression bounds, but it demonstrates that 'prefer simple' is not a sufficient design prescription for robust or semantically correct learning.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: NeurIPS 2020 proceedings version, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33

reviewed_competitors.title: The Implicit Bias of Benign Overfitting
reviewed_competitors.difference: Shamir proves that benign overfitting in regression is biased toward particular problem families and should not be expected for several natural extensions of plain linear regression, while classification is more favorable. It supports non-neural analysis but tempers Wilson's broad intuitive treatment with precise conditions under which interpolation is not benign.

reviewed_competitors.title: Deep Double Descent: Where Bigger Models and More Data Hurt
reviewed_competitors.difference: Nakkiran et al. demonstrate model-wise, epoch-wise, and sample-wise double descent across modern tasks and propose effective model complexity. Wilson emphasizes older and linear precedents plus compression/effective dimension, but does not newly test whether that account predicts all three forms under a common protocol.

reviewed_competitors.title: Non-Vacuous Generalization Bounds for Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lotfi et al. extend compression bounds to unbounded log loss with prediction smoothing and accelerate evaluation by subsampling, using SubLoRA for models up to 849 million parameters. This supports the position's scale claim while showing why its elementary bounded i.i.d. theorem is not itself sufficient for LLMs.

reviewed_competitors.title: Compute-Optimal LLMs Provably Generalize Better with Scale
reviewed_competitors.difference: Finzi et al. derive an empirical Freedman-style martingale bound decomposed into parameters per token, loss variance, and fixed-bitrate quantization error, then connect decreasing variance/error to compute-optimal scale. It is a more specific, dependence-aware theory than the position paper's generic simplicity narrative and supplies testable components that can be challenged separately.

reviewed_competitors.difference: MegaByte already treats a global patch model and local within-patch model as end-to-end differentiable modules for million-byte sequences, including raw ImageNet density estimation, with compute-controlled comparisons. FractalAR generalizes the two-scale pattern into a deeper spatial tree and improves ImageNet64 from the cited 3.40 to 3.14 bits/dim, but recursive depth rather than generative-model modularization alone is the distinctive step.

reviewed_competitors.title: Matryoshka Diffusion Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Matryoshka Diffusion jointly denoises nested resolutions with parameters and features of smaller models embedded in larger ones and demonstrates pixel-space generation through 1024x1024. It is not autoregressive and its nesting is across resolution rather than patch subtrees, but it predates the broad new-paradigm claim for recursively nested end-to-end generative models.

reviewed_competitors.title: Autoregressive Image Generation without Vector Quantization
reviewed_competitors.relationship: foundational component and strongest internal baseline
reviewed_competitors.difference: The authors' earlier MAR paper supplies the random-order masked generator, continuous-token philosophy, and strong tokenizer-free image baseline used inside FractalMAR. The focal work replaces diffusion-loss patch emission with a recursively nested route to categorical raw pixels; gains should therefore be separated from the already-established MAR sampling and guidance machinery.

reviewed_competitors.title: Visual Autoregressive Modeling: Scalable Image Generation via Next-Scale Prediction
reviewed_competitors.difference: VAR generates discrete tokens coarse to fine and reports 1.73 FID, 350.2 IS, roughly 20x faster inference, scaling curves, and editing on ImageNet 256x256. FractalMAR uniquely avoids a tokenizer and retains atomic pixels, but its 6.15 FID and unmeasured matched latency show the cost of that choice relative to a mature scale-autoregressive design.

reviewed_competitors.title: JetFormer: An Autoregressive Generative Model of Raw Images and Text
reviewed_competitors.difference: JetFormer learns an invertible flow and AR soft-token model jointly from raw pixels, supplies likelihood bounds, and unifies image generation and understanding with text. FractalGen cites its 6.64 FID and is smaller/better in that ImageNet table, while JetFormer has a more general multimodal interface and a principled transformed-density objective.

reviewed_competitors.title: PixelFlow: Pixel-Space Generative Models with Flow
reviewed_competitors.difference: PixelFlow also eliminates a pretrained VAE, trains end to end in raw pixel space, and uses cascaded resolutions to control compute; it reports 1.98 FID on ImageNet 256x256 and text-to-image results. This later result shows that recursion is one route, not a necessary route, to high-quality tokenizer-free high-resolution generation.

reviewed_competitors.title: FARMER: Flow AutoRegressive Transformer over Pixels
reviewed_competitors.difference: FARMER combines an invertible autoregressive flow, self-supervised channel reduction, AR modeling, and distillation. Its 556M likelihood model reports 2.61 bits/dim on ImageNet64 and its 1.9B generator reaches 3.60 FID on ImageNet256, improving both focal endpoints while explicitly retaining a normalized likelihood—an especially important comparison given FractalMAR's pseudo-likelihood issue.

reviewed_competitors.title: Parallel Rollout Approximation for Pixel-Space Autoregressive Image Generation
reviewed_competitors.relationship: post-submission pixel-AR quality and exposure-bias competitor
reviewed_competitors.difference: PRA diagnoses high-dimensional single-step error and teacher-forced rollout mismatch, learns compact intermediate states with a pixel decoder, and approximates inference-time inputs during parallel training. It reports FID 2.58 at 135M and 1.94 at 511M, showing a much stronger parameter-quality frontier and a direct alternative to FractalMAR's recursive masked schedule.

reviewed_competitors.title: FGM-HD: Boosting Generation Diversity of Fractal Generative Models through Hausdorff Dimension Induction
reviewed_competitors.difference: FGM-HD takes the focal model's weak recall as its target, adding a learned Hausdorff-dimension loss schedule and rejection sampling and reporting a 39 percent diversity improvement. Whatever the merits of its fractal interpretation, the extension independently confirms that distribution coverage—not precision or Inception Score—is the central practical weakness of the original FractalMAR endpoint.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Cao et al. establish the original shallow-CNN benign/harmful transition under a homogeneous feature-noise model and an SNR condition. Xu and Chen preserve that architecture and gradient-dynamics program but add label-dependent covariance, a second correlation-ratio axis, multiclass imbalance, and a long-tail-specific upper bound.

reviewed_competitors.title: Benign Overfitting in Two-layer ReLU Convolutional Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kou et al. give algorithm-dependent risk bounds and a sharp SNR transition for standard ReLU CNNs with label-flipping noise. The present paper generalizes the data-specific noise from homogeneous to class-dependent sub-Gaussian transforms and cross-entropy from binary to K-class analysis, but shifts attention away from random label corruption.

reviewed_competitors.title: Benign Overfitting in Two-Layer ReLU Convolutional Neural Networks for XOR Data
reviewed_competitors.difference: Meng et al. extend shallow-CNN benign-overfitting theory beyond linearly separable Bayes rules to XOR data and supply a matching harmful-regime lower bound. Xu and Chen instead keep orthogonal explicit class means and make the residual covariance informative; their novelty is heterogeneous implicit structure rather than nonlinear target logic.

reviewed_competitors.title: What Neural Networks Memorize and Why: Discovering the Long Tail via Influence Estimation
reviewed_competitors.difference: Feldman and Zhang already show that atypical memorized examples can have unusually high marginal utility using repeated subsampled training. Xu and Chen propose a mechanistic covariance model and a much cheaper leave-one-out covariance statistic, but their real-data experiment does not directly compare that proxy's ranking quality with subsampled influence.

reviewed_competitors.title: Memorization Through the Lens of Curvature of Loss Function Around Samples
reviewed_competitors.difference: Garg et al. use average per-example loss curvature during training, validate it against memorization scores, and identify atypical, mislabeled, and conflicting samples. Xu and Chen's covariance score is training-free and theory-motivated but cannot by itself separate useful tails from corruptions and is not benchmarked against curvature.

reviewed_competitors.title: Benign overfitting in leaky ReLU networks with moderate input dimension
reviewed_competitors.difference: Karhadkar et al. derive benign versus harmful SNR conditions for two-layer leaky-ReLU networks while reducing prior near-orthogonality dimension requirements from roughly quadratic to linear in sample size. Xu and Chen allow heterogeneous class covariance and multiclass imbalance but retain strong rank, orthogonality, and overparameterization conditions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Is Memorization Helpful or Harmful? Prior Information Sets the Threshold
reviewed_competitors.difference: Cheng and Barber give distribution-prior conditions under which optimal generalization in an overparameterized Bayesian linear model requires near interpolation or instead requires training error near the noise level. Their Fisher-information thresholds are model-agnostic with respect to a specific shallow-network dynamic but linear/Bayesian; Xu and Chen give a nonlinear gradient-dynamics mechanism tied to label-dependent covariance.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Road Less Scheduled

reviewed_competitors.relationship: closest contemporary residual-routing baseline with broader scaling
reviewed_competitors.difference: Hyper-Connections expands the residual stream into multiple paths and learns static or dynamic width connections, validating dense and MoE models at 1B and 7B parameters for up to 500B tokens. DCA instead mixes all prior depths into separate Q/K/V inputs but reports a substantially smaller scale and shorter context.

reviewed_competitors.difference: LAuReL learns residual weights, low-rank transformations, and access to previous activations while emphasizing minimal parameter and runtime overhead. It offers a lighter residual-path intervention, whereas DCA spends additional computation on input-dependent and Q/K/V-specific depth mixtures.

reviewed_competitors.title: MUDDFormer: Breaking Residual Bottlenecks in Transformers via Multiway Dynamic Dense Connections
reviewed_competitors.difference: MUDDFormer also learns token-dependent dense connections and decouples the Q, K, V, and residual streams, making it especially close architecturally. It reports Pythia-scale results through 2.8B parameters, model and code releases, and explicit parameter and compute overhead, which provide stronger scaling and reproducibility tests than DCA.

reviewed_competitors.title: mHC: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections
reviewed_competitors.difference: mHC constrains Hyper-Connection routing matrices to a stability-preserving manifold and couples the formulation to systems optimizations. It directly treats activation-scale and gradient-stability risks that DCA only assesses through visually smooth loss curves.

reviewed_competitors.title: Attention Residuals
reviewed_competitors.difference: Attention Residuals applies a softmax directly over previous sublayer outputs and introduces a blockwise approximation, with scaling-law experiments reaching 48B total and 3B active parameters over 1.4T tokens. DCA instead uses unnormalized gated mixtures before ordinary token attention and is validated at much smaller scale.

reviewed_competitors.title: Rethinking Cross-Layer Information Routing in Diffusion Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work diagnoses magnitude inflation, gradient decay, and representation redundancy in diffusion-transformer cross-layer routing, then introduces timestep-adaptive aggregation. Its explicit failure analysis and diffusion experiments complement DCA's language-model focus and expose stability dimensions not measured in DCA.

reviewed_competitors.title: Low-Rank Attention Residuals
reviewed_competitors.difference: Low-Rank Attention Residuals route with low-dimensional keys while keeping full-dimensional values and add sliced variants with very small reported FLOP overhead. It directly optimizes the depth-routing cost-quality frontier that k-DCA approaches only by aggregating older outputs.

reviewed_competitors.title: SimpleRL-Zoo: Investigating and Taming Zero Reinforcement Learning for Open Base Models in the Wild

reviewed_competitors.relationship: Exact architectural predecessor under the name Sandwich-LN
reviewed_competitors.difference: CogView introduced normalization before and after each residual sublayer to prevent numerical overflow in a 4B Transformer, matching the core Peri-LN topology. Peri-LN contributes a much more systematic decoder-LM comparison, multi-seed scaling study, and activation diagnostics, but it should be framed as analysis and renaming of Sandwich-LN rather than invention of the placement.

reviewed_competitors.title: Gemma 2: Improving Open Language Models at a Practical Size
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Exact deployed predecessor for the Peri-LN core block
reviewed_competitors.difference: Gemma 2 applies RMSNorm to both the input and output of every attention and feed-forward sublayer, so its residual block has the same core x + Norm(Module(Norm(x))) topology at 2B, 9B, and 27B scale. It predates Peri-LN but does not isolate normalization placement experimentally; Peri-LN's contribution is therefore the controlled placement study and mechanism analysis, not first deployment of the architecture.

reviewed_competitors.title: NormFormer: Improved Transformer Pretraining with Extra Normalization
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct predecessor for extra normalization that balances Pre-LN gradients
reviewed_competitors.difference: NormFormer's attention branch matches Peri-LN's input/output placement but adds head-wise scaling; its feed-forward branch places the second LayerNorm before the output projection rather than after the complete MLP. It evaluates causal and masked models up to 2.7B and reports compute-matched wall-time gains and ablations. Peri-LN uses the simpler uniform full-branch output norm and more seeds at up to 3.2B, but does not compare compute-for-compute or cite this especially close design; NormFormer also reports that CogView-style final-FFN output normalization did not help in its setting.

reviewed_competitors.title: On Layer Normalization in the Transformer Architecture
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational Pre-LN versus Post-LN theory and experimental baseline
reviewed_competitors.difference: Xiong et al. use mean-field analysis of the full initialized Transformer to explain large output-side Post-LN gradients and warmup sensitivity, then validate several tasks. Peri-LN's valuable extension is tracking trained large-LM activations beyond initialization, but its local softmax-block proposition does not match the end-to-end model as closely as this predecessor's formal setup.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformers Get Stable: An End-to-End Signal Propagation Theory for Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kedia et al. derive forward and backward moment recurrences covering vanishing and exploding gradients, rank collapse, and attention instability, then propose DeepScaleLM and train up to 1,000 layers across language, speech, and vision. Peri-LN supplies richer observations over the course of billion-parameter LM training and a simple placement intervention, but its claimed analytical foundation omits covariance and most end-to-end Transformer structure.

reviewed_competitors.title: Magneto: A Foundation Transformer
reviewed_competitors.difference: Magneto places two Sub-LayerNorm operations inside attention and feed-forward sublayers and combines them with a theoretically scaled initialization, with experiments spanning language, translation, vision, speech, and multimodal pretraining. Peri-LN preserves the clean residual path with a branch-output norm and offers strong decoder-LM seed studies, but lacks Magneto's modality breadth and direct best-recipe comparison.

reviewed_competitors.title: DeepNet: Scaling Transformers to 1,000 Layers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Alternative normalization-residual scaling solution for stable depth
reviewed_competitors.difference: DeepNorm retains a Post-LN-like architecture but derives depth-dependent residual and initialization scaling to bound model updates and trains Transformers with up to 1,000 layers. Peri-LN instead caps every branch output and is tested at up to 32 layers; a head-to-head test would reveal whether extra normalization or principled depth scaling is the better stability-compute tradeoff.

reviewed_competitors.title: 2 OLMo 2 Furious
reviewed_competitors.difference: OLMo 2 reorders RMSNorm from sublayer input to output and combines it with QK-Norm, reporting improved gradient stability in a fully open 7B/13B recipe. Peri-LN retains both input and output normalization and better isolates placement across controlled 400M-3.2B runs, but its own appendix finds the output-only OLMo 2 style comparable at 3.2B and does not measure the cost of the extra input norms.

reviewed_competitors.title: Mix-LN: Unleashing the Power of Deeper Layers by Combining Pre-LN and Post-LN
reviewed_competitors.difference: Mix-LN applies Post-LN in earlier layers and Pre-LN in deeper layers to balance gradients without adding both norms everywhere, and evaluates 70M-7B models plus SFT and RLHF. Peri-LN offers cleaner branch-scale control and stronger massive-activation diagnostics, but does not compare against this accepted ICLR 2025 alternative or test whether placement should vary with depth.

This postdates the reviewed work and supports its direction, while providing a more principled representation-dynamics framework than the paper's 256-sample angular-distance interpretation.

reviewed_competitors.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational baseline and direct parameterization ancestor.
reviewed_competitors.difference: LoRA optimizes the two low-rank factors directly and can merge them into the base weight. RepLoRA retains the same deployed update but overparameterizes its training path with learned generators and couples query and value factors.

reviewed_competitors.title: NOLA: Compressing LoRA using Linear Combination of Random Basis
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest prior work explicitly reparameterizing LoRA factors.
reviewed_competitors.difference: NOLA expresses LoRA factors as learned linear combinations of frozen random bases and targets adapter storage below rank-one LoRA. It predates RepLoRA's generic reparameterization claim but does not use disposable nonlinear MLPs or argue an MoE sample-complexity transition.

reviewed_competitors.title: VeRA: Vector-based Random Matrix Adaptation
reviewed_competitors.difference: VeRA shares a frozen random low-rank basis across layers and learns small scaling vectors, sharply reducing trainable and stored parameters. RepLoRA instead adds learned generators during training and stores ordinary layer-specific factors, prioritizing accuracy and low-data behavior over minimum adapter size.

reviewed_competitors.title: Tied-LoRA: Enhancing parameter efficiency of LoRA with Weight Tying
reviewed_competitors.difference: Tied-LoRA directly ties selected A or B matrices across layers and selectively freezes factors, often using a fraction of LoRA's parameters. RepLoRA learns a nonlinear within-layer generator and distinct outputs, so its sharing is softer but its trainable count is larger than LoRA in the reported tables.

reviewed_competitors.title: DoRA: Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Primary empirical baseline and alternative no-inference-overhead improvement.
reviewed_competitors.difference: DoRA separates pretrained-weight magnitude and direction and applies LoRA to directional updates, improving stability across LLaMA, LLaVA, and VL-BART. RepLoRA changes factor optimization through a generator; the two mechanisms are composable and the paper's own baseline results do not isolate matched training cost.

reviewed_competitors.title: LoRA-GA: Low-Rank Adaptation with Gradient Approximation
reviewed_competitors.difference: LoRA-GA aligns the initial low-rank product gradient with full fine-tuning and reports faster convergence without adding a learned generator architecture. It offers a cleaner test of whether LoRA's weakness is initialization and conditioning rather than statistical sample complexity.

reviewed_competitors.title: LoRA-Pro: Are Low-Rank Adapters Properly Optimized?
reviewed_competitors.difference: LoRA-Pro derives adjusted factor gradients whose induced low-rank update better approximates the full-fine-tuning gradient. It studies the actual factor optimization geometry, whereas RepLoRA's central rate theorem studies an expert-specific mixture regression that differs from deployed LoRA.

reviewed_competitors.title: RandLoRA: Full-rank parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large models
reviewed_competitors.difference: RandLoRA learns diagonal scalings over fixed random low-rank bases whose sum yields a full-rank update, explicitly separating parameter count from update-rank capacity. RepLoRA preserves one rank-r deployed update and uses nonlinear train-time overparameterization; comparing the two can diagnose whether its gain comes from optimization or representational rank.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding the Learning Dynamics of LoRA: A Gradient Flow Perspective on Low-Rank Adaptation in Matrix Factorization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Xu et al. analyze gradient-flow dynamics, initialization, and adaptation in matrix factorization, focusing on the optimization actually induced by LoRA factors. Its scope is also simplified, but it avoids identifying token attention with an overfitted MoE and provides a complementary mechanism for convergence behavior.

reviewed_competitors.title: LoRA-One: One-Step Full Gradient Could Suffice for Fine-Tuning Large Language Models, Provably and Efficiently
reviewed_competitors.difference: LoRA-One uses one full-gradient step to initialize a task-relevant low-rank subspace and then fine-tunes efficiently, connecting a concrete algorithm to provable matrix-recovery behavior. It improves LoRA without disposable MLP capacity and offers a more direct theory-to-implementation correspondence.

reviewed_competitors.title: Make LoRA Great Again: Boosting LoRA with Adaptive Singular Values and Mixture-of-Experts Optimization Alignment
reviewed_competitors.difference: GOAT constructs an actual SVD-structured mixture of LoRA experts and derives scaling intended to align its optimization with full fine-tuning, evaluating 25 datasets. RepLoRA instead uses the MoE view as a statistical surrogate for ordinary attention and deploys one generated low-rank update rather than routed adapter experts.

reviewed_competitors.title: DoRAN: Stabilizing Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation via Noise Injection and Auxiliary Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct current successor with overlapping authors.
reviewed_competitors.difference: DoRAN combines DoRA stabilization with auxiliary networks that generate low-rank factors and couple parameters across layers, explicitly extending RepLoRA's generator idea. It makes cross-layer coupling and stability central, while inheriting the need to validate that auxiliary-network theory matches the implemented generator and resource budget.

reviewed_competitors.difference: SetPINNs uses set-based attention over grouped points; ProPINN uses a per-query local stencil and lightweight pooling, but its theoretical guarantee does not apply directly to the implemented mixer.

reviewed_competitors.title: PirateNets: Physics-informed Deep Learning with Residual Adaptive Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Strong residual-network architecture baseline for difficult PDE optimization.
reviewed_competitors.difference: PirateNets uses adaptive residual blocks and random Fourier features to improve trainability and scaling; ProPINN adds local multiscale coordinate neighborhoods and wins the reviewed benchmark panel but is not parameter or compute matched.

reviewed_competitors.title: RoPINN: Region Optimized Physics-Informed Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Same-group regional optimization predecessor and complementary method.
reviewed_competitors.difference: RoPINN optimizes over trust regions around collocation points with generalization analysis; ProPINN changes the network architecture to aggregate differentiable region features and reports additive gains when the two are combined.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Dual Cone Gradient Descent Method for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Optimizer-side alternative grounded in conflicts among the actual PINN loss gradients.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Dual-cone descent constructs directions that reduce multiple physics-loss components and gives nonconvex convergence analysis; ProPINN changes the architecture and analyzes cross-coordinate output gradients instead of competing objective gradients.

reviewed_competitors.title: Challenges in Training PINNs: A Loss Landscape Perspective
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct optimization and conditioning account of PINN training difficulty.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Rathore et al. connect PINN differential operators to ill-conditioned loss landscapes and test second-order remedies such as NysNewton-CG; ProPINN attributes failure to local output-Jacobian coupling and uses an architectural remedy.

reviewed_competitors.title: Kronecker-Factored Approximate Curvature for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Curvature-aware optimizer competitor that directly challenges optimizer-agnostic kernel claims.
reviewed_competitors.difference: KFAC changes the parameter-space metric to address PINN conditioning, making raw Euclidean output-gradient alignment insufficient to predict the update; ProPINN does not analyze its G quantity under this preconditioner.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Limitations of the Neural Tangent Kernel for Understanding Generalization in Physics-Informed Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct warning about extrapolating PINN behavior from linearized kernel dynamics.
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work studies when nonlinear PINN training departs from NTK predictions; ProPINN treats an instantaneous output-Jacobian product as a root-cause diagnostic without testing nonlinear-regime validity.

reviewed_competitors.title: PINNacle: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving PDEs
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Broader benchmark defining the empirical bar for general PINN claims.
reviewed_competitors.difference: PINNacle evaluates many methods over more than twenty PDEs with varied domains and properties; ProPINN reports six tasks, four of them closely related standard 1D+time failure cases.

reviewed_competitors.title: PINNMamba: A sequence modeling framework for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current direct propagation-oriented architecture with a different causal account.
reviewed_competitors.difference: PINNMamba attributes difficulty to simplicity bias and discrete-continuity mismatch and uses selective state-space sequence modeling; ProPINN uses local coordinate stencils and output-gradient alignment. The later method reports broad reductions and raises the architecture baseline.

reviewed_competitors.title: Gradient Alignment in Physics-informed Neural Networks: A Second-Order Optimization Perspective
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later diagnostic and optimizer work centered on actual loss-gradient conflict.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Gradient Alignment studies directions among physics-loss gradients and uses a second-order optimizer across ten PDEs including harder flow regimes; ProPINN studies output Jacobians across coordinates and does not include the residual values or optimizer metric in G.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Consistency of Physics-Informed Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later theory giving a stronger criterion for whether small PINN loss identifies the physical solution.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The consistency work states necessary and sufficient conditions and constructs pathological cases; ProPINN's local kernel criterion is neither shown necessary nor sufficient for convergence from residual loss to the correct solution.

reviewed_competitors.title: PINN Balls: A Local Mixture of Experts for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later local-region architecture and domain-decomposition competitor.
reviewed_competitors.difference: PINN Balls uses local experts, adaptive sampling, and second-order optimization to allocate capacity spatially; ProPINN keeps one global network and augments each coordinate with a dense local stencil.

reviewed_competitors.title: NeuSA: Neural Spectral Architectures for Physics-Informed Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later architecture addressing spectral and causal training limitations.
reviewed_competitors.difference: NeuSA builds spectral structure and causality into the representation and releases a broader artifact; ProPINN uses spatial stencil pooling without an explicit spectral treatment of high-frequency solutions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Dual Natural Gradient Descent for Scalable Physics-Informed Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Dual natural gradient works in residual space with Gauss-Newton structure and scales to models reported up to 12.8 million parameters; ProPINN reports low-dimensional coordinate tasks and its dense stencil count grows exponentially with input dimension.

reviewed_competitors.title: Per-Loss Adapters for Gradient Conflict in Physics-Informed Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current diagnostic-first work testing when loss-gradient conflict actually occurs.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Per-Loss Adapters evaluates gradient conflict across sixty PDE configurations up to fifty dimensions and finds the mechanism is not universal; ProPINN makes a broad root-cause claim from a local output-kernel diagnostic on six low-dimensional tasks.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Pearce et al. train bilinear GLUs whose computation is exactly quadratic, so interaction tensors and their eigenvectors come directly from weights and are studied on toy, vision, and language tasks. The reviewed paper instead approximates ordinary ReLU/GELU/GLU modules post hoc, preserving pretrained architectures but making interpretability conditional on reference-distribution fidelity.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Networks Learn Statistics of Increasing Complexity
reviewed_competitors.difference: Belrose et al. test distributional simplicity bias by evaluating networks on maximum-entropy distributions with matched low-order moments and by editing class statistics, including evidence in language models. The reviewed work supplies analytic polynomial projections and a sharper linear-versus-quadratic trajectory on MNIST, but does not extend the empirical result beyond that shallow setting.

reviewed_competitors.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sparse autoencoders learn an overcomplete, sparsely active dictionary from actual model activations and demonstrate finer causal localization on a language-model circuit. Polynomial conversion needs no auxiliary feature-learning model and exposes weight-derived interactions, but assumes an input distribution, scales poorly beyond degree two, and has not yet shown semantic language features.

reviewed_competitors.title: PolySAE: Modeling Feature Interactions in Sparse Autoencoders via Polynomial Decoding
reviewed_competitors.difference: PolySAE retains sparse learned activation features but augments decoding with polynomial terms to capture compositional interactions, reporting improved probing while avoiding a full dense input polynomial. It targets representation decomposition rather than closed-form approximation of MLP weights and illustrates a scalable hybrid direction between SAE dictionaries and polynomial interactions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Shampoo: Preconditioned Stochastic Tensor Optimization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Shampoo maintains Kronecker-factored tensor second moments and inverse roots throughout training. EGOP instead chooses a gradient-covariance eigenbasis and then delegates coordinate scaling to Adam/Adagrad; its full-vector basis is less structurally constrained but far less scalable.

reviewed_competitors.title: Gradient Descent for Low-Rank Functions
reviewed_competitors.difference: Low-Rank Gradient Descent first identifies significant EGOP directions and then estimates gradients along them to reduce directional-oracle complexity for exactly or approximately low-rank functions. The present paper retains full-dimensional optimization and uses the basis to improve diagonal adaptive geometry under spectral decay.

reviewed_competitors.title: GaLore: Memory-Efficient LLM Training by Gradient Low-Rank Projection
reviewed_competitors.difference: GaLore periodically projects matrix gradients into a low-rank subspace to reduce optimizer-state memory in LLM training. EGOP estimates covariance across parameter samples and uses a full or auxiliary coordinate rotation; it targets convergence geometry rather than primarily memory.

reviewed_competitors.title: SOAP: Improving and Stabilizing Shampoo using Adam
reviewed_competitors.difference: SOAP repeatedly rotates matrix gradients into Shampoo's left/right preconditioner eigenbases and applies Adam there, reporting LLM-scale gains. EGOP uses a generally unrestricted vector basis and argues one up-front estimate can suffice, but its large-scale implementation reintroduces blocks, sharing, and periodic updates.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding Adam Requires Better Rotation Dependent Assumptions
reviewed_competitors.difference: Maes et al. show transformer Adam degrades under random rotations and evaluate structured rotations and rotation-dependent assumptions. That work diagnoses the phenomenon and explores matrix-shaped bases; EGOP proposes a distributional full-vector basis and a conditional Adagrad bound.

reviewed_competitors.title: Muon is Scalable for LLM Training
reviewed_competitors.difference: Muon orthogonalizes matrix momentum rather than estimating a gradient-covariance basis, and reports distributed MoE training plus roughly twofold compute efficiency over AdamW. It is less adaptive to a population EGOP but much more directly validated at frontier training scale.

reviewed_competitors.title: Purifying Shampoo: Investigating Shampoo's Heuristics by Decomposing its Preconditioner
reviewed_competitors.difference: Purifying Shampoo separates eigenvalue correction from eigenbasis refresh and supplies an adaptive refresh criterion. It directly tackles basis staleness and scaling, two issues left unformalized in periodic EGOP, while retaining Kronecker structure.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Stable Whitening Optimizer for Efficient Neural Network Training
reviewed_competitors.difference: SPlus combines a historical matrix eigenbasis with bounded instantaneous normalization, shape-aware scaling, and iterate averaging, and benchmarks language, vision, and diffusion transformers. Its validation and engineering directly target stable low-overhead whitening that EGOP's one-shot/full-basis story does not establish.

reviewed_competitors.title: AdaMuon: Adaptive Muon Optimizer
reviewed_competitors.difference: AdaMuon applies elementwise second-moment adaptation after orthogonalizing updates and RMS-aligns its scale to Adam. It combines adaptivity and spectral geometry online without a sampled EGOP, challenging the need for an expensive precomputed unrestricted basis.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding and Improving Shampoo and SOAP via Kullback-Leibler Minimization
reviewed_competitors.difference: KL-Shampoo treats structured second-moment tracking as covariance estimation and improves conditioning and stability without Adam's extra state. It attacks the estimation problem online, whereas EGOP provides no finite-sample estimator-to-convergence analysis.

reviewed_competitors.title: How do simple rotations affect the implicit bias of Adam?
reviewed_competitors.difference: The same authors show coordinate rotations can reverse Adam's richness bias in binary classification and use EGOP-style reparameterization to restore rotation equivariance. It strengthens the motivation but studies implicit bias, not scalable convergence or estimator validity.

reviewed_competitors.title: DASH: Faster Shampoo via Batched Block Preconditioning and Efficient Inverse-Root Solvers
reviewed_competitors.difference: DASH batches Shampoo blocks and adds faster, better-scaled inverse-root solvers, reporting up to 4.83x faster optimizer steps and releasing code. It narrows the wall-clock objection to structured preconditioners that supports EGOP's ImageNet comparison against an older SOAP implementation.

reviewed_competitors.title: SOAP, Muon, and Beyond: Pushing LLM Pretraining Scales
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work scales SOAP and Muon to multi-billion-parameter and MoE training, identifies stale-basis SOAP instabilities, repairs them with current-gradient per-step updates and KL covariance estimation, and releases a distributed library. It supplies the scale, state/basis diagnostics, and modern comparator suite absent from the EGOP paper.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
reviewed_competitors.relationship: closest prior framework for test-time compute scaling
reviewed_competitors.difference: Snell et al. compare process-verifier search and adaptive distribution updates, show strong dependence on per-prompt difficulty, and derive a compute-optimal allocation that is over four times more efficient than best-of-N. s1 deliberately removes reward/search machinery and gains mechanical token control, but uses uniform budgets and does not solve the harder allocation problem.

reviewed_competitors.title: Inference Scaling Laws: An Empirical Analysis of Compute-Optimal Inference for Problem-Solving with Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wu et al. evaluate greedy, voting, best-of-N, weighted voting, and tree search across model sizes and budgets, including explicit cost-performance Pareto comparisons. s1 contributes a much simpler sequential delimiter intervention and an open distilled checkpoint, but its proposed slope/control summaries are narrower and its cross-algorithm accounting is not compute matched.

reviewed_competitors.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: concurrent stronger open reasoning and natural test-time scaling approach
reviewed_competitors.difference: DeepSeek-R1 uses large-scale reinforcement learning and multi-stage post-training to induce long reasoning, self-reflection, and adaptive compute without manually overriding every stop. It is far more resource intensive, while s1 is cheap and reproducible; however, R1 strongly outperforms s1 and becomes the teacher whose traces produce the paper's better s1.1 model.

reviewed_competitors.title: LIMO: Less is More for Reasoning
reviewed_competitors.difference: LIMO independently argues that a strong pretrained knowledge base can be activated by a few strategically designed reasoning demonstrations and reports strong AIME/MATH results with 817 examples. It reinforces s1's elicitation thesis while showing that sample efficiency is not unique to budget forcing; later versions report higher math accuracy and emphasize template quality and OOD generalization.

reviewed_competitors.title: It's Not That Simple. An Analysis of Simple Test-Time Scaling
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wu reproduces the distinction visible but underemphasized in s1: most of the curve comes from scaling down with maximum lengths, while appending 'Wait' gives inconsistent scaling up and can oscillate among solutions. The audit argues that genuine test-time scaling should exceed a model's unconstrained peak rather than manufacture a curve by progressively lowering its upper bound.

reviewed_competitors.title: Does Thinking More always Help? Mirage of Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: subsequent multi-model audit of extended thinking and alternative
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ghosal et al. find a recurring improve-then-decline pattern from forced longer traces, model it as increased output variance, and report that matched-budget parallel thinking with majority selection can beat extended thinking by up to 20%. This directly challenges s1's intuition that sequential scaling is inherently more effective, an intuition s1 tests with confounded checkpoints.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning a Continue-Thinking Token for Enhanced Test-Time Scaling
reviewed_competitors.relationship: direct learned replacement for fixed 'Wait' forcing
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ringel et al. freeze a distilled reasoning model and use reinforcement learning to train only a dedicated continue-thinking embedding. It improves over both no intervention and fixed 'Wait' on several math tasks, suggesting that continuation should be learned as an action with outcome feedback rather than triggered by an arbitrary ordinary-language token.

reviewed_competitors.title: Non-vacuous Generalization Bounds for Deep Neural Networks without any modification to the trained models
reviewed_competitors.difference: This 2025 PAC-Bayes work targets unmodified pretrained networks and ImageNet-scale certification, addressing model and data scales not tested by the thesis, while requiring a more elaborate rigorous certificate than the universal 2 N_out/P heuristic.

reviewed_competitors.title: Non-Gaussian processes and neural networks at finite widths
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yaida develops perturbative finite-width non-Gaussian corrections around the infinite-width process; the thesis instead studies a non-perturbative proportional P/N limit and turns its correction into data-dependent kernel renormalization.

reviewed_competitors.title: Asymptotics of representation learning in finite Bayesian neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work derives universal leading finite-width corrections to learned kernels; the thesis pursues an order-one proportional-width regime where width and data scale together and the Gaussian-process expansion is no longer sufficient.

reviewed_competitors.title: Critical feature learning in deep neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Fischer et al. derive exact proportional-limit feature-learning equations for deep nonlinear Bayesian networks as a superposition of Gaussian processes with forward-backward MAP kernels; this more explicitly characterizes deep representation adaptation than the thesis's approximate forward scalar renormalization.

reviewed_competitors.title: A theory of representation learning gives a deep generalisation of kernel methods
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yang et al. obtain a scalable deep kernel machine from a Bayesian representation-learning limit; the thesis holds P/width finite and emphasizes finite-width non-Gaussianity and scalar kernel renormalization instead.

reviewed_competitors.title: Kernel Renormalization in Bayesian Deep Neural Networks: the Equivalent Wishart Ansatz in the Proportional Regime
reviewed_competitors.difference: The 2026 equivalent-Wishart approach reaches nonlinear MLPs of depth around ten, P around one thousand, and convolutional local kernels while documenting systematic deviations, directly extending and stress-testing the thesis's approximate deep renormalization program.

reviewed_competitors.title: Precise gradient descent training dynamics for finite-width multi-layer neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Han and Imaizumi give non-asymptotic state evolution for actual gradient-descent iterates and generalization in a finite-width proportional feature/sample regime; their bounded-width single-index setting is narrower in another direction but covers dynamics absent from the thesis's equilibrium Bayesian theory.

reviewed_competitors.title: On Learnability via Gradient Method for Two-Layer ReLU Neural Networks in Teacher-Student Setting

reviewed_competitors.title: Get rich quick: exact solutions reveal how unbalanced initializations promote rapid feature learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kunin et al. derive how layerwise initialization variances and learning rates select lazy versus rich dynamics and validate the mechanism in deeper finite networks; this makes parametrization and optimizer balance independent causal axes beyond the thesis's P/N_tot transition.

reviewed_competitors.title: Cross-modality Matching and Prediction of Perturbation Responses with Labeled Gromov-Wasserstein Optimal Transport
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct implementation for the paper's unpaired-distribution and missing-cross-modality problem.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Labeled Gromov-Wasserstein OT aligns perturbation-labeled modalities and validates cross-modality prediction on multimodal single-cell data; the reviewed paper names OT as an appropriate loss but does not instantiate or compare it in its demonstration.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Scalable Gene Network Model of Regulatory Dynamics in Single Cells
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later semi-mechanistic ODE competitor that turns gene-regulatory structure and pseudotime into a scalable predictive model.
reviewed_competitors.difference: FLeCS fits coupled gene-level dynamics across differentiation, K562 Perturb-seq, and drug trajectories and evaluates regulatory interpretation; it operationalizes the reviewed paper's general argument at far greater scale but still inherits pseudotime and dynamical-model assumptions.

reviewed_competitors.title: CLAMP: Steady-State ODE Inference of Gene Regulatory Networks from Single-Cell Perturbations
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current direct realization of the reviewed paper's steady-state regulatory-model thesis.
reviewed_competitors.difference: CLAMP learns one nonlinear Hill-kinetics network across perturbations and differentiates through constrained fixed points to predict combinatorial responses from endpoint snapshots; the reviewed proof only regularizes an implicit NODE with presumed steady states and does not recover a shared interpretable regulatory object.

reviewed_competitors.title: Compositional Generalization in Unsupervised Compositional Representation Learning: A Study on Disentanglement and Emergent Language
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest architectural and empirical predecessor and the direct VAE+EL baseline.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Xu et al. already use a VAE-backed sender-receiver discrete reconstruction game and compare emergent messages with disentangled continuous representations. CELEBI adds iterated transmission, prefix reconstruction, final-state imitation, and diversity regularization, but retains the same synthetic-factor evaluation regime.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Correspondence between Compositionality and Imitation in Emergent Neural Communication
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest apparently uncited predecessor for imitation inside a reconstruction Lewis game.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The prior work studies sender and receiver imitation, including imitation through decoded reconstructions, and finds compositional languages easier to imitate. CELEBI's narrower distinction is to reset only the sender and train it through a frozen old receiver's final-output equivalence classes rather than establishing reconstruction-level imitation itself.

reviewed_competitors.title: Emergent Communication: Generalization and Overfitting in Lewis Games
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct theoretical predecessor for reconstruction Lewis games and co-adaptation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Rita et al. decompose Lewis-game error into information and co-adaptation losses and improve structure by regularizing listener convergence. CELEBI instead alternates generations and modifies prefix, state-imitation, and diversity objectives without explicitly separating those two overfitting sources.

reviewed_competitors.title: Compositional Languages Emerge in a Neural Iterated Learning Model
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ren et al. establish that alternating learning and interaction amplifies easy-to-learn compositional protocols and improves generalization. CELEBI applies the principle to image reconstruction and changes the transmitted target from messages to final receiver states.

reviewed_competitors.title: Ease-of-Teaching and Language Structure from Emergent Communication
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Early direct work on teachability pressure and populations in emergent language.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Li and Bowling use teaching between agents to select structured languages and study population effects. CELEBI uses a single teacher-receiver state target and does not evaluate heterogeneous learners or population communication.

reviewed_competitors.title: An Iterated Learning Model of Language Change That Mixes Supervised and Unsupervised Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: This model jointly uses separately learned signal-to-meaning and meaning-to-signal networks as an autoencoder across generations and reports expressive, compositional, stable languages. It makes the broad autoencoder-plus-IL combination prior; CELEBI differs in high-dimensional images, a discrete bottleneck, progressive prefixes, and frozen-receiver FiSI.

reviewed_competitors.title: Compositionality and Generalization in Emergent Languages
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Key metric and transmission study that complicates equating TopSim with generalization.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chaabouni et al. find that compositionality and generalization can decouple while compositional protocols are easier to transmit, and introduce factor-sensitive diagnostics. CELEBI uses TopSim as its primary structure metric and does not perform a held-out learner transmission test.

reviewed_competitors.title: Entropy Minimization in Emergent Languages
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational information-theoretic pressure on discrete emergent protocols.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kharitonov et al. distinguish entropy and mutual information in learned languages and use entropy minimization to shape protocols. CELEBI instead maximizes a batch-marginal diversity surrogate during imitation; its theory should explicitly distinguish message entropy, conditional entropy, and input-message mutual information.

reviewed_competitors.title: Concept-Best-Matching: Evaluating Compositionality in Emergent Communication
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct evaluation competitor to TopSim-only compositionality claims.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Concept-Best-Matching recovers interpretable word-to-concept assignments and measures compositional alignment directly. CELEBI's claims that prefixes and symbols encode structured factors would be stronger with this type of concept-level validation rather than distance correlation and selected reconstructions alone.

reviewed_competitors.title: Improving Compositional Generalization Using Iterated Learning and Simplicial Embeddings
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest prior combination of iterated learning, discrete-like representations, Kolmogorov motivation, and visual factor tasks.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ren et al. use simplicial embeddings and validate on vision plus real molecular graphs, giving broader downstream evidence. CELEBI centers an explicit sender-receiver reconstruction channel and introduces final-state and prefix objectives but evaluates only rendered images.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Complexity-Based Theory of Compositionality
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Concurrent formal account of compositionality as expressivity under reusable description-length compression.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Elmoznino et al. define an explicit Kolmogorov-compression ratio and test prequential-code surrogates, showing where TopSim disagrees. CELEBI uses informal code-length comparisons to motivate a training regularizer but never estimates the description length of its learned messages.

reviewed_competitors.title: Interaction Asymmetry: A General Principle for Learning Composable Abstractions
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporary alternative for learning composable visual representations from decoder structure.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Brady et al. derive identifiability conditions from cross-concept interaction asymmetry and implement an attention-regularized Transformer VAE. CELEBI imposes communication and cultural-transmission pressures, with weaker identifiability theory but a discrete anytime channel.

reviewed_competitors.title: Semantics and Spatiality of Emergent Communication
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporary formal analysis of semantic structure induced by reconstruction objectives.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The paper proves that reconstruction rules out some semantically inconsistent optima and encourages distance-preserving meaning structure. CELEBI can claim that its added pressures improve selected empirical structure measures, but not that reconstruction's semantic-geometric inductive bias is itself new.

reviewed_competitors.title: Additive Decoders for Latent Variables Identification and Cartesian-Product Extrapolation
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Stronger identifiability and unseen-recombination alternative for composable visual representations.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lachapelle et al. derive conditions under which additive decoders identify latent components and extrapolate over their Cartesian product. CELEBI's generic frozen VAE decoder has neither guarantee, so TopSim and reconstruction gains should not be interpreted as component identification or guaranteed recombination.

reviewed_competitors.title: Object-Centric Learning with Slot Attention
reviewed_competitors.difference: Slot Attention learns exchangeable object-bound slots through reconstruction, providing a much stronger structural prior than an ordered token string. CELEBI's symbols are not object slots; any object-centric interpretation requires binding, permutation, and multi-object recombination tests against this family.

reviewed_competitors.title: Compositionality with Variation Reliably Emerges in Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct evidence on compressibility-expressivity pressures in iterated neural communication.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Conklin and Smith show that structured but variable languages emerge when learning, interaction, and transmission bottlenecks are balanced and introduce additional language-variation measures. CELEBI adapts this pressure balance to reconstruction but its own appendix finds those measures inconclusive.

reviewed_competitors.title: Emergent Communication at Scale
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Large-scale study of environmental and population pressures on emergent protocols.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chaabouni et al. study many agents and vast meaning spaces, exposing how scale, community structure, and training conditions shape language. CELEBI uses two LSTM agents and two fixed synthetic datasets, allowing cleaner reconstruction ablations but much narrower ecological validity.

reviewed_competitors.title: LazImpa: Lazy and Impatient Neural Agents Learn to Communicate Efficiently
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct predecessor for supervising listener predictions at each message prefix.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Rita et al.'s impatient listener predicts after every prefix and combines this with a length pressure in referential games. CELEBI's Progressive Decoding transfers the same anytime-information idea to pixel reconstruction and uses geometric prefix weighting, making PD an adaptation more than a wholly new principle.

reviewed_competitors.title: Iterated Learning Improves Compositionality in Large Vision-Language Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Higher-scale visual-language application of iterated cultural transmission.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zheng et al. reset vision or language agents during CLIP-style training on CC3M and CC12M and improve SugarCrepe, supplying natural-image and large-model evidence. CELEBI offers finer discrete-channel mechanisms and reconstruction diagnostics but does not test whether they scale to such data.

reviewed_competitors.title: Emergent Corpus Pre-training Benefits Vision Language Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later downstream validation of emergent discrete visual tokens in pretrained VLMs.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ogunleye et al. use an emergent corpus for VLM pretraining and report gains on visual referring expression and entailment tasks. It tests external usefulness at a much higher semantic level, whereas CELEBI isolates protocol geometry and reconstruction on known-factor renders.

reviewed_competitors.title: CtD: Composition through Decomposition in Emergent Communication
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest later visual competitor with explicit concept codes and novel composition.
reviewed_competitors.difference: CtD learns an explicit concept codebook and decomposes scenes so agents can compose and sometimes zero-shot communicate unseen images. It uses stronger concept supervision and is not a concept-label-free reconstruction IL method, but its semantic and recombination tests are substantially more direct than CELEBI's TopSim evidence.

reviewed_competitors.title: OmniPred: Language Models as Universal Regressors
reviewed_competitors.difference: OmniPred trains one language model across heterogeneous black-box optimization tasks with both inputs and scalar outputs serialized as text. Decoding-based Regression isolates the output side by attaching a tiny decoder to a fixed feature representation, adds normalized and floating-point vocabularies, compares ordinary heads, and studies conditional density estimation rather than cross-task transfer.

reviewed_competitors.title: From Words to Numbers: Your Large Language Model Is Secretly A Capable Regressor When Given In-Context Examples
reviewed_competitors.difference: Vacareanu et al. prompt pretrained service and open models with regression examples and study regret without gradient updates. The target instead trains a small numeric head from scratch on arbitrary encoder features and attributes data efficiency to hierarchical output representation; it does not test pretrained in-context reasoning.

reviewed_competitors.title: Regression Aware Inference with LLMs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lukasik et al. show that ordinary autoregressive samples are suboptimal for regression metrics and estimate Bayes-optimal decisions from an LLM's generated responses. The target cites this point-estimation principle but focuses on the head's representation, histogram risk, and density fit; its sampling and aggregation rule remains a tuned application choice.

reviewed_competitors.title: Better autoregressive regression with LLMs via regression-aware fine-tuning
reviewed_competitors.difference: RAFT derives a Bayes-optimal regression-aware fine-tuning loss for decoder LLMs and compares autoregressive and predictive-head approaches across natural-language regression benchmarks. Decoding-based Regression keeps standard token cross-entropy, isolates a lightweight numeric head on tabular encoders, and uniquely evaluates arbitrary one-dimensional densities and hierarchical histogram risk.

reviewed_competitors.title: Regress, Don't Guess: A Regression-like Loss on Number Tokens for Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Number Token Loss augments cross-entropy with Lp- or Wasserstein-based distance between numeric token values, improves arithmetic, matches a regression head on one regression task, and scales to 3B parameters without inference overhead. It directly addresses the nominal-token-loss weakness that the target accepts and tries to overcome through hierarchical coding and data.

reviewed_competitors.title: Beyond Token-level Supervision: Unlocking the Potential of Decoding-based Regression via Reinforcement Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chen et al. explicitly build on decoding-based regression and replace purely token-level supervision with sequence-level numerical rewards optimized by ReMax or GRPO. They report gains over token-loss and traditional heads on tabular and code-metric regression, narrowing the target's claim that ordinary cross-entropy plus representation design is sufficient for highest precision.
