reviewed_competitors.difference: It is diagnostic rather than an equilibrium circuit-selection theory, but demonstrates that optimiser dynamics contain predictive signal beyond static efficiency.

reviewed_competitors.title: Grokking as the Transition from Lazy to Rich Training Dynamics
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct lazy-kernel to feature-learning theory with an explicit zero-weight-decay regime.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It covers the no-decay case the target explicitly cannot explain and focuses on representation dynamics rather than circuit norm allocation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Grokking as a First Order Phase Transition in Two Layer Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Adaptive-kernel and statistical-physics account of abrupt feature transitions.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It analytically models trainable feature dynamics without hard-coded memorising and generalising lookup circuits.

reviewed_competitors.title: Dichotomy of Early and Late Phase Implicit Biases Can Provably Induce Grokking
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Proves a long early kernel-like phase followed by a late min-norm or max-margin phase.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It gives a rigorous optimisation transition in neural settings rather than assuming slow and fast scalar circuit strengths.

reviewed_competitors.title: To grok or not to grok: Disentangling generalization and memorization on corrupted algorithmic datasets
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Identifies and prunes memorising neurons while retaining generalising representations under label corruption.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It supports coexistence of solution types but provides more component-level causal evidence and compares several regularisers.

reviewed_competitors.title: Deep Networks Always Grok and Here is Why
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Explains delayed generalisation and robustness through migration of local spline-region complexity on realistic vision data.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It has broader task and architecture scope and does not require a two-circuit logit-efficiency decomposition.

reviewed_competitors.title: Why Do You Grok? A Theoretical Analysis on Grokking Modular Addition
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Formal analysis of early kernel failure and later bounded-norm feature learning for modular addition.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It studies how the generalising representation is found, which the target's fixed lookup-table model assumes away.

reviewed_competitors.title: Grokking Group Multiplication with Cosets
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Mechanistically reverse-engineers group-multiplication circuits with subgroup and coset structure.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It shows that actual learned algorithms can be task-specific and supports causal circuit analysis rather than a generic residual label.

reviewed_competitors.title: Grokfast: Accelerated Grokking by Amplifying Slow Gradients
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Causally accelerates grokking by amplifying slow gradient components across multiple domains.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It intervenes on the proposed slow-learning signal directly and does not require measuring logit-per-norm circuit efficiency.

reviewed_competitors.title: Progress Measures for Grokking on Real-world Tasks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Evaluates activation sparsity, weight entropy, and local circuit-complexity proxies on real-world tasks.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It broadens progress measurement beyond L2 norm and challenges treating Euclidean norm as the primary causal statistic.

reviewed_competitors.title: Grokking at the Edge of Numerical Stability
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Attributes delay to cross-entropy logit scaling and Softmax Collapse and uses StableMax and gradient interventions.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It supplies strong causal alternatives and enables or accelerates grokking without the target's weight-decay-mediated circuit competition.

reviewed_competitors.title: Grokking Beyond the Euclidean Norm of Model Parameters
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct generalisation of norm-based grokking to sparsity, low rank, and other explicit or implicit regularisers.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It shows L2 norm can increase while grokking occurs, directly limiting the target's Euclidean efficiency metric.

reviewed_competitors.title: Grokking at the Edge of Linear Separability
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Produces arbitrarily delayed generalisation in a minimal logistic setting near a separability critical point.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It sharply defines memorising and generalising solutions without discrete neural circuits or a dataset-dependent norm-efficiency crossover.

reviewed_competitors.title: Emergence in non-neural models: grokking modular arithmetic via average gradient outer product
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Demonstrates modular-arithmetic grokking in recursive feature machines and kernel-like non-neural models.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It shows task-feature emergence can suffice without neural circuit competition or ordinary network gradient descent.

reviewed_competitors.title: Model Capacity Determines Grokking through Competing Memorisation and Generalisation Speeds
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current direct competition model based on measurable capacity-dependent memorisation and generalisation times.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It keeps the competition picture but makes relative learning speed and capacity, rather than equilibrium parameter efficiency, primary.

reviewed_competitors.title: What Does the Weight Norm Control in Grokking? Logit-Scale Mediation under Cross-Entropy
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Uses norm clamps and output-temperature interventions to separate weight magnitude from effective logit scale.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It partly supports attention to logits but argues norm is an upstream handle rather than an intrinsic circuit-efficiency cause.

reviewed_competitors.title: Circuit Synchronization Precedes Generalization: A Causal Precursor to Grokking
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Introduces a circuit-progress metric, permutation controls, and a weight-decay intervention preceding generalisation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It offers a more causal circuit measurement and timing law but does not use the target's logit-per-norm efficiency proxy.

reviewed_competitors.title: Structure-Specific Representational Priors Causally Control the Grokking Delay
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Uses matched true, sibling, random, and norm-controlled structure priors to manipulate grokking delay.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It causally separates task structure from norm and argues feature-formation time, not only low-norm selection, controls delay.

reviewed_competitors.title: Cross-Trajectory Chimera Interventions Reveal Dissociable Roles of Weight Magnitude and Direction in Grokking
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Cross-seed interventions decompose the causal roles of parameter direction and magnitude.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It finds direction transfers circuit identity while magnitude mainly modulates delay, a stronger causal decomposition than whole-model norm correlations.

reviewed_competitors.difference: OFA progressively shrinks depth, width, kernel size, and resolution, then searches the trained supernet for hardware-specific subnetworks. reviewed_competitors.title: Sorted LLaMA: Unlocking the Potential of Intermediate Layers of Large Language Models for Dynamic Inference
reviewed_competitors.difference: The authors' follow-up specializes sorted intermediate-layer supervision to LLaMA and develops dynamic inference in substantially more detail. It narrows, rather than independently validates, the reviewed paper's brief one-task LLaMA demonstration.

reviewed_competitors.title: MatFormer: Nested Transformer for Elastic Inference
reviewed_competitors.difference: MatFormer jointly trains nested FFN granularities and extracts hundreds of Mix'n'Match variants across language and vision up to 2.6B parameters. SortedNet covers more architectural axes in principle, but provides smaller-scale evidence and no public artifact; MatFormer also exposes that heuristic or NAS selection remains distinct from nested training.

reviewed_competitors.title: Flextron: Many-in-One Flexible Large Language Model
reviewed_competitors.difference: Flextron transforms pretrained GPT-3 and Llama-2 models into nested elastic LLMs using 7.63% of original pretraining tokens and learns input-adaptive routing to latency/accuracy targets. SortedNet is simpler and earlier but evaluates one LLaMA-13B task without a trained router or matched large-scale language frontier.

reviewed_competitors.title: Draft & Verify: Lossless Large Language Model Acceleration via Self-Speculative Decoding
reviewed_competitors.difference: Draft & Verify skips intermediate LLaMA-2 layers for drafting, verifies with the unchanged model, requires no training or extra memory, guarantees identical output, and reports up to 1.99x speedup. SortedNet reports a similar peak speed but requires training and its aggregate GSM8K accuracy changes from full decoding.

reviewed_competitors.title: HydraViT: Stacking Heads for a Scalable ViT
reviewed_competitors.difference: HydraViT varies embedding width and attention-head count and directly benchmarks SortedNet on ImageNet-1K, reporting up to five percentage points higher accuracy at equal GMACs and seven at equal throughput across ten subnetworks. This is the clearest later primary evidence against SortedNet's broad empirical-superiority framing.

reviewed_competitors.title: LLaMaFlex: Many-in-one LLMs via Generalized Pruning and Weight Sharing
reviewed_competitors.difference: LLaMaFlex starts from Llama 3.1 8B, performs about 60B tokens of elastic continuation, and learns a Gumbel-Softmax router that yields width/depth-pruned variants from 1B to 8B without per-variant tuning. It supplies modern LLM scale and automatic budget routing absent from SortedNet, though at substantial post-training cost.

reviewed_competitors.title: ThinkingViT: Matryoshka Thinking Vision Transformer for Elastic Inference
reviewed_competitors.difference: ThinkingViT progressively activates attention heads per image and recycles earlier features, directly comparing against SortedNet, MatFormer, and HydraViT on ImageNet-1K. Version 3 reports gains up to 2.0 points at equal throughput and 2.9 at equal GMACs over nested baselines, adding input adaptivity that SortedNet only proposes as future work.

reviewed_competitors.title: Star Elastic: Many-in-One Reasoning LLMs with Efficient Budget Control
reviewed_competitors.difference: Star Elastic adds routed nested SSM, embedding, MoE, and FFN submodels to Nemotron Nano reasoning models in one 160B-token post-training run and varies submodels across thinking and answering phases. As a 2026 preprint it is not peer-reviewed, but it extends the many-in-one idea to hybrid 30B-class reasoning models and phase-adaptive budgets far beyond SortedNet's GSM8K study.

reviewed_competitors.title: Predicting the Generalization Gap in Deep Networks with Margin Distributions
reviewed_competitors.difference: Jiang and colleagues summarize normalized Taylor-margin distributions at multiple hidden layers and fit a regression model to generalization gaps. The target paper instead uses one scalar mean distance in the common input space, avoids a learned regressor and layer matching, and changes the metric through a PCA-restricted search; it does not reproduce Jiang's cross-model regression protocol.

reviewed_competitors.title: Representation Based Complexity Measures for Predicting Generalization in Deep Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Natekar and Sharma's winning PGDL solution scores internal representation clustering and augments hidden-margin signals with mixup or transformed samples. It achieves a lower held-out average in the target's imported table but wins several individual tasks, has released code, and probes learned features; constrained margin needs no augmentation or hidden-layer choice but adds PCA and iterative-gradient assumptions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Measuring Generalization with Optimal Transport
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chuang and colleagues normalize output or hidden margins with an optimal-transport k-variance that captures class-feature concentration and accompany the estimator with generalization bounds. The target uses unlabeled input PCA and projected input gradients, reports stronger selected PGDL aggregates, but supplies no generalization bound and does not validate PCA variance as feature concentration or data support.

reviewed_competitors.title: Predicting Deep Neural Network Generalization with Perturbation Response Curves
reviewed_competitors.difference: Schiff and colleagues integrate accuracy over intra- and inter-class mixup perturbation strengths into Gi and Pal statistics. Their signal measures functional response without solving a boundary or fitting PCA and is the strongest held-out comparator imported by the target; constrained margin reports a higher held-out average but only a four-point per-task win count and no unified rerun.

reviewed_competitors.title: On Predicting Generalization using GANs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhang and colleagues train class-conditional GANs and use classifier accuracy on generated labeled samples as a pseudo-test score, winning four of six retained PGDL tasks but failing to support two small imbalanced datasets. The target explicitly excludes this comparator, avoids generator training, and offers an intrinsic geometric score, but lacks the GAN paper's direct accuracy interpretation and broad model-pool regressions.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Missing Margin: How Sample Corruption Affects Distance to the Boundary in ANNs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Theunissen, Mouton, and Davel show that noise types can produce similarly small input margins while affecting generalization differently, linking margins to sample remoteness and nearest different-target samples. That result already undermines a global raw-margin statistic; the target responds by selecting high-variance PCA directions, but does not establish that those directions resolve the predecessor's class-conditional or noise-type ambiguities.

reviewed_competitors.title: Disentangling Adversarial Robustness and Generalization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Stutz, Hein, and Schiele construct or approximate generative manifolds and distinguish on-manifold adversarial errors from ordinary off-manifold perturbations, directly testing robustness and generalization on synthetic and real datasets. The target borrows this intuition but replaces a generative manifold with a global PCA plane and never verifies that its boundary points are on-manifold.

reviewed_competitors.title: On margin-based generalization prediction in deep neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Mouton's thesis embeds the target study in a broader audit of input and hidden margins, reports additional failure analysis, and frames the real open problem as choosing an appropriate distance metric. It consolidates rather than independently reproduces the constrained-margin result, so it strengthens provenance and context but is not external validation.

It requires an unlabeled population sample and a certifiable surrogate, unlike the target's training-only scalar, but yields a formal certificate instead of benchmark correlation and illustrates how the field had moved beyond uncalibrated model-zoo ranking by 2026.

reviewed_competitors.difference: ITI learns truth directions and head selection from hundreds of labeled examples and applies them across inference positions, reporting a truthfulness-helpfulness trade-off. ActAdd needs only one prompt pair and targets broader behaviors, but supplies no comparable truthfulness benchmark or learned selectivity.

reviewed_competitors.title: Representation Engineering: A Top-Down Approach to AI Transparency
reviewed_competitors.difference: RepE systematizes population-level reading and control with multiple direction-estimation and intervention methods across honesty, harmlessness, power seeking, and other safety behaviors. ActAdd contributes an earlier, narrower, unusually cheap prompt-pair arithmetic interface and concrete topic, sentiment, and toxicity experiments.

reviewed_competitors.title: Steering Llama 2 via Contrastive Activation Addition
reviewed_competitors.difference: CAA averages residual differences over many paired positive and negative behavioral examples and adds the resulting vector at all post-prompt token positions on Llama 2 Chat. It offers broader behavioral datasets, capability checks, and prompt/finetuning combinations; ActAdd is much cheaper to specify but more sensitive to one hand-built pair.

reviewed_competitors.title: DESTEIN: Navigating Detoxification of Language Models via Universal Steering Pairs and Head-wise Activation Fusion
reviewed_competitors.difference: DeStein self-induces universal toxic/non-toxic pairs and fuses detoxification vectors head-wise across several white-box models, directly targeting the toxicity-quality frontier. ActAdd uses one general love-minus-hate residual tensor and is simpler, but its detoxification comparison predates and omits this stronger task-specific design.

reviewed_competitors.title: AxBench: Steering LLMs? Even Simple Baselines Outperform Sparse Autoencoders
reviewed_competitors.difference: AxBench compares prompting, finetuning, difference-in-means, probes, SAEs, and rank-one representation finetuning on Gemma-2-2B/9B. It finds prompting best for steering and difference-in-means strong for detection, directly challenging conclusions drawn from ActAdd's narrow per-task imported baselines.

reviewed_competitors.title: Painless Activation Steering: An Automated, Lightweight Approach for Post-Training Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: PAS removes hand-crafted prompt pairs and feature annotation by constructing steering vectors automatically from labeled datasets, evaluating three modern models on 18 tasks and separating behavioral from intelligence outcomes. It spends more data than ActAdd but directly addresses ActAdd's manual contrast and hyperparameter bottleneck.

reviewed_competitors.title: Activation Steering with a Feedback Controller
reviewed_competitors.difference: PID Steering casts ActAdd and related fixed additions as proportional controllers, then adds integral and derivative feedback to reduce persistent error and overshoot across layers. Its ICLR 2026 experiments target robustness across multiple model families; ActAdd is the simpler open-loop special case without stability guarantees.

reviewed_competitors.title: Towards Understanding Steering Strength
reviewed_competitors.difference: Taimeskhanov et al. theoretically characterize nonmonotonic next-token, concept, and cross-entropy behavior as steering strength changes and validate across 11 models. This supplies analysis for the coefficient failures ActAdd observes empirically but does not explain, while ActAdd contributes broader task-level generation evidence.

reviewed_competitors.title: On The Effectiveness-Fluency Trade-Off In LLM Conditioning: A Systematic Study
reviewed_competitors.difference: Macocco et al. compare injection and removal methods while measuring generation quality, finding efficient activation steering often pays a steep fluency cost and is much less effective on instruction-tuned than base models. This generalizes and sharpens the quality degradation already visible but underemphasized in ActAdd's Tables 3-4.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Geva et al. analyze FFN parameters and activations as key-value memories, finding shallow patterns in lower layers and more semantic patterns in upper layers, with outputs refined through residual connections. Those results cut against treating pointwise layers as marginalizable static filters or inferring that all layers necessarily operate at one abstraction level.

The audited paper uses the shared-space intuition more globally but neither isolates causal components nor demonstrates that its pooled concepts govern prediction.

reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct competing mechanistic account of in-context learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Olsson et al. define an induction-head algorithm, connect its appearance during training to a measured in-context-loss improvement, and provide causal evidence in small attention-only models plus correlational evidence in larger models. The audited paper cites the residual-stream framework but dismisses in-context learning based on fixed weights, without an intervention that refutes activation-level algorithms.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Xie et al. formalize ICL as inference of a latent document-level concept, prove conditions for its emergence in mixtures of HMMs, and reproduce scale and prompt-order phenomena on synthetic data. It agrees that weights remain fixed but treats context conditioning as a learned inference algorithm, making the disagreement with the audited paper primarily an operational and testable definition rather than a fact about parameter updates.

reviewed_competitors.title: What learning algorithm is in-context learning? Investigations with linear models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Algorithmic alternative with constructions and activation evidence
reviewed_competitors.difference: Akyurek et al. construct transformers that implement gradient descent and closed-form regression, compare trained predictors with standard estimators, and find late-layer encodings of weights and moments. The scope is controlled linear tasks, but it supplies exactly the behavioral and internal tests missing from the audited paper's claim that no inner learning algorithm can run with fixed outer weights.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformers learn in-context by gradient descent
reviewed_competitors.difference: Von Oswald et al. give a weight construction equating a linear self-attention transformation with one regression gradient step and show trained attention-only transformers recover related weights and behaviors, including curvature correction. The audited paper notes the restricted setting but incorrectly treats lack of parameter updates as enough to deny ICL; this competitor instead makes the inner loss, task, and predicted computation explicit.

reviewed_competitors.title: Pretraining task diversity and the emergence of non-Bayesian in-context learning for regression
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Empirical boundary test for whether ICL is mere conditioning on memorized training tasks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Raventos et al. vary pretraining-task diversity and report a threshold beyond which transformers outperform the Bayes estimator tied to the finite pretraining task prior and align with ridge regression over unseen tasks. This controlled novelty test directly probes the audited paper's predetermined-path intuition and shows why finite weights alone do not decide whether behavioral learning generalizes beyond seen task instances.

reviewed_competitors.title: Linear Transformers Are Secretly Fast Weight Programmers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Earlier formal account of sequence-dependent fast state in attention
reviewed_competitors.difference: Schlag et al. prove an equivalence between linearized attention and fast-weight programmers whose sequence of outer-product updates writes a transient associative memory, then test improved update rules on retrieval, translation, and language modeling. Although limited to linearized attention, it demonstrates a precise sense in which fixed slow weights can program dynamic context-dependent state, a possibility the audited paper rules out terminologically.

reviewed_competitors.title: In-Context Learning Creates Task Vectors
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later direct test of context compression into an activation-space task representation
reviewed_competitors.difference: Hendel et al. test whether demonstrations can be compressed into a single task vector that modulates an LLM supplied only the query, across models and tasks. This is close to the audited paper's concept-vector intuition but operationalizes a task and intervention; it does not assume that generic mean pooling at semantically selected boundaries must preserve the full language-model computation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Function Vectors in Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Causal follow-up on vector representations of abstract functions
reviewed_competitors.difference: Todd et al. use causal mediation to locate attention heads that transport compact function vectors, inject them into zero-shot and natural-text contexts, and test partial vector composition. This provides stronger evidence for a bounded version of concept vectors than HellaSwag similarity, while also showing that output-space information alone is insufficient and that the effect is concentrated in particular heads and layers.

reviewed_competitors.title: Unveiling Induction Heads: Provable Training Dynamics and Feature Learning in Transformers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later formal multi-component account of attention-based ICL
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chen et al. analyze a two-attention-layer transformer with relative positions, softmax attention, an FFN, and normalization on n-gram Markov data, proving convergence to a copier-selector-classifier mechanism and validating it experimentally. Its result directly challenges reductions of attention to undirected association or of MLPs to marginal filters by assigning distinct, jointly necessary computational roles.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformer models are gauge invariant: A mathematical connection between AI and particle physics
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later mathematical caution about intrinsic hidden-space geometry
reviewed_competitors.difference: Van Nierop explicitly analyzes transformer gauge redundancy and argues that common parameterizations only partially remove it. The paper is a short theoretical contribution rather than an empirical benchmark, but it makes the identifiability issue omitted by the audited paper concrete: some coordinate descriptions can change while the represented model function does not.

reviewed_competitors.title: How do Transformer Embeddings Represent Compositions? A Functional Analysis
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current adjacent empirical study of embedding compositionality
reviewed_competitors.difference: Nagar et al. compare six explicit composition models across Mistral, OpenAI, Google, and BERT embeddings and use a transparent synthetic adjective-noun dataset, reporting strong but model-dependent compositionality with ridge regression best and addition close. This is narrower than a theory of all hidden states but supplies controlled comparisons missing from the audited paper's single-benchmark, oracle-pooled concept test.

reviewed_competitors.title: Selective Induction Heads: How Transformers Select Causal Structures In Context
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current mechanistic account of context-dependent structure selection
reviewed_competitors.difference: D'Angelo et al. vary causal lag across interleaved Markov chains, identify a selective induction-head circuit that chooses the relevant lag in context, and give a three-layer construction converging to maximum likelihood. The restricted synthetic setting does not settle natural-language ICL, but it is a direct counterexample to the claim that attention has no mechanism to select relevance or dynamically recognize a sequence structure.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Emergence of Induction Heads for In-Context Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current training-dynamics follow-up on an explicit ICL circuit
reviewed_competitors.difference: Musat et al. prove that training dynamics for a minimal modified transformer remain in a 19-dimensional subspace, empirically find three dimensions dominate induction-head emergence, and derive a quadratic context-length emergence time. It is deliberately minimal, but its falsifiable dynamical predictions contrast with the audited paper's post-hoc use of all possible paths as an explanation.

reviewed_competitors.title: SchNet: A continuous-filter convolutional neural network for modeling quantum interactions
reviewed_competitors.relationship: An early force-field benchmark predecessor that introduced ISO17 specifically to test chemical and conformational variation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: ISO17 separated known-molecule/new-conformation and unknown-molecule/new-conformation generalization years before the reviewed paper's cross-molecule fixture. The reviewed work adds an explicit chronological-window scan and atom-resolved rMD17 projections, but its claim that cross-dataset generalization is a missed benchmarking opportunity is too broad.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the role of gradients for machine learning of molecular energies and forces
reviewed_competitors.relationship: The source of revised MD17 and a direct label-efficiency study across same-molecule geometries and unseen molecules.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Christensen and von Lilienfeld quantify how energy and force labels affect learning curves within and across molecules and discuss label-cost tradeoffs. The reviewed paper uses rMD17 chronology to add temporal windows, but omits label cost and does not compare its learning curve across models or molecules.

reviewed_competitors.title: Active learning of linearly parametrized interatomic potentials
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A principled predecessor for detecting extrapolation and selecting new configurations during atomistic simulation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Podryabinkin and Shapeev use D-optimality and an extrapolation grade inside on-the-fly MD and structure relaxation. The reviewed paper merely observes a post-hoc SOAP/error association and speculates about a threshold without calibration, intervention, or new labels.

reviewed_competitors.title: Active Learning of Uniformly Accurate Inter-atomic Potentials for Materials Simulation
reviewed_competitors.relationship: DP-GEN is a mature exploration-label-training loop for sample-efficient and transferable interatomic potentials.
reviewed_competitors.difference: DP-GEN uses ensemble model deviation to identify uncertain configurations, obtains reference labels, and retrains across alloy state spaces. The reviewed fixture measures an offline similarity proxy on one completed trajectory and never tests whether its proposed alarm maintains accuracy or stability.

reviewed_competitors.title: On-the-Fly Active Learning of Interpretable Bayesian Force Fields for Atomistic Rare Events
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A direct alternative for deployment-time OOD detection, sparse labeling, and rare-event coverage.
reviewed_competitors.difference: FLARE evaluates predictive uncertainty at each MD step, calls first-principles calculations when needed, and publishes an open implementation. The reviewed paper's mean SOAP score is cheaper but neither calibrated against local error nor exercised online, and averaging can miss rare dangerous environments.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Open Catalyst 2020 (OC20) Dataset and Community Challenges
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A large preexisting scientific benchmark with explicit chemical OOD splits, application tasks, baselines, open data, and a leaderboard.
reviewed_competitors.difference: OC20 separates in-domain, unseen adsorbate, unseen catalyst, and jointly unseen shifts over 1.28 million DFT relaxations and multiple graph models. The reviewed work's seven-molecule hand-picked combinations are far smaller and lack standardized aggregate scores, but add temporal analysis relevant to MD trajectories.

reviewed_competitors.title: Challenges for Machine Learning Force Fields in Reproducing Potential Energy Surfaces of Flexible Molecules
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A close predecessor on sparse-data generalization, transition-region failure, and local-versus-global force-field design.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Vassilev-Galindo et al. compare sGDML, SchNet, GAP/SOAP, and BPNN on multiple azobenzene transition mechanisms and already propose multiple local models for different PES regions. The reviewed paper reaches a similar partition-and-route suggestion from one NequIP cross-molecule panel without testing routing or transitions.

reviewed_competitors.title: E(3)-Equivariant Graph Neural Networks for Data-Efficient and Accurate Interatomic Potentials
reviewed_competitors.relationship: The NequIP source paper whose architecture and data-efficiency claims underlie every reviewed experiment.
reviewed_competitors.difference: NequIP already reports strong data-efficiency results across diverse molecular and materials benchmarks and long-time MD. The reviewed work contributes alternate split diagnostics, but using NequIP alone cannot show whether its rankings or temporal sensitivity generalize across architecture classes.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Local Equivariant Representations for Large-Scale Atomistic Dynamics
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A contemporaneous equivariant MLIP and obvious missing model baseline on rMD17 and OOD dynamics.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Allegro reports revised-MD17 accuracy, OOD generalization, physical structural and kinetic observables, and 100-million-atom scaling. The reviewed benchmark selects only NequIP, so it cannot establish model rankings, and it omits both autonomous observables and performance scaling.

reviewed_competitors.title: Uncertainty-aware molecular dynamics from Bayesian active learning for Phase Transformations and Thermal Transport in SiC
reviewed_competitors.relationship: An application-level alternative that joins uncertainty-aware sampling with physical validation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Xie et al. exercise an autonomous active-learning workflow and validate phase transitions, vibrational properties, and thermal transport against ab-initio and experiment. The reviewed work neither closes the alarm/retraining loop nor measures any downstream property, despite framing its metrics as real-world indicators.

reviewed_competitors.title: Accurate global machine learning force fields for molecules with hundreds of atoms
reviewed_competitors.relationship: MD22 supplies a harder scale and long-range generalization benchmark than small rMD17 molecules.
reviewed_competitors.difference: MD22 spans 42-370 atom systems and validates global sGDML with nanosecond path-integral MD, directly probing system size and long-range interactions. The reviewed paper is complementary in chronological splitting but does not test whether its findings survive larger systems or autonomous trajectories.

reviewed_competitors.title: SPICE, A Dataset of Drug-like Molecules and Peptides for Training Machine Learning Potentials
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A broader preexisting chemical-transfer resource for testing general molecular potentials.
reviewed_competitors.difference: SPICE contains more than 1.1 million conformations, 15 elements, charged and neutral systems, noncovalent interactions, peptides, forces, and energies. The reviewed seven-molecule H/C/O-dominated panel isolates simple local transfer but excludes unseen elements and cannot substantiate broad cross-dataset capability.

reviewed_competitors.title: Forces are not Enough: Benchmark and Critical Evaluation for Machine Learning Force Fields with Molecular Simulations
reviewed_competitors.relationship: The closest direct predecessor, explicitly cited by the reviewed paper, for application-aligned MLFF benchmarking.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Fu et al. benchmark multiple models on water, organic molecules, a peptide, and materials using autonomous rollouts, stability, and task-specific scientific observables, and release code. The reviewed work adds learning-curve, temporal-window, and cross-molecule split diagnostics but then still evaluates only static force/energy errors, making its real-world validation materially weaker.

reviewed_competitors.title: Fast Uncertainty Estimates in Deep Learning Interatomic Potentials
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A direct competitor to SOAP similarity as a low-overhead deployment-time accuracy indicator.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhu et al. learn single-network predictive uncertainty, compare it against deep ensembles across configuration space, and test active learning. The reviewed paper's fixed SOAP descriptor needs no model change but provides no uncertainty calibration, error ranking, intervention results, or comparison with this stronger model-aware signal.

reviewed_competitors.title: Single-model uncertainty quantification in neural network potentials does not consistently outperform model ensembles
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A pre-submission comparative benchmark for OOD alarms on rMD17 and harder molecular/material shifts.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Tan et al. compare ensembles, mean-variance estimation, evidential regression, and Gaussian mixtures on multiple error-versus-uncertainty metrics across rMD17, ammonia inversion, and silica. Their finding that alarm quality is regime-dependent directly cautions against promoting one tiny-range SOAP correlation without calibrated detection tests.

reviewed_competitors.title: Discrepancies and Error Evaluation Metrics for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A very close pre-submission paper on why low average MLIP errors fail to predict dynamics and properties.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Liu et al. diagnose discrepancies in dynamics, defects, and rare events, construct property-linked quantitative metrics, and show metric-guided optimization improves multiple properties. The reviewed paper was submitted after its v1 but does not discuss it and stops at held-out MAE, leaving its claim of scientifically meaningful real-world assessment comparatively weak.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scientific machine learning benchmarks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: The general scientific-benchmark design framework cited by the reviewed paper.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Thiyagalingam et al. require a scientific problem, curated dataset, reference implementation, domain metrics, uncertainty where needed, reporting/compliance, coverage, and extensibility. The reviewed paper sharpens OOD concerns for MLFF, but lacks the pinned reference implementation, uncertainty, compliance rules, broad coverage, and reproducible outputs that this framework treats as benchmark essentials.

reviewed_competitors.title: Matbench Discovery -- A framework to evaluate machine learning crystal stability predictions
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A later, independently developed example of application-aligned AI4S benchmarking with prospective splits and task outcomes.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Submitted 17 days after the reviewed paper, Matbench Discovery scores the actual crystal-stability screening decision, contrasts task classification with regression error, benchmarks many model families, publishes a package, and maintains a leaderboard. It therefore supports the reviewed thesis that domain outcomes matter while showing the infrastructure and multi-model evidence missing from this case study.

reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporaneous negative qualification of interpreting small aggregate NC1 as loss of within-class information.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yang, Steinhardt, and Hu recover fine-grained latent classes from apparently collapsed features and show that residual variation faithfully encodes input structure. The reviewed paper tracks only low-dimensional aggregate ratios and therefore cannot support its stronger language that almost all intra-class variation has been removed.

reviewed_competitors.title: Deep Neural Collapse Is Provably Optimal for the Deep Unconstrained Features Model
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporaneous theory for neural collapse across multiple nonlinear layers.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sukenik, Mondelli, and Lampert prove all deep-NC properties at the unique global optimum of a binary deep unconstrained-features model and compare gradient solutions with trained networks. The reviewed paper supplies multiclass real-network plots across more datasets but no theory explaining why or when progressive collapse occurs.

reviewed_competitors.title: Average gradient outer product as a mechanism for deep neural collapse
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later data-dependent mechanism for progressive within-class collapse.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Beaglehole et al. prove and measure deep NC in Recursive Feature Machines through AGOP projections and connect trained-network weight singular structure to removal of within-class variability. This directly supplies a causal/mechanistic candidate absent from the reviewed paper's purely layer-correlational account.

reviewed_competitors.title: Are all layers created equal: A neural collapse perspective
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later large-scale extension of progressive neural collapse to generalization, memorization, architecture, noise, and pruning.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhou, Jiang, and Zhu test larger models and more complex/noisy datasets, contrast transformers and CNNs, and identify redundant middle layers plus depth-dependent memorization/generalization trade-offs. The reviewed paper is an early small-benchmark observation without held-out or noisy-data evidence, so later work substantially supersedes its practical scope.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Persistence of Neural Collapse Despite Low-Rank Bias
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later theoretical counterpoint showing deep NC need not be globally optimal under common regularized objectives.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Garrod and Keating prove that high-rank deep-NC structures are generally suboptimal in deep unconstrained-feature models under MSE and cross-entropy because of low-rank bias, while explaining why NC remains prevalent in the loss landscape. The reviewed empirical presence of NC therefore should not be interpreted as universal optimality or necessity.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Cohen and Sompolinsky analyze soft-margin solutions, training error, test error, support structure, and regularization for object manifolds. reviewed_competitors.relationship: Structured-manifold capacity alternative based on exact group symmetry.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Farrell et al. exploit equivariance and the group-fixed subspace to derive capacity for all transformed views of each object. reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Efficient Coding of Natural Images with Maximum Manifold Capacity Representations

reviewed_competitors.difference: Yerxa et al. introduce Maximum Manifold Capacity Representations, optimize a simplified capacity surrogate, and evaluate learned visual representations and neural predictivity. Wakhloo et al. derive how full cross-manifold covariance affects the estimator and only hypothesize a correlation-shaping objective; MMCR tests learning but does not solve the same arbitrary-covariance capacity problem.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding Emergent Abilities of Language Models from the Loss Perspective
reviewed_competitors.difference: Du et al. test controlled Transformer families and find that, with corpus, tokenizer, and architecture fixed, matched pretraining loss predicts several downstream tasks and some abilities cross loss thresholds. That is much closer to an empirical validation of the target's loss lens, while its fixed-recipe scope also highlights the untested invariances hidden in the target's general cloze assumption.

reviewed_competitors.title: Language models scale reliably with over-training and on downstream tasks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Gadre et al. train 104 models from 11M to 6.9B parameters on three distributions and fit a power law from perplexity to average top-1 error over downstream tasks. Their result makes the target's proposed bridge testable but is an aggregate, within-recipe empirical relation rather than a guarantee for each latent skill or unseen tuple.

reviewed_competitors.title: Observational Scaling Laws and the Predictability of Language Model Performance
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ruan et al. infer a low-dimensional capability space from roughly 100 public models and model several emergent phenomena as smooth sigmoids predictable from smaller systems. Unlike the target's unobservable random skill graph, their axes are fit to model evaluations across families, though the observational approach does not explain causal skill acquisition.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scaling Laws for Downstream Task Performance of Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: distribution-alignment stress test for downstream scaling
reviewed_competitors.difference: Isik et al. show machine-translation quality scales predictably when pretraining and downstream distributions align, but can fluctuate or worsen under moderate misalignment even as downstream cross-entropy improves. This empirically supports the target's in-distribution caveat and shows why its framework cannot justify broad deployment or out-of-distribution emergence claims.

reviewed_competitors.title: Skill-Mix: a Flexible and Expandable Family of Evaluations for AI models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: direct operational follow-up by overlapping authors
reviewed_competitors.difference: Skill-Mix turns the target's tuple idea into a generation evaluation by sampling named skill subsets, using GPT-4 and LLaMA-2-70B graders plus human spot checks, and comparing chatbots up through k=5. It is valuable evidence that the original paper lacks, but generated named-skill demonstrations are not the same as cloze competence on randomly mixed natural text and remain exposed to grader and contamination effects.

reviewed_competitors.title: Do Large Language Models Have Compositional Ability? An Investigation into Limitations and Scalability
reviewed_competitors.relationship: competing empirical and theoretical account of composition
reviewed_competitors.difference: Xu et al. separate simple composites that apply mappings to distinct input segments from multi-step composites that share sequential state; scaling helps the former but generally not the latter. This task-structure dependence cuts against treating all k-tuples as exchangeable composite nodes, though their in-context held-out tasks are outside the target's in-distribution guarantee.

reviewed_competitors.title: Can Models Learn Skill Composition from Examples?
reviewed_competitors.relationship: direct experimental successor by overlapping authors
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhao et al. fine-tune 7B and 13B models on GPT-4-generated texts combining one to three skills and measure transfer to four- and five-skill prompts, including held-out categories. It provides controlled evidence that richer composition data can help, but tests an explicit synthetic curriculum rather than the target's claim that ordinary random skill mixing plus smooth pretraining loss is sufficient.

reviewed_competitors.title: Physics of Skill Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: newer mechanistic toy theory of skill dynamics
reviewed_competitors.difference: Liu et al. model sequential 'Domino' skill acquisition with geometry, resource, and modular toy systems, relate a geometry model to Chinchilla-style laws, and derive training interventions. It tackles the dynamics the target deliberately omits; both depend on abstractions, but the newer work exposes trajectory-level predictions and code rather than only endpoint graph coverage.

It does not require a human-named prerequisite graph, while SKILL-IT offers an interpretable target-conditioned transfer structure.

reviewed_competitors.difference: The same authors already derive two information-temperature constructions for binary Markov chains and illustrate text-oriented use. The reviewed paper's main addition is the entropy-derivative complexity proposal and the speculative intelligence framing.

reviewed_competitors.title: Shannon information, LMC complexity and Renyi entropies: a straightforward approach
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work develops the entropy-times-disequilibrium LMC family that the reviewed paper directly reuses as C = hD; the intermediate order-disorder maximum is therefore not new evidence for the temperature construction.

reviewed_competitors.title: A computational mechanics approach to estimate entropy and (approximate) complexity for the dynamics of the 2D Ising Ferromagnet
reviewed_competitors.difference: Computational mechanics estimates entropy and causal-state complexity from simulated Ising dynamics and observes structure near criticality. It supplies a process-organization interpretation and empirical estimator absent from the derivative-only proposal.

reviewed_competitors.title: Physical Complexity of Symbolic Sequences
reviewed_competitors.difference: Adami and Cerf define sequence complexity relative to an environment and apply it to biological symbols. That explicit conditioning distinguishes functional information from raw entropy structure, whereas information heat has no semantic or environmental reference.

reviewed_competitors.title: Language Modeling Is Compression
reviewed_competitors.difference: This study evaluates general-purpose compressors and language models on text and non-text prediction, giving an operational held-out measure. It is empirically broader than assigning a temperature to a toy Markov family, though compression is still not intelligence by itself.

reviewed_competitors.title: Compression Represents Intelligence Linearly
reviewed_competitors.difference: This paper tests a compression-derived representation across 31 language models and 12 benchmarks. Its empirical correlation design is a materially stronger validation of a text statistic as a capability surrogate, while also showing what validation the reviewed proposal lacks.

reviewed_competitors.title: Beyond the Imitation Game: Quantifying and extrapolating the capabilities of language models
reviewed_competitors.difference: BIG-bench measures performance on 204 diverse tasks with human and model comparisons. It evaluates behavioral capabilities directly instead of inferring intelligence from a single surface-sequence statistic.

reviewed_competitors.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: HELM evaluates models across scenarios and accuracy, calibration, robustness, fairness, bias, toxicity, and efficiency. Its multidimensional design exposes the construct-validity loss in reducing agent intelligence to one temperature-derived number.

reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct competing Bayesian finite-CNN theory with self-consistent adaptive Gaussian processes.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Naveh and Ringel derive strong finite-width effects, a feature/lazy transition, and tests ranging from a solvable two-layer linear CNN to a realistic Myrtle CNN. The reviewed work instead isolates a spatial full-matrix renormalization in a nonlinear shallow proportional action, but validates it only indirectly.

reviewed_competitors.title: Separation of scales and a thermodynamic description of feature learning in some CNNs
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct predecessor giving an effective-GP and thermodynamic account of finite-CNN feature learning.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Seroussi et al. focus on scale separation and self-consistent equations across several CNN settings. The reviewed paper derives a simpler patch-pair order parameter and architecture ablation, offering interpretability at the cost of a more restrictive stride, depth, and Gaussian-closure regime.

reviewed_competitors.title: Tensor Programs IV: Feature Learning in Infinite-Width Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Competing infinite-width framework showing that feature learning can persist with a different parameterization.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yang and Hu construct maximal-update infinite-width limits that outperform NTK and can retain feature learning. This makes clear that the reviewed paper's static-kernel and FC disadvantage statements concern standard/lazy or Bayesian scaling, not infinite width in general.

reviewed_competitors.title: A theory of representation learning gives a deep generalisation of kernel methods
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporaneous competing Bayesian representation-learning limit with adaptive layerwise covariances.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yang et al. develop a deep Bayesian representation-learning limit with interpretable optimized posterior covariances. The reviewed work specializes to shallow spatial architectures and exposes patch-pair structure, but its nonlinear Gaussian equivalence is heuristic and it does not cover depth.

reviewed_competitors.title: Feature learning and random features in standard finite-width convolutional neural networks: An empirical study
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Empirical competitor measuring the benefit of learned finite CNN features against finite linearizations on standard architectures.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Samarin et al. test LeNet and AlexNet across MNIST variants, CIFAR-10, and an ImageNet subset and find task difficulty widens the feature-learning gap. The reviewed paper offers a candidate Bayesian kernel mechanism but evaluates only a stylized shallow binary task.

reviewed_competitors.title: Critical feature learning in deep neural networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later proportional-width Bayesian theory for kernel adaptation throughout deep nonlinear networks.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Fischer et al. derive coupled forward-backward equations for maximum-a-posteriori kernels in all layers and connect adaptation to prior fluctuations and criticality. It extends beyond the reviewed paper's single hidden layer while offering a different mechanism and depth-dependent predictions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Feature Learning in Finite-Width Bayesian Deep Linear Networks with Multiple Outputs and Convolutional Layers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later rigorous treatment of finite-width Bayesian convolutional kernel-shape renormalization in deep linear networks.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bassetti et al. give exact non-asymptotic Gaussian-mixture priors, analytic posteriors, and a rigorous large-deviation description for linear convolutional networks. It supplies mathematical guarantees absent from the reviewed paper's nonlinear Gaussian closure, though at the cost of linear activations.

reviewed_competitors.title: Kernel Renormalization in Bayesian Deep Neural Networks: the Equivalent Wishart Ansatz in the Proportional Regime
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Recent follow-on extending scalar and local kernel renormalization to deep nonlinear Bayesian networks.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Baglioni et al. use an approximate equivalent-Wishart ansatz for depth around ten, derive hierarchical local CNN renormalization, and quantitatively compare posterior sampling on benchmark data. It directly addresses the reviewed paper's depth and quantitative-validation gaps while remaining approximate.

reviewed_competitors.title: Sharp Minima Can Generalize For Deep Nets
reviewed_competitors.difference: Dinh et al. show that function-preserving reparameterization can make a generalizing network arbitrarily sharp, disproving sharp-implies-bad before this paper. The reviewed work contributes the converse-style fixed-parameterization construction: a globally flattest interpolator itself can generalize maximally poorly.

reviewed_competitors.title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Efficiently Improving Generalization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Foret et al. introduce SAM's neighborhood min-max objective and PAC-Bayes motivation. The reviewed paper does not dispute SAM's utility; it argues that the final trace sharpness of the selected solution cannot be the complete causal explanation.

reviewed_competitors.title: When Do Flat Minima Optimizers Work?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kaddour et al. benchmark SAM and SWA across tasks and find domain-dependent benefits. They establish empirical heterogeneity but do not construct a globally trace-flattest worst-generalizing interpolator or an equal-flat optimizer-selection case.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Dynamics of Sharpness-Aware Minimization: Bouncing Across Ravines and Drifting Towards Wide Minima
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bartlett, Long, and Bousquet analyze local SAM drift toward wider points along a manifold. The reviewed work asks whether the resulting wide or globally flattest points generalize and shows that the answer depends on architecture and optimizer selection.

reviewed_competitors.title: How Does Sharpness-Aware Minimization Minimize Sharpness?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wen, Ma, and Li distinguish SAM sharpness notions and derive a local trace or average-sharpness bias for 1-SAM. The reviewed paper assumes that mechanism and tests whether it suffices to explain generalization.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Modern Look at the Relationship between Sharpness and Generalization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Andriushchenko et al. find weak or negative adaptive-sharpness correlations across modern vision and language settings and expose training confounds. The reviewed work supplies exact shallow nonlinear constructions rather than the first empirical decoupling evidence.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Crucial Role of Normalization in Sharpness-Aware Minimization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Dai, Ahn, and Sra argue that normalization stabilizes SAM and enables drift along manifolds of minima. This is a pre-target extra mechanism related to the normalization-dependent scenarios, but it does not give the reviewed bad or equal-flat constructions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization Leads to Low-Rank Features
reviewed_competitors.difference: Andriushchenko et al. show before this paper that SAM prunes ReLU activations and induces low-rank features across MLPs, CNNs, and vision transformers. The reviewed paper's Figure 2 is compatible with that mechanism, so beyond-sharpness representation bias was not a new general suggestion here.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Implicit Regularization of Dynamical Stability in Stochastic Gradient Descent
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wu and Su's Theorem 4.3 independently overlaps the positive bias-free two-layer-ReLU result and predates the target's first posting. The reviewed revision explicitly acknowledges learning of it later; the sharper novelty lies in the biased and equal-flat scenarios.

reviewed_competitors.title: Normalization Layers Are All That Sharpness-Aware Minimization Needs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Mueller et al. show that perturbing only affine normalization parameters can outperform full SAM and can improve generalization without a simple global-sharpness story. This pre-target result already casts doubt on final flatness as the sole mechanism in realistic normalized networks.

reviewed_competitors.title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization Enhances Feature Quality via Balanced Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Springer, Nagarajan, and Raghunathan directly cite the reviewed work and propose that SAM suppresses already learned features so alternate, more robust features develop. This supports the call for another mechanism but does not independently replicate the XOR scenarios.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Universal Class of Sharpness-Aware Minimization Algorithms
reviewed_competitors.difference: Tahmasebi et al. generalize trace and maximum-eigenvalue penalties to universal Hessian functions such as Frobenius and determinant objectives. It broadens the metric family rather than rebut the reviewed equal-trace or trace-minimizer constructions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Forget Sharpness: Perturbed Forgetting of Model Biases Within SAM Dynamics
reviewed_competitors.difference: Vani et al. find that perturbed forgetting correlates more strongly with SAM's gains than flatness and that output-bias perturbation can produce sharper yet better models. This is strong empirical support for another mechanism, not a reproduction of the constructive theorems.

reviewed_competitors.title: Implicit Regularization of Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Scale-Invariant Problems
reviewed_competitors.difference: Li, Zhang, and He build on the beyond-sharpness gap and prove a global balancedness bias for SAM in scale-invariant problems, introducing balancedness-aware regularization. Their LoRA-style setting supplies a candidate mechanism distinct from the reviewed XOR construction.

reviewed_competitors.title: Rényi Sharpness: A Novel Sharpness that Strongly Correlates with Generalization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhang et al. use this counterexample to motivate a Hessian-spectrum entropy measure. Their proposal qualifies the result as a failure of conventional trace or maximum-eigenvalue measures, not every possible spectral statistic, and does not reproduce the target setup.

reviewed_competitors.title: Flat Minima and Generalization: Insights from Stochastic Convex Optimization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Schliserman, Vansover-Hager, and Koren give smooth nonnegative convex examples with flat empirical minima of constant population risk and algorithmic failures for SA-GD or SAM. This extends the negative message beyond shallow nonconvex ReLU networks rather than contradicting it.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Unified Stability Analysis of SAM vs SGD: Role of Data Coherence and Emergence of Simplicity Bias
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chang and Khanna reuse the exact two-layer-ReLU, MSE, XOR, and memorization setup, connect per-example curvature coherence to memorization, and construct same-trace families with different feature sharing. It is the closest partial replication and supplies a simplicity-bias mechanism for Scenario III, but does not reproduce all three scenarios line by line.

reviewed_competitors.title: Flatness and Generalization: Learning Multi-Index Models with Homogeneous Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Vardhan, Taheri, and Mazumdar characterize the reviewed XOR example as worst-case and discrete and prove that orderwise-flattest interpolators generalize in low-noise Gaussian multi-index settings, including biased models. The result is explicitly non-contradictory and sharpens the paper's distributional scope boundary.

reviewed_competitors.title: Certification of Machine Learning Models via Directional Sharpness
reviewed_competitors.difference: Tan et al. cite the equal-static-sharpness ambiguity and propose a directional, training-dynamics-aware sharpness certificate. It offers a possible resolution through path stability rather than falsifying the reviewed static-trace construction.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding deep learning requires rethinking generalization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhang et al. establish that standard convolutional networks can fit randomized labels and that capacity or common regularizers alone do not explain generalization. The reviewed paper takes random-label fitting as its operational memorization probe and asks where the corresponding function is realized, adding interventions but not revisiting whether random-label and natural memorization share a mechanism.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Closer Look at Memorization in Deep Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Arpit et al. show that networks learn shared simple patterns before noise and that tuned dropout can suppress fitting noise without sacrificing real-data generalization. The reviewed work localizes influence and proposes stable example-keyed dropout, but its ordinary-dropout comparison is much narrower and omits test performance.

reviewed_competitors.title: What Neural Networks Memorize and Why: Discovering the Long Tail via Influence Estimation
reviewed_competitors.difference: Feldman and Zhang estimate counterfactual sample memorization and influence through many subsampled retrainings and show that memorizing rare examples can help related test examples. The reviewed paper borrows the C-score approximation for its natural extension but operationalizes most evidence with incorrect labels and can discard the very useful tail examples highlighted by this predecessor.

reviewed_competitors.title: Deep Learning Through the Lens of Example Difficulty
reviewed_competitors.difference: Baldock et al. introduce effective prediction depth and synthesize the view that early layers generalize while later layers memorize. Maini et al. directly challenge a universal late-layer interpretation using rewinding and retraining, but their one-layer interventions do not rule out distributed late-stage geometry or a definition-dependent layer effect.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the geometry of generalization and memorization in deep neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Stephenson et al. connect object-manifold radius and dimension to deeper-layer memorization and recover generalization by reverting final layers. The reviewed work broadens rewinding across models, datasets, and layer groups and finds no universal final-layer locus, but it does not reproduce the predecessor's geometric measurements or reconcile different layer grouping and memorization definitions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Do Localization Methods Actually Localize Memorized Data in LLMs? A Tale of Two Benchmarks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chang, Thomason, and Jia introduce INJ, with known injected ground-truth weights, and DEL, which tests deletion of pretrained sequences, and find that successful methods still select neurons nonspecific to one sequence. This directly exposes what the reviewed critical-unit search lacks: ground-truth localization, sequence specificity, and a separation between deleting one behavior and locating exclusive storage.

reviewed_competitors.title: Localizing Paragraph Memorization in Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Stoehr et al. study extracted paragraphs, find larger gradients in lower layers, unlearn through high-gradient weights, localize one low-layer rare-token attention head, and perturb prefix tokens. It supports distributed influence but shows that layer conclusions depend on memorization type and architecture; it targets natural language recall rather than incorrect image labels.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learnable Privacy Neurons Localization in Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chen et al. learn binary masks adversarially and report PII-specific neurons spread across LLM layers, then deactivate them for privacy mitigation. This resembles the reviewed sparse-across-layers conclusion in a privacy setting, but it optimizes masks rather than greedy activation cuts and evaluates PII rather than label inconsistency.

reviewed_competitors.title: Finding NeMo: Localizing Neurons Responsible For Memorization in Diffusion Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: NeMo localizes sample-specific cross-attention neurons in diffusion models and tests whether deactivation prevents training-image replication while preserving diversity. It extends the neuron-removal idea to generative leakage and sometimes reports a single responsible neuron, but uses model- and modality-specific generation evidence rather than supervised prediction flips.

reviewed_competitors.title: Localizing Memorization in SSL Vision Encoders
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wang et al. define label-free forward-pass LayerMem and UnitMem for self-supervised vision encoders, finding depth-increasing memorization but high-memorization units throughout the encoder and especially high values for atypical points. This partially reconciles deeper-layer trends with distributed units and covers unlabeled pretraining, whereas the reviewed probes require supervised labels and repeated interventions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Memorization Sinks: Isolating Memorization during LLM Training
reviewed_competitors.relationship: same-author scaled successor to example-tied dropout
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ghosal, Maini, and Raghunathan show that natural-sequence memorization is mechanistically entangled under ordinary training and replace example-tied dropout with deterministic sequence-identified sink neurons protected from interference, scaling to 1.7B parameters and billion-token data. The successor narrows the original post-hoc localization premise, explicitly studies co-adaptation and learning-forgetting dynamics, and supplies a scalable on-the-fly mask design absent from the 2023 artifact.

reviewed_competitors.title: Guess or Recall? Training CNNs to Classify and Localize Memorization in LLMs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Dentan et al. show that many extractable continuations are guessed through language regularity rather than recalled and find different attention-localization patterns for lower-layer Guess and upper-layer Recall. This reinforces that a single memorized/non-memorized partition can mix mechanisms and limits transfer of the reviewed five-neuron conclusion beyond uniformly wrong labels.

reviewed_competitors.title: Natively Unlearnable Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: NULLs ties sparsely activated sinks to data sources, scales routing to roughly six million Wikipedia articles, and evaluates source removal against retraining, adversarial extraction, relearning, shared-fact preservation, and downstream capability. It operationalizes the deletion tests missing from example-tied dropout and routes by source rather than by every image, while requiring a modified model trained from scratch.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Bresler and Nagaraj divide nonlinear units into groups that sequentially approximate and correct the errors of earlier groups, providing a direct pre-2023 conceptual predecessor for additive residual-stage function approximation. MSNN adds residual normalization, explicit spectral scaling, and a PINN residual heuristic, but does not cite or compare with this close corrective formulation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Multi-Grade Deep Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Xu freezes previous shallow networks, trains each new grade on the leftover, and sums the resulting staircase network; the paper also proves strict reduction of optimal approximation error when a new grade is nontrivial. This appeared five months before MSNN and overlaps its core sequential correction mechanism, while MSNN's distinctive elements are amplitude normalization, sine-frequency scaling, and the PINN extension.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: arXiv 2302.00150 abstract and revision record checked 2026-08-23

reviewed_competitors.title: Precision Machine Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Michaud, Liu, and Tegmark study very-high-precision approximation, scaling with parameters and data, and training tricks that approach numerical precision. MSNN cites it and focuses more narrowly on staged residual corrections and PINNs, but its broad framing that ordinary networks cannot get past an inherent precision ceiling should be judged against this earlier evidence that optimization interventions can already reach the numerical floor.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: arXiv 2210.13447 abstract and revision record checked 2026-08-23

reviewed_competitors.title: Fourier Features Let Networks Learn High Frequency Functions in Low Dimensional Domains
reviewed_competitors.difference: Tancik et al. use a tunable Fourier feature input map and NTK analysis to accelerate high-frequency learning in low-dimensional regression. MSNN instead chooses a separate sine-scaled correction network after inspecting each residual. A fair comparison would test whether one multi-band Fourier-feature model at matched total compute removes the need for stages.

reviewed_competitors.title: Implicit Neural Representations with Periodic Activation Functions
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sitzmann et al.'s SIREN supplies periodic activations, a principled initialization, derivative representation, and Poisson, Helmholtz, wave, and Eikonal boundary-value experiments. MSNN borrows a sine first layer with a residual-dependent scale but does not implement a compute-matched SIREN baseline or show that sequential stages outperform a fully periodic network.

reviewed_competitors.title: Finite Basis Physics-Informed Neural Networks: a scalable domain decomposition approach for solving differential equations
reviewed_competitors.difference: FBPINNs address spectral bias and large or multiscale domains with many compactly supported local networks and per-subdomain normalization, enabling parallel divide-and-conquer training. MSNN is global and sequential; FBPINNs are a particularly relevant alternative for the high-dimensional, steep-gradient, and localized regimes MSNN leaves unresolved.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: arXiv 2107.07871 abstract and revision record checked 2026-08-23

reviewed_competitors.title: PINNsFormer: A Transformer-Based Framework For Physics-Informed Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: PINNsFormer constructs pseudo sequences, uses attention to propagate temporal constraints, and introduces a wavelet activation for spectral content. It targets difficult time-dependent and higher-dimensional cases through a single integrated architecture, whereas MSNN relies on manual stage construction and residual-spectrum heuristics.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: arXiv 2307.11833 abstract and revision record checked 2026-08-23

reviewed_competitors.title: Multi-level Neural Networks for Accurate Solutions of Boundary-Value Problems
reviewed_competitors.difference: Aldirany et al. iteratively solve the PDE residual error with new networks of increasing complexity and report that some boundary-value examples reach machine precision. Posted shortly after MSNN, it independently occupies almost the same multilevel defect-correction niche and applies to strong or weak neural formulations; comparative experiments are needed to distinguish the methods.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: arXiv 2308.11503 abstract and revision record checked 2026-08-23

reviewed_competitors.title: Multi-Grade Deep Learning for Partial Differential Equations with Applications to the Burgers Equation
reviewed_competitors.difference: Xu and Zeng extend multi-grade residual learning to 1D, 2D, and 3D viscous Burgers equations and prove that each grade can reduce the objective. It is less focused on floating-point precision and spectral scaling than MSNN but offers broader dimension coverage and a clearer connection to the earlier multi-grade theory.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: arXiv 2309.07401 abstract and revision record checked 2026-08-23

reviewed_competitors.title: Mitigating Propagation Failures in Physics-informed Neural Networks using Retain-Resample-Release Sampling
reviewed_competitors.relationship: preexisting PINN sampling and failure-mode competitor
reviewed_competitors.difference: Daw et al. identify propagation failure, propose R3 and causal R3 sampling, theoretically analyze the sampler, and compare multiple adaptive methods with repeated-run uncertainty. MSNN uses RAR and resampling as supporting components but does not isolate their contribution or test its staged method on the hard convection and Allen-Cahn regimes used by R3.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: ICML 2023 PMLR Volume 202 official record checked 2026-08-23

reviewed_competitors.title: On Residual Minimization for PDEs: Failure of PINN, Modified Equation, and Implicit Bias
reviewed_competitors.difference: Luo and Zhou show that residual minimization can bias a PINN toward a modified equation rather than the intended exact solution, particularly with discontinuous coefficients. This directly challenges MSNN's assumption that driving sampled residuals lower is sufficient evidence of true-solution accuracy.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: arXiv 2310.18201 abstract and revision record checked 2026-08-23

reviewed_competitors.title: PirateNets: Physics-informed Deep Learning with Residual Adaptive Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: PirateNets diagnose derivative trainability and PDE-residual instability, initialize as shallow networks, and learn adaptive residual connections that progressively deepen during training. Their broad benchmark evidence and released implementation provide a stronger modern residual-architecture baseline than MSNN's manually appended frozen stages.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: arXiv 2402.00326 abstract and revision record checked 2026-08-23

reviewed_competitors.title: PINNacle: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving PDEs
reviewed_competitors.difference: PINNacle supplies more than 20 PDEs spanning complex geometry, multiscale behavior, nonlinearity, and high dimension, with about ten PINN methods in a unified toolbox. MSNN's four manufactured equation families are too narrow to establish a general advantage without evaluation on a benchmark of this breadth.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks official OpenReview record checked 2026-08-23

reviewed_competitors.title: Efficient Error Certification for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Eiras et al. target worst-case residual certification across the continuous spatiotemporal domain rather than relying on pointwise solver comparisons. Their verifier addresses exactly the missing evidentiary step in MSNN: determining whether a tiny sampled loss or residual really certifies uniformly high PDE accuracy.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: ICML 2024 PMLR Volume 235 official record checked 2026-08-23

reviewed_competitors.title: Stacked-Residual PINN for State Reconstruction of Hyperbolic Systems
reviewed_competitors.difference: Eshkofti and Barreau iteratively refine a low-fidelity PINN with scaled residual blocks while decreasing artificial viscosity, specifically targeting steep hyperbolic solutions. This is a narrower but more task-aligned staged correction for a regime MSNN declares out of scope.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: arXiv 2503.14222 abstract and revision record checked 2026-08-23

reviewed_competitors.title: Enhancing Physics-Informed Neural Networks Through Feature Engineering
reviewed_competitors.difference: SAFE-NET combines adaptive Fourier features, a single hidden layer, and effective conditioning, reporting comparable or better accuracy with far fewer parameters and much faster epochs than large modern PINNs. It tests whether deliberately engineered features can replace deep or staged complexity and is therefore a natural current efficiency baseline for MSNN.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: TMLR accepted submission official OpenReview record checked 2026-08-23

reviewed_competitors.title: Neuro-Spectral Architectures for Causal Physics-Informed Networks
