reviewed_competitors.title: Learning in High Dimension Always Amounts to Extrapolation
reviewed_competitors.difference: Balestriero, Pesenti, and LeCun define interpolation by membership in the convex hull of the represented training data and show theoretically and empirically that it becomes exceedingly rare as representation dimension grows. Bonnasse-Gahot directly disputes the operating-regime conclusion by first learning a low-dimensional autoencoder chart. The new result is conditional on that chart and does not invalidate the target paper's dimensional argument; both papers ultimately expose that hull-based terminology is a representation-dependent and weak account of generalization.

reviewed_competitors.title: Intrinsic dimension of data representations in deep neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ansuini and collaborators already report low intrinsic dimension in trained hidden representations, a rise-then-fall layer profile, and correlation between last-layer dimension and test accuracy using dedicated nonlinear dimension estimators. The present paper cites and qualitatively echoes that result; its distinct element is combining a classifier-preserving autoencoder bottleneck with convex-hull and proximity analysis, but that bottleneck is less directly tied to intrinsic-dimension estimation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Dimensionality compression and expansion in Deep Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Recanatesi and collaborators independently characterize expansion followed by compression of neural-representation dimension and connect low-dimensional late representations to generalization. Their analysis spans layers and proposes an SGD-noise account, whereas Bonnasse-Gahot probes only the last hidden layer and centers convex hull and nearest-neighbor distance. Consequently the low-dimensional-representation premise and generalization correlation are prior, while the chart-specific interpolation argument is narrower.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Intrinsic Dimension of Images and Its Impact on Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Pope and collaborators estimate intrinsic dimension for image datasets, validate estimators with GAN-generated data whose dimension can be manipulated, and test how data dimension affects learning and generalization. That work addresses input-data geometry with explicit estimator validation and public code, while Bonnasse-Gahot studies learned last-layer activities and adds hull/proximity diagnostics. It supplies a stronger precedent for separating estimator validation from downstream task preservation.

reviewed_competitors.title: The geometry of hidden representations of large transformer models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Valeriani and collaborators extend intrinsic-dimension and local-neighborhood analysis to large self-supervised protein and image transformers and relate layerwise dimension minima to semantic downstream utility. It has broader architecture and layer coverage and uses a dedicated TwoNN estimator with neighbor-composition analysis. Bonnasse-Gahot predates it and uniquely emphasizes convex-hull interpolation, but does not establish that its final-layer pattern transfers to modern self-supervised models.

reviewed_competitors.title: Rethinking Intrinsic Dimension Estimation in Neural Representations
reviewed_competitors.difference: Schulte and Rügamer theoretically and empirically argue that common neural-representation intrinsic-dimension estimators do not track true underlying dimension and investigate alternative drivers of reported trends. This 2026 AISTATS result directly increases the evidentiary burden for treating a classification-preserving autoencoder width as intrinsic dimension. Bonnasse-Gahot's empirical compression result remains interesting, but its geometric interpretation requires the identifiability and estimator checks highlighted by this later work.

reviewed_competitors.title: Deep Learning Generalization and the Convex Hull of Training Sets
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work evaluates convex-hull membership and decision-boundary extrapolation across pixel, wavelet, and internal representations on MNIST and CIFAR. It is a closer task-and-mechanism predecessor than dimension-only studies and reinforces that hull conclusions depend on the chosen representation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Decision boundaries and convex hulls in the feature space that deep learning functions learn from images
reviewed_competitors.difference: This pre-paper study analyzes convex hulls and decision boundaries in last-hidden ResNet feature space. It directly precedes the reviewed hidden-representation hull question, while the reviewed work adds an autoencoder chart and distance analysis but provides weaker artifact support.

reviewed_competitors.title: Topology and Phase Transitions I. Preliminary Results
reviewed_competitors.difference: The 2005 result used finite-N diffeomorphicity of configuration submanifolds to obtain uniform free-energy convergence; the present work adds an explicit asymptotic C^k condition after that formulation faced a phi^4 counterexample.

reviewed_competitors.title: Topology and Phase Transitions II. Theorem on a necessary relation
reviewed_competitors.difference: Part II related entropy-derivative growth to Morse-index changes; this revision broadens the relevant event to asymptotic loss of diffeomorphicity even without finite-N critical points.

reviewed_competitors.title: Unattainability of a purely topological criterion for the existence of a phase transition for non-confining potentials
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kastner shows similar topology changes can occur with and without a transition in nonconfining models, undermining purely topological sufficiency; the present theorem restricts its domain and claims only necessity.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the apparent failure of the topological theory of phase transitions
reviewed_competitors.difference: Gori et al. numerically argue the 2D lattice phi^4 transition has an asymptotic topology change without a critical point; the present paper turns that intuition into a uniform-diffeomorphism definition and revised theorem.

reviewed_competitors.title: Why Are Convolutional Nets More Sample-Efficient than Fully-Connected Nets?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Li, Zhang, and Arora prove a natural task with an O(1) versus Omega(d squared) sample gap by exploiting the orthogonal equivariance of Gaussian-initialized gradient methods. Xiao and Pennington generalize the diagnostic to several CNN readouts, transformed image data, finite versus infinite width, and learning-curve interactions, but their broad empirical group-dimension story is less rigorous than this predecessor's constructed lower bound.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning with invariances in random features and kernel models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Mei, Misiakiewicz, and Montanari derive a d-to-the-alpha sample and feature saving for invariant random features and kernels and show when data augmentation matches an invariant estimator. The present paper focuses on mismatch and feature-learning departures from infinite kernels on real image benchmarks rather than a high-dimensional risk theorem.

reviewed_competitors.title: Data-driven emergence of convolutional structure in neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ingrosso and Goldt analytically and numerically show localized, space-tiling receptive fields emerging from higher-order local image statistics in an initially fully connected model. That work offers a concrete pattern-formation mechanism for learning convolutional structure, whereas DIDE infers a function-class transition primarily from performance and output distances.

reviewed_competitors.title: Approximately Equivariant Networks for Imperfectly Symmetric Dynamics
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wang, Walters, and Yu relax exact equivariance for dynamics whose symmetries are only approximate, directly targeting the risk that an overly large hard-coded group is spurious. Xiao and Pennington diagnose harmful mismatch but do not train an adaptive continuum between invariant and unrestricted models.

reviewed_competitors.title: Equivariance with Learned Canonicalization Functions
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kaba and colleagues learn a canonical representative before an ordinary backbone, offering exact equivariance without constraining every layer to a specialized architecture. This is a practical response to the data-model compatibility problem, although it assumes the target group is known and does not address DIDE scaling.

reviewed_competitors.title: Generative Adversarial Symmetry Discovery
reviewed_competitors.difference: LieGAN adversarially learns continuous equivariances from data and then transfers them into equivariant models, replacing manual group choice with an empirical discovery procedure. It tackles an operational gap left here, but learned transformations still require checks that they preserve labels and rare exceptions rather than only marginal data appearance.

reviewed_competitors.title: Efficient Learning and Symmetry Discovery under Exact Invariances
reviewed_competitors.difference: Soleymani and colleagues give polynomial-time algorithms and sample guarantees for exact known invariances and recover unknown finite-group symmetries under their regression assumptions. This provides a sharper computational and statistical target than the present paper's heuristic group-dimension explanation, while covering a much more restricted exact-invariance setting than natural images.

reviewed_competitors.title: Entropy-SGD: Biasing Gradient Descent Into Wide Valleys
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chaudhari et al. define a local-entropy objective around a parameter point, derive an optimizer that estimates its gradient with Langevin dynamics, and test convolutional and recurrent networks. Zhang instead estimates a global joint density over a bounded cube and test accuracy; it supplies no optimizer that follows that density.

reviewed_competitors.title: Entropic gradient descent algorithms and wide flat minima
reviewed_competitors.difference: Pittorino et al. analyze maximum-flatness estimators in a Gaussian-mixture model and evaluate Entropy-SGD and Replicated-SGD on modern ResNet and EfficientNet settings. Zhang's global Wang-Landau slice is distinct, but its single spiral experiment is much narrower and does not compare with those entropy-guided algorithms.

reviewed_competitors.title: Sharp Minima Can Generalize For Deep Nets
reviewed_competitors.difference: Dinh et al. prove that ReLU reparameterizations can change common parameter-space sharpness measures arbitrarily while preserving the network function. Zhang's normalized cube volume uses a different statistic but leaves the same coordinate and symmetry problem uncontrolled.

reviewed_competitors.title: Why flatness does and does not correlate with generalization for deep neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhang et al. show that flatness-generalization correlations can break under rescaling and optimizer changes, and find a function prior more robust. The reviewed paper studies global volume rather than local flatness, but never compares its coordinate-dependent volume against a function-space predictor or under reparameterization.

reviewed_competitors.title: Deep Networks on Toroids: Removing Symmetries Reveals the Structure of Flat Regions in the Landscape Geometry
reviewed_competitors.difference: Pittorino et al. explicitly remove continuous scaling and discrete permutation symmetries and examine local energy in a normalized-and-aligned geometry across MLP, convolutional, and VGG models. Zhang retains raw cube coordinates and therefore cannot tell functional volume from redundant parameter volume.

reviewed_competitors.title: Entropy-SGD optimizes the prior of a PAC-Bayes bound: Generalization properties of Entropy-SGD and data-dependent priors
reviewed_competitors.difference: Dziugaite and Roy distinguish a tempting entropy interpretation from a valid generalization guarantee: a data-dependent prior violates the basic PAC-Bayes condition unless additional control is supplied. Zhang gives a descriptive volume correlation and no risk bound, held-out guarantee, or comparable dependency analysis.

reviewed_competitors.title: Randomized Positional Encodings Boost Length Generalization of Transformers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct follow-up and positional-encoding intervention from overlapping authors.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The follow-up trains more than 6,000 models and reports roughly a 12-point average improvement by exposing short sequences to positions sampled from longer ranges. It supports the original diagnosis that unseen position indices matter but weakens any claim that failure is an intrinsic Transformer or Chomsky-class limit.

reviewed_competitors.title: What Algorithms can Transformers Learn? A Study in Length Generalization
reviewed_competitors.relationship: ICLR 2024 successor offering a competing predictor of algorithmic extrapolation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhou et al. relate generalization to the existence of short RASP-L programs and controlled data properties. Program simplicity and representability provide a more task-specific hypothesis than assigning each transduction a broad Chomsky class.

reviewed_competitors.title: Position Coupling: Improving Length Generalization of Arithmetic Transformers Using Task Structure
reviewed_competitors.difference: Position coupling aligns structurally corresponding digits and reports over 95% exact-match accuracy on addition up to 200 digits after training on at most 30 digits, with theoretical analysis for a one-layer Transformer. It shows that explicit task structure can overturn the original addition failure under a stricter metric.

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformers Can Do Arithmetic with the Right Embeddings
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later positional-embedding counterexample to arithmetic extrapolation failure.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Abacus embeddings index digits relative to the start of each number and enable strong extrapolation on addition, multiplication, and sorting, including high accuracy on 100-digit addition after training through 20 digits. This makes the interface between task structure and position a primary causal variable absent from a hierarchy-only account.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Formal Framework for Understanding Length Generalization in Transformers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later formalization of what finite length-generalization experiments can identify.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The framework studies identifiability and sufficient conditions for causal Transformers with positional encodings, separating agreement on short data from recovery of a length-generalizing rule. It addresses the logical gap between finite accuracy and arbitrary-length claims more directly than the original empirical threshold.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Expressive Capacity of State Space Models: A Formal Language Perspective
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later architecture competitor using the same formal-language lens.
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work analyzes state-space models including Mamba and compares their exact state-tracking behavior with RNNs and Transformers under explicit assumptions. It expands the architecture set and makes clearer how precision and recurrence assumptions determine formal-language conclusions.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Role of Sparsity for Length Generalization in LLMs
reviewed_competitors.relationship: ICML 2025 competing structural theory of length generalization.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Golowich et al. study tasks with sparse dependency structure and predictive position coupling, yielding guarantees and experiments tied to which input positions determine each output. Dependency sparsity is a finer-grained explanatory variable than a single language-class label.

reviewed_competitors.title: When Can Transformers Count to n?
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current formal and empirical study of the counting capability highlighted by the original paper.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yehudai et al. isolate conditions under which Transformers can learn counting and generalize in length rather than treating counting as an informal exception within a broad class. The narrower setup permits sharper claims about representation, learning, and failure.

reviewed_competitors.title: An Algebraic View of the Expressivity of Recurrent Language Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current theoretical refinement of recurrent-model expressivity.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The algebraic treatment makes the arithmetic model and quantization assumptions explicit and shows that expressive classifications can change with finite precision and state representation. Those implementation assumptions are largely suppressed in the original empirical mapping from architecture names to automata.

reviewed_competitors.title: Evaluating the Formal Reasoning Capabilities of Large Language Models through Chomsky Hierarchy
reviewed_competitors.difference: ChomskyBench extends coverage across hierarchy levels, adds process traces and symbolic verification, and interprets observed weaknesses partly as efficiency barriers rather than absolute expressivity bounds. It provides a more explicit validation harness while retaining the hierarchy as an organizing axis.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Stochastic Tunneling Approach for Global Minimization of Complex Potential Energy Landscapes
reviewed_competitors.difference: Stochastic tunneling already applies a dynamically adjusted nonlinear scalar transformation to the original potential energy so a stochastic search can cross otherwise inaccessible barriers. Hamiltonian alternation instead switches deterministic or discrete local minimization between the original and a thresholded transform, emphasizing shared versus reversed critical points; the close landscape-transformation precedent materially narrows the novelty claim and is not used as an experimental baseline.

reviewed_competitors.title: An Augmented Filled Function for Global Nonlinear Integer Optimization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Filled-function methods construct an auxiliary landscape after reaching a local solution so subsequent local search escapes its basin, including discrete nonlinear problems and solver-independent variants. Hamiltonian alternation uses the unusually simple global composition K(H) and alternates repeatedly, but it does not compare against filled functions or analyze their shared issue of auxiliary-function parameter choice.

reviewed_competitors.title: On Graduated Optimization for Stochastic Non-Convex Problems
reviewed_competitors.difference: Graduated optimization follows a sequence of increasingly less-smoothed objectives and provides global convergence rates for a characterized nice function family. Hamiltonian alternation instead flips high-energy inherited curvature while retaining the original landscape every other call, supports discrete local search heuristically, and lacks comparable conditions or complexity bounds.

reviewed_competitors.title: Faster Perturbed Stochastic Gradient Methods for Finding Local Minima
reviewed_competitors.difference: LENA combines perturbations with variance-reduced stochastic gradients and gives oracle-complexity guarantees for approximate second-order local minima. It targets saddle escape rather than global minima, while Hamiltonian alternation targets both high local minima and inherited saddles; LENA has stronger finite-time theory but no claim of global basin discovery.

reviewed_competitors.title: Using Stochastic Gradient Descent to Smooth Nonconvex Functions: Analysis of Implicit Graduated Optimization
reviewed_competitors.difference: This later work interprets SGD noise as objective smoothing controlled by learning rate, batch size, and gradient variance, then derives a graduated schedule and tests ResNets. It changes landscape scale implicitly rather than composing objective values and supplies machine-learning evidence absent from Hamiltonian alternation, but depends on stochastic gradients and smoothing assumptions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Classical and Quantum Speedups for Non-Convex Optimization via Energy Conserving Descent
reviewed_competitors.difference: Energy Conserving Descent replaces dissipative descent with conservative dynamics to avoid exponentially rare noise-driven escapes and provides hitting-time analysis in an initial one-dimensional theory. Hamiltonian alternation keeps an arbitrary local optimizer but changes the potential; both use physical landscape intuitions, while ECD offers sharper escape-time claims and Hamiltonian alternation offers simpler modularity and discrete applicability.

reviewed_competitors.title: Invariant Spectral Foliations with Applications to Model Order Reduction and Synthesis
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct predecessor introducing the invariant-spectral-foliation theory and data-fitting idea used by the target.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The predecessor already defines the smoothest local invariant foliation as a unique nonlinear modal factor and fits it to beam vibration data. The target's additions are the four-diagram taxonomy, HT-compressed high-dimensional encoder, fixed-leaf recovery, coordinate-corrected physical quantities, and broader comparisons.

reviewed_competitors.title: Data-driven Discovery of Coordinates and Governing Equations
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Pre-target end-to-end autoencoder plus sparse latent-dynamics alternative.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Champion et al. jointly learn nonlinear coordinates and a parsimonious SINDy model using reconstruction, derivative, and latent-dynamics losses. It targets approximate dynamics on low-dimensional behavior rather than exact full-cloud semiconjugacy, so it is not refuted by the target's restricted reconstruction baseline and should have been a capacity-matched comparison.

reviewed_competitors.title: Model Reduction of Dynamical Systems on Nonlinear Manifolds Using Deep Convolutional Autoencoders
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Pre-target nonlinear-manifold projection framework using autoencoder geometry.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lee and Carlberg derive manifold Galerkin and manifold LSPG residual minimization with error analysis and use convolutional decoders for advection-dominated systems. It assumes access to governing residuals rather than only state pairs and is approximate rather than invariant, illustrating a major ROM class excluded by the target's taxonomy.

reviewed_competitors.title: Operator Inference for Non-Intrusive Model Reduction with Quadratic Manifolds
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Concurrent nonintrusive polynomial-manifold and reduced-dynamics method.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Geelen, Wright, and Willcox combine a POD-plus-quadratic decoder with operator inference to learn scalable approximate ROMs from high-dimensional data. It lacks exact invariant-foliation guarantees but directly challenges the claim that foliation fitting is the only meaningful offline ROM route under standard predictive definitions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Data-Driven Modeling and Prediction of Non-Linearizable Dynamics via Spectral Submanifolds
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest concurrent invariant-manifold competitor using offline trajectory data.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Cenedese et al. fit attracting spectral submanifolds and sparse normal-form dynamics from unforced numerical and experimental trajectories and test forced-response prediction. Their need for data close to the SSM is a coverage limitation, not closed-loop necessity, and their broader systems and predictive tests qualify the target's categorical offline-manifold claim.

reviewed_competitors.title: Fast Data-Driven Model Reduction for Nonlinear Dynamical Systems
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Concurrent explicit and computationally faster SSM-learning alternative.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Axas, Cenedese, and Haller replace implicit SSMLearn fits with explicit manifold and normal-form calculations under additional tangent-space assumptions and report orders-of-magnitude speedups. It supplies scalability and timing evidence absent from the target's HT-complexity claim, though it requires data near the target SSM.

reviewed_competitors.title: Smooth Invariant Foliations and Koopman Eigenfunctions about Stable Equilibria of Semiflows
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Post-target mathematical generalization and clarification of foliation-Koopman equivalence.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Buza proves existence and uniqueness for C-r semiflows on Banach spaces under spectral conditions and treats Koopman eigenfunctions systematically, including a Navier-Stokes application. It strengthens the infinite-dimensional theory but does not offer the target's data-fitting algorithm or empirical ROM comparisons.

reviewed_competitors.title: Machine-Learning Invariant Foliations in Forced Systems for Reduced Order Modelling
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Author's direct extension beyond the target's autonomous equilibrium setting.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Szalai extends the workflow to external, parametric, periodic, and quasi-periodic forcing around invariant tori and explicitly highlights unresolved limitations of fitting invariant structures. It addresses one major scope limitation while retaining strong smoothness, representation, and identifiability assumptions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Data-Driven Nonlinear Model Reduction to Spectral Submanifolds via Oblique Projection
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current pragmatic approximation to the invariant-foliation projection emphasized by the target.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bettini et al. agree that an exact stable foliation would pair off-manifold trajectories with SSM dynamics, but argue that reconstructing it is unrealistic from feasible experimental data and instead learn an oblique projection from a single non-normal beam trajectory. This directly tests the target's key practical premise and favors approximate task-oriented projection when data coverage is limited.

reviewed_competitors.title: Data-Driven Modelling of Autonomous and Forced Dynamical Systems
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current author follow-up consolidating autonomous and forced foliation identification.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The follow-up claims data-efficient fits from single or multiple trajectories, adds forced and parameter-dependent systems, uses multiple local foliations to recover manifolds, and addresses over/underfitting through function-representation selection. It is the most direct current evolution of the target and should be checked before reusing its 2022 algorithmic details.

reviewed_competitors.title: HALO: Hybrid Auto-encoded Locomotion with Learned Latent Dynamics, Poincare Maps, and Regions of Attraction
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current autoencoder ROM counterpoint with stability structure in a hybrid dynamical setting.
reviewed_competitors.difference: HALO learns an autoencoded latent Poincare map from trajectory data and evaluates whether latent Lyapunov and region-of-attraction structure lifts to simulated full-order locomotion. It does not satisfy the target's exact full-neighborhood invariance definition, but demonstrates why approximate, task-specific latent ROMs remain scientifically meaningful outside smooth equilibrium dynamics.

reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational result whose terminology and operational interpretation the reviewed paper revises.
reviewed_competitors.difference: McClean et al. define the problem through exponentially concentrated gradients and fixed-precision gradient-estimation probability. The reviewed distinction between laziness and delta-loss is conceptually useful but does not remove that measurement-complexity lower-level obstacle.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: arXiv record for Nature Communications 2018 article

reviewed_competitors.title: Quantum Lazy Training
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Independent and earlier formal treatment of lazy training in local parameterized quantum circuits.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Abedi et al. prove parameter-motion and linearization-error bounds for geometrically local circuits as qubit count grows. This directly overlaps the reviewed naming/concept, while using locality rather than global random-design averaging and not claiming that laziness resolves trainability.

reviewed_competitors.title: Theory of overparametrization in quantum neural networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Prior landscape-level theory of the overparameterization transition.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Larocca et al. define the critical parameter count through reachable Lie-algebra/QFI/Hessian rank and numerically show spurious minima disappearing. That structural criterion is more problem/ansatz-aware than raw L, while also warning the critical dimension can be exponential.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Convergence Theory for Over-parameterized Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporaneous rigorous convergence and noise analysis for a concrete variational task.
reviewed_competitors.difference: You et al. connect VQE to Riemannian gradient flow and give system- and ansatz-dependent sufficient thresholds plus empirical tests. It is less universal but more task-specific than the reviewed scalar random-design recurrence.

reviewed_competitors.title: Beyond Barren Plateaus: Quantum Variational Algorithms Are Swamped With Traps
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct contemporaneous counterpoint to the inference that non-barren landscapes contain accessible good minima.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Anschuetz and Kiani prove broad shallow models can lack barren plateaus yet have a superpolynomially small fraction of good minima, and derive noisy statistical-query barriers. They explicitly note favorable overparameterized transitions can require intractable parameter counts.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: arXiv record for Nature Communications 2022 article

reviewed_competitors.title: Noise-induced barren plateaus in variational quantum algorithms
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Rigorous competing account of physical noise effects.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wang et al. model local Pauli channels in the circuit and prove exponentially vanishing gradients when noisy depth grows linearly with qubits. That mechanism changes the objective/kernel itself and is absent from the reviewed additive i.i.d. angle-noise recursion.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: arXiv record for Nature Communications 2021 article

reviewed_competitors.title: Dynamical transition in controllable quantum neural networks with large depth
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later nonperturbative extension of QNTK training dynamics, including hardware validation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhang et al. identify frozen-kernel, critical, and frozen-error regimes through a transcritical bifurcation and test the theory on IBM devices. It shows the reviewed exponential frozen-kernel law is one phase, not a complete late-time dynamics theory.

reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational UFM gradient-flow analysis for squared error and strong neural collapse.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It analyzes a special invariant subspace and initialization-sensitive linearized dynamics directly; the review summarizes it and adds a mean-squared scaling calculation but does not supply new trajectory evidence.

reviewed_competitors.relationship: Primary MSE dynamics work deriving a least-squares central path and validating NC in canonical networks.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It provides a focused theorem and executable empirical study; the review's broader normalization interpretation combines this result with several other surrogate settings.

reviewed_competitors.relationship: Establishes the regularized cross-entropy UFM's benign landscape and simplex global minimizers and evaluates fixed ETF classifiers.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It is a direct landscape theorem under one surrogate and reports concrete memory reductions; the review integrates it with unregularized, MSE, imbalance, and normalization variants while sometimes blurring their nonshared assumptions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Limitations of Neural Collapse for Understanding Generalization in Deep Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest contemporaneous negative result separating train collapse, test collapse, and transferable representation quality.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It foregrounds falsification experiments and concludes NC is primarily an optimization phenomenon with unclear generalization links; the review incorporates much of this warning but places it beside conditional positive bounds.

reviewed_competitors.title: Why Do Better Loss Functions Lead to Less Transferable Features?
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct empirical counterweight to claims that tighter class separation or source collapse improves transfer.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It systematically tunes nine ImageNet objectives and evaluates eight downstream datasets, finding a source-discriminability/fixed-feature-transfer trade-off; the review cites the result but supplies no comparable causal experiment.

reviewed_competitors.title: Quantifying the Variability Collapse of Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Metric competitor motivated by numerical instability and transfer interpretation of existing NC1 measures.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It proposes the Variability Collapse Index with invertible-linear invariance and a relationship to linear-probe loss; the review relies on the pseudoinverse trace ratio and explicitly leaves standardized metrics open.

reviewed_competitors.title: Are Neurons Actually Collapsed? On the Fine-Grained Structure in Neural Representations
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct empirical challenge to interpreting small within-class variation as loss of all data-dependent structure.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It recovers original CIFAR-10 fine labels at 93% after training on five coarse classes and shows residual variations preserve intrinsic information; this postdates the review and makes null-space/fine-structure audits essential.

reviewed_competitors.title: Feature Learning in Deep Classifiers through Intermediate Neural Collapse
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Extends empirical NC analysis from the penultimate layer to successive intermediate layers.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It measures layerwise covariance, mean subspaces, weight spectra, and NCC behavior directly; the review merely proposes deeper-layer extension as future work and focuses overwhelmingly on the last two layers.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Collapse in Deep Linear Networks: From Balanced to Imbalanced Data
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Deep-layer and imbalance extension of UFM geometry under MSE and cross-entropy.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It proves layerwise results for arbitrary-depth linear networks and derives class-size-dependent orthogonal geometry and imbalance thresholds; the review's extended UFM stops largely at one added layer and two-level imbalance summaries.

reviewed_competitors.title: Generalized Neural Collapse for a Large Number of Classes
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Addresses the review's acknowledged impossibility of a K-simplex when K exceeds feature dimension.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Collapse vs. Low-Rank Bias: Is Deep Neural Collapse Really Optimal?
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct challenge to simply extending simplex collapse through deeper nonlinear UFMs.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It shows that beyond two layers or two classes, multi-layer regularization can prefer solutions of still lower rank than deep NC, exposing a qualitative failure of the incremental-extension intuition in the review's future-work section.

reviewed_competitors.title: Can Kernel Methods Explain How the Data Affects Neural Collapse?
reviewed_competitors.relationship: The review author's own later attempt to address the UFM's missing data dependence using NNGP, NTK, and a data-aware Gaussian-process kernel.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It proves NTK is not more collapsed than NNGP for Gaussian data and finds a data-aware kernel can lower NC1 without fully matching shallow networks, turning the review's qualitative limitation into a testable kernel analysis.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Collapse Beyond the Unconstrained Features Model: Landscape, Dynamics, and Generalization in the Mean-Field Regime
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current data-specific theory for NC1 in a three-layer feature-learning network rather than free sample features.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It links small loss and gradient norm to approximate NC1, proves MSE gradient-flow convergence, and obtains simultaneous test error/NC1 for separated distributions; its scope remains NC1 and special data, but it crosses the UFM boundary the review leaves open.

reviewed_competitors.difference: It weakens NC with entropy regularization for generalization and enforces ETF geometry for detection at different layers, empirically treating collapse as a controllable trade-off rather than an unqualified benefit.

reviewed_competitors.title: Gradient Descent Provably Optimizes Over-parameterized Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational direct two-layer ReLU regression baseline
reviewed_competitors.difference: Du et al. prove linear convergence for randomly initialized two-layer ReLU regression under a positive limiting Gram eigenvalue and sufficiently large width by keeping weights near initialization. The audited paper tries to sharpen this NTK-style trajectory analysis with activation angles, but does not validly control its nonsmooth one-step remainder or activation spectrum.

reviewed_competitors.title: Towards moderate overparameterization: global convergence guarantees for training shallow neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Oymak and Soltanolkotabi obtain geometric convergence to a nearby global optimum when the square root of parameter count exceeds sample size, focusing mainly on smooth activations and extending parts to ReLU. Their data, scaling, and trained-parameter setup differ, so the audited paper's exponent table is not a controlled dominance result.

reviewed_competitors.title: Quadratic Suffices for Over-parametrization via Matrix Chernoff Bound
reviewed_competitors.difference: Song and Yang reduce a two-layer ReLU convergence width to a quadratic-scale result using matrix Chernoff under additional separation quantities. The audited paper explicitly contrasts its cubic formula and purportedly milder assumptions, but the latter also imposes d>=n, a lower bound on sigma_min(X), and an invalid concentration chain.

reviewed_competitors.title: Global Convergence of Deep Networks with One Wide Layer Followed by Pyramidal Topology
reviewed_competitors.difference: Nguyen and Mondelli prove linear convergence with one wide layer followed by constant-width pyramidal layers and obtain roughly quadratic first-layer width under LeCun initialization and sub-Gaussian data. This is a different smooth-activation and topology regime, but it already undermines broad claims that the audited cubic result is the mildest general picture of high-dimensional trainability.

reviewed_competitors.title: Subquadratic Overparameterization for Shallow Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Song et al. prove a roughly n^(3/2) parameter scaling with linear convergence while training both layers under standard initialization, using smooth activation and random-matrix plus PL analysis. The activation differs from exact ReLU, but this accepted result predates the audited preprint and was omitted from its state-of-the-art tables despite directly competing on width and training all layers.

reviewed_competitors.title: Improved Overparametrization Bounds for Global Convergence of Stochastic Gradient Descent for Shallow Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Polaczyk and Cyranka use differential inclusions to treat nonsmooth shallow networks and report approximately N^1.25 hidden width for linear convergence of mini-batch SGD under probabilistic data assumptions. Their setup is not identical, but their explicit nonsmooth machinery highlights the missing cross-activation analysis in the audited paper and their result predates its submission.

reviewed_competitors.title: Bounding the Width of Neural Networks via Coupled Initialization -- A Worst Case Analysis
reviewed_competitors.difference: Munteanu, Omlor, Song, and Woodruff prove an n^2-width guarantee for two-layer ReLU regression with square loss, fixed output signs, and training only first-layer weights, but use paired identical hidden weights with opposite output signs so the initial network output is exactly zero. The architecture and objective are especially close to the audited paper, while the coupled initialization is a material extra condition; the result shows why broad minimality claims require initialization-matched comparisons.

reviewed_competitors.title: Memorization and Optimization in Deep Neural Networks with Minimum Over-parameterization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bombari et al. lower-bound the NTK spectrum for deep smooth networks with roughly linear total parameter count and widths as small as sqrt(N), then derive memorization and gradient-descent optimization guarantees under i.i.d. Lipschitz-concentrated data and pyramidal widths. It appeared before this preprint and makes its unqualified state-of-the-art and minimality language untenable, although activation and data assumptions differ.

reviewed_competitors.title: Over-Parameterization Exponentially Slows Down Gradient Descent for Learning a Single Neuron
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later counterpoint on the effect of ReLU overparameterization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Xu and Du give matching O(T^-3) upper and lower rates for an overparameterized two-layer ReLU student learning one ReLU teacher under Gaussian inputs, showing overparameterization can exponentially slow convergence relative to exact parameterization. The teacher-student population setting is narrower, but it directly contradicts any universal narrative that more width monotonically improves optimization speed.

reviewed_competitors.title: Global Convergence Analysis of Local SGD for Two-layer Neural Network without Overparameterization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bao, Shehu, and Liu prove global convergence of vanilla local SGD for a two-layer teacher-student network without overparameterization or injected noise under Gaussian inputs, using a self-correction mechanism and exact directional recursion. Its structured population problem is much narrower than arbitrary finite labels, but it shows that by 2023 the frontier included non-NTK, non-overparameterized dynamics rather than only sharper polynomial width exponents.

reviewed_competitors.title: Deep symbolic regression: Recovering mathematical expressions from data via risk-seeking policy gradients
reviewed_competitors.difference: DSR generates expression trees with an RNN trained by risk-seeking policy gradients and supports structural constraints during generation. CoNSoLe instead chooses layered connection graphs with value learning and a convex action surrogate, but its theoretical relaxation guarantees are unsupported and its comparison reports best-of-five DSR against one CoNSoLe run.

reviewed_competitors.title: AI Feynman: a Physics-Inspired Method for Symbolic Regression
reviewed_competitors.difference: AI Feynman recursively exploits dimensional structure, symmetry, separability, and compositionality to reduce symbolic search and reports exact recovery over a much larger physics-formula suite. CoNSoLe learns a generic staged search policy over a fixed operator graph but does not exploit those physical decomposition tests or demonstrate comparable benchmark breadth.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Symbolic Regression that Scales
reviewed_competitors.difference: NeSymReS amortizes search through Transformer pretraining on synthetic expressions and can decode candidate skeletons quickly at test time. CoNSoLe trains its reward and Q search machinery afresh on each dataset, allowing task-specific constraints but paying repeated architecture and coefficient-fitting cost.

reviewed_competitors.title: End-to-end symbolic regression with transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: This Transformer directly predicts expressions including numerical constants, optionally followed by constant refinement, and evaluates on SRBench with much faster inference than genetic programming. CoNSoLe separates discrete structure from per-architecture coefficient fitting and was submitted before this close concurrent work appeared, so the paper's empirical panel does not cover it.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: arXiv v1, 2022-04-22; no later arXiv revision

reviewed_competitors.title: Contemporary Symbolic Regression Methods and their Relative Performance
reviewed_competitors.difference: SRBench compares 14 symbolic-regression and seven machine-learning methods over 252 datasets with accuracy, complexity, and exact-recovery measures. CoNSoLe evaluates only two synthetic equations and two simulators and omits this available benchmark, leaving its comparative scope much narrower.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: arXiv v1, 2021-07-29; NeurIPS 2021 Datasets and Benchmarks

reviewed_competitors.title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Science with PySR and SymbolicRegression.jl
reviewed_competitors.difference: PySR combines asynchronous island evolution, adaptive parsimony, symbolic simplification, coefficient optimization, rich constraints, and a reproducible Python/Julia software ecosystem. It lacks CoNSoLe's convex value-learning framing but offers a stronger maintained artifact and explicit accuracy-complexity frontier.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: arXiv v3, 2023-05-05; current package ecosystem checked 2026-08-24

reviewed_competitors.title: Transformer-based Planning for Symbolic Regression
reviewed_competitors.difference: TPSR injects Monte Carlo tree search into pretrained Transformer decoding so external accuracy and complexity rewards guide expression construction. Both methods frame symbolic regression as sequential planning, but TPSR searches token trees with an explicit fit-complexity objective and released code rather than relying on an unproven convex connection-action relaxation.

reviewed_competitors.title: LLM-SR: Scientific Equation Discovery via Programming with Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: LLM-SR evolves equation programs proposed with language-model scientific priors and evaluates out-of-domain physical accuracy on four contamination-conscious tasks. CoNSoLe is independent of pretrained language knowledge and has a tighter fixed graph representation, but its operator pool is hand chosen and its simulation tests are less demanding.

reviewed_competitors.title: Symbolic regression via MDLformer-guided search: from minimizing prediction error to minimizing description length
reviewed_competitors.difference: MDLformer guides search with a learned description-length objective that explicitly trades data fit against expression complexity. CoNSoLe rewards only normalized prediction error and therefore has no mechanism to penalize nuisance structure such as its extra near-identity cosine factor.

reviewed_competitors.title: GENSR: Symbolic Regression Based in Equation Generative Space
reviewed_competitors.difference: GENSR searches a learned continuous generative space of equations and reports modern benchmark comparisons across accuracy, simplicity, efficiency, and noise robustness. It shares CoNSoLe's goal of smoothing combinatorial symbolic search, but learns a latent equation manifold rather than asserting convexity of a relaxed layer-connection Q function.

reviewed_competitors.title: Normalized Direction-preserving Adam
reviewed_competitors.difference: ND-Adam explicitly preserves neural weight directions for generalization and memory savings, but its magnitude-oriented updates are not designed to move geometric points freely or prove rotation-equivariant optimization trajectories. VectorAdam uses the vector norm only for the adaptive denominator and retains directional motion.

reviewed_competitors.title: Riemannian Adaptive Optimization Methods
reviewed_competitors.difference: Riemannian Adam, Adagrad, and AMSGrad adapt across factors of a product manifold and provide regret or convergence analysis for geodesically convex objectives. VectorAdam is a much simpler Euclidean grouped update aimed specifically at SO(n) coordinate rotations and practical mesh or rendering artifacts.

reviewed_competitors.title: Shampoo: Preconditioned Stochastic Tensor Optimization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Shampoo exploits matrix or tensor structure with Kronecker-factored full-matrix preconditioners, retaining richer anisotropic conditioning at higher cost. VectorAdam uses one invariant scalar per vector, making its rotation proof and memory footprint simpler but its conditioning less expressive.

reviewed_competitors.title: ELRA: Exponential learning rate adaption gradient descent optimization method
reviewed_competitors.difference: ELRA adapts a global learning rate from relationships between successive gradients and claims coordinate-rotation-invariant paths on general objectives. It avoids per-coordinate Adam moments, whereas VectorAdam preserves Adam-like momentum and adaptivity separately for declared geometric vectors.

reviewed_competitors.title: LoRA Done RITE: Robust Invariant Transformation Equilibration for LoRA Optimization
reviewed_competitors.difference: LoRA-RITE constructs adaptive matrix preconditioning invariant to rotations and rescalings of the two equivalent LoRA factors. It addresses a gauge redundancy in low-rank weight parameterization rather than physical rotations of explicit geometry, but shows how richer matrix statistics can preserve a targeted symmetry.

reviewed_competitors.title: How do simple rotations affect the implicit bias of Adam?
reviewed_competitors.difference: DePavia et al. show that even small feature rotations can reverse Adam's favorable implicit bias in classification and study an objective reparameterization that makes first-order methods rotation equivariant. This broadens the coordinate-bias problem beyond explicit geometry and offers a wrapper-style alternative to VectorAdam's grouped moments.

reviewed_competitors.title: Dead-Direction Conditioners: Gauge-Equivariant Preconditioning for Deep Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: DDC conditions Adam or Muon state in symmetry-orbit decompositions for logit shifts, activation rescalings, normalization scales, and attention-head rotations. It targets multiple deep-network gauges with richer machinery, whereas VectorAdam gives a minimal norm-based construction for explicit vector rotations.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural reparameterization improves structural optimization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Hoyer and colleagues use convolutional-network implicit bias to improve final structural designs over 116 tasks. The reviewed work instead derives a Jacobian-preconditioning interpretation, builds the parameterization from a sparse graph Hessian, and targets time-to-solution rather than mainly design quality.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Preconditioner for Conjugate Gradient PDE Solvers
reviewed_competitors.difference: This method trains a GNN across systems to predict an approximate matrix decomposition used inside preconditioned conjugate gradient for linear second-order PDEs. The reviewed method is per-instance and unsupervised, changes solution coordinates, and also addresses nonlinear graph energies, but lacks the structure and stopping guarantees of PCG.

reviewed_competitors.title: Graph Neural Preconditioners for Iterative Solutions of Sparse Linear Systems
reviewed_competitors.difference: Graph Neural Preconditioners train a nonlinear GNN preconditioner and evaluate it across more than 800 sparse matrices against ILU, AMG, and Krylov alternatives. That is a broader and more solver-centered validation than the reviewed paper, whose analytical GCN is tied to an initial Laplacian-like Hessian but does not require an offline training corpus.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning incomplete factorization preconditioners for GMRES
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work makes a GNN output a sparse invertible approximate LU factorization and optimizes explicit spectral/iteration objectives for GMRES. It supplies an algebraically constrained preconditioner, whereas neural reparameterization uses an unconstrained trainable coordinate map and relies on switching when its initial-Hessian proxy degrades.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning to accelerate distributed ADMM using graph neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: The 2026 approach unrolls graph-structured ADMM and learns adaptive step sizes and communication weights while preserving the base algorithm's convergence properties. The reviewed work obtains a quasi-Newton-like metric through coordinates and applies more broadly to graph energies, but offers no comparable learned-iteration convergence preservation.

reviewed_competitors.title: On Kolmogorov Structure Functions
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later direct theoretical critique of using Kolmogorov structure functions for physical data.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Epstein argues that strings with little mutual information with the halting sequence have flat structure functions and, under an independence postulate, that non-flat examples are mathematical rather than natural. This directly challenges the target's physical emergence signature and motivates restricted description classes.

reviewed_competitors.title: Computational Mechanics: Pattern and Prediction, Structure and Simplicity
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational alternative that defines objective structure through minimal predictive causal states.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Computational mechanics is process- and prediction-centered and offers causal-state reconstruction procedures under statistical assumptions; the target is an individual-string, universal-description ideal whose optimal models are uncomputable and need not be predictive.

reviewed_competitors.title: Reconciling emergences: An information-theoretic approach to identify causal emergence in multivariate data
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct quantitative alternative for multiscale causal emergence.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Rosas et al. define downward causation and causal decoupling with computable multivariate information measures and demonstrate them on Game of Life, flocking, and neural data; the target is more universal but supplies no practical estimator or real-data validation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Emergence as the conversion of information: A unifying theory
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporary information-theoretic theory of why a macrodescription can contain more of a useful information type.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Varley and Hoel operationalize emergence through conversion among redundant, unique, and synergistic information under coarse-graining and test Boolean networks; the target instead searches for multiple description-length drops without committing to a causal variable decomposition.

reviewed_competitors.title: BERTs of a feather do not generalize together: Large variability in generalization across models with similar test set performance
reviewed_competitors.relationship: direct behavioral precursor and source model collection
reviewed_competitors.difference: McCoy et al. establish that 100 similarly accurate MNLI-fine-tuned BERTs vary dramatically on HANS and attribute the variability speculatively to multiple local minima. The reviewed paper contributes a pairwise loss-geometry analysis of those models, but inherits the same diagnostic ambiguity and does not causally validate the local-minimum explanation.

reviewed_competitors.title: What is being transferred in transfer learning?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Neyshabur et al. report that models initialized from the same pretrained vision model stay close and linearly connected, motivating a shared-basin account of transfer. The reviewed paper supplies text-classification counterexamples, but uses a fixed parameterization and a validation-loss chord rather than establishing disconnected optimizer basins.

reviewed_competitors.title: Linear Mode Connectivity and the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis
reviewed_competitors.difference: Frankle et al. use linear connectivity under resampled SGD noise to locate when vision training becomes stable and connect that transition to lottery-ticket success. The reviewed paper borrows the early basin-selection intuition for QQP, but does not test a prospective stability time or intervention on unseen trajectories.

reviewed_competitors.title: Model soups: averaging weights of multiple fine-tuned models improves accuracy without increasing inference time
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wortsman et al. exploit the frequent low-error connectivity of models fine-tuned from a common pretrained checkpoint to average many endpoints. The reviewed work identifies a concrete failure condition for such averaging in text classifiers: cross-group chords can incur loss barriers even when endpoint in-domain scores are similar.

reviewed_competitors.title: Git Re-Basin: Merging Models modulo Permutation Symmetries
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ainsworth et al. align hidden-unit permutations before interpolation and recover zero-barrier connections for independently trained networks, while also discussing counterexamples. The reviewed paper notes limited transformer alignment experiments but does not exhaust symmetries, so some apparent separation can remain coordinate-dependent.

reviewed_competitors.title: Mechanistic Mode Connectivity
reviewed_competitors.relationship: direct mechanistic formalization and intervention successor
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lubana et al. define mechanism similarity through shared input invariances, prove that lack of linear connectivity implies mechanism dissimilarity under their conditions, and introduce connectivity-based fine-tuning to reduce spurious reliance on synthetic benchmarks. This converts the reviewed paper's empirical strategy association into a clearer formal and interventional target, though on more controlled data.

reviewed_competitors.title: Generalized Linear Mode Connectivity for Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: Theus et al. align permutations, semi-permutations, orthogonal transformations, and general invertible maps, recovering low- or zero-barrier chords between independently trained Vision Transformers and GPT-2 models. Their result makes symmetry-aware reanalysis essential before interpreting the reviewed paper's raw BERT barriers as distinct functional basins.

reviewed_competitors.title: Unveiling the Basin-Like Loss Landscape in Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chen et al. study scale-dependent random- and worst-case perturbation regions, distinguishing a pretraining basic-capability basin from fine-tuned capability basins such as safety, math, and code. It broadens basin analysis to modern LLM scale and capability preservation, but uses local perturbation stability rather than pairwise seed clustering or heuristic diagnostics.

reviewed_competitors.title: Exact Solutions of a Deep Linear Network
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct mathematical foundation on which the reviewed paper's global-minimum reduction depends.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ziyin et al. characterize global minima, the zero local basin, and initialization sensitivity for weight-decayed stochastic deep-linear nets. The reviewed work repackages the induced regularization path as Ehrenfest phase transitions and adds thermodynamic/posterior-collapse interpretations.

reviewed_competitors.title: How Regularization Affects the Critical Points in Linear Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Earlier competing analysis of bifurcations and critical points induced by regularization in linear networks.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Taghvaei et al. use characteristic equations and bifurcation theory to trace all critical points under weight decay. The reviewed paper focuses on global value nonanalyticity and a scalar order parameter, so its claim of uniquely identifying phase-like transitions needs to be read against this predecessor.

reviewed_competitors.title: Posterior Collapse of a Linear Latent Variable Model
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporaneous direct treatment of posterior collapse with an explicit latent-variable model.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wang and Ziyin analyze a genuine posterior-collapse threshold in a linear latent-variable/VAE setting. The reviewed paper instead studies a penalized neural-network MAP objective and asserts posterior collapse without representing or comparing posterior and prior distributions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Controlling Posterior Collapse by an Inverse Lipschitz Constraint on the Decoder Network
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later rigorous posterior-collapse definition and intervention for VAE decoders.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kinoshita et al. define collapse by closeness/equality of posterior and prior, derive architectural guarantees, and test VAEs. This highlights the missing distributional criterion in the reviewed paper's zero-MAP analogy.

reviewed_competitors.title: Why Do We Need Weight Decay in Modern Deep Learning?
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Modern competing account of weight decay across vision networks and language models.
reviewed_competitors.difference: D'Angelo et al. emphasize optimization dynamics, SGD implicit regularization, and bias-variance/stability rather than an explicit complexity penalty selecting a global minimum. Their practical regimes are largely outside the reviewed deep-linear thermodynamic model.

reviewed_competitors.title: On Dropout and Nuclear Norm Regularization
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Alternative exact characterization of stochastic regularization in deep linear networks.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Mianjy and Arora derive the rescaling-invariant path/nuclear-norm regularizer induced by dropout and characterize optima. The reviewed work folds multiplicative noise into a specific effective scalar loss but does not separate its implicit regularization from explicit L2 decay.

reviewed_competitors.title: Form2Fit: Learning Shape Priors for Generalizable Assembly from Disassembly
reviewed_competitors.difference: Form2Fit learns surface descriptors and object-to-kit correspondences from real robotic disassembly, then executes pick-and-place on novel kits. FAN instead solves a supplied 2D target silhouette from arbitrary polygon fragments by sequential selection and dense pose prediction; it addresses stronger combinatorics in image space but omits perception and physical execution.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learn2Assemble with Structured Representations and Search for Robotic Architectural Construction
reviewed_competitors.difference: Learn2Assemble combines a multi-head attention graph, model-free reinforcement learning, Monte Carlo planning, and robot-in-the-loop feasibility for stable 3D structures made from building blocks. FAN uses supervised inverse-fragmentation and greedy 2D pose maps for non-unit polygon pieces; it is faster and simpler but has no search, stability, or execution layer.

reviewed_competitors.title: PuzzleFusion: Unleashing the Power of Diffusion Models for Spatial Puzzle Solving
reviewed_competitors.difference: PuzzleFusion generates all piece translations and rotations through iterative diffusion and evaluates synthetic Voronoi jigsaws plus real MagicPlan room layouts. FAN commits one selected fragment at a time and conditions on an explicit target mask; its key advantages are a lightweight greedy decomposition and damaged-piece studies, while diffusion offers joint multimodal pose reasoning without a handcrafted sequence.

reviewed_competitors.title: DiffAssemble: A Unified Graph-Diffusion Model for 2D and 3D Reassembly
reviewed_competitors.difference: DiffAssemble treats pieces as spatial-graph nodes and jointly denoises their positions and rotations across both 2D visual puzzles and 3D fractured objects, reporting state-of-the-art results and an 11× speedup over its quickest optimization baseline. FAN is restricted to sequential 2D raster placement but uniquely studies exact target masks, variable counts, abnormal fragments, and the role of supervised order.

reviewed_competitors.title: Rearrangement Planning for General Part Assembly
reviewed_competitors.difference: GPAT directly predicts precise poses for unseen 3D parts by matching each part to a novel target and validates on CAD models and real scans. FAN handles unordered synthetic 2D fragments with a selection-plus-placement policy, but its evidence for unseen targets, real geometry, and physical pose generalization is much narrower.

reviewed_competitors.title: 3D Geometric Shape Assembly via Efficient Point Cloud Matching
reviewed_competitors.difference: PMTR uses coarse- and fine-level local point-cloud correspondences plus an approximate high-order Proxy Match Transform on the large-scale Breaking Bad 3D benchmark. FAN uses global raster/set context and a supplied 2D target rather than mating-surface correspondence; PMTR shows how the geometric-assembly agenda moved toward realistic 3D fragments and scalable matching.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Reynolds and McDonell already show zero-shot prompts that ask a model to decompose problems into steps, including a closely related solve-by-splitting instruction. The target's advance is controlled multi-task quantification, model-scale analysis, and comparison with CoT demonstrations.

reviewed_competitors.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wei et al. establish large-model gains with hand-written few-shot rationales. Zero-shot-CoT removes demonstration authoring through a fixed trigger, typically at lower accuracy than carefully engineered few-shot CoT and with a second answer-extraction call.

reviewed_competitors.title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Self-consistency samples and marginalizes multiple reasoning paths instead of committing to one greedy chain. The target adopts it in a PaLM appendix and gains accuracy at roughly forty-path inference cost.

reviewed_competitors.title: Least-to-Most Prompting Enables Complex Reasoning in Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Least-to-Most explicitly decomposes hard problems into ordered subproblems and tests easy-to-hard compositional generalization. It uses demonstrations and more task structure, whereas Zero-shot-CoT is cheaper to author but does not evaluate length extrapolation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Automatic Chain of Thought Prompting in Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Auto-CoT uses Zero-shot-CoT to generate diverse demonstrations automatically, aiming to recover few-shot performance while reducing manual rationale writing and mitigating errors through diverse question selection.

reviewed_competitors.title: Plan-and-Solve Prompting: Improving Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought Reasoning by Large Language Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: Plan-and-Solve targets calculation, missing-step, and semantic-misunderstanding failures by asking for a plan before execution. It reports improvements across ten datasets but uses a more elaborate instruction.

reviewed_competitors.title: On Second Thought, Let's Not Think Step by Step! Bias and Toxicity in Zero-Shot Reasoning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Shaikh et al. test socially sensitive settings absent from the target and find zero-shot CoT can increase harmful or stereotyped generations, sometimes worsening with scale, limiting claims that the trigger is universally desirable.

reviewed_competitors.title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
reviewed_competitors.difference: Turpin et al. causally manipulate biasing features and show models can rationalize answers without revealing the true influence. This challenges interpreting Zero-shot-CoT text as transparent internal reasoning rather than useful generated context.

reviewed_competitors.title: Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lanham et al. intervene on chains and find faithfulness varies strongly by task and model and can decrease with capability, supporting a separation between the target's accuracy gains and claims that printed chains explain computation.

reviewed_competitors.title: The large learning rate phase of deep learning: the catapult mechanism
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lewkowycz et al. discover the catapult phase, solve a two-layer linear-network case, and connect the large-rate window to flatter minima and strong performance in practical networks. The reviewed paper's novelty is a second-order Taylor surrogate for nonlinear ReLU networks and a rank-two multi-example extension, but it inherits the predecessor's phase framing and does not provide an unbiased or mechanistic generalization test.

reviewed_competitors.title: Second-order regression models exhibit progressive sharpening to the edge of stability
reviewed_competitors.difference: Agarwala, Pedregosa, and Pennington analyze progressive sharpening and near-edge stabilization in general second-order regression models, extending quadratic surrogates from an early spike to longer curvature dynamics. The reviewed paper is stronger on an explicit catapult amplitude window for its special NQM and on network/NQM test plots, but weaker on later edge-of-stability behavior and generic model structure.

reviewed_competitors.title: Catapult Dynamics and Phase Transitions in Quadratic Nets
reviewed_competitors.difference: Meltzer, Chen, and Liu prove catapult behavior for a broader class of quadratic models and two-layer homogeneous networks via weight-norm reduction and add ReLU sparsity experiments. Its current journal revision explicitly notes that initialization Taylor expansions break down after substantial weight movement, directly qualifying the reviewed paper's surrogate interpretation. The reviewed work retains more neural-versus-NQM generalization plots but a narrower and error-prone multi-example proof.

reviewed_competitors.title: Phase diagram of early training dynamics in deep neural networks: effect of the learning rate, depth, and width
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kalra and Barkeshli map multiple loss and Hessian-sharpness transitions over depth and width in FC, convolutional, and residual networks, including a distinct early sharpness-reduction phase. It offers a richer empirical phase atlas for real networks; the reviewed paper offers a more explicit quadratic-output recurrence but covers fewer formal settings and measures tangent-kernel rather than full-loss Hessian dynamics.

reviewed_competitors.title: Catapults in SGD: spikes in the training loss and their impact on generalization through feature learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: The same authors extend the catapult account to repeated SGD loss spikes, show concentration in top tangent-kernel eigenspaces, and propose AGOP alignment as a feature-learning route to improved test performance. That successor is substantially stronger on the stochastic setting and on a candidate generalization mechanism; the reviewed paper provides the earlier fixed-Hessian GD surrogate but only correlates best test loss with learning rate.

reviewed_competitors.title: From Stability to Chaos: Analyzing Gradient Descent Dynamics in Quadratic Regression
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chen et al. derive a cubic-map phase diagram with monotone, catapult, periodic, chaotic, and divergent regimes and precise boundaries for quadratic regression, noting that the reviewed NQM result does not directly extend to their setting. It supersedes the simple three-phase picture for its solvable class and studies trajectory-averaged generalization; the reviewed paper remains closer to neural Taylor models but lacks beyond-catapult attractor analysis.

reviewed_competitors.title: Universal Sharpness Dynamics in Neural Network Training: Fixed Point Analysis, Edge of Stability, and Route to Chaos
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kalra, He, and Barkeshli use a two-layer linear UV model and function-space fixed points to connect early sharpness reduction, progressive sharpening, edge-of-stability conditions, and period-doubling chaos, with neural and language-model evidence. It provides a more complete long-run dynamical mechanism, whereas the reviewed paper isolates the initial catapult in an NQM and emphasizes second-order neural approximation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Edge of Stochastic Stability: Revisiting the Edge of Stability for SGD
reviewed_competitors.difference: Andreyev and Beneventano show that minibatch SGD stabilizes directional Batch Sharpness near 2/eta rather than the full-batch top Hessian eigenvalue. This cautions against transferring the reviewed paper's full-batch tangent-kernel thresholds to its SGD generalization panel; the reviewed paper neither derives a stochastic recurrence nor measures the appropriate batchwise stability statistic.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Defense of the Quadratic Model
reviewed_competitors.difference: Meterez et al. stress-test local quadratic loss and model expansions at intermediate checkpoints in a 150M-parameter language model and report predictive windows up to roughly ten percent of training, plus Hessian-spectrum and stochastic-stability analyses. It provides the kind of direct approximation-error evidence absent from the reviewed work, but studies repeatedly recentered local quadratics rather than one initialization NQM spanning a catapult.
