reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational model family and training approach whose claim of continuous-time parameterization motivates the validation problem.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chen et al. introduce black-box adaptive-solver training, latent ODEs, and continuous normalizing flows; they do not propose the paper's post-training held-out step-size convergence criterion for scientific vector-field recovery.

reviewed_competitors.title: Continuous-in-Depth Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct predecessor by overlapping authors that already diagnoses Euler/ResNet discretization dependence and introduces the ContinuousNet name.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The predecessor focuses on continuous-depth network graph invariance and incremental-depth training; this paper repurposes the idea as an a posteriori scientific-dynamics validation test, adds held-out trajectories, SINDy, and scalar error analysis. Consequently, the high-order-integrator intuition and ContinuousNet framing are not wholly new here.

reviewed_competitors.title: ResNet After All? Neural ODEs and Their Numerical Solution
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest prior empirical diagnosis of solver dependence in trained Neural ODEs.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ott et al. test whether switching to an equal- or lower-error numerical solver preserves performance and recommend sufficiently accurate training integration. The present paper formalizes a held-out h-to-zero curve and heuristic pass rule, applies it to physical trajectory learning and SINDy, and derives a scalar bound, but reaches a substantially overlapping warning.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Differential Equations that are Easy to Solve
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Competing solver-aware training strategy that changes the learned vector field rather than only diagnosing it after training.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kelly et al. penalize higher total derivatives as a differentiable surrogate for adaptive-solver cost and evaluate accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs across classification, density estimation, and time series. The present test targets training-step overfit and physical-resolution transfer, without regularizing solve difficulty or reporting compute tradeoffs.

reviewed_competitors.title: On Numerical Integration in Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Concurrent, more general mathematical account of the same training-discretization phenomenon.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhu et al. use inverse modified differential equations to show that training approximates a solver-dependent modified equation, bound true-ODE discrepancy by learning plus discretization error, and analyze conservation-law failure for non-symplectic schemes. The present work contributes a simple observable validation curve, but its proof is restricted to scalar Taylor-polynomial roots and contains a sign error in the Euler example.

reviewed_competitors.title: DynaDojo: An Extensible Platform for Benchmarking Scaling in Dynamical System Identification
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Competing evaluation infrastructure for learned dynamics and system-identification methods.
reviewed_competitors.difference: DynaDojo standardizes seven algorithms, twenty systems, sample-complexity and system-complexity scaling, target-error efficiency, out-of-distribution conditions, and active learning. The paper under review supplies a focused discretization diagnostic on a handful of synthetic systems but no cross-method benchmark or scaling analysis.

reviewed_competitors.title: DySLIM: Dynamics Stable Learning by Invariant Measure for Chaotic Systems
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Successor approach that trains and validates dynamics using long-run distributional signal excluded by this paper.
reviewed_competitors.difference: DySLIM regularizes any learning objective toward the invariant measure and reports pointwise plus long-term statistical accuracy on dissipative chaotic systems. The convergence test only asks whether numerical refinement preserves observed-time trajectory error and explicitly excludes chaos, so it cannot replace invariant-measure validation.

reviewed_competitors.title: When are dynamical systems learned from time series data statistically accurate?
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current theory and validation framework exposing why small test error or a smooth learned generator may still be physically wrong.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Park et al. define ergodic, dynamics-aware generalization, evaluate statistical moments and Lyapunov spectra, and show benefits from Jacobian information across MLP, ResNet, Fourier, and recurrent models on chaotic systems. Those criteria directly cover false positives that can pass the paper's step-size test.

reviewed_competitors.title: Adaptive Higher Order Reversible Integrators for Memory Efficient Deep Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current solver-design alternative for irregular observations and high-accuracy learned dynamics.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Maslovskaya et al. construct higher-order reversible integrators with adaptive steps to combine depth-independent memory, variable observation intervals, accuracy, and speed. The present fixed-step nudge-and-sweep algorithm names adaptive stepping as future work and offers no compatible convergence criterion for tolerance-controlled solvers.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations for Model Order Reduction of Stiff Systems
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current method addressing the stiff-system regime excluded from the convergence-test demonstrations.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Caldana and Hesthaven learn a data-driven time reparameterization induced by an implicit solver, converting stiff reduced dynamics into a form cheaply integrated explicitly and evaluating robustness, accuracy, and extrapolation. The present paper observes that stiffness shifts convergence failure to smaller steps but provides neither a stiff solver strategy nor a validated pass rule for it.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning by Directional Gradient Descent
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Concurrent independent work using directional derivatives and candidate directions to train state representations without conventional backpropagation, cited anonymously in the target's cached manuscript.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Silver et al. focus on online recurrent/state-representation learning and study random plus approximate-gradient candidate directions; Baydin et al. present the generic unbiased rank-one estimator, a custom exact forward-AD engine, and feedforward runtime comparisons.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scaling Forward Gradient With Local Losses
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct follow-on that identifies the high variance of naive parameter-space forward gradients and seeks to scale them to standard vision tasks.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ren et al. perturb activations, introduce many local losses, and design LocalMixer to reduce effective dimensionality, partially trading global end-to-end unbiasedness for practical MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet performance.

reviewed_competitors.title: Can Forward Gradient Match Backpropagation?
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct empirical and methodological study of the difficulty of guessing useful forward-gradient directions in high-dimensional neural networks.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Fournier et al. deliberately bias direction guesses using local auxiliary-network gradients and systematically compare targets and guesses; the target paper uses isotropic Gaussian directions to retain a simple globally unbiased estimator.

reviewed_competitors.title: Fine-Tuning Language Models with Just Forward Passes
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Adjacent forward-only optimization that directly tests the memory motivation at language-model scale, including models up to 66 billion parameters.
reviewed_competitors.difference: MeZO uses two ordinary finite-difference forward passes and can optimize nondifferentiable objectives, incurring zeroth-order bias but achieving inference-level memory; Baydin et al. require JVP-capable differentiation and obtain an exact directional derivative on small from-scratch models.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: NeurIPS 2023, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 36

reviewed_competitors.title: Second-Order Forward-Mode Automatic Differentiation for Optimization
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later extension by overlapping authors that adds forward-mode second-order information to address challenges of backpropagation-free optimization.
reviewed_competitors.difference: FoMoH uses hyper-dual numbers to obtain directional derivatives and quadratic Hessian terms for k-dimensional hyperplane search; the target method uses only one first-order JVP and a vanilla rank-one SGD update.

reviewed_competitors.title: Variance-reduced Zeroth-Order Methods for Fine-Tuning Language Models
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Adjacent work making forward-only language-model optimization more stable through explicit stochastic variance reduction.
reviewed_competitors.difference: MeZO-SVRG applies control-variate ideas to finite-difference zeroth-order fine-tuning and reports broad GLUE results; the target paper neither analyzes nor reduces its exact-JVP estimator variance and evaluates only MNIST-scale learning.

reviewed_competitors.title: DGM: A deep learning algorithm for solving partial differential equations
reviewed_competitors.difference: DGM already trains a neural solution by sampling a PDE residual and boundary/initial conditions without a global grid. HFD changes derivative evaluation to finite stencils but supplies no high-dimensional study comparable to DGM's motivating regime.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Deep Ritz method: A deep learning-based numerical algorithm for solving variational problems
reviewed_competitors.difference: Deep Ritz minimizes an energy functional and can avoid strong-form second derivatives. It is a major alternative to both AD and FD strong residuals that HFD does not benchmark.

reviewed_competitors.title: Physics Informed Deep Learning (Part I): Data-driven Solutions of Nonlinear Partial Differential Equations
reviewed_competitors.difference: Raissi, Perdikaris, and Karniadakis establish coordinate networks trained with PDE, boundary, initial, and data residuals. HFD's contribution is numerical rather than automatic input differentiation, not the physics-informed optimization framework itself.

reviewed_competitors.title: Deep Nitsche Method: Deep Ritz Method with Essential Boundary Conditions
reviewed_competitors.difference: Deep Nitsche handles essential boundary conditions consistently through a variational formulation and proves an energy-norm error estimate. HFD uses soft and, in Equation 28, cancellable boundary penalties without an error estimate.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding and mitigating gradient pathologies in physics-informed neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work identifies numerical stiffness and unbalanced gradients across composite PINN losses and proposes adaptive weighting. HFD reports residual scales differing by orders of magnitude but neither measures nor controls their gradient imbalance.

reviewed_competitors.title: hp-VPINNs: Variational Physics-Informed Neural Networks With Domain Decomposition
reviewed_competitors.difference: hp-VPINNs localize training through hp-refined test spaces and weak residuals, avoiding some high-order strong derivatives. HFD instead uses point stencils and does not compare localization accuracy, training cost, or refinement behavior.

reviewed_competitors.title: PFNN: A Penalty-Free Neural Network Method for Solving a Class of Second-Order Boundary-Value Problems on Complex Geometries
reviewed_competitors.difference: PFNN uses a weak form and separate networks to satisfy essential boundaries without penalty on complex domains, with a convergence result. HFD's novelty and validation should have been distinguished from this direct predecessor.

reviewed_competitors.title: PhyGeoNet: Physics-Informed Geometry-Adaptive Convolutional Neural Networks for Solving Parameterized Steady-State PDEs on Irregular Domain
reviewed_competitors.difference: PhyGeoNet maps irregular physical domains to regular reference domains, applies finite-difference convolutional residuals, and hard-encodes boundaries. It predates HFD and directly challenges any broad claim that FD-informed neural solving on irregular geometry is new.

reviewed_competitors.title: When and why PINNs fail to train: A neural tangent kernel perspective
reviewed_competitors.difference: The NTK analysis attributes failure to unequal convergence rates among PINN loss components and proposes adaptive calibration. HFD's curves alone cannot establish that finite differences fix this mechanism, particularly under unmatched loss scales.

reviewed_competitors.title: Exact imposition of boundary conditions with distance functions in physics-informed deep neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sukumar and Srivastava use approximate distance functions and R-functions to satisfy Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin conditions exactly on complex geometry. HFD uses distance only to choose a stencil radius and retains soft boundary losses.

reviewed_competitors.title: Characterizing possible failure modes in physics-informed neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Krishnapriyan et al. show that soft PDE regularization can create ill-conditioned landscapes even on modest convection, reaction, and diffusion problems, and propose curriculum and time decomposition. HFD does not test whether its gains survive those controlled failure regimes.

reviewed_competitors.title: When Do Extended Physics-Informed Neural Networks (XPINNs) Improve Generalization?
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work formalizes when local decomposition helps or hurts generalization and demonstrates both outcomes. HFD uses local numerical structure but offers no analogous generalization condition or out-of-sample domain study.

reviewed_competitors.title: CAN-PINN: A Fast Physics-Informed Neural Network Based on Coupled-Automatic-Numerical Differentiation Method
reviewed_competitors.difference: CAN-PINN explicitly couples neighbor numerical differences with automatic derivatives and reports accuracy and speed on challenging flows. HFD cites it but does not compare, so HFD's narrow distinction is switching derivative schemes by region plus SDF-selected local steps.

reviewed_competitors.title: Gradient-enhanced physics-informed neural networks for forward and inverse PDE problems
reviewed_competitors.difference: gPINN adds derivatives of the PDE residual and adaptive refinement to improve accuracy with fewer points. It attacks the same sparse-sample problem through more derivative information rather than finite-difference replacement.

reviewed_competitors.title: Respecting causality is all you need for training physics-informed neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Causal weighting addresses failure from optimizing an entire time domain at once and tests difficult chaotic and turbulent systems. HFD's time-dependent examples are short and do not distinguish derivative error from causal training pathologies.

reviewed_competitors.title: Error estimates for physics informed neural networks approximating the Navier-Stokes equations
reviewed_competitors.difference: De Ryck, Jagtap, and Mishra relate total error to training error, network size, and quadrature points for Navier-Stokes PINNs. HFD reports sampled losses without a bridge from its discrete residual to solution error.

reviewed_competitors.title: A comprehensive study of non-adaptive and residual-based adaptive sampling for physics-informed neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wu et al. show across more than 6,000 simulations that grid, random, quasi-random, resampling, and residual-adaptive choices materially change PINN accuracy. This makes HFD's grid-versus-random comparison an identified confound, not a minor detail.

reviewed_competitors.title: RBF-MGN:Solving spatiotemporal PDEs with Physics-informed Graph Neural Network
reviewed_competitors.difference: The authors later replace axis-aligned SDF stencils with graph learning and radial-basis-function finite differences on unstructured irregular domains. That design directly addresses HFD's geometry and background-grid limitations but remains a different architecture and validation target.

reviewed_competitors.title: Can Physics-Informed Neural Networks beat the Finite Element Method?
reviewed_competitors.difference: A systematic matched study finds PINNs did not outperform FEM in solution time or accuracy on its PDE suite. HFD never compares against FEM or FDM under matched tolerance, so its efficiency rhetoric remains unsupported.

reviewed_competitors.title: Efficient Error Certification for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: The certification work shows finite test samples can miss catastrophic residual peaks and introduces continuous-domain upper bounds. HFD relies entirely on finite plots and point estimates, including its complex-geometry claims.

reviewed_competitors.title: An efficient hp-Variational PINNs framework for incompressible Navier-Stokes equations
reviewed_competitors.difference: FastVPINNs extends tensorized variational residuals to vector flows, inverse problems, and complex geometries while reporting training-time improvement. It offers a stronger modern efficiency protocol than HFD's iteration-only curves.

reviewed_competitors.title: Finite difference physics-informed neural networks enable improved solution accuracy of the Navier-Stokes equations
reviewed_competitors.difference: Roy et al. combine FD-PINNs with domain decomposition for high-Reynolds-number cavity flow and explicitly measure corner vortices against references. It extends the concept to harder flow structure but still needs resource-aware comparison.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Ill-Posed Foundations of Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Their Finite-Difference Variants
reviewed_competitors.difference: Langer proves nonuniqueness for finite-collocation AD- and FD-PINN minimizers while showing FD minimizers align with discrete solutions on the stencil under conditions. This supplies both a structural explanation and a limitation absent from HFD's empirical argument.

reviewed_competitors.title: Physics Informed Neural Network using Finite Difference Method
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lim, Dutta, and Rotaru revisit finite-difference PDE losses for Laplace and Burgers problems and report runtime as well as error. Their results suggest FD can match AD, a narrower conclusion than HFD's broad superiority claim.

reviewed_competitors.title: Optimize discrete loss with finite-difference physics constraint and time-stepping for PDE solving
reviewed_competitors.difference: FDTO combines finite-difference loss optimization with explicit time stepping and curvilinear body-fitted grids, reporting memory and error on flow benchmarks. It directly addresses long-time conditioning and resource metrics omitted by HFD.

reviewed_competitors.title: PINNs Failure Modes are Overfitting
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work reframes important PINN failures as finite-collocation overfitting, emphasizing evaluation away from residual points. HFD's sparse plots, ambiguous data splits, and no continuous certificate leave exactly that failure unresolved.

reviewed_competitors.title: Global Convergence of DGM and PINN Algorithms for Solving Nonlinear PDEs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sirignano, Spiliopoulos, and Cohen give convergence results for a class of semilinear nonlinear PDE residual objectives. HFD provides no conditions under which its finite-difference objective converges to the intended continuous PDE solution.

reviewed_competitors.title: Derivative Computation in PINNs: Automatic Differentiation, Finite Differences and Beyond
reviewed_competitors.difference: Mikulski and Uhl systematically calibrate FD step size, compare accuracy, speed, and GPU memory, and expose incorrect standard autograd for inter-sample architectures. They find calibrated FD matches AD on tested PDEs rather than universally beating it, providing the direct controlled study HFD lacks.

reviewed_competitors.title: A unified deep artificial neural network approach to partial differential equations in complex geometries
reviewed_competitors.difference: Berg and Nystrom already solve PDEs on genuinely complex geometries with a neural trial function and backpropagated derivatives. HFD's narrower contribution is a geometry-aware numerical derivative primitive rather than neural PDE solving on complex domains itself.

reviewed_competitors.title: Physics-informed Convolutional Neural Networks for Temperature Field Prediction of Heat Source Layout without Labeled Data
reviewed_competitors.difference: This earlier paper, sharing HFD's last author Wen Yao, trains a convolutional model with a finite-difference heat-equation loss and hard Dirichlet/Neumann padding. HFD moves to a coordinate MLP and SDF-adaptive local stencils, but should have distinguished this same-team numerical-residual lineage.

reviewed_competitors.title: A hybrid physics-informed neural network for nonlinear partial differential equation
reviewed_competitors.difference: This contemporary hybrid switches between automatic differentiation in smooth regions and WENO numerical differentiation near nonsmooth regions using a discontinuity indicator. HFD switches by geometry and boundary clearance instead, so its defensible novelty is the SDF criterion rather than spatial hybridization by itself.

reviewed_competitors.title: Physics-informed ConvNet: Learning Physical Field from a Shallow Neural Network
reviewed_competitors.difference: PICN publicly preceded HFD by weeks and combines a shallow field generator with pretrained convolutional finite-difference filters and interpolation loss for irregular geometries. It is not an SDF-driven coordinate MLP, but it prevents broad priority claims for FD-informed neural solving on irregular domains.

reviewed_competitors.title: Physics-informed PointNet: A deep learning solver for steady-state incompressible flows and thermal fields on multiple sets of irregular geometries
reviewed_competitors.difference: PIPN appeared five days before HFD and learns across multiple point-cloud geometries using automatic-differentiation residuals. It does not use local FD stencils, but it is a necessary baseline for HFD's broader claims about irregular-domain flexibility and geometry generalization.

reviewed_competitors.title: Accelerated Training of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) using Meshless Discretizations
reviewed_competitors.difference: DT-PINN replaces spatial AD with reusable sparse high-order RBF-FD matrices on irregular point clouds while retaining AD for time and reports matched runtime and precision effects. It supplies the high-order meshless accuracy, resource, and floating-point controls absent from HFD.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Only On Boundaries: a Physics-Informed Neural operator for Solving Parametric Partial Differential Equations in Complex Geometries
reviewed_competitors.difference: The boundary-integral neural operator reduces sampling from a volume to its boundary and supports parametric and unbounded domains. It avoids interior virtual-stencil placement entirely and tests a stronger form of geometry reuse than HFD's one-network-per-instance examples.

reviewed_competitors.title: Physics-informed neural networks for transformed geometries and manifolds
reviewed_competitors.difference: This approach uses a diffeomorphic reference-domain map and correctly transformed differential operators for varying geometries, manifolds, and shape optimization. It contrasts global coordinate consistency with HFD's purely local distance-to-boundary control.

reviewed_competitors.title: Finite Volume Physical Informed Neural Network (FV-PINN) with Reduced Derivative Order for Incompressible Flows
reviewed_competitors.difference: FV-PINN integrates over control volumes and uses Gauss-theorem boundary quadrature to lower derivative order while preserving local conservation. HFD's pointwise squared stencil residual has no corresponding conservation guarantee.

reviewed_competitors.title: Topological Insulators and C^*-Algebras: Theory and Numerical Practice
reviewed_competitors.difference: Hastings and Loring derive and implement matrix-based invariants for disordered topological insulators with mathematical structure and direct numerical evaluation. The reviewed paper uses their Bott index to generate labels and seeks amortized neural inference, trading exact per-instance computation for distribution-dependent approximation and an expensive offline label corpus.

reviewed_competitors.title: Machine Learning Topological Invariants with Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhang, Shen, and Zhai already train neural networks to infer topological invariants from Hamiltonian inputs and inspect learned representations. Their principal example is fixed-format one-dimensional winding numbers, whereas the reviewed work targets a two-dimensional disordered real-space Chern problem and adds a reusable size-reduction block.

reviewed_competitors.title: Real space mapping of topological invariants using artificial neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Carvalho and collaborators learn local topological domains from local density-matrix projections and combine the model with the Kernel Polynomial Method for non-translational systems with tens of thousands of atoms. That pipeline requires electronic-state information but produces spatially resolved topology; the reviewed model consumes Hamiltonian parameters directly and predicts one global invariant through learned coarse graining.

reviewed_competitors.title: Deep Learning Topological Invariants of Band Insulators
reviewed_competitors.difference: Sun and collaborators train deep networks to predict winding and Chern invariants from momentum-space Hamiltonians and show intermediate features resembling analytic invariant formulas. The reviewed paper moves to disordered real-space inputs and scale reuse, but provides weaker evidence that its intermediate learned Hamiltonians correspond to a physical formula.

reviewed_competitors.title: Chern numbers as half-signature of the spectral localizer
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work expresses even index pairings as half the signature of a finite spectral-localizer matrix and numerically studies a two-dimensional disordered topological insulator, retaining a direct invariant interpretation. It is an exact or mathematically controlled alternative family; the reviewed neural approximation may amortize faster but offers neither a per-instance certificate nor a direct invariant check of its reduced output.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scalable neural networks for the efficient learning of disordered quantum systems
reviewed_competitors.difference: Saraceni, Cantori, and Pilati evaluate convolutional architectures whose inputs naturally accept arbitrary sizes, quantify accuracy as size changes, and demonstrate small-to-large transfer for disordered ground-state energies. They do not predict topology, but they precede the reviewed paper's general theme of one neural architecture spanning disordered-system sizes and supply a relevant scalable-architecture baseline that is not compared empirically here.

reviewed_competitors.title: Calculations of Chern number: equivalence of real-space and twisted-boundary-condition formulae
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lin and collaborators derive noncommutative real-space and Bott formulas from twisted boundary conditions and numerically establish their equivalence for Chern and quantum-spin-Hall models. This later work strengthens exact interpretability rather than amortized speed; it highlights a route for validating whether the reviewed network's reduced Hamiltonians preserve the same invariant under independent formulas.

reviewed_competitors.title: Real-space formulation of the Chern invariant and topological phases in a disordered Chern insulator
reviewed_competitors.difference: Hattori and Nakata formulate an integer-quantized supercell Wilson-loop Chern number, show agreement with the Bott index for sufficiently large systems, and report a simpler, more efficient numerical computation on disordered Chern insulators. It offers a current non-ML efficiency direction with direct physical semantics, while the reviewed approach depends on learned distribution transfer and does not certify individual predictions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Can We Gain More from Orthogonality Regularizations in Training Deep CNNs?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bansal et al. regularize the learned convolutional weights toward several notions of orthogonality and report faster, more stable convergence. Orthogonal-SGDM instead projects each update direction to a polar factor while leaving the eventual weights unconstrained, trading representational freedom for a per-step matrix decomposition.

reviewed_competitors.title: Orthogonal Convolutional Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Orthogonal CNNs enforce orthogonality of the full doubly block-Toeplitz convolution operator, arguing that kernel-vector orthogonality is insufficient, and retain orthogonal weights during learning. The reviewed method orthogonalizes reshaped filter gradients instead; it is architecture-agnostic in principle but supplies no guarantee that either weights or convolution operators remain orthogonal.

reviewed_competitors.title: Gradient Centralization: A New Optimization Technique for Deep Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Gradient Centralization is another optimizer-agnostic gradient transformation, subtracting the per-vector mean and interpreting the result as projected descent. It is much cheaper than an SVD and improves several vision tasks, but it removes only the all-ones direction rather than equalizing all singular directions or explicitly separating component updates.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scalable Optimization in the Modular Norm
reviewed_competitors.difference: Modular-norm optimization derives architecture-aware natural norms and normalizes updates recursively so learning rates transfer across width and depth. It supplies a scaling framework missing from Orthogonal-SGDM; for matrix modules, spectral geometry helps motivate polar-style updates, but the objective is coherent whole-network scaling rather than pairwise filter diversification.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding Gradient Orthogonalization for Deep Learning via Non-Euclidean Trust-Region Optimization
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work interprets matrix gradient orthogonalization as spectral-norm trust-region descent, analyzes momentum variants, recovers Muon as a special case, and explicitly explains why Muon can outperform the reviewed Orthogonal-SGDM. It shifts the mechanism from heuristic feature diversification to non-Euclidean geometry and also highlights that orthogonalizing momentum, scaling, and weight decay matter.

reviewed_competitors.title: Preconditioning Benefits of Spectral Orthogonalization in Muon
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ma et al. prove condition-number-independent linear convergence for simplified Muon on matrix factorization and linear-transformer in-context learning, attributing gains to spectral preconditioning. This is narrower theoretically but stronger mechanistic evidence than the reviewed paper's activation-cosine correlations, and it studies the momentum-orthogonalization lineage used in modern language-model training.

reviewed_competitors.difference: It finds SPSA strong under noise and Nelder-Mead among methods most damaged by slight noise, conflicting with portable noisy Nelder-Mead guidance.

reviewed_competitors.title: Performance comparison of optimization methods on variational quantum algorithms
reviewed_competitors.difference: It studies sampling floors, telescoping shots, and extensive tuning on chemistry/material tasks and finds rankings problem- and system-dependent.

reviewed_competitors.title: Noisy Bayesian optimization for variational quantum eigensolvers
reviewed_competitors.difference: It targets noisy VQE at low iteration counts with Gaussian-process modeling, a family omitted from the target's standard optimizer sweep.

reviewed_competitors.title: Latency considerations for stochastic optimizers in variational quantum algorithms
reviewed_competitors.difference: It shows optimizer choice depends jointly on latency, shot time, and iterations; the target explicitly excludes scaling and shots.

reviewed_competitors.title: Surviving The Barren Plateau in Variational Quantum Circuits with Bayesian Learning Initialization
reviewed_competitors.difference: It combines Bayesian global localization with a fast local optimizer, treating initialization and optimizer composition as central rather than ranking isolated methods from random starts.

reviewed_competitors.title: Stochastic optimization algorithms for quantum applications
reviewed_competitors.difference: It compares first-, second-, and natural-gradient methods and introduces complex variants beyond the target's ordinary real-valued families.

reviewed_competitors.title: Beyond Barren Plateaus: Quantum Variational Algorithms Are Swamped With Traps
reviewed_competitors.difference: It proves useful minima can be superpolynomially rare even without a barren plateau, so optimizer wins on small successful runs do not resolve trainability.

reviewed_competitors.title: Benchmarking of Different Optimizers in the Variational Quantum Algorithms for Applications in Quantum Chemistry
reviewed_competitors.difference: Molecular Hamiltonians and device-derived noise yield ideal and noisy winners that differ from a general Adam/Nelder-Mead ordering.

reviewed_competitors.title: Resource frugal optimizer for quantum machine learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Refoqus samples datasets and measurement operators for orders-of-magnitude shot savings, directly addressing resource dimensions omitted by the target.

reviewed_competitors.title: Randomized Benchmarking of Local Zeroth-Order Optimizers for Variational Quantum Systems
reviewed_competitors.difference: It partially randomizes optimization tasks because conclusions from task-specific benchmarks need not transfer, directly challenging global rankings from the target suite.

reviewed_competitors.title: Random Natural Gradient
reviewed_competitors.difference: It cuts natural-gradient state-preparation cost and evaluates accuracy jointly with quantum resources, unlike final-loss-only ranking.

reviewed_competitors.title: Parallel variational quantum algorithms with gradient-informed restart to speed up optimisation in the presence of barren plateaus
reviewed_competitors.difference: It detects plateaus and restarts parallel particles instead of selecting one static optimizer, with gains tied to plateau prevalence.

reviewed_competitors.title: On Optimizing Hyperparameters for Quantum Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: It studies preprocessing, initialization, ansatz, entanglement, dataset, and optimizer jointly, showing optimizer identity cannot be isolated from the full configuration.

reviewed_competitors.title: Surrogate optimization of variational quantum circuits
reviewed_competitors.difference: It uses an approximate classical simulator for Hessian information and demonstrates a 40-qubit QPU case beyond the target's conventional simulated menu.

reviewed_competitors.title: Benchmarking Optimizers for Qumode State Preparation with Variational Quantum Algorithms
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Optimizer benchmark successor in a distinct VQA regime.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It partly supports Powell robustness and SPSA dimensional efficiency for qumode state preparation, while reinforcing that conclusions are regime-specific.

reviewed_competitors.title: Physics-Informed Bayesian Optimization of Variational Quantum Circuits
reviewed_competitors.difference: EMICoRe builds exact trigonometric structure into its Gaussian-process kernel, exploiting information absent from off-the-shelf optimizers.

reviewed_competitors.title: Benchmarking Variational Quantum Algorithms for Combinatorial Optimization in Practice
reviewed_competitors.difference: It fixes total resources and includes a same-start classical greedy baseline and instance-level correlations, dimensions absent from the target.

reviewed_competitors.title: Benchmarking a wide range of optimisers for solving the Fermi-Hubbard model using the variational quantum eigensolver
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest large resource-aware optimizer benchmark successor.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Thirty optimizers on 372 instances show tuning and finite-difference choices matter, and quantum-natural-gradient iteration gains vanish when total calls are counted.

reviewed_competitors.title: Interpolation-based coordinate descent method for parameterized quantum circuits
reviewed_competitors.difference: It unifies Rotosolve-like methods, derives noise-optimal interpolation nodes, and outperforms ordinary gradient or random-coordinate methods in its tested regime.

reviewed_competitors.title: Preconditioning Natural and Second Order Gradient Descent in Quantum Optimization: A Performance Benchmark
reviewed_competitors.difference: It benchmarks natural and second-order families and stabilizes noisy BFGS, exploring a major family outside the target's first-order recommendations.

reviewed_competitors.title: Regularizing quantum loss landscapes by noise injection
reviewed_competitors.difference: It deliberately smooths high-frequency landscape components and combines with quantum natural gradient rather than merely selecting an off-the-shelf optimizer.

reviewed_competitors.title: Statistical Benchmarking of Optimization Methods for Variational Quantum Eigensolver under Quantum Noise
reviewed_competitors.difference: Across several decoherence models it reports BFGS as accurate and evaluation-efficient and COBYLA as a low-cost option, differing sharply from a universal Adam/Nelder order.

reviewed_competitors.title: A framework to evaluate the performance of Variational Quantum Algorithms
reviewed_competitors.difference: It separates feasibility, quality, reproducibility, success probability, and computational resources; the target reports two aggregate loss summaries with minimal repetition.

reviewed_competitors.title: SPSA Hyperparameter Tuning for Variational Quantum Natural Language Inference
reviewed_competitors.difference: Even tuned SPSA remains 16-19 test-accuracy points behind parameter-shift AdamW and BuresQNG on its 60-parameter QNLI task, illustrating variance-driven context dependence.

reviewed_competitors.title: Fourier Features Let Networks Learn High Frequency Functions in Low Dimensional Domains
reviewed_competitors.difference: Tancik et al. analyze the infinite-width NTK and tune a stationary kernel's bandwidth to overcome ordinary MLP low-frequency bias. The focal paper instead studies finite shallow ridge spectra and asks why excessive bandwidth can harm sparse-region interpolation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Implicit Neural Representations with Periodic Activation Functions
reviewed_competitors.difference: SIREN supplies periodic activations, principled initialization, and broad signal/derivative tasks. The focal paper treats SIREN as one backbone and adds a local sensitivity penalty to counter high-bandwidth interpolation artifacts.

reviewed_competitors.title: Multiplicative Filter Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: MFNs express an exponential Fourier or Gabor basis through multiplicative filters and make spectral composition structurally explicit. They offer an architectural alternative to regularizing a conventional compositional coordinate MLP.

reviewed_competitors.title: Rethinking Positional Encoding
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zheng et al. explain positional encodings through stable rank and distance preservation rather than only Fourier content. That framework directly cautions that a bandwidth-only account can miss geometric conditioning.

reviewed_competitors.title: Beyond Periodicity: Towards a Unifying Framework for Activations in Coordinate-MLPs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Beyond Periodicity proposes nonperiodic coordinate activations and studies hidden-layer eigenvalue structure and initialization robustness. The focal paper reuses Gaussian activations but shifts from activation design to explicit interpolation regularization.

reviewed_competitors.title: BACON: Band-limited Coordinate Networks for Multiscale Scene Representation
reviewed_competitors.difference: BACON was submitted before the focal paper and constrains the analytic Fourier support of intermediate outputs, enabling predictable unsupervised-point behavior and multiscale reconstruction. It addresses interpolation through architecture-level band limits rather than a stochastic smoothness loss.

reviewed_competitors.title: MINER: Multiscale Implicit Neural Representations
reviewed_competitors.difference: MINER uses a Laplacian pyramid and patchwise MLPs so capacity grows only where residual signal energy demands it. This supplies spatial and scale locality that the focal paper's single global penalty lacks.

reviewed_competitors.title: Residual Multiplicative Filter Networks for Multiscale Reconstruction
reviewed_competitors.difference: Residual MFNs add skip connections and frequency-aware initialization for explicit coarse-to-fine optimization. They preserve earlier scales structurally rather than hoping random local smoothing selects a balanced spectrum.

reviewed_competitors.title: DINER: Disorder-Invariant Implicit Neural Representation
reviewed_competitors.difference: DINER learns a hash-table coordinate mapping to make signal values easier for the following INR and reports multiple inverse tasks. It attacks training spectral bias through input reordering rather than penalizing local feature derivatives.

reviewed_competitors.title: WIRE: Wavelet Implicit Neural Representations
reviewed_competitors.difference: WIRE uses complex Gabor wavelets localized jointly in space and frequency and evaluates accuracy, speed, and robustness across denoising, inpainting, super-resolution, tomography, and NeRF. That localization is better aligned with heterogeneous spectra than a global Fourier argument.

reviewed_competitors.title: Regularize implicit neural representation by itself
reviewed_competitors.difference: INRR learns a Dirichlet-energy regularizer that combines signal self-similarity with Laplacian smoothness and explicitly targets nonuniform sampling. It is a direct, more structured alternative to the focal paper's isotropic finite difference.

reviewed_competitors.title: FINER: Flexible spectral-bias tuning in Implicit NEural Representation by Variable-periodic Activation Functions
reviewed_competitors.difference: FINER uses variable-periodic activations and initialization bias ranges to select a broader task-relevant frequency set across image, SDF, and NeRF fitting. It improves spectral flexibility architecturally without the focal penalty.

reviewed_competitors.title: Improved Implicit Neural Representation with Fourier Reparameterized Training
reviewed_competitors.difference: Fourier reparameterized training composes MLP weights from fixed Fourier bases and gives a training-bias analysis across vanilla, encoded, and advanced-activation INRs. It intervenes in parameterization rather than adding output-agnostic smoothness.

reviewed_competitors.title: Towards the Spectral bias Alleviation by Normalizations in Coordinate Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Cai et al. connect spectral bias to the coordinate network NTK eigenvalue distribution and use batch, layer, and combined normalization across six application families. Their mechanism is trainability of frequencies, not explicit local smoothing.

reviewed_competitors.title: Inductive Gradient Adjustment For Spectral Bias In Implicit Neural Representations
reviewed_competitors.difference: Inductive gradient adjustment estimates an empirical-NTK transformation and deliberately changes frequency learning dynamics across INR architectures. It more directly tests an optimization mechanism than the focal paper's fixed-weight spectral intuition.

reviewed_competitors.title: Dynamical Implicit Neural Representations
reviewed_competitors.difference: DINR models feature evolution as a continuous-time dynamical system, analyzes Rademacher complexity and NTK behavior, and regularizes dynamics complexity. It offers a more explicit depth model than the focal paper's stationary-phase heuristic.

reviewed_competitors.title: Escaping Spectral Bias without Backpropagation: Fast Implicit Neural Representations with Extreme Learning Machines
reviewed_competitors.difference: ELM-INR fits overlapping local predictors in closed form, while BEAM refines regions according to spectral Barron complexity. It directly allocates capacity to heterogeneous local spectra and avoids backpropagation's spectral training bias.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Augenstein et al. differentiate through a Fourier neural operator and VAE for 3D nanophotonic design, validate champions with full-wave FDTD, and report training-data and optimization costs, but remain domain-specific and show substantial optimized-field error.

reviewed_competitors.title: Reference Neural Operators: Learning the Smooth Dependence of Solutions of PDEs on Geometric Deformations

reviewed_competitors.title: Accelerating PDE-Constrained Optimization by the Derivative of Neural Operators
reviewed_competitors.difference: Cheng et al. make surrogate derivative accuracy an explicit training target and hybridize neural operators with numerical solvers to prevent optimization derailment, directly addressing the paper's unmeasured-gradient and open-loop-surrogate weaknesses.

reviewed_competitors.title: NeuralFoil: An Airfoil Aerodynamics Analysis Tool Using Physics-Informed Machine Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: NeuralFoil covers an 18-dimensional shape space, broad angle, Reynolds, Mach, and transition ranges, embeds analytical limits, exposes smooth gradients and an uncertainty signal, and includes practical constraints; it sacrifices cross-domain aspiration for stronger airfoil coverage and robustness.

reviewed_competitors.title: Thin-Shell Object Manipulations With Differentiable Physics Simulations
reviewed_competitors.difference: ThinShellLab uses an analytically differentiable simulator, finds that neither gradients nor sampling alone handle contact-rich thin-shell tasks, combines them, calibrates parameters from force and tactile data, and demonstrates a real robot transfer, setting a stronger validation standard in a narrower domain.

reviewed_competitors.title: Thermodynamic curvature: pure fluids to black holes
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ruppeiner curvature is an invariant scalar of a thermodynamic information metric with links to fluctuation length; this work uses an asserted extrinsic shape operator of a conditional GMRF parameterization and interprets a driven trajectory.

reviewed_competitors.title: Thermodynamic Geometry, Phase Transitions, and the Widom Line

reviewed_competitors.title: Detecting Quantum and Classical Phase Transitions via Unsupervised Machine Learning of the Fisher Information Metric
reviewed_competitors.difference: ClassiFIM estimates the Fisher metric from limited samples and quantitatively benchmarks transition localization across many classical/quantum models; this paper analytically parameterizes one GMRF and does not test detection accuracy.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization in Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Jacot, Gabriel, and Hongler define the infinite-width tangent kernel and show that it stays constant during gradient descent in the NTK parameterization. Mori and Ueda use its fully connected ReLU recursion as the lazy comparator, but compare it with differently initialized finite networks whose width changes with depth.

reviewed_competitors.title: On Lazy Training in Differentiable Programming
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chizat, Oyallon, and Bach show that lazy behavior is induced by scaling and bound agreement between nonlinear and linearized optimization paths, while also finding degraded CNN performance in a lazy regime. Mori and Ueda infer non-laziness mainly from a learning-rate/NTK performance gap without measuring path distance or tangent-kernel evolution.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Fine-Grained Spectral Perspective on Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yang and Salman directly analyze how depth changes CK and NTK spectra for Boolean, spherical, and high-dimensional Gaussian inputs and connect those spectra to polynomial degree, optimization, and generalization. Mori and Ueda instead report a finite-network sparse-versus-shift-summed phenomenon that the FC NTK spectrum does not reproduce at the selected learning rates.

reviewed_competitors.title: Linearized two-layers neural networks in high dimension
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ghorbani et al. prove that rotationally invariant random-feature and neural-tangent methods learn polynomial degrees sequentially as width or sample size scales with powers of d. This supplies a quantitative spectral baseline for Mori and Ueda's isotropic Gaussian polynomials, but does not model target-dependent feature adaptation or their multi-layer finite-width tradeoff.

reviewed_competitors.title: When Do Neural Networks Outperform Kernel Methods?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ghorbani et al. characterize when isotropic covariates make RKHS methods suffer while nonlinear neural networks learn a low-dimensional target representation, and when matching structure in the covariates removes that gap. This more directly supports a sparsity/low-dimensional-structure interpretation of Mori and Ueda's local targets than a generic claim about depth.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Functions: When Is Deep Better Than Shallow
reviewed_competitors.difference: Mhaskar, Liao, and Poggio prove approximation and capacity advantages when a deep network graph matches a target's hierarchical compositional graph. This supplies a genuine structural reason for depth, but Mori and Ueda's isolated coordinate monomial is not given such a hierarchy and their shifted sum is parallel rather than recursively compositional.

reviewed_competitors.title: Locality defeats the curse of dimensionality in convolutional teacher-student scenarios
reviewed_competitors.difference: Favero, Cagnetta, and Wyart call a sum of shared low-dimensional patch functions a convolutional teacher, essentially the functional form that Mori and Ueda label k-global. They show that local or convolutional kernels can achieve learning-curve exponents controlled by patch size rather than ambient dimension. This reveals that the FC-NTK failure is architecture-specific and that Mori's terminology reverses a common convolutional notion of locality.

reviewed_competitors.title: Approximation and Learning with Deep Convolutional Models: a Kernel Perspective
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bietti characterizes multi-layer convolutional RKHSs as additive patch-interaction models and derives benefits from locality, pooling, and spatial regularity. It demonstrates that a kernel can encode both depth and locality when its architecture is aligned, whereas Mori and Ueda test only the rotationally symmetric fully connected NTK.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning with convolution and pooling operations in kernel methods
reviewed_competitors.difference: Misiakiewicz and Mei exactly characterize one-layer convolution, pooling, and downsampling RKHSs and quantify gains from patch locality and approximate translation invariance. If Mori and Ueda's cyclic index order is granted spatial meaning, their shift-summed target is particularly aligned with convolution plus global averaging; the negative kernel conclusion therefore applies to the fully connected NTK, not kernels generally.

reviewed_competitors.title: Local Signal Adaptivity: Provable Feature Learning in Neural Networks Beyond Kernels
reviewed_competitors.difference: Karp et al. prove that an SGD-trained CNN can find a sparse local signal amid high-variance noise while its corresponding fixed-feature NTK cannot, then test the mechanism on corrupted MNIST and CIFAR-10. Mori and Ueda give a cleaner depth sweep but neither align the architecture to locality nor measure the signal-selection mechanism.

reviewed_competitors.title: Tensor Programs IV: Feature Learning in Infinite-Width Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yang and Hu classify parameterizations into kernel and feature-learning infinite-width limits and give computable non-NTK limits. Their framework makes parameterization an explicit causal variable; Mori and Ueda equate their finite large-learning-rate regime with feature learning but do not specify a matched rich-limit parameterization.

reviewed_competitors.title: Identifying good directions to escape the NTK regime and efficiently learn low-degree plus sparse polynomials
reviewed_competitors.difference: Nichani, Bai, and Lee formalize the sparse/dense polynomial distinction that Mori and Ueda's local/global monomials approximate: the NTK is effective for dense low-degree structure but sample-inefficient for sparse higher-degree terms, while controlled movement into quadratic features can combine both. They provide end-to-end guarantees with an explicit regularizer rather than an observational depth trend.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Networks can Learn Representations with Gradient Descent
reviewed_competitors.difference: Damian, Lee, and Soltanolkotabi prove that gradient descent on a two-layer network can learn the few relevant directions of f*(x)=g(Ux), reducing sample complexity relative to kernels and enabling transfer when their expected-Hessian signal condition holds. That condition directly covers Mori and Ueda's quadratic local monomial but not their cubic monomial, whose expected Hessian vanishes, so it explains part rather than all of the reported phenomenon and does not require extra depth.

reviewed_competitors.title: The merged-staircase property: a necessary and nearly sufficient condition for SGD learning of sparse functions on two-layer neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Abbe, Boix-Adsera, and Misiakiewicz identify a hierarchical condition governing dimension-efficient mean-field SGD learning of low-coordinate Boolean functions and prove linear-feature methods cannot match it. A pure degree-k parity or monomial has no chain of lower-degree support terms and is not merged-staircase for k>=2, so this result says sparsity alone is insufficient; it neither places Mori's target in the fast shallow class nor proves depth solves it.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the non-universality of deep learning: quantifying the cost of symmetry
reviewed_competitors.difference: Abbe and Boix-Adsera prove that, for broad equivariant noisy-gradient methods on fully connected networks over the Boolean cube or sphere, depth two is as powerful as arbitrary depth for weak learning and extend sparse-function necessity beyond mean field. Their distribution, weak-learning objective, and symmetry hypotheses differ from Mori's finite-sample Gaussian regression, but the result directly limits any universal claim that support locality itself creates a need for depth.

reviewed_competitors.title: SGD learning on neural networks: leap complexity and saddle-to-saddle dynamics
reviewed_competitors.difference: Abbe, Boix-Adsera, and Misiakiewicz define leap complexity for low-support functions under isotropic Boolean or Gaussian inputs and analyze sequential support discovery by saddle-to-saddle SGD. Mori's pure degree-k local monomial is a leap-k target, associated with about d^max(k-1,1) online-SGD steps and d^max(k,2) total computation in their framework. Proved achievability is restricted to two-layer smooth networks with specialized layerwise, projected online SGD; it predicts no depth advantage and the full-support cyclic sum violates the low-latent-dimension premise.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural network learns low-dimensional polynomials with SGD near the information-theoretic limit
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lee, Oko, Suzuki, and Wu show that a two-layer network with minibatch reuse can learn arbitrary polynomial single-index Gaussian targets in nearly linear-in-d samples and time, bypassing correlational statistical-query barriers. Mori's coordinate product is multi-index, so the theorem does not cover it directly, but it shows that training protocol rather than architectural depth can remove high-degree polynomial barriers.

reviewed_competitors.title: SGD with Large Step Sizes Learns Sparse Features
reviewed_competitors.difference: Andriushchenko et al. connect large-step-size loss stabilization and SGD noise to increasingly sparse learned features, with explicit feature statistics, theory in simplified models, code, and deep-network experiments. This offers a competing mechanism for Mori and Ueda's large-rate advantage and shows which diagnostics their paper would need to support a sparse-feature explanation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Mean-Field Analysis for Learning Subspace-Sparse Polynomials with Gaussian Input
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chen and Ge study two-layer SGD on the same standard-Gaussian, low-dimensional polynomial class and derive a necessary and almost-sufficient learnability condition with exponential loss decay under the stronger condition. They replace Mori and Ueda's qualitative feature-learning conjecture with target- and activation-dependent mean-field criteria, while not studying depth.

reviewed_competitors.title: What Can Be Learnt With Wide Convolutional Neural Networks?
reviewed_competitors.difference: Cagnetta, Favero, and Wyart characterize the spectrum of infinitely wide deep convolutional kernels and prove adaptation to the spatial scale of targets whose relevant coordinates form adjacent subsets. This shows that depth and target locality can be visible inside a kernel regime when architecture and coordinate geometry agree; Mori's arbitrary-coordinate junta lacks that adjacency, and its FC kernel encodes no such bias.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: ICML 2023, PMLR 202; arXiv:2208.01003v5, 2023-05-31; later J. Stat. Mech. 2024

reviewed_competitors.title: Role of Locality and Weight Sharing in Image-Based Tasks: A Sample Complexity Separation between CNNs, LCNs, and FCNs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lahoti et al. construct a dynamic local-signal task and prove optimizer-aware sample-complexity separations among CNNs, locally connected networks, and FCNs, distinguishing locality from weight sharing. That crossed architectural comparison directly addresses a control absent from Mori and Ueda and shows why FCN-only results cannot establish a general depth-locality law.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Computational Advantage of Depth: Learning High-Dimensional Hierarchical Functions with Gradient Descent
reviewed_competitors.difference: Dandi et al. prove large sample and computational advantages for deep gradient-trained networks on explicitly hierarchical Gaussian single- and multi-index targets, with successive layers reducing effective dimension. This is a strong positive theory for depth under genuine latent composition; it does not imply that Mori and Ueda's isolated sparse monomial, which lacks a specified recursive hierarchy, receives the same benefit.

reviewed_competitors.title: Shallow Neural Networks Learn Low-Degree Spherical Polynomials with Feature Learning by Learnable Channel Attention
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yang proves that a finite-width two-layer model with specialized learnable channel attention attains minimax risk for low-degree spherical polynomial regression through feature learning. The architecture and distribution differ from standard ReLU SGD and it does not exploit coordinate sparsity, but it is a current counterexample to treating polynomial interaction order or an NTK gap as evidence that depth is intrinsically required.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Latent Road to Atoms: Backmapping Coarse-grained Protein Structures with Latent Diffusion

reviewed_competitors.difference: It replaces a one-step Gaussian VAE decoder with iterative latent diffusion to model complex protein conformations; CGVAE supplies a simpler exact map-consistent decoder and an explicit arbitrary-assignment construction.

reviewed_competitors.title: Revisiting Spatial Invariance with Low-Rank Local Connectivity
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Introduces spatially varying mixtures of basis filters that interpolate between convolution and local connectivity.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It is the direct translation-only precursor; this paper generalizes the relaxation idea to group and steerable convolution for rotation, scale, and dynamics.

reviewed_competitors.title: Residual Pathway Priors for Soft Equivariance Constraints
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Adds unrestricted residual pathways to equivariant models with a prior favoring the structured component and evaluates dynamics and RL.
reviewed_competitors.difference: RPP retains a separate unrestricted path; RGroup and RSteer relax the sharing constraints inside convolutional kernels and scale better to fields than equivariant-plus-MLP constructions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Partial Equivariances from Data
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Learns layer-wise partial or full group support for discrete and continuous group convolutions.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Partial G-CNNs restrict which transformations are enforced; the reviewed paper permits position- or group-element-specific deviations even when the full candidate group remains specified.

reviewed_competitors.title: Relaxing Equivariance Constraints with Non-stationary Continuous Filters
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Uses non-stationary continuous filters to interpolate efficiently among unrestricted linear maps, equivariant convolution, and invariance.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It supplies a more explicit adjustable interpolation and automatic gradient learning on vision tasks, contemporaneously generalizing the same non-stationarity principle.

reviewed_competitors.title: Regularizing Towards Soft Equivariance Under Mixed Symmetries
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Regularizes an unrestricted model toward several candidate symmetry types and automatically tunes their strengths under mixed approximate symmetries.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It addresses multiple simultaneous groups and hyperparameter learning directly, whereas the reviewed paper usually tunes one or two hand-chosen relaxations.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Layer-wise Equivariances Automatically using Gradients
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Learns type and amount of soft equivariance per layer using marginal likelihood estimated by differentiable Laplace approximations.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It explicitly balances data fit and model complexity to avoid the reviewed paper's manual bank-count and alpha selection.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Probabilistic Approach to Learning the Degree of Equivariance in Steerable CNNs
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Parameterizes transformation support as a regularized probability distribution over compact groups, shared or layer specific.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Its learned distribution gives an interpretable symmetry degree and arbitrary compact subgroups, rather than inferring degree indirectly from spatially varying kernel coefficients.

reviewed_competitors.title: Discovering Symmetry Breaking in Physical Systems with Relaxed Group Convolution
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Directly extends relaxed group convolution to identify interpretable phase, isotropy, homogeneity, and time-reversal symmetry-breaking factors in physical systems.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It adds theory and physical interpretability experiments that the reviewed prediction-focused paper explicitly lacked.

reviewed_competitors.title: Relaxed Equivariant Graph Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Introduces controlled symmetry-breaking weights in E(3)-equivariant graph networks for three-dimensional physical systems.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It realizes the reviewed paper's proposed graph extension and handles continuous 3D geometric structure rather than regular 2D grids.

reviewed_competitors.title: Approximately Equivariant Graph Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Formalizes graph-domain approximate symmetry through coarsening and derives a bias-variance tradeoff for choosing a symmetry group.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It gives statistical theory for selecting a group between exact automorphisms and full permutation symmetry, complementary to kernel-coefficient relaxation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Approximate Equivariance in Reinforcement Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Defines approximately symmetric MDPs, bounds the resulting Q-function deviation, and applies relaxed group layers to control and financial data.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It transports the architecture to sequential decision making and provides task-level value theory rather than only function-defect observations.

reviewed_competitors.title: Symmetry-Based Structured Matrices for Efficient Approximately Equivariant Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Uses group matrices and generalized displacement structure to build compact approximately equivariant networks for discrete groups.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It makes parameter and evaluation efficiency central and reports one-to-two-order parameter reductions, addressing costs not measured in the reviewed work.

reviewed_competitors.title: Symmetry Breaking and Equivariant Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Analyzes the inability of strictly equivariant functions to break stabilizer symmetries of individual samples and defines a different relaxed-equivariance construction.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It treats sample-level output symmetry breaking rather than imperfect dataset-level covariance, clarifying two distinct reasons exact equivariance can be too restrictive.

reviewed_competitors.title: A General Theory of Equivariant CNNs on Homogeneous Spaces
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Characterizes equivariant convolutional kernels on homogeneous spaces using representation theory.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It supplies the exact kernel-constraint endpoint from which RSteer departs; the reviewed work adds trainable violations without an equivalent expressivity theory.

reviewed_competitors.title: Scale-Equivariant Steerable Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Constructs steerable networks with exact scale equivariance and is used as the strict scale baseline in the paper.
reviewed_competitors.difference: RSteer relaxes its kernel-basis constraints to accommodate bounded, imperfect scale structure at the cost of losing exact guarantees.

reviewed_competitors.title: Generalizing Convolutional Neural Networks for Equivariance to Lie Groups on Arbitrary Continuous Data
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Builds LieConv, a general equivariant architecture for arbitrary Lie groups and continuous point data.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It broadens exact equivariance across groups and domains; the reviewed paper instead broadens the degree of constraint and targets large regular velocity grids.

reviewed_competitors.title: Optimal Transport Mapping via Input Convex Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Makkuva et al. parameterize Brenier potentials with input-convex networks and recover deterministic quadratic-cost maps with structural guarantees. NOT removes convex architectures and adds stochastic weak plans, gaining flexibility while losing the same direct optimal-map identification.

reviewed_competitors.title: Generative Modeling with Optimal Transport Maps
reviewed_competitors.difference: Rout et al. use essentially the deterministic semi-dual/maximin mechanism for strong quadratic and embedded costs and evaluate restoration and generation. NOT's main algorithmic extension is atomless noise plus weak conditional costs, enabling mass splitting but introducing fake-plan ambiguity.

reviewed_competitors.title: Score-based Generative Neural Networks for Large-Scale Optimal Transport
reviewed_competitors.difference: Daniels et al. learn an entropy-regularized Sinkhorn coupling and sample its conditionals with Langevin dynamics, with convergence analysis for potential training. NOT targets unregularized strong and weak costs and amortizes conditional sampling in one map, but offers weaker recovery guarantees.

reviewed_competitors.title: Do Neural Optimal Transport Solvers Work? A Continuous Wasserstein-2 Benchmark
reviewed_competitors.difference: Korotin et al. build continuous pairs with known quadratic OT maps and show downstream generative quality can disagree with OT accuracy. NOT cites this benchmark for its deterministic special case but does not extend its exact-map evaluation to stochastic weak plans.

reviewed_competitors.title: Kernel Neural Optimal Transport
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kernel NOT explicitly proves that the present paper's weak quadratic objective may learn fake, non-distribution-preserving plans, then introduces strictly convex kernel weak costs to remove that ambiguity. It is the closest correction to the evaluated stochastic method.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Optimal Transport with General Cost Functionals
reviewed_competitors.difference: Asadulaev et al. extend neural stochastic-plan learning to costs over whole plans, add class- and pair-guided functionals, and provide recovery error analysis. This directly pursues NOT's proposed task-specific-cost direction and supplies stronger quantitative theory.

reviewed_competitors.title: Entropic Neural Optimal Transport via Diffusion Processes
reviewed_competitors.difference: ENOT models the dynamic Schrödinger-bridge form of entropic OT with a diffusion and fast learned inference, explicitly trading regularization bias for a unique smoother coupling. NOT is a static amortized map for unregularized weak costs and avoids iterative Langevin sampling.

reviewed_competitors.title: Improving and Generalizing Flow-Based Generative Models with Minibatch Optimal Transport
reviewed_competitors.difference: OT-CFM trains a continuous normalizing flow with a stable regression objective and minibatch couplings; with a true plan it approximates dynamic OT and supports translation. It largely avoids NOT's adversarial saddle training, though minibatch OT is only an approximation to the population coupling.

reviewed_competitors.title: ENOT: Expectile Regularization for Fast and Accurate Training of Neural Optimal Transport
reviewed_competitors.difference: Expectile-regularized NOT replaces near-exact nonconvex c-transform optimization with a regularized potential loss and reports up to threefold lower error and tenfold faster runtime on W2 benchmarks. It targets exactly the inner-optimization instability left open here, primarily for strong costs.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Estimation Of Entropic Optimal Transport
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wang and Goldfeld parameterize the entropic semi-dual and prove nonasymptotic neural approximation and sample-error bounds for both cost and plan, including minimax-rate results on compact supports. NOT's universality result lacks this statistical bridge from samples to a recovered coupling.

reviewed_competitors.title: Overcoming Spurious Solutions in Semi-Dual Neural Optimal Transport: A Smoothing Approach for Learning the Optimal Transport Plan
reviewed_competitors.difference: OTP derives conditions under which semi-dual maximin maps are genuine, then smooths the source and learns a plan to handle cases without deterministic maps. It directly addresses spurious solutions for standard quadratic OT and reports stronger one-to-many translation results than earlier semi-dual solvers.

reviewed_competitors.title: Optimizing Neural Networks with Kronecker-factored Approximate Curvature
reviewed_competitors.relationship: The originating K-FAC optimizer and factorwise damping framework that the target dissects.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Martens and Grosse derive an efficiently invertible layerwise Kronecker approximation to natural-gradient curvature and show strong stochastic optimization. The target's distinctive contribution is to separate exact curvature, block structure, factorization, and damping, then argue that the empirically useful regime resembles an activation-only preconditioner.

reviewed_competitors.title: Natural Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A prior activation-whitening optimizer with a mathematically similar loss-independent input-side preconditioner.
reviewed_competitors.difference: PRONG implicitly whitens each layer's representation and amortizes reparameterization, scaling as far as ImageNet. FOOF offers a direct ridge layer-output derivation and a focused K-FAC causal audit, but the activation-geometry update family and amortization idea are not new in isolation.

reviewed_competitors.title: LocoProp: Enhancing BackProp via Local Loss Optimization
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A contemporaneous layerwise objective framework whose squared local loss yields closely related implicit parameter updates.
reviewed_competitors.difference: LocoProp varies local targets, losses, and regularizers to approach second-order performance using first-order solvers. FOOF has a simpler closed-form activation-covariance update, stronger direct wall-clock and K-FAC ablations, but less general local-objective machinery.

reviewed_competitors.title: Studying K-FAC Heuristics by Viewing Adam through a Second-Order Lens
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A direct post-target investigation of whether K-FAC's stabilizing heuristics rather than curvature explain its performance.
reviewed_competitors.difference: AdamQLR transfers K-FAC-style damping and learning-rate selection onto Adam directions and finds the standalone benefits variable across tasks and tuning schemes. It reinforces the target's call to isolate heuristics while tempering any universal conclusion that the same heuristic always dominates curvature.

reviewed_competitors.title: Structured Inverse-Free Natural Gradient Descent: Memory-Efficient & Numerically-Stable KFAC
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A modern K-FAC successor addressing dense-state memory and low-precision inversion instability while retaining a natural-gradient interpretation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: SINGD uses inverse-free structured Kronecker updates and reports modern half-precision advantages over AdamW. It competes directly with FOOF's efficiency motivation and shows that second-order/factored designs can be made stable, but does not answer the target's exact-Fisher-versus-damping mechanism question.

reviewed_competitors.title: SOAP: Improving and Stabilizing Shampoo using Adam
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A current matrix-preconditioned optimizer combining factored geometry with Adam-like coordinate adaptation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: SOAP interprets Shampoo as Adafactor in a slowly changing eigenbasis and reports large iteration and wall-clock gains over AdamW on 360M/660M language models. It substantially exceeds the target's architecture scale and evaluates language pretraining, while FOOF is simpler and uniquely probes K-FAC's damping mechanism.

reviewed_competitors.title: Modular Duality in Deep Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A later architecture-aware account of mapping weight gradients into semantically appropriate layerwise update geometries.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Modular dualization assigns operator norms to modules and derives GPU-friendly Newton-Schulz dual maps for embeddings, linear layers, and convolutions, providing a reparameterization/scaling theory behind Muon-like updates. FOOF instead uses empirical activation covariance and offers a sharper K-FAC ablation, but lacks a general module algebra or transformer-scale theory.

reviewed_competitors.title: Hyperparameter Transfer Enables Consistent Gains of Matrix-Preconditioned Optimizers Across Scales
reviewed_competitors.relationship: A current evaluation framework showing that apparent matrix-optimizer gains can disappear under incorrect scale transfer.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Qiu et al. study Shampoo, SOAP, and Muon from 190M to 1.4B parameters, derive width/depth and weight-decay transfer rules, and show about 1.4x speedups over AdamW only with correct scaling. This exposes the key missing validation for FOOF: its two-dimensional grid robustness on small vision models is not evidence that damping and learning rate transfer across model scale.

reviewed_competitors.title: SOAP, Muon, and Beyond: Pushing LLM Pretraining Scales
reviewed_competitors.relationship: The newest large-scale systems and stability benchmark for layerwise matrix-preconditioned optimizers.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Khona et al. use update-RMS matching, modify SOAP for large-batch stability, and distribute layerwise optimizer state across multi-billion-parameter models trained on trillions of tokens. It does not study FOOF, but it sets the empirical standard the target now lacks: numerical stability, communication, memory, and fair learning-rate transfer at realistic scale.

reviewed_competitors.relationship: Earlier Hamiltonian optimizer family with formal rates.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Maddison et al. design nonstandard kinetic energies with conformal dissipation and prove linear convergence on broad convex classes; BBI instead conserves energy and targets global exploration without comparable general rates.

reviewed_competitors.title: Frictionless Hamiltonian Descent and Coordinate Hamiltonian Descent for Strongly Convex Quadratic Problems and Beyond
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wang resets kinetic energy after exact Hamiltonian-flow segments and derives convergent coordinate schemes for quadratic systems; BBI retains one loss-dependent conserved energy and uses random bounces, emphasizing nonconvex basin exploration.
