reviewed_competitors.difference: Damian, Ma, and Lee glue local phases to show progress toward stationary points of a sharpness-regularized objective and include experiments on neural networks. The reviewed work instead derives a path-level singular limit for general covariance and proves global convergence only in its specialized quadratic model.

reviewed_competitors.title: Implicit Bias of SGD for Diagonal Linear Networks: a Provable Benefit of Stochasticity
reviewed_competitors.difference: Pesme et al. study stochastic gradient flow for diagonal linear networks, characterize its selected interpolator, and supply convergence bounds and experiments. The reviewed paper offers a more general manifold limit and an O(kappa log d) label-noise construction, but no finite-rate or empirical validation.

reviewed_competitors.title: SGD with Large Step Sizes Learns Sparse Features
reviewed_competitors.difference: Andriushchenko et al. analyze the loss-stabilization and hidden sparse-feature dynamics produced by practically large step sizes and validate them in neural networks. That regime lies outside the reviewed infinitesimal-step theorem and provides more direct empirical contact at the cost of less general asymptotic geometry.

reviewed_competitors.title: Simplicity Bias via Global Convergence of Sharpness Minimization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Gatmiry et al. connect global sharpness minimization under label-noise SGD to rank-one feature simplicity in a class of two-layer networks using local geodesic convexity. It advances beyond sparse linear recovery toward nonlinear feature structure, while remaining specialized rather than handling arbitrary covariance.

reviewed_competitors.title: Adam Reduces a Unique Form of Sharpness: Theoretical Insights Near the Minimizer Manifold
reviewed_competitors.difference: Li, Wen, and Lyu extend near-manifold SDE analysis to Adam and related adaptive methods, finding a diagonal-preconditioned sharpness measure rather than trace Hessian and deriving stronger sparsity behavior. This directly addresses an optimizer family left as future work by the reviewed paper.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Learning Dynamics of Two-layer Linear Networks with Label Noise SGD
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhang et al. analyze explicit two-phase escape and alignment dynamics for two-layer overparameterized linear networks, extend the mechanism to SAM, and release code with synthetic and real-world experiments. It offers a more operational account of the transition from lazy to rich regimes than the reviewed eta-to-zero endpoint theorem.

reviewed_competitors.title: Discovering Governing Equations from Data: Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamical Systems
reviewed_competitors.difference: SINDy selects a sparse linear combination from a user-specified nonlinear library and is computationally efficient and interpretable, but its standard form relies on pointwise derivative estimates and cannot express functions outside the library span. D-CODE replaces derivative labels with weak moments and free-form expression trees, trading the restricted linear solve for a much harder symbolic search.

reviewed_competitors.title: Weak SINDy: Galerkin-Based Data-Driven Model Selection
reviewed_competitors.difference: WSINDy already avoids pointwise derivatives through weak test functions, models the residual covariance, and reports accurate recovery under large white noise with error analysis. It remains linear in a prescribed candidate library; D-CODE's distinctive step is to use a related weak residual as black-box fitness for arbitrary symbolic trees. The D-CODE paper does not compare against or cite this direct predecessor.
reviewed_competitors.source_version: arXiv v3/SIAM Journal on Applied Dynamical Systems record checked 2026-08-23

reviewed_competitors.title: Data-Driven Discovery of Free-Form Governing Differential Equations
reviewed_competitors.difference: Atkinson et al. also use genetic programming to search arbitrary compositions of functions and differential operators after fitting differentiable surrogates, and add active experiments where candidate laws are deficient. D-CODE's weak residual is less dependent on accurate automatic derivatives of that surrogate and is explicitly tested under noise, but it is not the first free-form genetic search for governing differential equations.

reviewed_competitors.title: Parametric Estimation of Ordinary Differential Equations with Orthogonality Conditions
reviewed_competitors.difference: Brunel et al. smooth observed trajectories and move differentiation onto test functions to construct orthogonality conditions, establishing root-n consistency and asymptotic normality for parameters in a known ODE family. D-CODE applies a closely related derivative-swapping idea to score unknown symbolic expressions, but gives only fixed-candidate nested-limit consistency rather than a finite-sample estimator theory.

reviewed_competitors.title: Direct Estimation of Parameters in ODE Models Using WENDy: Weak-form Estimation of Nonlinear Dynamics
reviewed_competitors.difference: WENDy treats the errors-in-variables covariance induced by noisy trajectories, uses compactly supported bump test functions, and iteratively reweights a weak-form parameter fit. It requires a specified parametric model, whereas D-CODE searches the model form; in return WENDy offers a more explicit finite-data noise model than D-CODE's unweighted global sine moments.

reviewed_competitors.title: Physics-informed Spline Learning for Nonlinear Dynamics Discovery
reviewed_competitors.difference: Physics-informed Spline Learning jointly updates a spline trajectory and sparse governing-law coefficients so that denoising receives feedback from the candidate physics. D-CODE's separate Gaussian-process smoother is modular and supports free-form trees, but errors introduced before search cannot be corrected by the discovered equation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Ensemble-SINDy: Robust Sparse Model Discovery in the Low-Data, High-Noise Limit, with Active Learning and Control
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ensemble-SINDy bootstraps data and library terms to improve low-data, high-noise recovery, exposes term inclusion probabilities, and uses model disagreement for active learning. D-CODE can represent laws outside a fixed library but returns one genetic-programming winner without calibrated structural uncertainty or an experiment-selection loop.

reviewed_competitors.title: Simultaneous Identification and Denoising of Dynamical Systems
reviewed_competitors.difference: SIDDS estimates clean state samples and sparse model coefficients simultaneously under the discrete dynamics constraints, and analyzes attainable parameter accuracy through a Cramer-Rao bound. D-CODE avoids repeated numerical integration while exploring open-form trees, but its one-way smoothing pipeline and symbolic selection have no comparable uncertainty or efficiency bound.

reviewed_competitors.title: ODEFormer: Symbolic Regression of Dynamical Systems with Transformers
reviewed_competitors.difference: ODEFormer pretrains on large synthetic equation-and-trajectory corpora and infers multidimensional symbolic ODEs from a single trajectory in a few forward passes, reporting stronger speed and robustness on ODEBench. D-CODE requires per-dataset combinatorial search but is not tied to a synthetic pretraining distribution and has a transparent weak-residual objective.

reviewed_competitors.title: D-CIPHER: Discovery of Closed-form Partial Differential Equations
reviewed_competitors.difference: D-CIPHER extends the variational symbolic-search program to higher-order ODEs and PDEs, learns a derivative-bound component, and introduces the CoLLie optimizer. Its own analysis characterizes D-CODE as the special first-order explicit case, confirming both the value and the narrow differential-equation class of the original framework.

reviewed_competitors.title: Symmetry-Informed Governing Equation Discovery
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yang et al. derive equivariance constraints from time-independent symmetries and inject them into sparse regression and genetic programming, compressing the search space and improving noisy recovery in direct comparisons that include D-CODE and WSINDy. D-CODE is more assumption-light but pays for a much broader search and can return physically inconsistent expressions.

reviewed_competitors.title: DDOT: A Derivative-directed Dual-decoder Ordinary Differential Equation Transformer for Dynamic System Modeling
reviewed_competitors.difference: DDOT adds an auxiliary derivative-prediction decoder and evaluates vector-field divergence over a state-space grid, reporting gains over ODEFormer on reconstruction and generalization. Its off-trajectory metric directly addresses D-CODE's along-trajectory pseudometric limitation, but DDOT inherits dependence on synthetic pretraining and derivative supervision in its generated training distribution.

reviewed_competitors.title: Grammar-based Ordinary Differential Equation Discovery
reviewed_competitors.difference: GODE learns a variational latent space over grammar-valid expressions and refines candidates with covariance-matrix adaptation, extending discovery to implicit and higher-order ODE forms. D-CODE has a simpler auditable weak objective for explicit first-order systems, but its unconstrained genetic search is less expressive structurally and does not amortize knowledge across tasks.

reviewed_competitors.title: Hamiltonian Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational HNN baseline whose bundled inductive biases are deconstructed by the reviewed paper.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Greydanus et al. learn a scalar Hamiltonian and obtain dynamics through its symplectic gradient, emphasizing conservation and data efficiency. The reviewed work's distinctive move is to ask which parts of that package matter and to recover much of the performance without a Hamiltonian.

reviewed_competitors.title: Benchmarking Energy-Conserving Neural Networks for Learning Dynamics from Data
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporary benchmark that also questions broad conclusions drawn from small HNN demonstrations.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Zhong et al. compare energy-conserving models across multiple systems, data regimes, and noise levels and find performance depends on the training scenario. The reviewed paper offers a sharper bias-level hypothesis and SO alternative, but a narrower and more confounded causal benchmark.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Contact Dynamics Using Physically Structured Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporary structured approach targeted specifically at discontinuous contact mechanics.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Hochlehnert et al. explicitly model contact structure and evaluate contact-rich rigid-body dynamics. NODE+SO is simpler and broadly applicable, but treats MuJoCo contacts as a smooth acceleration field and provides no event- or constraint-level validation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Physics-Constrained Deep Active Learning for Spatiotemporal Modeling
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporary alternative that imposes physical constraints while actively choosing informative data.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The physics-constrained NODE framework integrates constraint residuals and data acquisition rather than discarding most physical structure. It addresses sample selection, whereas the reviewed work isolates architectural biases but assumes fixed trajectory data.

reviewed_competitors.title: Symplectic Spectrum Gaussian Processes: Learning Hamiltonians from Noisy and Sparse Data
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Post-publication exact-structure alternative for data-limited Hamiltonian learning.
reviewed_competitors.difference: This method places structured Gaussian-process priors on Hamiltonian vector fields and targets sparse noisy observations with uncertainty. It suggests that the value of symplectic structure may emerge most clearly outside the dense, clean neural-rollout regime used in the reviewed experiments.

reviewed_competitors.title: Unravelling the Performance of Physics-Informed Graph Neural Networks for Dynamical Systems
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Post-publication systematic analysis of which physics-informed GNN ingredients drive performance.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Like the reviewed paper, it resists treating physics priors as monolithic, but studies graph-based simulators, scale and training choices with a benchmark orientation. It is a close methodological precedent for factorial, matched-budget deconstruction.

reviewed_competitors.title: Separable Hamiltonian Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Post-publication HNN design that focuses on separability and efficient structure rather than abandoning Hamiltonian bias.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Separable HNNs exploit decomposable Hamiltonians for efficient symplectic integration and long-term prediction. They offer a counterpoint to NODE+SO: simplify the Hamiltonian representation and solver while preserving exact geometric structure when the domain warrants it.

reviewed_competitors.title: Noether's Razor: Learning Conserved Quantities
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Post-publication model-selection approach for learning rather than assuming useful conservation laws.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Noether's Razor uses a minimum-description-length principle to discover conserved quantities and symmetries supported by data. It directly addresses the reviewed paper's unresolved question of when a structural bias is warranted, rather than choosing HNN or SO globally in advance.

reviewed_competitors.title: Action-Conditioned Hamiltonian Generative Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Post-publication Hamiltonian world model evaluated both as a predictor and inside reinforcement learning.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Troch et al. condition structured latent Hamiltonian dynamics on actions and include downstream RL evaluation. This directly fills the reviewed paper's largest MuJoCo evidence gap: rollout accuracy alone is not evidence that a model improves planning or control return.

reviewed_competitors.title: DeepMechanics: A Systematic Benchmark of Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Dynamical Systems
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current broad benchmark of Hamiltonian, Lagrangian, and symplectic neural dynamics.
reviewed_competitors.difference: DeepMechanics evaluates multiple architecture families across six systems including bouncing, chaotic, and nonconservative regimes and reports that strong priors can struggle outside their assumptions. Its broader standardized evidence supports the reviewed paper's caution while exposing the need for hybrid/event-aware and OOD tests beyond its small suite.

reviewed_competitors.title: Algorithmic Regularization in Learning Deep Homogeneous Models: Layers are Automatically Balanced
reviewed_competitors.difference: Du, Hu, and Lee show that gradient flow preserves differences of squared layer norms and analyze diminishing or small positive steps for asymmetric factorization. The audited paper's distinctive proposal is that a much larger finite step actively shrinks pre-existing imbalance rather than merely preserving a balanced initialization, but its extension to deep homogeneous networks remains conjectural.

reviewed_competitors.title: The large learning rate phase of deep learning: the catapult mechanism
reviewed_competitors.difference: Lewkowycz et al. characterize a narrow stable large-learning-rate phase in solvable wide-network dynamics and validate catapult behavior and flatter convergence on practical networks. The audited paper supplies a different exact factorization recurrence, but offers no comparable neural-network evaluation or test-performance result.

reviewed_competitors.title: Noisy Gradient Descent Converges to Flat Minima for Nonconvex Matrix Factorization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Liu et al. use injected perturbations to select a noise-determined flat global optimum from arbitrary initialization. The audited work isolates deterministic finite-step effects instead, but its general-rank stability proof is incomplete and its convergence result is far narrower.

reviewed_competitors.title: Global Convergence of Gradient Descent for Asymmetric Low-Rank Matrix Factorization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ye and Du prove polynomial-rate global convergence from random initialization for asymmetric low-rank factorization without a balancing regularizer. Their step is in a conventional controlled regime and does not establish large-step selection, while the audited paper's arbitrary-A theorem assumes convergence and therefore does not supersede this guarantee.

reviewed_competitors.title: Implicit Bias of the Step Size in Linear Diagonal Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Nacson et al. use dynamic stability to show that a large stable step can move diagonal linear regression from kernel-like to sparsity-inducing rich behavior and prove a sparse-regression generalization consequence. It makes the audited paper's missing bridge from parameter flatness to generalization especially salient.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding Gradient Descent on the Edge of Stability in Deep Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: Arora, Li, and Panigrahi derive an implicit flow along a minimizer manifold that reduces top Hessian curvature in stylized normalized-GD and transformed-loss settings. Their framework directly analyzes motion along non-isolated minima, the step that the audited paper assumes rather than proves in its rank-one alignment argument.

reviewed_competitors.title: Self-Stabilization: The Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent at the Edge of Stability
reviewed_competitors.difference: Damian, Nichani, and Lee use a cubic local expansion to explain how an unstable top-Hessian direction lowers curvature and makes GD track sharpness-constrained projected dynamics, with explicit predictions checked on standard models. This provides a more general local mechanism than factor norm balancing, though under its own regularity and scale-separation assumptions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Special Properties of Gradient Descent with Large Learning Rates
reviewed_competitors.difference: Mohtashami, Jaggi, and Stich prove on constructed nonconvex classes that large-step full-batch GD can escape local minima that small-step GD does not, then separate this effect from stochastic noise in neural-network experiments. It broadens the discrete-time benefit beyond homogeneous balance and supplies practical validation absent here.

reviewed_competitors.title: Good regularity creates large learning rate implicit biases: edge of stability, balancing, and catapult
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wang et al. place balancing, catapult, and edge-of-stability behavior in one regularity-based family of non-globally-smooth nonconvex objectives and add a non-asymptotic convergence-rate claim plus neural-network experiments. It is the natural successor to the audited paper, while still acknowledging theory for only specific functions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Dynamics of Deep Linear Networks Beyond the Edge of Stability
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ghosh et al. analyze deep linear matrix factorization beyond the edge of stability, including period doubling, low-dimensional oscillation subspaces, and monotone decay of the inter-layer balancing gap at a two-period orbit. It directly extends the phenomenon from two factors converging to a point toward deeper networks and persistent oscillatory regimes that the audited proof does not cover.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Minimalist Example of Edge-of-Stability and Progressive Sharpening
reviewed_competitors.difference: Liu et al. prove progressive sharpening, self-stabilization, and non-asymptotic behavior along the entire GD trajectory for a two-layer width-one network with a two-dimensional input. It supplies the kind of rigorous entry and recurrence control missing from the audited scalar and rank-one phase arguments, while remaining a deliberately low-dimensional model.

reviewed_competitors.title: Convergence Rates for Gradient Descent on the Edge of Stability in Overparametrised Least Squares
reviewed_competitors.difference: MacDonald et al. decompose dynamics tangent and normal to a global-minimizer manifold and prove rates in subcritical, critical, and supercritical regimes, including convergence toward a period-two orbit. This directly addresses the audited paper's missing control of tangential motion, finite entry, and non-fixed limit sets in an overparameterized least-squares setting.

reviewed_competitors.title: Generalization at the Edge of Stability
reviewed_competitors.difference: Tuci et al. model stochastic optimizers as random dynamical systems, define a sharpness dimension using the full Hessian spectrum, and prove a corresponding generalization bound with MLP and Transformer experiments. It provides a direct, spectrum-wide bridge to generalization that the audited paper motivates but neither proves nor measures.

reviewed_competitors.title: SGD at the Edge of Stability: Stochastic Stabilization with Large Learning Rates
reviewed_competitors.difference: Emmanouilidis et al. prove repeated stochastic self-stabilization and best-iterate convergence for multiclass cross-entropy in linear classifiers and two-layer networks. It advances the SGD and realistic-loss directions absent from the audited deterministic matrix-factorization theory and explicitly controls returns from unstable to stable regimes.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Spectral Bias of Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Rahaman and collaborators establish the Fourier low-frequency bias, manifold-complexity effects, and parameter-perturbation diagnostic that the present paper directly adopts. The Pi-Net paper's distinct contribution is to propose multiplicative polynomial interactions as an architectural reduction of that bias and to attempt an NTK eigendecay explanation; its perturbation evidence is less normalized than the inherited question requires.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Inductive Bias of Neural Tangent Kernels
reviewed_competitors.difference: Bietti and Mairal develop the NTK RKHS, spherical-harmonic eigenvalue, smoothness, and approximation framework used by the present analysis. The Pi-Net paper specializes the question to a product kernel induced by multiplicative features, but its claimed product-kernel decay advantage fails under direct audit of the coefficient asymptotics.

reviewed_competitors.title: Frequency Bias in Neural Networks for Input of Non-Uniform Density
reviewed_competitors.difference: Basri and collaborators show that NTK frequency-learning dynamics depend on input density and analyze both shallow and deep fully connected networks. The present theorem assumes uniform sphere inputs and changes architecture through Hadamard products; it does not test whether the claimed advantage survives nonuniform sampling, so Basri's result limits the scope of its distribution-independent rhetoric.

reviewed_competitors.title: Fourier Features Let Networks Learn High Frequency Functions in Low Dimensional Domains
reviewed_competitors.difference: Tancik and collaborators provide a simple input mapping that converts the effective NTK into a stationary kernel with tunable bandwidth and demonstrate high-frequency learning in low-dimensional graphics tasks with public code. Pi-Nets instead learn through multiplicative hidden interactions and do not expose an equally direct frequency knob; their potential benefit is architectural expressivity, while Fourier features offer a more reproducible and controllable bias intervention.

reviewed_competitors.title: Deep Polynomial Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chrysos and collaborators introduce the Pi-Net polynomial parameterizations, tensor decompositions, and public polynomial_nets repository. The present paper does not introduce the architecture; its intended novelty is a spectral-bias analysis and supporting experiments. The earlier repository remains useful for Pi-Net tasks but does not contain the spectral experiments audited here.

reviewed_competitors.title: Extrapolation and Spectral Bias of Neural Nets with Hadamard Product: a Polynomial Net Study
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wu and collaborators subsequently analyze finite-width NTKs and kernel-regression equivalence for polynomial networks, give spectral and extrapolation separations, and extend experiments across broader Hadamard-product networks. It is the closest current primary competitor and raises the standard beyond this paper's shallow limiting kernel and rough width sketch. Its separate theorems must be evaluated on their own and do not repair Theorem 2 here.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding the dynamics of the frequency bias in neural networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Molina and collaborators derive a PDE for frequency-error dynamics in a two-layer NTK regime and show that initialization and Fourier-feature distributions can eliminate or control the bias, with numerical comparison to the PDE. This provides a later, explicitly controllable theoretical mechanism. The Pi-Net paper instead changes architecture and qualitatively links deep experiments to a theorem whose decay proof is invalid.

reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct predecessor and principal baseline for additive physical-plus-neural dynamics.
reviewed_competitors.difference: APHYNITY minimizes the augmentation norm subject to matching trajectories and supplies the same decomposition template. The reviewed paper adds a separate physical-mismatch constraint, proxy supervision, partial-observation recognition, and alternating penalties, but inherits the predecessor's component-overlap identifiability risk.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Dynamical Systems: Balancing Structure and Flexibility in Physical Prediction
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Prior gray-box system-identification method with trajectory-conditioned parameter inference and residual dynamics.
reviewed_competitors.difference: NDS explicitly handles dynamics varying across rollouts and tests real fusion-reactor data and control. The reviewed method instead focuses on constraint geometry and component penalties, with stronger latent-component reporting but fixed parameters and no downstream control test.

reviewed_competitors.title: Universal Differential Equations for Scientific Machine Learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational general framework and software competitor for embedding universal approximators in scientific differential equations.
reviewed_competitors.difference: UDEs cover ODEs, SDEs, delays, constraints, stiff solvers, sparse discovery, and scalable sensitivity tooling. The reviewed work offers a more specific alternating identifiability heuristic and partial-ocean case study but no comparable reusable implementation or solver breadth.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Partially Known Stochastic Dynamics with Empirical PAC Bayes
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporaneous probabilistic alternative for partially known dynamics.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Haußmann et al. combine partial drift knowledge with Bayesian neural SDEs and optimize a PAC-Bayesian generalization objective, explicitly representing epistemic uncertainty and stochasticity. The reviewed paper instead targets deterministic component identification and proxy physics without uncertainty calibration.

reviewed_competitors.title: Integrating Expert ODEs into Neural ODEs: Pharmacology and Disease Progression
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporaneous latent hybrid ODE for partially observed real-world systems.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The latent hybridisation model links expert-designed pharmacology states, learned latent dynamics, and clinical observations and reports real ICU data with released code. The reviewed method more directly penalizes physical and residual components and evaluates hidden fields, but only on simulated or simulator-derived data and without a durable implementation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Recognition Models to Learn Dynamics from Partial Observations with Neural ODEs
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct successor-era method for physics-structured neural ODE identification from partial observations.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Buisson-Fenet et al. derive recognition models from nonlinear observer ideas and evaluate numerical systems plus a robotic-exoskeleton experiment. The reviewed paper uses a task-specific U-Net recognizer and component penalties; it does not provide the observer-based observability analysis or physical experiment.

reviewed_competitors.title: Hybrid^2 Neural ODE Causal Modeling and an Application to Glycemic Response
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later hybrid neural ODE addressing loss of mechanistic causal validity.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Hybrid^2 adds intervention-ranking knowledge through a causal loss and evaluates post-exercise glucose dynamics, explicitly showing prediction alone can sacrifice mechanistic grounding. The reviewed component norms are cheaper and more general-purpose but do not validate counterfactual or causal correctness.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Identifiability of Hybrid Deep Generative Models: Meta-Learning as a Solution
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later direct identifiability challenge to flexible physics-plus-neural generative models.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ye et al. theoretically and empirically demonstrate unidentifiability with unconditional priors and use cross-task meta-learning for identifiable formulations. Although their model class is broader than additive ODEs, their result reinforces that component penalties and one-environment trajectory fit are not a general identifiability proof.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Governing Equations of Unobserved States in Dynamical Systems
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Later direct competitor for equation recovery from partially observed hybrid neural ODEs.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Grigorian et al. train neural missing-state equations and then apply ensemble symbolic regression to recover explicit governing equations under noise. The reviewed method directly interprets a chosen physical component and handles images, but retains an opaque residual and does not test noisy observations or symbolic recovery.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Osaka et al. evaluate fine-tuned hybrid models under multicopter concept shifts and quantify target-domain sample efficiency even with unidentified physical parameters. The reviewed work gives richer component constraints but evaluates only in-distribution splits and therefore does not establish the generalization advantage often claimed for hybridization.

reviewed_competitors.difference: Zou and Tian impose domain-informed graph restrictions and data-driven sparsification to improve robustness and remove unnecessary mechanistic states and interactions. reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Missing Physics from Legacy Simulators with Alternating Neural Integrators

reviewed_competitors.difference: Alternating Neural Integrators wrap callable or frozen prior step maps through operator-splitting compositions rather than learning the reviewed paper's additive vector-field decomposition. They add assumption-qualified analysis, ten ODE/PDE benchmarks, two measured-data studies, long-horizon and matched additive controls, symbolic distillation, public code, and Zenodo data; the reviewed method instead emphasizes two-sided component penalties and partial-state ocean recognition but has no executable artifact.

reviewed_competitors.title: Data-driven discovery of partial differential equations
reviewed_competitors.difference: PDE-FIND directly estimates derivatives, constructs a candidate library, and selects sparse terms with STRidge and Pareto analysis. The target paper retains that discovery engine but inserts learned high-resolution reconstruction before it and coefficient recurrent fine-tuning after it, trading more priors and computation for noise tolerance.

reviewed_competitors.title: PDE-Net: Learning PDEs from Data
reviewed_competitors.difference: PDE-Net jointly learns constrained convolutional differential operators and nonlinear responses for prediction and discovery. PeRCNN hard-encodes selected operators and uses multiplicative features before a separate sparse regression stage; the paper's comparator is an adapted delta-t block inside its own recurrent scaffold rather than a direct PDE-Net reproduction.

reviewed_competitors.title: Physics-informed learning of governing equations from scarce data
reviewed_competitors.difference: PiDL combines a continuous neural field, automatic differentiation, physics residuals, and sparse regression and includes experimental as well as numerical studies. The target paper replaces the continuous black-box field with a hard-encoded discrete recurrent surrogate, making known grid physics explicit but restricting geometry and time stepping.

reviewed_competitors.title: Weak SINDy: Galerkin-Based Data-Driven Model Selection
reviewed_competitors.difference: WSINDy avoids pointwise noisy derivatives by integrating against test functions and supplies favorable coefficient-error scaling under white noise. The target paper instead learns a dense surrogate before standard differentiation; it can exploit hard physics but is computationally heavier and introduces reconstruction bias.

reviewed_competitors.title: PDE-READ: Human-readable Partial Differential Equation Discovery using Deep Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: PDE-READ uses rational networks to learn the response and hidden PDE, followed by parameter-free sparse extraction, and tests six equations with open-source software. PeRCNN uses a stronger fixed-grid physics encoding and conventional STRidge with manual Pareto tuning, but evaluates fewer systems and requires more prior structure.

reviewed_competitors.title: Encoding physics to learn reaction-diffusion processes
reviewed_competitors.difference: This earlier PeRCNN work establishes the product block, hard finite-difference and boundary encoding, reconstruction, generalization, and interpretability used by the target. The ICLR paper's incremental contribution is the explicit three-stage coupling to STRidge and coefficient fine-tuning, not a new recurrent architecture.

reviewed_competitors.title: Physics-Guided Discovery of Highly Nonlinear Parametric Partial Differential Equations
reviewed_competitors.difference: This method incorporates observational constraints and basic physical laws to discover PDEs with highly nonlinear spatially varying coefficients, including three-dimensional cases, and provides an error-reduction analysis. The target focuses on constant-coefficient polynomial 2D systems and uses physics mainly to reconstruct a clean grid before sparse selection.

reviewed_competitors.title: Automating the Discovery of Partial Differential Equations in Dynamical Systems
reviewed_competitors.difference: ARGOS-RAL automates differentiation, library construction, and recurrent adaptive-lasso selection and tests noise, sample size, nonuniform sampling, and pure-noise rejection. The target gains robustness through a physics-encoded neural reconstructor but leaves library design and Pareto support selection substantially manual.

reviewed_competitors.title: PhysPDE: Rethinking PDE Discovery and a Physical Hypothesis Selection Benchmark
reviewed_competitors.difference: PhysPDE reframes discovery as selecting and fitting interpretable physical hypotheses through nonlinear mixed-integer optimization and evaluates fluid-mechanics and laser-fusion tasks. The target searches a generic polynomial-derivative library on three canonical simulations, offering cleaner coefficients but weaker physical-hypothesis and benchmark coverage.

reviewed_competitors.title: Unrolled-SINDy: A Stable Explicit Method for Non linear PDE Discovery from Sparsely Sampled Data
reviewed_competitors.difference: Unrolled-SINDy explicitly decouples numerical integration step size from the observation interval and works with both closed-form and gradient-based fitting, targeting sparse temporal sampling without requiring dense learned super-resolution. PeRCNN reconstructs a dense grid first and can inject more spatial physics, but does not analyze sampling-step bias.

reviewed_competitors.title: Hamiltonian Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Foundational learned-Hamiltonian baseline used by the paper.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Greydanus et al. regress Hamiltonian derivatives and demonstrate energy-aware extrapolation but do not allocate integration work or training weight to rare intervals. SANN adds next-state integration, interval scoring, and reweighting, though its comparison does not equalize those interventions.

reviewed_competitors.title: Symplectic Recurrent Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Closest structure-preserving next-state baseline used in the paper.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chen et al. train through a symplectic integrator for separable Hamiltonians. SANN retains that general machinery but adds SAI-conditioned partitions and resampling; a decisive comparison would give SRNN the same compute and weighted intervals.

reviewed_competitors.title: Symplectic ODE-Net: Learning Hamiltonian Dynamics with Control
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Contemporaneous Hamiltonian architecture with explicit physical parameterizations and control inputs.
reviewed_competitors.difference: SymODEN handles controlled systems, embedded angle coordinates, and interpretable mass and potential components. SANN instead targets rare locally difficult intervals, but does not compare against SymODEN's stronger parameter constraints or controlled/partial-coordinate scope.

reviewed_competitors.title: Simplifying Hamiltonian and Lagrangian Neural Networks via Explicit Constraints
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Pre-publication alternative that enforces known coordinate and physical constraints in HNNs and LNNs.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Finzi et al. simplify learning through explicit constraints and evaluate chaotic N-pendulum systems. SANN focuses on sample/integration allocation, while leaving its kinetic matrix weakly constrained and not separating curriculum gains from physics-prior gains.

reviewed_competitors.title: Sparse Symplectically Integrated Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Pre-publication structure-preserving Hamiltonian learner with higher-order symplectic integration and sparse interpretability.
reviewed_competitors.difference: SSINN explicitly couples sparse Hamiltonian parameterization with a fourth-order symplectic integrator and includes noise-oriented experiments. SANN supplies rare-event reweighting but is less robust to noise and does not compare integrator order at equal work.

reviewed_competitors.title: SympNets: Intrinsic Structure-Preserving Symplectic Networks for Identifying Hamiltonian Systems
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Pre-publication exact-symplectic flow-map alternative for separable and nonseparable systems.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Jin et al. build maps that are symplectic by construction and test irregular data and three-body dynamics. SANN learns a Hamiltonian vector field with curriculum-weighted numerical integration, but omits this direct baseline and irregular-sampling comparison.

reviewed_competitors.title: Data-driven Prediction of General Hamiltonian Dynamics via Learning Exactly-Symplectic Maps
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Pre-publication exact-symplectic map learner with a long-time error analysis.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Chen and Tao's generating-function networks learn general Hamiltonian maps and derive linear long-time error under stated conditions. SANN addresses locally difficult samples but provides no comparable structural rollout guarantee or direct exact-map control.

reviewed_competitors.title: Stiff Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Direct pre-publication work on training neural differential equations for genuinely multiscale stiff dynamics.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kim et al. analyze stiff NODE optimization and use scaling to stabilize gradients on systems with separated time scales. SANN instead uses data-local ranking and sampling, which can target intermittent events but is not validated against solver-defined stiffness or the scaling baseline.

reviewed_competitors.title: Fundamental Challenges in Deep Learning for Stiff Contact Dynamics
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Pre-publication empirical audit isolating stiffness as a cause of learning and generalization failure in contact dynamics.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Parmar et al. vary compliant-contact stiffness and show degradation in training, data efficiency, and generalization. SANN proposes a mitigation for selected Hamiltonian examples but never sweeps a physical stiffness parameter or demonstrates that its score tracks the isolated cause.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Hamiltonian Systems with Mono-Implicit Runge-Kutta Methods
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Post-publication inverse-integrator approach for learning Hamiltonian vector fields from trajectory pairs.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Noren et al. use mono-implicit Runge-Kutta structure to obtain higher-order inverse learning with small datasets. This attacks discretization bias directly, whereas SANN allocates different counts of second-order substeps based on a heuristic label.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Dynamical Systems from Noisy Data with Inverse-Explicit Integrators
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Post-publication numerical-integration alternative explicitly designed for noisy inverse dynamics learning.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Noren et al. derive inverse-explicit and mean inverse integrators that reduce noise sensitivity, including on Hamiltonian systems. SANN's forward-difference score and endpoint target both degrade under noise, making this a direct remedy for its strongest documented failure.

reviewed_competitors.title: Training Stiff Neural Ordinary Differential Equations with Implicit Single-Step Methods
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Post-publication direct stiff-NODE method based on implicit single-step integration.
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work uses implicit stability to train stiff NODEs rather than inferring stiff intervals from relative speed. It offers the missing method-class comparison for deciding whether SANN's curriculum is preferable to a solver designed for stiffness.

reviewed_competitors.title: Training Stiff Neural Ordinary Differential Equations with Explicit Exponential Integration Methods
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Post-publication direct stiff-NODE approach using exponential integration.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The exponential method treats the stiff linear component analytically and avoids relying solely on tiny explicit steps. SANN keeps Leapfrog and spends more substeps on ranked examples, so the two expose a useful solver-versus-curriculum trade-off.

reviewed_competitors.title: Structure-Preserving Neural Ordinary Differential Equations for Stiff Systems
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Post-publication stiff-system learner combining exponential integration with structural stability control.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The method separates a stiff linear operator from a Lipschitz-controlled nonlinear component and gives stability analysis near fixed points. SANN offers a simpler data heuristic but lacks a method-level stability guarantee and can misidentify fast Hamiltonian modes.

reviewed_competitors.title: H-FEX: A Symbolic Learning Method for Hamiltonian Systems
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current symbolic-Hamiltonian alternative emphasizing interpretable recovery and stiff examples.
reviewed_competitors.difference: H-FEX searches symbolic Hamiltonians and can reveal governing expressions instead of only fitting a neural potential. SANN may be cheaper when the form is unknown, but its unrestricted kinetic matrix and rational network do not supply comparable identifiability or interpretability.

reviewed_competitors.title: Symplectic Neural Networks for Learning Generalized Hamiltonians
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Current generalized-Hamiltonian learner using implicit symplectic structure and noise-aware experiments.
reviewed_competitors.difference: The method expands beyond separable canonical Hamiltonians, develops efficient adjoint training and backward-error analysis, and evaluates noisy trajectories. SANN's curriculum is simpler but substantially narrower and fails its own noise test.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Hamiltonian neural Koopman operator and simultaneously sustaining and discovering conservation law
reviewed_competitors.difference: HNKO learns Hamiltonian Koopman structure, conservation laws, and high-dimensional dynamics under noisy perturbations, broadening the benchmark beyond SANN's small canonical systems while using a different operator-learning bias.

reviewed_competitors.title: Stability-Informed Initialization of Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
reviewed_competitors.difference: Westny et al. analyze solver stability regions and their implicit regularization of learned dynamics, then initialize models accordingly; this is a more direct numerical-stability treatment than using state speed as stiffness.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations for Model Order Reduction of Stiff Systems
reviewed_competitors.difference: Caldana and Hesthaven learn a state-to-time reparameterization induced by an implicit solver so the transformed reduced dynamics are nonstiff and cheaply integrated, replacing event oversampling with an explicit learned change of clock.

reviewed_competitors.title: Machine Learning Hamiltonian Dynamical Systems with Sparse and Noisy Data
reviewed_competitors.difference: Adaptable SRNNs train from as few as two irregular, noisy time points per trajectory and then support symbolic recovery, directly addressing SANN's failure under noise and its dependence on dense adjacent finite differences.

reviewed_competitors.title: Analyzing Inverse Problems with Invertible Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Ardizzone and colleagues already learn a joint invertible map from parameters to measurements plus latent variables and sample ambiguous inverse solutions by fixing a measurement and varying the latent. BundleNet's clearest addition is the explicit local-chart and fiber-bundle framing, neighborhood conditioning, and topology-aware latent study, so its claim to introduce the underlying many-to-one sampling task should be read narrowly.

reviewed_competitors.title: SurVAE Flows: Surjections to Bridge the Gap between VAEs and Flows
reviewed_competitors.difference: SurVAE Flows make many-to-one and stochastic inverse transformations explicit composable layers with likelihood accounting. BundleNet instead augments a supervised output with a fiber latent to restore local bijectivity and optimizes point-cloud losses rather than a general surjective likelihood framework.

reviewed_competitors.title: Multi-Chart Flows
reviewed_competitors.difference: Kalatzis and colleagues use multiple coordinate charts to learn distributions on topologically nontrivial manifolds. Their target is unconditional manifold density, while BundleNet specializes charts to a supervised many-to-one map and conditional fibers; both rely on locality to avoid one global Euclidean parameterization.

reviewed_competitors.title: Fiber Bundle Morphisms as a Framework for Modeling Many-to-Many Maps
reviewed_competitors.difference: Coda and colleagues extend the same fiber-bundle program to stochastic many-to-many relations using bundle morphisms and test against conditional GANs and conditional normalizing flows. It broadens BundleNet's deterministic ground-truth map but remains a small synthetic workshop study rather than a high-dimensional validation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Universal Joint Approximation of Manifolds and Densities by Simple Injective Flows
reviewed_competitors.difference: Puthawala and colleagues characterize when injective flows can jointly approximate embedded manifolds and densities and prove that embedding dimension controls topological obstructions. BundleNet supplies an empirical local conditional construction but no analogous approximation or topology-recovery theorem.

reviewed_competitors.title: Understanding and Mitigating Exploding Inverses in Invertible Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Behrmann and colleagues show that nominally invertible architectures can become numerically non-invertible and fail at sampling or change-of-variables calculations. BundleNet relies on inverse evaluation but does not report bi-Lipschitz control, conditioning diagnostics, or out-of-distribution inverse stability.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning geometry and topology via multi-chart flows
reviewed_competitors.difference: Yu and colleagues give a general multi-flow gluing scheme and algorithms for geometry and topology estimation, showing significant topology-recovery gains over a single flow. This advances the chart-consistency and learned-topology questions that BundleNet leaves to manually selected neighborhoods and priors.

reviewed_competitors.title: AutoInt: Automatic Integration for Fast Neural Volume Rendering
reviewed_competitors.difference: AutoInt trains a coordinate network through its derivative graph so the recovered antiderivative yields a definite integral in two network evaluations. It is specialized to coordinate signals and ray integrals rather than expectations over a learned data density, but it directly predates the focal paper's broad practical-neural-integration framing and actually reports a speed-quality tradeoff.

reviewed_competitors.title: Neural Additive Models: Interpretable Machine Learning with Neural Nets
reviewed_competitors.difference: NAMs jointly train one neural shape function per observed feature and show competitive interpretable prediction. The focal model adds a bijective feature transform and product-density integration, gaining flexible coordinates but losing NAM's input-feature interpretability and retaining the same additive interaction restriction in latent space.

reviewed_competitors.title: Density estimation using Real NVP
reviewed_competitors.difference: Real NVP established tractable exact likelihood, inversion, sampling, and latent manipulation through coupling transforms. The focal work's novelty is downstream factorized expected-loss supervision, not the bijective change-of-variables machinery, and it inherits flows' density-modeling and dimension-preservation costs.

reviewed_competitors.title: Glow: Generative Flow with Invertible 1x1 Convolutions
reviewed_competitors.difference: Glow supplies the exact image architecture used by the focal experiments and improves flow likelihood through invertible 1x1 convolutions. The focal contribution is the separable classifier and integral regularizers; its weaker density and classification results should therefore be evaluated as costs layered on this existing backbone.

reviewed_competitors.title: Do Deep Generative Models Know What They Don't Know?
reviewed_competitors.relationship: Critical prior on flow-likelihood OOD failure
reviewed_competitors.difference: Nalisnick et al. show that flows, VAEs, and PixelCNNs can assign higher likelihood to semantic OOD images and analyze background statistics as a cause. The focal approach acknowledges this work yet depends on a faithful flow density to define its global OOD integral, a vulnerability visible in its CIFAR-10/SVHN results.

reviewed_competitors.title: Likelihood Ratios for Out-of-Distribution Detection
reviewed_competitors.difference: Likelihood ratios subtract a background model to remove population-level statistics that confound raw deep likelihood. The focal method instead imposes a broad contrastive latent prior and reject loss; it does not explicitly cancel background complexity and therefore offers no corresponding semantic-likelihood correction.

reviewed_competitors.title: Deep Anomaly Detection with Outlier Exposure
reviewed_competitors.difference: Outlier Exposure trains against a diverse auxiliary dataset and shows transfer to unseen anomalies across vision and language. The focal paper avoids real OOD data by integrating a synthetic q, but OE is much stronger on SVHN/CIFAR and directly tests whether analytic latent coverage compensates for realism and diversity of observed outliers.

reviewed_competitors.title: Energy-based Out-of-distribution Detection
reviewed_competitors.difference: Energy OOD uses log-sum-exp logits as a post-hoc score or trainable objective and reports large FPR95 improvements with conventional WideResNets. The focal method integrates related exponential logit moments but pays for a flow and additive head, while not comparing matched FPR95 or modern discriminative accuracy.

reviewed_competitors.title: VOS: Learning What You Don't Know by Virtual Outlier Synthesis
reviewed_competitors.difference: VOS samples low-likelihood class-conditional feature regions and contrastively shapes an uncertainty boundary for both classification and object detection. It targets boundary-relevant outliers rather than averaging a fixed global q, making it the closest contemporary test of whether adaptive synthesis is more useful than factorized full-volume integration.

reviewed_competitors.title: Non-Parametric Outlier Synthesis
reviewed_competitors.difference: NPOS removes VOS's parametric Gaussian feature assumption and interprets boundary synthesis as rejection sampling around a learned nonparametric embedding distribution. It offers a more adaptive modern alternative to the focal paper's fixed independent Gaussian-mixture geometry and should be included in any current empirical revival.

reviewed_competitors.title: Virtual Adversarial Training: A Regularization Method for Supervised and Semi-Supervised Learning
reviewed_competitors.difference: VAT finds the local direction that maximally changes the predictive distribution and needs no label, directly targeting a worst local inconsistency. The focal method averages a uniform latent box and can factor that expectation, but does not show that average coverage beats an inexpensive adversarial direction on real tasks.

reviewed_competitors.title: FixMatch: Simplifying Semi-Supervised Learning with Consistency and Confidence
reviewed_competitors.difference: FixMatch combines confidence-thresholded pseudo-labels with weak-to-strong augmentation and supplies extensive ablations and strong low-label vision results. The focal method replaces domain augmentation with latent integration for tabular portability, but also uses pseudo-labels and never isolates which component causes its gains.

reviewed_competitors.title: Certified Adversarial Robustness via Randomized Smoothing
reviewed_competitors.difference: Randomized smoothing converts noise-stable classifiers into classifiers with tight l2 certificates and scales to ImageNet. The focal local integral also averages a neighborhood distribution, but it neither changes the prediction rule to obtain a certificate nor evaluates real images, so robustness should be described as regularization rather than guarantee.

reviewed_competitors.title: On the Effectiveness of Interval Bound Propagation for Training Verifiably Robust Models
reviewed_competitors.difference: IBP trains against an upper bound on worst-case loss and reports verified accuracy on MNIST, CIFAR-10, SVHN, and downscaled ImageNet. The focal expected latent-box loss can be cheaper for its separable head but provides no all-points guarantee and is assessed only on a synthetic adversary.

reviewed_competitors.title: Towards Stable and Efficient Training of Verifiably Robust Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: CROWN-IBP mixes inexpensive interval bounds with tighter linear relaxations to improve verified l-infinity robustness. It demonstrates the evaluation standard missing from the focal work: clean accuracy, verified error, explicit epsilon, and real-image datasets under a mathematically worst-case objective.

reviewed_competitors.title: OpenOOD: Benchmarking Generalized Out-of-Distribution Detection
reviewed_competitors.difference: OpenOOD implements more than thirty methods under standardized generalized-OOD settings designed to prevent unfair and inconclusive comparisons. It supplies the natural modern validation harness for the focal regularizer, whose tables mix copied baseline numbers, unspecified AUPR conventions, and different architectures.

reviewed_competitors.title: Fourier Neural Operator for Parametric Partial Differential Equations

reviewed_competitors.title: Towards Physics-informed Deep Learning for Turbulent Flow Prediction

reviewed_competitors.title: Solver-in-the-Loop: Learning from Differentiable Physics to Interact with Iterative PDE-Solvers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: alternative remedy for stable long-horizon learned correction
reviewed_competitors.difference: Solver-in-the-Loop backpropagates through iterative PDE evolution so training sees the model's effect on future solver states; the focal paper uses independent one-step supervision and denoising noise, avoiding differentiable-solver coupling but retaining exposure-bias and conservation risks.

reviewed_competitors.title: Using Machine Learning to Augment Coarse-Grid Computational Fluid Dynamics Simulations
reviewed_competitors.difference: This work inserts learned corrections into a coarse CFD pipeline for high-Rayleigh-number convection; the focal model replaces time integration end to end, which is simpler to port but lacks the numerical solver's built-in structure and guarantees.

reviewed_competitors.title: Turbulence forecasting via Neural ODE
reviewed_competitors.difference: The Neural ODE formulation learns continuous-time reduced turbulence dynamics and examines phenomenology and dissipation; the focal work predicts full coarse grid states at fixed discrete steps and validates on more demanding 3D solver-generated regimes.

reviewed_competitors.title: Accelerating Eulerian Fluid Simulation With Convolutional Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Tompson et al. use a CNN to approximate the pressure projection while retaining the classical Eulerian operator-splitting pipeline; the focal paper learns the full coarse transition and therefore removes more engineering at the cost of less explicit physics.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Mesh-Based Simulation with Graph Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: MeshGraphNets applies encode-process-decode message passing and denoising-style training on unstructured adaptive meshes; the focal paper transfers those principles to simpler grid CNNs and focuses on turbulent spectral and statistical fidelity.

reviewed_competitors.title: Stable a posteriori LES of 2D turbulence using convolutional neural networks: Backscattering analysis and generalization to higher Re via transfer learning
reviewed_competitors.relationship: stability- and OOD-focused learned turbulence closure
reviewed_competitors.difference: This paper evaluates a neural LES closure a posteriori, analyzes backscatter, and transfers to higher Reynolds number inside a solver; the focal work is end-to-end and includes 3D regimes, but demonstrates weaker physical-parameter extrapolation and no closure-level interpretability.

reviewed_competitors.title: Message Passing Neural PDE Solvers
reviewed_competitors.difference: MP-PDE uses message passing and temporal bundling to handle irregular discretizations and generalize across PDE parameters, topology, and resolution; the focal CNN has stronger specialized turbulence diagnostics and 3D Athena++ data but retrains by domain and step size.

reviewed_competitors.title: A Numerical Proof of Shell Model Turbulence Closure
reviewed_competitors.difference: The shell-model work tests a recurrent closure on long-time low- and high-order inertial-range statistics in a narrow reduced system; the focal paper covers richer spatial fields and multiple domains but offers no claim of statistically indistinguishable closure and exhibits OOD failures.

reviewed_competitors.title: PDE-Refiner: Achieving Accurate Long Rollouts with Neural PDE Solvers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: later direct response to autoregressive spectrum and stability failure
reviewed_competitors.difference: PDE-Refiner iteratively denoises predictions at multiple noise levels to recover low-amplitude frequencies and supplies uncertainty signals for long rollouts; the focal method uses one correction scale and no predictive uncertainty, making the later work a natural extension of its empirical noise result.

reviewed_competitors.title: Differentiable Turbulence: Closure as a partial differential equation constrained optimization
reviewed_competitors.difference: Differentiable Turbulence optimizes closures through PDE-constrained rollouts and systematically studies inductive biases and OOD behavior; the focal method is easier to deploy without a differentiable solver but cannot inherit its conservation structure or solver-coupled objective.

reviewed_competitors.title: Generalizable data-driven turbulence closure modeling on unstructured grids with differentiable physics
reviewed_competitors.difference: This approach couples graph neural closures with differentiable finite elements on unstructured 2D and 3D domains and targets generalization across geometry; the focal model is restricted to structured grids and shows that translation-equivariant convolutions alone do not solve box-size extrapolation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Weight-space symmetry in deep networks gives rise to permutation saddles, connected by equal-loss valleys across the loss landscape
reviewed_competitors.difference: Brea et al. construct permutation collision points and equal-loss paths in deep networks and numerically identify permutation saddles. The present paper studies the distinct outgoing-weight split symmetry and derives a finer local Hessian block for it.

reviewed_competitors.title: Geometry of the Loss Landscape in Overparameterized Neural Networks: Symmetries and Invariances
reviewed_competitors.difference: Simsek et al. count and connect affine subspaces of symmetry-induced critical points and global minima under width expansion. This submission zooms into adding one neuron and classifies the new local curvature using Y and V.

reviewed_competitors.title: Spurious Local Minima are Common in Two-Layer ReLU Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Safran and Shamir give computer-assisted spurious-minimum results for matched-width ReLU teacher-student networks with Gaussian inputs and orthonormal teachers for widths 6-20. This paper's benign claim is only for a softplus student of width one, while its width-four numerics again find spurious minima.

reviewed_competitors.title: The Effects of Mild Over-parameterization on the Optimization Landscape of Shallow ReLU Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Safran et al. prove under technical conditions that adding one ReLU neuron turns non-global minima into saddles and analyze local convexity near global minima. This paper gives an activation-agnostic split-line inertia mechanism but does not show that every bad minimum is annihilated.

reviewed_competitors.title: Analytic Study of Families of Spurious Minima in Two-Layer ReLU Neural Networks: A Tale of Symmetry II
reviewed_competitors.difference: Arjevani and Field analytically estimate losses and Hessian spectra of symmetric ReLU spurious minima at finite dimension and locate fractional dimensions where saddles become minima. The present paper instead follows a single neuron-splitting parameter through a general smooth-network Hessian.

reviewed_competitors.title: Annihilation of Spurious Minima in Two-Layer ReLU Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Arjevani and Field show analytically that added neurons annihilate symmetric ReLU minima while less symmetric minima require more width, using interlacing and representation theory. It addresses how much width removes bad minima more directly than the one-split local classification here.

reviewed_competitors.title: Gradient flow dynamics of shallow ReLU networks for square loss and orthogonal inputs
reviewed_competitors.difference: Boursier et al. prove convergence, implicit bias, initial alignment, and saddle-to-saddle dynamics for shallow ReLU gradient flow on orthogonal inputs at small initialization. This paper characterizes local critical geometry but supplies no comparable trajectory or convergence theorem.

reviewed_competitors.title: Should Under-parameterized Student Networks Copy or Average Teacher Weights?
reviewed_competitors.difference: The successor replaces the broad archived headline with a systematic copy-average theory, proves the one-neuron orientation under explicit interaction assumptions, gives closed forms for erf and ReLU, and treats multi-neuron underparameterization. It reports radius uniqueness numerically for general differentiable activations rather than relying on the archived converse step.

reviewed_competitors.title: Expand-and-Cluster: Parameter Recovery of Neural Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Martinelli et al. operationalize overparameterization by training wider students and clustering their learned neurons to recover a target network, including deep synthetic targets. It uses width as an optimization aid and then compresses, whereas this submission studies fixed few-neuron landscape geometry.

reviewed_competitors.title: Hidden Minima in Two-Layer ReLU Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Arjevani studies spurious minima that standard optimization empirically avoids and distinguishes them via locally minimizing arcs when leading Hessian spectra coincide. This shows why local eigenvalues and basin counts alone, the main diagnostics here, may miss dynamically hidden structure.

reviewed_competitors.title: Loss Landscape of Shallow ReLU-like Neural Networks: Stationary Points, Saddle Escape, and Network Embedding
reviewed_competitors.difference: Wu, Simsek, and Ged handle nonsmooth ReLU-like empirical losses with directional stationarity, define first-order escape neurons, and analyze embedding into wider networks. It extends the width-growth question beyond the twice-differentiable setting assumed here and connects geometry more directly to descent.

reviewed_competitors.title: Flat Channels to Infinity in Neural Loss Landscapes
reviewed_competitors.difference: Martinelli et al. turn this submission's qualitative late-snapshot observation into a dedicated theory and empirical study of slowly decreasing channels where incoming weights merge and cancelling output weights diverge, including SGD and Adam. It supersedes the ad hoc toy explanation of local minima at infinity.

reviewed_competitors.title: Simplicity Bias and Optimization Threshold in Two-Layer ReLU Networks
reviewed_competitors.difference: Boursier and Flammarion show that even overparameterized ReLU networks can converge to simpler spurious minima beyond an optimization threshold. This cautions against inferring practical success merely from the new escape dimensions exposed by splitting.

reviewed_competitors.title: Graph Element Networks: adaptive, structured computation and memory
reviewed_competitors.relationship: GEN is a direct predecessor and a baseline in the draft: it represents spatial processes with graph nodes whose positions and connectivity can be optimized, then maps between nodes and query locations.
reviewed_competitors.difference: GEN already supplies adaptive spatial computation and variable-precision evaluation but uses simpler interpolation and is framed mainly as a learned input-output process. GraphSplineNets adds C1 temporal and spatial reconstruction plus an ABD solver; the comparison should therefore separate spline choice from the preexisting adaptive-node idea.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning continuous-time PDEs from sparse data with graph neural networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: This ICLR 2021 work is a close prior continuous-time, data-driven GNN model for unknown PDE dynamics on arbitrary spatial and temporal grids, including sparse and noisy observations.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It learns the continuous-time vector field and integrates it with a method-of-lines/ODE formulation, whereas GraphSplineNets predicts coarse state updates and interpolates between them. It directly tests irregular time steps and unstructured grids, evidence missing from this draft, but pays numerical integration cost that GraphSplineNets aims to avoid.

reviewed_competitors.title: Multipole Graph Neural Operator for Parametric Partial Differential Equations
reviewed_competitors.relationship: MGNO is an early graph neural operator designed to learn discretization-invariant PDE solution maps with linear-complexity multilevel graph interactions.
reviewed_competitors.difference: MGNO targets operator learning and demonstrates mesh-refinement transfer, while GraphSplineNets targets fast autoregressive dynamics and obtains continuous queries through a post-prediction polynomial basis. MGNO is a stronger comparison for continuum and resolution claims; GraphSplineNets offers a simpler local structured solve and temporal interpolation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Mesh-Based Simulation with Graph Networks
reviewed_competitors.relationship: MeshGraphNets is the architectural ancestor of the paper's MPNN baseline and an established learned simulator with adaptive meshes over diverse fluids, solids, and cloth.
reviewed_competitors.difference: MeshGraphNets advances discrete states with learned message passing and can adapt mesh resolution, while GraphSplineNets reduces rollout nodes and steps then reconstructs a C1 field. MeshGraphNets covers much broader geometry and physical systems; GraphSplineNets uniquely emphasizes arbitrary coordinate queries and a differentiable spline solve.

reviewed_competitors.title: Message Passing Neural PDE Solvers
reviewed_competitors.relationship: MP-PDE is a contemporaneous learned message-passing solver explicitly designed for resolution, topology, geometry, boundary-condition, and irregular-discretization generalization with stable autoregressive rollouts.
reviewed_competitors.difference: MP-PDE learns neural numerical components and a zero-stability-inspired training procedure rather than filling coarse predictions with a fixed spline. It is a much stronger baseline for general solver and stability claims, whereas GraphSplineNets may use fewer neural steps and provides an explicit C1 coordinate-query representation.

reviewed_competitors.title: Continuous PDE Dynamics Forecasting with Implicit Neural Representations
reviewed_competitors.relationship: DINo is the closest contemporaneous alternative: a data-driven model of continuous-time dynamics over spatially continuous implicit neural representations, trainable on sparse irregular grids and queryable at new locations and resolutions.
reviewed_competitors.difference: DINo evolves a compact neural-field latent state with a neural ODE, while GraphSplineNets evolves coarse graph states and uses fixed local polynomials. DINo directly evaluates spatial and temporal extrapolation and grid transfer; GraphSplineNets offers structured, potentially cheaper reconstruction but does not run those validation tests in this draft.

reviewed_competitors.title: Operator Learning with Neural Fields: Tackling PDEs on General Geometries
reviewed_competitors.relationship: CORAL is a later coordinate-based neural-operator approach covering initial-value prediction, dynamics, inverse design, arbitrary sampling, and convex, nonconvex, and manifold geometries.
reviewed_competitors.difference: CORAL represents whole functions with modulated neural fields and processes compact latent codes, avoiding tensor-product spline restrictions and demonstrating resolution/geometry transfer. GraphSplineNets has an analytically structured local basis and linear system that may be more interpretable and faster, but its geometry and resolution evidence is far narrower.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning Space-Time Continuous Neural PDEs from Partially Observed States
reviewed_competitors.relationship: This later work directly combines collocation and the method of lines in a space-time continuous latent neural PDE learned from noisy, partial observations on irregular spatiotemporal grids.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It learns a probabilistic latent PDE and performs variational inference with multiple shooting, explicitly addressing missing and noisy data; GraphSplineNets is a deterministic coarse-rollout surrogate with a much cheaper algebraic reconstruction. It is also a useful contrast because its collocation actually participates in a differential dynamics model rather than only fitting predicted values.

reviewed_competitors.title: Geometry-Informed Neural Operator for Large-Scale 3D PDEs
reviewed_competitors.relationship: GINO is a later scalable geometry-aware neural operator that maps irregular point clouds through graph operators to a Fourier latent grid and back, with a discretization-convergence claim and large 3-D CFD evaluation.
reviewed_competitors.difference: GINO tackles varying 3-D geometries, boundary conditions, and mesh refinement at industrial scale, far beyond the regular 2-D tests here. GraphSplineNets is lighter-weight and designed for temporal rollouts, but its tensor-product spline does not inherit GINO's geometry or discretization guarantees.

reviewed_competitors.title: Space and Time Continuous Physics Simulation From Partial Observations
reviewed_competitors.relationship: This later recurrent-GNN and spatiotemporal-attention model addresses essentially the same continuous forecast-and-interpolate task from sparse observations and evaluates arbitrary locations in both space and time.
reviewed_competitors.difference: It uses two interlinked dynamics systems and an attention observer rather than a fixed spline, making it more flexible but potentially more expensive. Its evaluation explicitly includes the extended continuous-query task that GraphSplineNets motivates but does not separately measure in the archived draft.

reviewed_competitors.title: Learning time-dependent PDE via graph neural networks and deep operator network for robust accuracy on irregular grids
reviewed_competitors.relationship: GraphDeepONet is a later autoregressive GNN/operator hybrid that predicts time-dependent PDE solutions on arbitrary grids and provides a universal-approximation analysis over arbitrary time intervals.
reviewed_competitors.difference: GraphDeepONet obtains continuous operator evaluation through a DeepONet branch-trunk factorization and tests irregular grids and time extrapolation. GraphSplineNets instead uses explicit local polynomial reconstruction with fewer neural rollout calls; its theory concerns the classical spline component rather than the learned end-to-end operator.

reviewed_competitors.title: AROMA: Preserving Spatial Structure for Latent PDE Modeling with Local Neural Fields
reviewed_competitors.relationship: AROMA is a later local-neural-field surrogate for irregular grids, point clouds, complex geometry, arbitrary spatial queries, and stable long rollouts.
reviewed_competitors.difference: AROMA compresses observations into spatially meaningful latent tokens and uses attention plus a diffusion-based dynamics objective, avoiding the global-latent and fixed-spline bottlenecks. It is more expressive and empirically broader; GraphSplineNets offers deterministic reconstruction and a simpler explicit accuracy-cost knob through collocation count.

reviewed_competitors.title: Vectorized Conditional Neural Fields: A Framework for Solving Time-dependent Parametric Partial Differential Equations
reviewed_competitors.relationship: VCNeF is a later space-time neural-field approach that evaluates many query coordinates in parallel and targets parameter generalization plus spatial and temporal zero-shot super-resolution.
reviewed_competitors.difference: VCNeF conditions a shared neural field on initial conditions and PDE parameters and models query interactions with attention. GraphSplineNets is local and structured, likely cheaper at low order, but does not test parameter transfer, dimensional scaling, or zero-shot super-resolution explicitly.

reviewed_competitors.title: CALM-PDE: Continuous and Adaptive Convolutions for Latent Space Modeling of Time-dependent PDEs
reviewed_competitors.relationship: CALM-PDE is a current direct alternative that learns continuous local convolution kernels and adaptive query points for compressed latent dynamics on regular and irregular domains.
reviewed_competitors.difference: Both methods reduce physical-space compute and optimize sampling locations. CALM-PDE learns epsilon-local continuous convolutional encoders and decoders and benchmarks memory and inference against transformer surrogates, whereas GraphSplineNets fixes a polynomial basis and specializes the linear solve. A modern comparison would test which adaptation signal, basis, and solver yields better conditioning and accuracy per byte.
